programs.program: Màster Universitari en Música com a Art Interdisciplinari / University Master's Degree in Music as an Interdisciplinary Art
programs.institution: Universitat de Barcelona (UB) with Universitat Rovira i Virgili (URV) and Escola Superior de Música de Catalunya (ESMUC), in collaboration with Institució Milà i Fontanals (CSIC)
programs.institutionType: Joint official university master run by two public universities plus the public Catalan music conservatoire, with a public research council institute (CSIC) collaborating
programs.publicPrivate: PUBLIC. UB and URV are public universities of the Catalan university system; ESMUC is a public centre of the Generalitat de Catalunya; CSIC is the Spanish state research council. Confirmed by the per-credit price, which follows the Catalan public 'preus públics' decree structure.
programs.qualification: Màster Universitari (official university master), 60 ECTS — a real state-recognised second-cycle degree giving doctoral access.
programs.accreditationStatus: Official university master, awarded by UB with URV and ESMUC. Genuine second-cycle degree, in the university (not enseñanzas artísticas) track.
programs.language: Catalan AND Spanish. This is the decisive field for this candidate: teaching is in both Catalan and Castilian, and Catalan is used as a normal medium of instruction, not as a courtesy. There is no English-taught route.
programs.languageRequirement: No certificate level is published for admission. In practice the applicant must be able to follow classes in Catalan and Spanish. UNVERIFIED whether the UB demands a formal certificate — ask the UB master's admissions office.
programs.englishTest: None.
programs.durationEcts: 60 ECTS, one academic year, September to June.
programs.focus: Music as an interdisciplinary art — the relationships between music and the plastic and visual arts, literature, cinema and new technologies. Musicological and humanities-led, not technical.
programs.whatYouStudy: Interdisciplinary connections across music, plastic arts, visual arts, literature, cinema and new technologies. New technologies appear as an object of study rather than as a production skill. There is no mixing, mastering, DAW, studio, spatial-audio or game-audio training.
programs.entryRequirements: A degree in humanities or social sciences, ideally art history, musicology, communication or musical studies. Graduates of other university disciplines may be considered on an individual basis. Notably, the programme states it 'does not require high-level musical knowledge', though musical knowledge is assessed at admission. A Software Engineering BSc would be an 'other discipline' case-by-case admission.
programs.auditionSpec: No audition. Admission is by individual assessment of the academic record and profile. Musical knowledge is assessed but a high level is explicitly not required.
programs.portfolioSpec: No portfolio requirement published. UNVERIFIED whether a motivation letter or writing sample is required — ask UB.
programs.equipmentRequired: None published — this is a seminar-based humanities master.
programs.facilities: UB humanities facilities plus ESMUC. No production studio provision relevant to this candidate's goals.
programs.tuitionEU: Approximately €27.67 per credit, i.e. approximately €1,660 for the 60-credit degree, under the Catalan public price decree.
programs.tuitionNonEU: Approximately €82 per credit for non-EU students not residing in Spain — approximately €4,920 for the 60-credit degree. This is the concrete number to remember: CATALONIA APPLIES AN APPROXIMATELY 3x SURCHARGE to non-EU non-resident students on official university masters. That multiplier will apply to every Catalan public option he considers (including any UPF or UB programme), and it is the single most useful transferable fee fact from the Spanish half of this sweep.
programs.otherFees: Standard UB administrative and insurance charges apply on top; amounts UNVERIFIED.
programs.totalCostEstimate: Approximately €4,920 tuition for a non-EU non-resident, plus Barcelona living costs of roughly €1,100–1,500/month for one academic year (September to June), so approximately €15,000–18,000 all-in.
programs.scholarships: UNVERIFIED — none advertised for this programme. Catalan and UB scholarship schemes generally require prior residence.
programs.intakes: September (one intake, September to June).
programs.applicationOpens: UNVERIFIED — not on the ESMUC page. UB official master pre-inscription normally opens in the winter/spring preceding the September start; check the UB master's admissions portal from about January 2027.
programs.deadline: UNVERIFIED — contact UB directly.
programs.visaEligible: Yes — an official Màster Universitari supports a Spanish student visa and student residence permit.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: Yes in principle — graduates of other disciplines are considered individually and high-level musical knowledge is explicitly not required. This is unusually open by Spanish standards.
programs.recommendation: DO NOT APPLY. Included because it is a genuine public option the earlier sweeps missed, because it is one of the few Spanish masters in this space that would actually let a non-musician in, and above all because it pins down the Catalan non-EU fee multiplier (€27.67 vs €82 per credit) that he will need for every other Catalan option. But it is wrong for him on two counts: it is taught in Catalan and Spanish, which he does not speak, and it is a musicology/interdisciplinary-arts degree with no production, engineering or electronic music content. It would not move him toward being a producer or DJ. Use the fee data point, discard the programme.

programs.program: DCSL34 — Diploma Accademico di Secondo Livello in Musica Elettronica (Biennio)
programs.institution: Conservatorio Statale di Musica "Giuseppe Verdi" di Torino
programs.institutionType: State conservatoire (Conservatorio Statale di Musica) within the AFAM system (Alta Formazione Artistica, Musicale e Coreutica), under the Ministero dell'Università e della Ricerca
programs.publicPrivate: PUBLIC. Known because it is a 'Conservatorio Statale' — a state institution directly under the MUR's AFAM division; its course code DCSL34 is a ministerial course code assigned by the MUR, and its fee regime is anchored to the EDISU Piemonte regional right-to-study tax.
programs.qualification: Diploma Accademico di Secondo Livello in Musica Elettronica. This IS a real state second-cycle degree: under Italian law the biennio di II livello is equated to a Laurea Magistrale for the purposes of public competitions and further study, at EQF level 7. It is not a private certificate.
programs.accreditationStatus: State-accredited. DCSL34 is a ministerial course code in the MUR's AFAM register (searchable at valutazioni-afam.mur.gov.it). Fully recognised across the EHEA.
programs.language: Italian. Confirmed by the admission process, which includes a dedicated Italian language test for international candidates.
programs.languageRequirement: An Italian language test is part of the entrance examination for international candidates ('prova di lingua italiana', conditional, for international applicants only). The required level is not stated on the course page — Italian conservatoires normally demand B2. UNVERIFIED exact level; ask the segreteria.
programs.englishTest: None. English is not the medium of instruction.
programs.durationEcts: 2 years, 120 CFA (the standard for a biennio di II livello). The Torino course page links a 'Piano di studi' PDF rather than stating the credit total inline — UNVERIFIED inline, but 120 CFA is the ministerial standard for DCSL34.
programs.focus: Electronic music — electroacoustic composition, music informatics, live electronics and studio practice, in the Italian conservatoire tradition.
programs.whatYouStudy: Electroacoustic repertoire and its analysis, electronic/electroacoustic composition, music informatics, electroacoustics. Specific module list is in the linked Piano di studi PDF — UNVERIFIED in detail.
programs.entryRequirements: Candidates must hold EITHER a conservatoire diploma (old or new system) OR 'a bachelor's/master's degree or equivalent foreign qualification'. THIS IS THE KEY POINT: a foreign three-year university degree explicitly qualifies. The candidate's BSc in Software Engineering meets the formal entry requirement. What he must then survive is the entrance examination.
programs.auditionSpec: Six-part entrance examination: (1) presentation of a composition portfolio — mandatory, submitted via Dropbox one week before the practical exams; (2) practical analysis of electroacoustic repertoire using a DAW, headphones and optional analysis tools; (3) a technical knowledge test in computing, music informatics and electroacoustics — explicitly NON-BINDING, i.e. it informs placement rather than gating entry; (4) a motivational interview covering general knowledge of electronic music; (5) a conditional composition practical — 'elaborazione di un breve brano elettroacustico a partire da campioni' (building a short electroacoustic piece from samples), required ONLY of candidates who are not electronic-music composition graduates, so this WOULD apply to him; (6) a conditional Italian language test for international candidates. Note that the non-binding status of the technical test and the sample-based nature of the conditional composition task make this materially more reachable than any Spanish conservatoire audition.
programs.portfolioSpec: A 'portfolio compositivo' is mandatory and must be delivered by Dropbox one week before the practical exams. This is the centre of gravity of the application. Contents are not further specified — build a portfolio of original electroacoustic and electronic works with documentation, plus evidence of DAW fluency, since a live DAW-based analysis task is also examined.
programs.equipmentRequired: For the analysis exam the candidate uses DAW software and headphones; whether these are provided or brought is UNVERIFIED. Bring your own headphones. A personal laptop with a DAW is effectively assumed.
programs.facilities: UNVERIFIED in detail — not published on the course page. Torino's Conservatorio has an established electronic music school; ask for a studio visit.
programs.tuitionEU: For Italian, EU and international students resident in Italy: a 'contributo onnicomprensivo annuale' of €2,300 for most schools, but €2,500 specifically for Musica elettronica and Direzione d'orchestra (Triennio and Biennio alike). Paid in three instalments: first instalment €156 (tassa EDISU + marca da bollo) at enrolment (20 May – 10 June), second by 30 December, third by 15 March. A 30% reduction is available for part-time enrolment.
programs.tuitionNonEU: €3,500 per year — THE RATE HE WOULD PAY. Verbatim from the official fee page: 'Per gli studenti Extra UE non residenti in Italia il contributo onnicomprensivo annuale è fissato in € 3.500'. This is a flat non-EU non-resident rate, and crucially it appears to be charged INSTEAD OF the ISEE-scaled band system, meaning he cannot reduce it by proving low family income the way he could at Bologna or Cuneo. Over two years: €7,000. Structured as €156 at enrolment plus two later instalments.
programs.otherFees: The €156 first instalment comprises the tassa regionale EDISU Piemonte plus marca da bollo, and is stated to be excluded from the contributo figure. Immatricolazione and frequenza charges are also stated as excluded from the contributo — amounts UNVERIFIED, ask the segreteria.
programs.totalCostEstimate: Approximately €7,000 tuition over two years, plus roughly €312 in EDISU/bollo, plus Turin living costs of roughly €800–1,100/month. Turin is among the cheaper large Italian cities. Two-year all-in estimate approximately €27,000–34,000 before any scholarship.
programs.scholarships: EDISU Piemonte (the regional right-to-study agency) runs income-based borse di studio that non-EU students CAN win; these can cover fees, a maintenance grant and subsidised housing, and are the realistic route to something approaching full funding in Italy. A Tunisian family income will generally place him in the lowest bracket. The EDISU bando normally opens in the summer preceding the academic year. The MAECI Italian Government scholarship (already in the database) is the other route. Programme-specific scholarships: none advertised. UNVERIFIED whether EDISU eligibility requires the ISEE parificato — it does in practice; budget for obtaining one via a CAF/Patronato.
programs.intakes: Autumn (Italian academic year begins late October/November; admission exams typically in September).
programs.applicationOpens: UNVERIFIED on the pages consulted. Italian conservatoire ammissioni bandi are typically published in spring and close in summer, with exams in September. For a 2027/28 start, watch conservatoriotorino.eu from about March 2027. Non-EU applicants must ALSO complete Universitaly pre-enrolment, which runs on a separate and earlier Ministry calendar — this is the step that most often derails non-EU applicants.
programs.deadline: UNVERIFIED. Note the enrolment instalment window of 20 May – 10 June referenced in the fee schedule (PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date), which suggests the admission cycle concludes earlier than the September exam date implies.
programs.visaEligible: Yes. A Diploma Accademico di Secondo Livello at a state conservatoire supports an Italian student visa (visto per studio) and permesso di soggiorno per studio. Non-EU applicants resident abroad must pre-enrol through the Universitaly portal before sitting the entrance exam, and are admitted against an annually published non-EU contingent (a reserved quota of places) — check the conservatoire's contingente for Musica Elettronica, as it can be very small.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: YES, formally. The published entry requirement accepts 'a bachelor's/master's degree or equivalent foreign qualification', and the conservatoire has built an explicit bridge for non-electronic-music graduates: a sample-based composition practical instead of assumed compositional training, and a technical test that is expressly non-binding. He is formally eligible. The real gate is the mandatory composition portfolio and the Italian language test.
programs.recommendation: APPLY — this is one of the two best Italian targets for him and should be on the shortlist. The formal door is open to a foreign three-year degree holder, the conditional composition task is sample-based rather than score-based, and the technical test is non-binding — which is as accommodating as an Italian state conservatoire gets. Two things must be started immediately in the portfolio year: (1) Italian to B2, which his French will make faster than he expects, and (2) a genuine 'portfolio compositivo' of original electroacoustic work, not DJ mixes — the examiners want composition and DAW-based analytical fluency. The cost warning is real: at €3,500/year for non-EU non-residents Torino is the most expensive Italian conservatoire in this sweep and, unlike Bologna and Cuneo, that flat rate appears not to be reducible by proving low family income. Offset it by applying to EDISU Piemonte in the same cycle. Verify the non-EU contingent for Musica Elettronica early — a tiny quota can make an otherwise open programme unreachable.

programs.program: DCSL34 — Diploma Accademico di Secondo Livello in Musica Elettronica, indirizzo Sound Design (Biennio)
programs.institution: Conservatorio di Musica "Giovan Battista Martini" di Bologna
programs.institutionType: State conservatoire within the AFAM system, under the Ministero dell'Università e della Ricerca
programs.publicPrivate: PUBLIC. Confirmed from the conservatoire's own fee regulation, whose letterhead reads 'Ministero dell'Università e della Ricerca — Alta Formazione Artistica, Musicale e Coreutica — Conservatorio di Musica "Giovan Battista Martini" di Bologna', and whose fee bands are set against the ER.GO regional right-to-study tax. State institution, Codice Fiscale 80074850373.
programs.qualification: Diploma Accademico di Secondo Livello in Musica elettronica (ind. Sound design) — a real state second-cycle degree, EQF 7, legally equated to a Laurea Magistrale for public competitions and doctoral access.
programs.accreditationStatus: State-accredited under ministerial course code DCSL34, in the MUR AFAM register. Genuine EHEA second-cycle qualification.
programs.language: Italian. Explicitly confirmed on the course page as the language of instruction.
programs.languageRequirement: Italian level B2, stated explicitly on the conservatoire's international students page. International students undergo 'verification of an adequate knowledge of the Italian language through the passing of a specific test'. This is a formal, tested requirement — not a soft expectation.
programs.englishTest: None. The conservatoire's international pages are in English but the teaching is not.
programs.durationEcts: 2 years, 120 CFA (60 CFA per year). Year 1: Electroacoustic Musical Composition 12, Integrated Audiovisual Composition 15, Sound Design Programming Techniques 4, Audio Systems and Programming Languages 7, Audio Recording Technologies 4, History of Electroacoustic Music 4, Non-European Music 4, Foreign Language 2, Electives 8. Year 2: Electroacoustic Musical Composition 12, Integrated Audiovisual Composition 10, Interactive Multimodal Environments 6, Music Media and Technologies 4, Multimedia Programming 6, Digital Audio Spatialisation 2, History of Electroacoustic Music 4, Electives 6, Final Thesis 10.
programs.focus: Electronic music with a declared Sound Design orientation — the most explicitly sound-design-badged of the state DCSL34 variants, with strong audiovisual, programming and spatial-audio content.
programs.whatYouStudy: See the credit breakdown above. Of direct interest to this candidate: Sound Design Programming Techniques, Audio Systems and Programming Languages, Multimedia Programming, Interactive Multimodal Environments and Digital Audio Spatialisation — a cluster that a software engineer would enter with a genuine advantage. Audio Recording Technologies covers studio practice. Note there is no commercial music production, DJ practice or music business content.
programs.entryRequirements: 'Completion of three-year electronic music studies or equivalent'. This is stricter than Torino's or Rovigo's wording and is the main obstacle: it points at a triennio in Musica Elettronica rather than any bachelor's degree. Whether a Software Engineering BSc plus a strong portfolio is accepted as 'equivalent' is UNVERIFIED and must be asked directly. The conservatoire also states generally that applicants must pass an admission test verifying theoretical, interpretative and/or compositional skills 'according to the parameters of the equivalent European musical institutions'.
programs.auditionSpec: An admission test is required, assessing theoretical, interpretative and/or composition skills. Content for DCSL34 specifically is UNVERIFIED — request the annual Bando di ammissione. A separate Italian language test applies to international students. The final examination of the degree itself is a creative project plus a written thesis discussion.
programs.portfolioSpec: UNVERIFIED for this course — not published on the course page. Given the sound design orientation, a portfolio is very likely central. Obtain the Bando di ammissione.
programs.equipmentRequired: UNVERIFIED — not published.
programs.facilities: UNVERIFIED in detail. The syllabus (spatialisation, interactive multimodal environments, audiovisual composition) implies a multichannel studio and interactive lab. Ask for specifics.
programs.tuitionEU: Precise, from the official Regolamento tasse e contributi a.a. 2025/2026. For Corsi accademici di II livello (Bienni) in Direzione d'Orchestra, Direzione di Coro, Musica Applicata, MUSICA ELETTRONICA and Corsi Jazz: imposta di bollo €16.00 + assicurazione €10.00 + tassa regionale per il diritto allo studio €140.00 + contributo di funzionamento MAXIMUM €2,000.00. So the maximum all-in is €2,166.00 per year. Other bienni are capped at €1,800.00 contributo; trienni at €1,600.00. The contributo is reduced on a sliding ISEEU scale: students with ISEEU at or below €22,000 and meeting merit conditions are fully exonerated from the contributo; between €22,001 and €40,000 the contributo is computed as a percentage (6% or 7% depending on band) of the ISEEU amount exceeding €13,000, producing figures such as €154, €455, €787.50 and €1,071 across the sub-bands; the €30,001–€40,000 band shows €1,150. Above €40,000 the maximum applies. Admission application fee: €100.00 for Bienni (non-refundable, payable per application).
programs.tuitionNonEU: THE RATE HE WOULD PAY, and this is the most important Italian finding in the sweep. Bologna's Art. 14 'Studenti internazionali non UE' states verbatim: 'Per gli studenti aventi la cittadinanza di Stati non appartenenti all'Unione Europea e non residenti in Italia sarà possibile accedere alle agevolazioni sul contributo di funzionamento solamente presentando le certificazioni ISEEE rilasciate dagli enti autorizzati.' In plain terms: a non-EU student CAN access the full income-based reduction — but ONLY by obtaining an ISEEE (Indicatore della Situazione Economica Equivalente all'Estero), the foreign-income equivalent of the ISEE, from an authorised body (a Patronato or CAF in Italy). Without it the rules are explicit and unforgiving: 'la mancata presentazione dell'ISEEE comporta l'attribuzione della Fascia di contribuzione più alta', and an ISEEE returning €0.00 'verrà in ogni caso rifiutato' and also triggers the highest band. PRACTICAL CONSEQUENCE: with a correctly filed ISEEE reflecting a typical Tunisian family income, he would very likely fall at or below the €22,000 threshold and pay little or no contributo — roughly €166/year in bollo, insurance and ER.GO tax. Without the ISEEE he pays the full €2,166/year. The paperwork is worth roughly €4,000 over two years.
programs.otherFees: Imposta di bollo €16.00/year; assicurazione €10.00/year; tassa regionale ER.GO per il diritto allo studio €140.00/year (payable separately by postal order or bank transfer, not through PagoPA, and NOT reducible by ISEE). Admission application fee €100.00. Late-payment penalties (indennità di mora) apply. Students from the second year fuori corso pay a higher contributo (bands rising to €1,790 and a maximum around €2,000+). Diploma issue fee applies at graduation — amount UNVERIFIED.
programs.totalCostEstimate: Best case with ISEEE filed: roughly €166/year in unavoidable charges, i.e. approximately €330 over two years, plus the €100 admission fee. Worst case without ISEEE: €2,166/year, approximately €4,332 over two years. Bologna living costs are high for Italy — roughly €900–1,300/month, and student housing is notoriously scarce. Two-year all-in estimate approximately €25,000–34,000 depending on housing, before any ER.GO scholarship.
programs.scholarships: ER.GO (Azienda Regionale per il Diritto agli Studi Superiori dell'Emilia-Romagna) runs income-based scholarships open to non-EU students, covering a maintenance grant, fee exemption and subsidised accommodation and meals. Combined with a low ISEEE this is the closest thing to full funding available in the Italian state conservatoire system. The ER.GO bando typically opens in summer. Obtaining the ISEEE through a Patronato or CAF is the prerequisite for both the fee reduction and the scholarship — treat it as the single most valuable piece of Italian paperwork. MAECI government scholarships (already in the database) are the alternative national route.
programs.intakes: Autumn — Italian academic year. Admission exams in the spring/summer preceding.
programs.applicationOpens: For a.a. 2025/26, applications for AMMISSIONI (all courses) and TRASFERIMENTI ran 17 March – 12 April 2025 (PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date). Expect a comparable mid-March opening in 2027 for a 2027/28 start. Non-EU applicants must separately complete Universitaly pre-enrolment before enrolling for the entrance examinations — this runs on the Ministry's own earlier calendar.
programs.deadline: For a.a. 2025/26 the application deadline was 12 April 2025 (PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date). After the ranking list is published, admitted candidates must enrol within 10 days — a very short window that requires funds and documents to be ready in advance.
programs.visaEligible: Yes. State conservatoire second-level diploma supports an Italian student visa and permesso di soggiorno per studio. The official international students page confirms: 'non-EU citizens not residing in Italy, before proceeding with their enrollment to the entrance examinations, will have to present a pre-enrollment request on the Universitaly portal.' Do not skip or delay this — missing the Universitaly window invalidates the whole application regardless of academic merit.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: UNCERTAIN, and less open than Torino, Rovigo or Cuneo. The stated requirement is completion of three-year electronic music studies 'or equivalent', which reads as pointing at a triennio in the discipline rather than at any bachelor's degree. Whether a Software Engineering BSc plus portfolio counts as equivalent must be confirmed in writing before investing in an application.
programs.recommendation: WORTH PURSUING, but ask the eligibility question first. The syllabus is the best technical fit in this entire sweep for a software engineer — Sound Design Programming Techniques, Audio Systems and Programming Languages, Multimedia Programming, Interactive Multimodal Environments and Digital Audio Spatialisation are modules where his background is an asset rather than a gap. And the money can be close to zero if he files an ISEEE. But the entry wording is the strictest of the four Italian conservatoires here, so the very first action is an email to the segreteria didattica asking whether a foreign three-year Computer/Software Engineering degree plus a documented electronic music portfolio is accepted as 'equivalent' for DCSL34 admission. Do that in autumn 2026, before spending the portfolio year optimising for this specific programme. Two non-negotiable preparations regardless: Italian to a tested B2, and the ISEEE paperwork route mapped out with a Patronato well before enrolment. Caution him that this is an electroacoustic composition and sound design degree, not a route to commercial dance-music production — it would make him a far better sound designer and audio programmer than DJ.

programs.program: DCSL60 — Diploma Accademico di Secondo Livello in Musica Applicata, indirizzo Sound Design (Biennio)
programs.institution: Conservatorio di Musica "Francesco Venezze" di Rovigo
programs.institutionType: State conservatoire within the AFAM system, under the Ministero dell'Università e della Ricerca
programs.publicPrivate: PUBLIC. A Conservatorio Statale di Musica; its right-to-study tax is administered by ESU Padova (the Veneto regional agency), and foreign students without a codice fiscale are directed to dirittoallostudio@esu.pd.it — both markers of a state AFAM institution.
programs.qualification: Diploma Accademico di Secondo Livello in Musica Applicata — explicitly stated on the official page as EHEA second cycle, EQF level 7. A real state-recognised second-cycle degree, equated to a Laurea Magistrale.
programs.accreditationStatus: State-accredited under ministerial course code DCSL60 in the MUR AFAM register. The official page itself states the EHEA 2° ciclo / EQF 7 mapping, which is unusually explicit and useful for credential recognition abroad.
programs.language: Italian. The requirement of B2 Italian for non-native speakers confirms the teaching language.
programs.languageRequirement: B2-level Italian proficiency is explicitly required of non-native Italian speakers as an admission condition. This is a stated, formal requirement.
programs.englishTest: None.
programs.durationEcts: 2 years, 120 ECTS/CFA: 55 CFA in year one, 56 CFA in year two, plus 10 CFA for the final thesis/project.
programs.focus: Applied music with a Sound Design orientation — DCSL60 'Musica Applicata' is a distinct ministerial course family from DCSL34 'Musica Elettronica', and is oriented toward music and sound applied to media rather than toward concert electroacoustic composition. For a candidate aiming at commercial and media work rather than academic art music, this framing is a better match.
programs.whatYouStudy: Composizione per la musica applicata alle immagini (15 CFA — composition for music applied to images, the largest single block); Composizione musicale elettroacustica – Sound Design; Informatica musicale; Storia della musica elettroacustica; audio post-production and mixing technologies.
programs.entryRequirements: Applicants must hold a 'diploma accademico di primo livello, o di diploma di laurea triennale, o di diploma di conservatorio', PLUS demonstrate B2 Italian for non-native speakers. THE KEY POINT: 'diploma di laurea triennale' — any three-year university degree — is listed as a qualifying route in its own right, alongside conservatoire diplomas. The candidate's BSc in Software Engineering satisfies this on its face. This is the most explicitly open entry wording of any Italian programme found in this sweep.
programs.auditionSpec: An oral assessment. The candidate must submit a portfolio containing video/audio works, electronic compositions, or scores, which the admissions committee evaluates for mastery of electronic production across multiple instrumentation contexts. Notably there is NO written theory paper, NO solfège/ear-training test and NO instrumental performance requirement published — the assessment is portfolio-plus-oral. For a self-taught candidate this is the lowest published barrier in the Italian state sector.
programs.portfolioSpec: Portfolio of video and/or audio works, electronic compositions, or scores, demonstrating command of electronic production across varied instrumentation contexts. Because scores are only ONE of the accepted alternatives, a purely audio/DAW-based portfolio is admissible — which is precisely what a year of self-directed work can produce. Build toward: music-to-picture cues (matching the 15-CFA composition-to-images core), original electronic pieces, and evidence of mixing and post-production competence.
programs.equipmentRequired: UNVERIFIED — not published. A personal laptop with a DAW should be assumed.
programs.facilities: UNVERIFIED — not published on the course page. The syllabus implies audio post-production and mixing facilities. Ask the conservatoire, and note that Rovigo is a small institution so studio access per student may be better than at a large conservatoire.
programs.tuitionEU: UNVERIFIED as to exact amounts. The mechanism is documented: the annual contributo is paid via PagoPA, is organised in ISEE-based income bands, and requires the ISEE certificate to be attached at enrolment to obtain reduction or exemption; the system verifies the ISEE against the INPS database and computes the amount due. Multi-sibling reductions apply (first child full, second 60%, third 40%). Total exemption applies for students with certified disability of 66% or more. For calibration only, comparable Veneto and Emilia-Romagna state conservatoires cap the biennio contributo between roughly €1,800 and €2,300 — but do NOT rely on that for Rovigo. Ask the segreteria for the current Regolamento contributi.
programs.tuitionNonEU: UNVERIFIED as to amount, but the mechanism is documented and favourable. Rovigo applies the standard Italian ISEE-band system rather than a flat non-EU surcharge: foreign students must present an ISEE (parificato/ISEEE), and if ISEE data is entered the system computes the amount due against the INPS database. Two documented facts help him directly: foreign candidates are EXEMPT from the admission examination fee ('i candidati stranieri sono esonerati dal versamento della tassa di esame di ammissione'), and foreign students without an Italian codice fiscale are told to contact ESU Padova at dirittoallostudio@esu.pd.it to sort out their position. Expect that with a low ISEEE reflecting Tunisian family income he lands in the lowest band or is exonerated. Confirm the exact band table by requesting the current Regolamento tasse e contributi from the segreteria.
programs.otherFees: Tassa regionale per il diritto allo studio universitario (ESU Veneto) — payable annually, amount UNVERIFIED; the conservatoire publishes an annual notice for this. Marca da bollo. Admission examination fee — WAIVED for foreign candidates.
programs.totalCostEstimate: Cannot be stated precisely without the contributi table. On the Italian pattern, with an ISEEE filed, expect anywhere from near-zero to roughly €2,000/year. Rovigo is a small provincial Veneto city with materially lower living costs than Bologna, Turin or Milan — roughly €600–850/month, and housing is far easier to find. This combination of a low barrier to entry and low cost of living is the reason this programme deserves serious attention.
programs.scholarships: ESU Padova (the Veneto regional right-to-study agency covering Rovigo) runs income-based borse di studio open to non-EU students, covering maintenance, fee exemption and subsidised housing. The conservatoire directs foreign students to ESU directly, which suggests a working pathway. MAECI government scholarships are the alternative national route. UNVERIFIED whether the conservatoire itself offers any internal award.
programs.intakes: Autumn — Italian academic year.
programs.applicationOpens: UNVERIFIED — not published on the course page. Italian conservatoire ammissioni bandi are typically issued in spring. Watch conservatoriorovigo.it from about March 2027, and complete Universitaly pre-enrolment on the Ministry calendar in parallel.
programs.deadline: UNVERIFIED — obtain the annual Bando di ammissione.
programs.visaEligible: Yes. A Diploma Accademico di Secondo Livello from a state conservatoire supports an Italian student visa and permesso di soggiorno per studio. Non-EU applicants resident abroad must pre-enrol via Universitaly and compete for places within the annually published non-EU contingent.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: YES — the clearest 'yes' in this sweep. The published entry list names 'diploma di laurea triennale' (any three-year university degree) as a qualifying title in its own right, and the assessment is a portfolio plus an oral, with no published theory paper, ear-training test or instrumental requirement. A Software Engineering BSc plus a genuine audio/audiovisual portfolio maps onto the stated requirements without needing an exception to be made.
programs.recommendation: APPLY — this is the single best-matched find of the whole sweep for this candidate, and it is the one to build the portfolio year around. Three things line up that never line up together: the formal entry route explicitly accepts any three-year university degree; the admission assessment is portfolio-and-interview with no musicianship examination published; and the cost sits inside the Italian ISEE system, so a low Tunisian family income should translate into a low or zero contributo rather than a flat foreign surcharge. Foreign candidates are even exempt from the admission exam fee. Against that, two real conditions: B2 Italian is a stated requirement, not a suggestion, so Italian study must start now (his French will make this the fastest language on his list); and the degree's centre of gravity is composition for images and applied media sound, not club music — the 15-CFA core is music-to-picture. Shape the portfolio accordingly: three to five scored-to-picture cues, several original electronic pieces, and demonstrable mixing and post-production work. Contact the segreteria in autumn 2026 to request the Bando di ammissione and the Regolamento tasse, and ask whether the B2 must be certified or is tested in-house. If he lands one place from this entire research effort, this is the most likely one.

programs.program: DCSL34 — Diploma Accademico di Secondo Livello in Musica Elettronica, indirizzo Composizione e Sound Design (Biennio)
programs.institution: METS — Scuola di Musica Elettronica, Conservatorio di Musica "Giorgio Federico Ghedini" di Cuneo
programs.institutionType: Specialist electronic music school (METS) within a state conservatoire in the AFAM system, under the Ministero dell'Università e della Ricerca
programs.publicPrivate: PUBLIC. METS is the electronic music school of the Conservatorio di Musica 'G.F. Ghedini' di Cuneo, a state conservatoire; the conservatoire's own Manifesto degli Studi describes it as an 'Istituto di Alta Formazione Artistica e Musicale' and its contribution system runs on ISEE with the standard state-conservatoire machinery. METS uses its own domain (metscuneo.it) but it is the conservatoire's department, and its programmes are linked from and administered by conservatoriocuneo.it.
programs.qualification: Diploma Accademico di Secondo Livello in Musica Elettronica. The conservatoire's own Manifesto degli Studi states these biennio courses give 'il massimo titolo di studio musicale, equiparato alla Laurea specialistica ai fini dell'accesso ai pubblici concorsi' — a real state second-cycle degree, EQF 7.
programs.accreditationStatus: State-accredited under ministerial course code DCSL34 in the MUR AFAM register. Genuine second-cycle qualification.
programs.language: Italian. No English-taught route advertised.
programs.languageRequirement: UNVERIFIED — no explicit level is published on the METS admission pages, which is unusual and worth confirming. Italian state conservatoires generally require or test B2. The oral admission components (motivational interview, discussion of works, music history) are conducted in Italian. Ask mets@conservatoriocuneo.it.
programs.englishTest: None.
programs.durationEcts: 2 years. Standard 120 CFA for a biennio di II livello — the METS study-plan page does not state CFA values inline (UNVERIFIED at source; request the piano di studi).
programs.focus: Electronic music with a Composition and Sound Design track. METS is one of the few Italian conservatoires with a dedicated, separately branded electronic music school running a full ladder — a preparatory course, two triennio tracks (DCPL34 Musica Elettronica indirizzo compositivo, DCPL61 Tecnico del suono) and two biennio tracks.
programs.whatYouStudy: Composition and sound design at second level. Detailed module list UNVERIFIED — request the piano di studi. The sister track (DCSL61, reported separately) covers sound engineering and multimedia.
programs.entryRequirements: A 'titolo di primo livello' — a first-level diploma. Ideally a first-level academic diploma in Electronic Music or Sound Engineering, BUT the school states explicitly that holders of other conservatoire diplomas OR three-year university degrees may also apply if they have 'adeguata e documentata preparazione' in relevant subjects, with additional bridging coursework (debiti formativi) assigned to close gaps. The candidate's BSc plus a documented portfolio is a recognised route, with the 'documented preparation' condition being the thing his portfolio year must satisfy.
programs.auditionSpec: IMPORTANT AND TWO-PART, and this is where the honest difficulty lies. FIRST EXAM (typically early September): a written component — waived for holders of first-level diplomas in Electronic Music or Applied Music, otherwise 'Analisi di un brano elettroacustico', analysis of an electroacoustic excerpt supplied by the examiners; plus an oral component covering presentation of the candidate's own electronic music pieces with documentation of live-set performances, demonstrated proficiency with audio editing, mixing and sound-processing software, knowledge of twentieth-century music, the history of electroacoustic music, acoustics and psychoacoustics, and a motivational interview. SECOND EXAM: waived for holders of first-level CONSERVATOIRE academic diplomas — but NOT waived for university graduates, so it WOULD apply to this candidate. It covers sung reading (lettura cantata), intonation and rhythm, ear training, and music history and historiography. That is a conventional musicianship examination and it is a genuine obstacle for someone with no conservatoire training. Note also, encouragingly, that the METS FAQ describes the biennio admission as consisting of a motivational interview with faculty at which candidates may present previous works — there is some tension between the FAQ's lighter description and the detailed exam page, which must be resolved directly with the school.
programs.portfolioSpec: Before the exam date, candidates email to mets@conservatoriocuneo.it their audio and multimedia works plus a CV, using permanent sharing links (Google Drive, Dropbox, OneDrive). The oral exam then requires presentation of the candidate's own electronic compositions WITH DOCUMENTATION OF LIVE-SET EXECUTIONS — a requirement that directly rewards a DJ/producer practice, and is the only place in this entire sweep where live electronic performance is explicitly credited. His career direction is an asset here, not a liability.
programs.equipmentRequired: UNVERIFIED — not published. Proficiency with audio editing, mixing and sound-processing software is examined, so a personal DAW setup is assumed.
programs.facilities: UNVERIFIED in detail. METS is a dedicated electronic music school with its own identity and staff, which normally implies better-than-average studio access. Ask for a visit or a facilities list at mets@conservatoriocuneo.it.
programs.tuitionEU: UNVERIFIED as to amounts. The conservatoire's Manifesto degli Studi 2025/2026 confirms the mechanism: 'Le tasse di frequenza — suddivise in massimo tre rate laddove previsto — sono organizzate in fasce di reddito', requiring a valid ISEE for university right-to-study purposes to be presented at first-year enrolment or re-enrolment, per a separate 'regolamento sulla contribuzione studentesca' annexed to the Manifesto. The METS FAQ confirms tuition is income-based (ISEE-dependent). Exact band amounts are in the Regolamento contributi — request it from the segreteria.
programs.tuitionNonEU: UNVERIFIED as to amount, but the mechanism is documented and stated bluntly in the Manifesto: 'Gli studenti stranieri devono presentare l'attestazione ISEE parificato' — foreign students MUST present an ISEE parificato — and 'chi non presenta certificazione ISEE, verrà inserito nella fascia reddituale più alta', i.e. anyone who does not file it is placed in the highest income band. So, exactly as at Bologna: the ISEE parificato is the lever. Filed correctly on a Tunisian family income it should place him at or near the bottom band; not filed, he pays the maximum. Obtain the exact band table by requesting the Regolamento contributi from the segreteria before applying.
programs.otherFees: Tassa regionale per il diritto allo studio (EDISU Piemonte) plus marca da bollo, payable with the first instalment via PagoPA through the Isidata platform. Amounts UNVERIFIED for Cuneo specifically — for reference the neighbouring Conservatorio di Torino bundles EDISU tax plus bollo at €156. Contributory irregularity blocks exam sittings, so payment discipline matters.
programs.totalCostEstimate: Cannot be stated precisely. On the Italian ISEE pattern with an ISEE parificato filed, expect low hundreds of euros per year; without it, the top band. Cuneo is a small Piedmontese city with the lowest living costs of any location in this sweep — roughly €550–800/month — and it is about 90 minutes from Turin. On a cost basis this is probably the cheapest genuinely relevant option found anywhere in the three countries.
programs.scholarships: EDISU Piemonte income-based scholarships are open to non-EU students and can cover fee exemption, a maintenance grant and subsidised housing. In addition, METS itself advertises paid collaboration contracts (contratti di collaborazione) and a limited number of scholarships to offset costs — an unusual and genuinely useful provision for a self-funding student. MAECI government scholarships are the national alternative.
programs.intakes: Autumn. Admission exams typically in early September, with teaching beginning in November.
programs.applicationOpens: UNVERIFIED as to the exact window. The conservatoire publishes an annual 'AMMISSIONI A.A. 20XX/20XX' notice — the 2026/2027 notice appeared in July 2026 (PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date). Admission exams typically take place in September, teaching starts November. Non-EU applicants must complete Universitaly pre-enrolment on the Ministry's separate and earlier calendar.
programs.deadline: UNVERIFIED — governed by the annual ammissioni notice. Note that portfolio materials must reach mets@conservatoriocuneo.it before the exam date.
programs.visaEligible: Yes. State conservatoire second-level diploma supports an Italian student visa and permesso di soggiorno per studio, subject to Universitaly pre-enrolment and the annual non-EU contingent.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: PARTIALLY. The formal entry route is open — three-year university degrees are explicitly named, with debiti formativi assigned to close gaps. But university graduates are NOT exempt from the second exam, which tests sung reading, intonation, rhythm, ear training and music history. That is a real musicianship hurdle for someone with no conservatoire background, and it is the single most important thing to resolve before committing. Set against it, the oral exam's demand for documented live-set performances is a requirement his intended practice actually satisfies.
programs.recommendation: APPLY, alongside Rovigo — but resolve the second-exam question first, because it is the difference between a realistic target and a wasted application. Email mets@conservatoriocuneo.it in autumn 2026 and ask three things plainly: (1) as a holder of a foreign three-year Software Engineering degree, must I sit the second exam covering lettura cantata, ear training and music history, and if so what standard is expected; (2) can documented live-set and production work substitute for conservatoire musicianship in the assessment; (3) what does the Regolamento contributi charge a student in the lowest ISEE parificato band. If the answer on the second exam is workable, this becomes arguably the best-value option in the entire sweep — a dedicated electronic music school, the cheapest living costs of any location found, an ISEE-based fee system that should reduce his cost to very little, paid collaboration contracts available from the school itself, and an admission process that explicitly credits live electronic performance. If the answer is that a full musicianship examination stands, he should put Rovigo first and treat Cuneo as the second choice. Either way, the ear-training and basic musicianship gap is worth closing during the portfolio year — it is the recurring obstacle across every conservatoire route in Italy and Spain.

programs.auditionSpec: UNVERIFIED for this track. The METS admission page covering the biennio exams did not specify separate requirements for 'Tecnico del Suono – Ingegneria del Suono e Multimedia'. The national DCSL61 profile points to an aptitude and motivational interview rather than a musicianship examination, which if true at Cuneo would make this track MORE accessible to him than the composition track — but that must be confirmed in writing before relying on it. This is the single highest-value unanswered question in the Italian half of this research.

Cuneo living costs are the lowest of any location in this sweep at roughly €550–800/month. Two-year all-in plausibly around €15,000–20,000, most of it living costs, before any EDISU scholarship.
programs.scholarships: EDISU Piemonte income-based scholarships open to non-EU students, covering fee exemption, maintenance and subsidised housing. METS additionally offers paid collaboration contracts and a limited number of internal scholarships. MAECI government scholarships as the national alternative.
programs.intakes: Autumn. Admission exams typically early September; teaching begins November.
programs.applicationOpens: UNVERIFIED as to exact window — governed by the conservatoire's annual ammissioni notice, which for 2026/2027 appeared in July 2026 (PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date). Universitaly pre-enrolment required separately for non-EU applicants on the Ministry's earlier calendar.
programs.deadline: UNVERIFIED — set by the annual ammissioni notice.
programs.visaEligible: Yes. State conservatoire second-level diploma supports an Italian student visa and permesso di soggiorno per studio, subject to Universitaly pre-enrolment and the annual non-EU contingent.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: LIKELY THE MOST OPEN OF ANY ITALIAN OPTION FOUND, but unconfirmed. The national DCSL61 admission profile points toward an aptitude and motivational interview rather than a musicianship examination, and a sound-engineering degree has less reason than a composition degree to demand solfège and ear training. If that holds at Cuneo, the second exam that burdens the composition track may not apply here — which would make this the single most accessible state-recognised second-cycle audio qualification in all three countries for a software engineer with no music training. programs.recommendation: INVESTIGATE AS A PRIORITY — potentially the best fit of all, and the most important open question left by this research. DCSL61 Tecnico del Suono is a real state second-cycle degree in sound engineering, at the same institution and cost base as the Cuneo composition track, but with an admission profile that appears to rest on an aptitude and motivational interview rather than conservatoire musicianship. For a software engineer with no music degree, that combination — an engineering-framed degree, an interview-based entry, an ISEE-scaled fee that a Tunisian family income should drive close to zero, and the cheapest living costs in the sweep — is potentially decisive. But the METS admission page did not publish separate requirements for this track, so nothing here is confirmed. Write to mets@conservatoriocuneo.it in autumn 2026 with the specific question: 'Per il biennio DCSL61 Tecnico del Suono — Ingegneria del Suono e Multimedia, quali sono i requisiti e le prove di ammissione per un laureato triennale straniero in Ingegneria Informatica? Si applica anche la seconda prova di lettura cantata ed ear training?' Get that answered before deciding between the Cuneo tracks. Meanwhile build a technical portfolio — multitrack recordings, mixes, masters, any DSP or audio-software work from his engineering degree — rather than a compositional one, since that is what this track will reward. Note that DCSL61 also runs at Frosinone, Reggio Calabria and Vibo Valentia, so if Cuneo does not work the code itself is worth chasing elsewhere.

programs.qualification: Diploma accademico di secondo livello — a real state second-cycle degree, EQF 7, equated to a Laurea Magistrale for public competitions and further study.

programs.whatYouStudy: Year one: audiovisual communication theory, orchestration, audiovisual composition, music informatics, and electives. programs.tuitionNonEU: UNVERIFIED — not published. Expect the standard Italian pattern: an ISEE parificato/ISEEE unlocks the income bands, and failure to file places the student in the highest band. Whether Como instead applies a flat non-EU rate as Torino does is UNVERIFIED and must be asked. Note that Lombardy's regional right-to-study agency and Como's proximity to Milan make living costs higher than at Cuneo or Rovigo.

programs.recommendation: DO NOT APPLY. Recorded because it is a distinct state conservatoire programme in exactly his subject area that the earlier sweeps missed, and because it usefully demarcates the boundary of what is reachable: Italian state conservatoire second-level courses vary enormously in openness, from Rovigo (any three-year degree, portfolio and oral) at one end to Como (composition diploma required, fugue examination) at the other. Knowing that Como sits at the closed end saves him from wasting an application on a well-known name. If he is drawn to the audiovisual composition subject matter specifically, Rovigo's DCSL60 Musica Applicata covers very similar ground — composition for music applied to images is its largest single credit block — and is open to him. Choose Rovigo over Como on every dimension that matters here.

programs.institution: Ankara Müzik ve Güzel Sanatlar Üniversitesi (Ankara Music and Fine Arts University, MGÜ)
programs.publicPrivate: PUBLIC. State university, founded by Turkish law as a devlet üniversitesi and run under YÖK/Ministry of National Education funding; it is one of only three universities named by the Turkish government's own Türkiye Bursları Art Scholarship as a state art institution (turkiyeburslari.gov.tr/fulltimeprograms lists it alongside Ankara Hacı Bayram Veli and İTÜ). Not a foundation (vakıf) university.
programs.institutionType: Specialist state university of music and fine arts (conservatoire-type), with its own Müzik ve Güzel Sanatlar Enstitüsü (graduate institute)
programs.qualification: Tezli Yüksek Lisans diploması — a real second-cycle degree. The Turkish Qualifications Framework register (TYÇ) classifies Turkish thesis master's diplomas at TYÇ level 7 / QF-EHEA level 2 / EQF-LLL level 7. Supports a Turkish student residence permit (öğrenci ikamet izni) for a non-EU national.
programs.accreditationStatus: State-recognised. YÖK-authorised programme at a state university; graduate degree at TYÇ/EQF level 7. A YÖK 'denklik belgesi' (recognition certificate) for the foreign bachelor's degree is REQUIRED of foreign applicants before admission — this is a real administrative hurdle and takes months, so a Tunisian SMU MedTech BSc must be sent to YÖK well in advance.
programs.language: Turkish. All teaching, all admission documents and the entrance examination are in Turkish. There is no English-taught track.
programs.languageRequirement: Turkish C1 certificate from a YÖK-recognised Turkish-teaching centre (e.g. TÖMER) is compulsory for foreign nationals who studied abroad. If the candidate is admitted without it, he is registered and put on one (1) year of leave to study Turkish; if he cannot present a C1 certificate at the end of that year, his registration is cancelled. No English certificate is required at all.
programs.englishTest: None. No IELTS/TOEFL is demanded — the foreign-language score requirement is explicitly waived for master's applicants ('Yabancı Dil Taban Puanı: Aranmaz'). The barrier is Turkish, not English.
programs.durationEcts: Standard Turkish tezli yüksek lisans: 4 semesters nominal (minimum 7 courses + seminar + thesis). Exact ECTS total not stated in the admission guide — UNVERIFIED; ask enstitu@mgu.edu.tr or the Ana Bilim Dalı (deren.karacan@mgu.edu.tr).
programs.focus: Music technology with a strong audio-engineering and acoustics bias — the guide states graduates should carry 'ileri düzeyde ses mühendisliği bilgisi' (advanced sound-engineering knowledge) and be able to conduct scientific work in music technology.
programs.whatYouStudy: Courses combining technical field knowledge with academic literature study in music technologies; the assessed competence areas signal the content: sound recording, sound programming, instrument making, sound electronics and acoustics. It is an academic/research master (thesis required), not a commercial music-production diploma — do not expect a DJ/producer curriculum.
programs.entryRequirements: Graduation from ANY bachelor's programme ('Herhangi bir lisans programından mezun olmak') — this is unusually open and is the single most important fact for this candidate. Minimum bachelor GPA 2.50/4.00 (or 65/100, or 3.1/5.00). No ALES required (and explicitly not required of foreign nationals). No foreign-language score required. Foreign nationals need a YÖK denklik belgesi and a Turkish C1 certificate (or the one-year Turkish grace period).
programs.acceptsNonMusic: YES — explicitly. The 2025-26 exam guide states any bachelor's degree is accepted. A BSc in Software Engineering is formally eligible. HOWEVER the entrance exam tests trained musical hearing (see auditionSpec), so formal eligibility and realistic competitiveness are two different things.
programs.portfolioSpec: Required at pre-evaluation (10% of the entrance score). Candidate must upload and also hand the jury three (3) printed copies of: (a) ONE self-produced work in sound recording, sound programming, instrument making, sound electronics or acoustics, as a digital copy (CD/DVD/USB) plus a written explanatory text; (b) a digital copy of other personal works in the field with audio files, software and/or written documents plus an index of them; (c) a CV. Scored on form, language and content: CV 11/11/11, field-specific CV 11/11/11, work report 11/11/12.
programs.auditionSpec: Two-stage entrance exam, in Turkish. Stage I (60% of entrance score) tests six areas: Müziksel İşitme / musical ear-training (27 pts), Mesleki İşitme / technical listening and classification of played sounds (27 pts), Mesleki Bilgi / professional knowledge (9), Problem Çözme (9), Analitik Düşünme (19), Akademik Araştırmaya Yatkınlık (9) — for the last, candidates must read in advance a named Turkish journal article on determining the acoustic properties of small-scale popular-music production spaces (dergipark.org.tr/tr/download/article-file/203754) and answer on it in writing, then defend the answer orally. Stage II (30%) is an oral examination on the submitted portfolio (main work mastery 57, written-exam review 28, general assessment 15). Pass mark 60/100. Final ranking = 70% entrance-exam score + 30% bachelor GPA.
programs.equipmentRequired: Not stated in the guide, but the portfolio effectively requires the candidate to have produced original recorded/programmed audio work beforehand — i.e. he needs a working DAW setup and a body of finished work by the time he applies. UNVERIFIED whether the university supplies anything; ask the Ana Bilim Dalı.
programs.facilities: Not detailed on the pages opened — UNVERIFIED. Ask deren.karacan@mgu.edu.tr / ugur.baloglu@mgu.edu.tr about studios, control rooms and acoustics labs before committing.
programs.intakes: One intake per year, Güz (autumn/September) semester.
programs.applicationOpens: 2026-2027 Güz: online applications 10 August 2026 09:00 – 24 August 2026 17:00 (official MGÜ announcement). For a SEPTEMBER 2027 start expect an equivalent window in roughly late July–August 2027 — PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. Separately, the Türkiye Bursları scholarship route opens 10 January and closes 20 February every year, so the funded route for Sept 2027 is 10 Jan – 20 Feb 2027.
programs.deadline: 24 August 2026 for the 2026-27 intake (official). 2025-26 cycle ran 29 July – 8 August 2025, exam 25 August 2025, results 3 September 2025 — PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. Türkiye Bursları deadline 20 February each year.
programs.tuitionEU: Not applicable in the EU sense. Turkish nationals pay no tuition for a state thesis master's (only nominal contributions).
programs.tuitionNonEU: 15,000 TL for the academic year for foreign nationals in a Tezli Yüksek Lisans at the Müzik ve Güzel Sanatlar Enstitüsü, payable as 7,500 TL + 7,500 TL in two instalments (MGÜ announcement '2024-2025 Eğitim-Öğretim Yılında Yabancı Uyruklu Öğrencilerden Alınacak Öğrenim Ücretleri'). PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date/amount; Turkish state fees are re-set annually by presidential decree and the lira figure will rise. This is the rate HE would pay as a Tunisian national. Waived entirely if he wins Türkiye Bursları.
programs.otherFees: YÖK denklik application costs, sworn translation and apostille of the Tunisian degree and transcript, Turkish C1 course fees if not covered (TÖMER courses typically run several thousand TL), residence-permit fee and health insurance. Exact amounts UNVERIFIED — ask enstitu@mgu.edu.tr and the İl Göç İdaresi.
programs.totalCostEstimate: Self-funded: roughly 15,000 TL/yr tuition plus Ankara living costs plus one year of Turkish language study before or during the degree. Under Türkiye Bursları: zero — the scholarship pays tuition, a monthly stipend, accommodation, health insurance, one return flight and a full year of Turkish language course. Precise living-cost figures UNVERIFIED.
programs.scholarships: Türkiye Bursları 'Art Scholarship Programme' (Sanat Burs Programı) explicitly lists Ankara Music and Fine Arts University and names 'Music Technologies' among the master's fields it funds (turkiyeburslari.gov.tr/fulltimeprograms). It is open to non-Turkish nationals, so a Tunisian applicant is eligible. Coverage: university and department placement, monthly stipend, tuition fee, one-year Turkish language course, accommodation, health insurance and a once-off flight ticket. Applications 10 January – 20 February annually via TBBS, free of charge, submittable in 8 languages. Master's applicants must generally be under 30.
programs.visaEligible: Yes. Full-time, on-campus, state-recognised second-cycle degree at a YÖK university — supports a Turkish student residence permit. Türkiye Bursları holders receive placement and support through YTB.
programs.recommendation: THE STRONGEST FIND OF THIS SWEEP FOR HIM, and the only fully-funded, formally-open door found in the four countries. It is the rare music-technology master that accepts ANY bachelor's degree, demands no ALES, no IELTS and no TOEFL, and is named by Türkiye Bursları as a funded art field. Realistic assessment: (1) the killer constraint is Turkish, not English — teaching, exam and admission are all in Turkish and a C1 certificate is required within a year; the Türkiye Bursları package includes exactly that year of Turkish, which makes the scholarship route far more viable than self-payment; (2) the entrance exam is 54/100 weighted on trained musical and technical ear (müziksel işitme + mesleki işitme) — with no conservatory background he must spend the coming year on ear training and critical listening, not only on beat-making; (3) the portfolio must be his OWN produced work in recording, sound programming, sound electronics or acoustics, with a written technical report — his software-engineering background is a genuine asset here if he builds audio-DSP or plug-in projects rather than only DJ sets; (4) only 2 foreign-national places were advertised in the 2025-26 guide, so it is competitive. Concrete plan: apply to Türkiye Bursları 10 Jan – 20 Feb 2027 naming this programme; start YÖK denklik and Turkish study in autumn 2026; build a portfolio of self-recorded/self-coded audio work with written technical documentation across 2026. Note also that the same programme is an academic/research master with a thesis — it will not by itself make him an international DJ; it will make him a credentialed audio technologist.

programs.program: Müzik Teknolojisi Yüksek Lisans (Music Technology master) — Müzik Bilimleri Ana Bilim Dalı, Güzel Sanatlar Enstitüsü
programs.institution: Dokuz Eylül Üniversitesi (Dokuz Eylul University)
programs.publicPrivate: PUBLIC. Long-established Turkish state university (devlet üniversitesi) under YÖK; its Güzel Sanatlar Enstitüsü is a state graduate institute. Not a foundation university.
programs.institutionType: Large comprehensive state university with a Faculty of Fine Arts and a separate Fine Arts Graduate Institute
programs.qualification: Yüksek Lisans diploması in Müzik Teknolojisi. The Turkish Qualifications Framework register carries 'Müzik Teknolojisi Tezli Yüksek Lisans Diploması' as a registered national qualification awarded by Dokuz Eylül University — i.e. a real, state-recognised second-cycle degree at TYÇ/EQF level 7, valid for a student residence permit.
programs.accreditationStatus: State-recognised, YÖK-authorised, entered in the Turkish Qualifications Framework (TYÇ) register. Foreign bachelor's degrees require YÖK denklik as with all Turkish universities.
programs.language: Turkish. The official Bologna course catalogue states the language of instruction is Turkish.
programs.languageRequirement: Turkish proficiency will be required (Turkish state universities normally demand a C1 TÖMER-type certificate of foreign graduates). The exact level and any grace period at DEÜ is UNVERIFIED — ask the Güzel Sanatlar Enstitüsü directly (gse.deu.edu.tr).
programs.englishTest: A foreign-language proficiency score is listed among admission requirements for Turkish applicants (YDS/YÖKDİL type), but whether a Tunisian applicant must sit it, and at what score, is UNVERIFIED — ask the Enstitü. No IELTS/TOEFL band is published for this programme.
programs.durationEcts: 120 ECTS over 2 years / 4 semesters of 15 weeks; minimum 7 courses + 1 seminar + specialisation work + thesis (min. 21 local credits). Source: official DEÜ course catalogue.
programs.focus: Music technology combining music arts/theory with technology; the discipline was established in 2009.
programs.whatYouStudy: Theoretical study alongside practical application through case studies and research projects, leading to a thesis. Aimed at candidates seeking academic careers or specialisation in music technology.
programs.entryRequirements: Bachelor's degree in music technology or a related discipline; official transcript; ALES score (or GRE/GMAT equivalent); foreign-language proficiency. The catalogue notes exceptions for conservatory and fine-arts graduates. NOTE the contrast with Ankara MGÜ: DEÜ does NOT advertise open admission to any bachelor's degree.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: Unclear and the key risk. The stated requirement is a bachelor's 'in music technology or related discipline'. Whether a Software Engineering BSc counts as 'related', and whether a bilimsel hazırlık (scientific preparation) year would be imposed, is UNVERIFIED — put this question in writing to the Güzel Sanatlar Enstitüsü before doing any other work on this option.
programs.portfolioSpec: Not published on the catalogue page — UNVERIFIED. Turkish fine-arts institutes normally run a special-talent (özel yetenek) entrance examination with a dossier; ask the Enstitü for the year's sınav kılavuzu.
programs.auditionSpec: UNVERIFIED. Expect a Güzel Sanatlar Enstitüsü entrance exam/interview; request the current 'giriş sınavı kılavuzu' from gse.deu.edu.tr.
programs.equipmentRequired: UNVERIFIED.
programs.facilities: The department reports a recording studio and an electronics laboratory, and participates in EU Erasmus mobility and internship schemes (official DEÜ catalogue).
programs.intakes: Autumn (Güz) intake in line with the Turkish academic calendar; exact dates UNVERIFIED.
programs.applicationOpens: UNVERIFIED — Turkish state graduate calls typically open in July–August for a September start. For September 2027 expect roughly July–August 2027; confirm with gse.deu.edu.tr.
programs.deadline: UNVERIFIED — ask the Güzel Sanatlar Enstitüsü.
programs.tuitionEU: Turkish nationals pay no tuition for a state thesis master's beyond nominal contributions.
programs.tuitionNonEU: UNVERIFIED. DEÜ sets an annual öğrenim ücreti for yabancı uyruklu students by senate decision under a presidential decree; the figure for the Güzel Sanatlar Enstitüsü was not published on any page opened. Ask gse.deu.edu.tr or DEÜ Öğrenci İşleri Daire Başkanlığı for the current 'yabancı uyruklu öğrenci öğrenim ücreti' table. Do not assume it matches Ankara MGÜ's 15,000 TL.
programs.otherFees: YÖK denklik, sworn translations, Turkish language course, residence permit and health insurance — amounts UNVERIFIED.
programs.totalCostEstimate: UNVERIFIED because the non-EU tuition rate is not published. İzmir living costs are lower than Istanbul's.
programs.scholarships: Türkiye Bursları's Art Scholarship Programme names only Ankara Music and Fine Arts University, Ankara Hacı Bayram Veli University and İstanbul Technical University — Dokuz Eylül is NOT on that list, so the art route does not cover it. He could instead apply under the general Türkiye Bursları Graduate (Master's) programme, but that competes against all disciplines. Institutional scholarships UNVERIFIED.
programs.visaEligible: Yes — full-time on-campus state-recognised second-cycle degree at a YÖK university, supports a Turkish student residence permit.
programs.recommendation: A genuine, well-established Turkish music-technology master with a recording studio and electronics lab, at a state university in İzmir — cheaper and pleasanter to live in than Istanbul. Two things make it a second choice behind Ankara MGÜ for this candidate: (1) admission is written as requiring a music-technology or related bachelor's, unlike MGÜ's explicit 'any bachelor's degree', so his eligibility is genuinely uncertain; and (2) it is not covered by the Türkiye Bursları Art Scholarship, which removes the fully-funded route. Teaching is entirely in Turkish. Action: send one email to the Güzel Sanatlar Enstitüsü asking (a) whether a Software Engineering BSc is accepted and whether bilimsel hazırlık would apply, (b) the current foreign-national tuition figure, (c) the Turkish-language requirement and any grace period. If the answer to (a) is yes, this becomes a solid backup.

programs.program: Müzik Yüksek Lisans Programı (Türkçe, Tezli ve Tezsiz) — Music, thesis and non-thesis master, Konservatuvar / Lisansüstü Eğitim Enstitüsü. Programme codes 34223501 (tezli) and 34223601 (tezsiz).
programs.institution: Bahçeşehir Üniversitesi (BAU), İstanbul
programs.publicPrivate: PRIVATE. A vakıf (foundation) university — established and owned by the Bahçeşehir Uğur Eğitim Vakfı, a private educational foundation, not state-funded. Foundation universities in Turkey are nonetheless YÖK-supervised and award state-recognised degrees; they charge full tuition to everyone, Turkish and foreign alike.
programs.institutionType: Private foundation university with its own Conservatory (Konservatuvar) and a Graduate Education Institute
programs.qualification: Yüksek Lisans (master's). The university's own Bologna information package states the award sits at TYYÇ level 7 / QF-EHEA level 2 / EQF-LLL level 7 — a real second-cycle degree, valid for a student residence permit.
programs.accreditationStatus: State-recognised, YÖK-authorised foundation university; the master's is listed in BAU's official AKTS/Bologna information package with its TYYÇ level. IMPORTANT WARNING attached to this institution: BAU also markets non-degree audio training through 'BAU IDEA' (bauidea.com, 'Audio & Sound Design'), which is a certificate operation and NOT a master's degree — do not confuse the two. Separately, BAU's conservatory graduate page still links a 'Ses Teknolojileri (Türkçe, Tezli/Tezsiz)' master's, but that link 404s on BAU's own site and the programme does NOT appear in BAU's live AKTS master's catalogue, so it appears dormant or discontinued even though 'Ses Teknolojisi Tezli/Tezsiz Yüksek Lisans Diploması' still exists as a registered qualification in the Turkish Qualifications Framework.
programs.language: Turkish. BAU's own AKTS page for the programme states the language of instruction is Turkish; the conservatory's graduate offer is listed as Turkish-medium throughout. (By contrast BAU's undergraduate Music Technology department and many BAU engineering masters are English-medium — the graduate music programme is not.)
programs.languageRequirement: Turkish proficiency required for a Turkish-medium programme; BAU's published general rule is an ALES or equivalent score for master's applicants and an English certificate only for English-medium programmes. The exact Turkish certificate demanded of a foreign applicant is UNVERIFIED — ask BAU's International Office (+90 212 381 01 54).
programs.englishTest: None for this Turkish-medium programme.
programs.durationEcts: UNVERIFIED. Standard Turkish tezli yüksek lisans is 4 semesters; the tezsiz (non-thesis) variant is normally 2-3 semesters. BAU's AKTS page did not render ECTS or duration — ask the Lisansüstü Eğitim Enstitüsü.
programs.focus: Music: the programme describes itself as combining musicology and performance practice to produce qualified research. It is NOT an audio-engineering or production degree.
programs.whatYouStudy: Musicology plus performance practice, thesis/project work, academic ethics and research method. BAU's Conservatory Music department does carry a 'Müzik Teknolojileri' sub-module and BAU runs an undergraduate Müzik Teknolojisi department teaching recording, audio editing, mixing and mastering, but the master's as described is research-and-performance oriented, not a production course.
programs.entryRequirements: BAU's general master's rule: ALES (or recognised equivalent) score, plus documents; English certificate only for English-medium programmes. Specific conditions for the Music master's — including whether a non-music graduate is admitted and whether an audition applies — UNVERIFIED. Ask the Lisansüstü Eğitim Enstitüsü.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: UNVERIFIED, and unlikely to be straightforward: this is a conservatory research/performance master. Ask directly before investing.
programs.portfolioSpec: UNVERIFIED — ask the Konservatuvar.
programs.auditionSpec: UNVERIFIED — a conservatory master normally requires an audition or an entrance interview; ask the Konservatuvar.
programs.equipmentRequired: UNVERIFIED.
programs.facilities: BAU's Conservatory runs a Music Technology department with studio-based teaching of recording, editing, mixing and mastering at undergraduate level; whether master's students get studio access is UNVERIFIED.
programs.intakes: Autumn (Güz) and Spring (Bahar) — BAU advertises both Güz and Bahar graduate application rounds.
programs.applicationOpens: BAU publishes rolling 'Lisansüstü Başvuru ve Kayıt Süreçleri' announcements per semester. Exact 2027 dates UNVERIFIED — watch bau.edu.tr graduate announcements from roughly May 2027 for a September 2027 start.
programs.deadline: UNVERIFIED.
programs.tuitionEU: Not applicable — a Turkish private foundation university charges the same published tuition to Turkish and foreign students. BAU's fee page states fees include KDV (VAT) and that a 10% discount applies for payment in full up front.
programs.tuitionNonEU: UNVERIFIED. BAU's graduate fee page (2026-2027) did not render the figure for the Music programme when opened; the page confirms only that fees include VAT and that a 10% up-front discount applies. Ask BAU Student Services or apply through aday.bau.edu.tr for the exact Müzik tezli/tezsiz figure. Expect a private-university price in the tens of thousands of TL per year — this is NOT a cheap option.
programs.otherFees: YÖK denklik, translations, residence permit, health insurance — UNVERIFIED amounts.
programs.totalCostEstimate: UNVERIFIED, but Istanbul living costs plus private-foundation tuition make this the most expensive of the Turkish options found. Do not treat it as 'genuinely cheap'.
programs.scholarships: Türkiye Bursları's Art Scholarship does NOT cover Bahçeşehir (only Ankara MGÜ, Ankara Hacı Bayram Veli and İTÜ). BAU offers its own graduate discounts/early-payment reductions; scale UNVERIFIED. For a candidate who strongly prefers full funding, this is a poor fit.
programs.visaEligible: Yes — a YÖK-recognised foundation university degree supports a Turkish student residence permit. The award is a genuine second-cycle degree, unlike BAU IDEA certificates, which are not.
programs.recommendation: Report as a caution rather than a target. Three findings matter here. (1) The programme that would have suited him — 'Ses Teknolojileri' (Sound Technologies) master's, thesis and non-thesis, Turkish — is still advertised on BAU's conservatory graduate page but its own page 404s and it is absent from BAU's live Bologna catalogue, so it appears dormant; the qualification title nevertheless survives in the Turkish national qualifications register. If he is interested, ask BAU in writing whether Ses Teknolojileri will admit for 2027-28; do not apply on the strength of the stale web page. (2) What is actually live is a Turkish-taught Müzik master oriented to musicology and performance — the wrong shape for a producer with no music degree. (3) BAU IDEA's 'Audio & Sound Design' offering is a private certificate, NOT a degree and NOT a basis for a student residence permit as a master's — exactly the kind of product the brief warns about. Overall: skip unless BAU confirms Ses Teknolojileri is reopening, and even then the private fees conflict with his funding preference.
