programs.program: ΠΜΣ «Τεχνολογίες Ήχου, Βίντεο και Μετάδοσης» / MSc in Audio, Video and Broadcasting Engineering — Department of Electrical and Electronic Engineering
programs.institution: Πανεπιστήμιο Δυτικής Αττικής / University of West Attica (UniWA)
programs.city: Athens (Ancient Olive Grove campus, Building Z)
programs.publicPrivate: PUBLIC. Greek state university (ΑΕΙ) created by law from the former TEI of Athens and TEI of Piraeus; funded by the Greek Ministry of Education. Its postgraduate programme was authorised by ministerial decision published in the Government Gazette (ΦΕΚ Β' 3257/8-8-2018), with the study regulation at ΦΕΚ Β' 4879/1-11-2018 — this Gazette publication is the standard proof of public, state-recognised status in Greece.
programs.institutionType: State technological/engineering-oriented university
programs.qualification: Δίπλωμα Μεταπτυχιακών Σπουδών (ΔΜΣ) in 'Τεχνολογίες Ήχου, Βίντεο και Μετάδοσης'. A real second-cycle Greek state degree, established by Government Gazette decision — supports a Greek student residence permit for a non-EU national.
programs.accreditationStatus: State-recognised: operating approval ΦΕΚ Β' 3257/8-8-2018, study regulation ΦΕΚ Β' 4879/1-11-2018. CAUTION ON CURRENCY: the programme's own website has published nothing newer than the 2021-22 call (applications to 23 September 2021) and its 2021-22 announcement is the last one on the site, although the department still lists the programme among its MSc offerings in 2026. Also note the programme does NOT appear in the Ministry's public 'Study in Greece' programme finder. Confirm it is still admitting before doing any work on it.
programs.language: Greek. Every page, the calls for applications and the application form are in Greek only; the programme has an English-language shell page but no evidence of English-medium teaching. Treat as Greek-taught.
programs.languageRequirement: Not published — UNVERIFIED. Greek ΠΜΣ normally require documented Greek and often a certificate of English for the literature. Ask eee@uniwa.gr / mscavb@uniwa.gr what a non-Greek-speaking applicant must present.
programs.englishTest: UNVERIFIED — not published. Ask the programme secretariat.
programs.durationEcts: Not published on any page opened — UNVERIFIED. Fees are quoted per semester with provision for part-time at 50%, and for 'extension' semesters, implying at least three teaching semesters. Ask the secretariat (+30 210 538 1514) for the exact ECTS and semester count.
programs.focus: Audio and acoustics, moving image/video and optics, and digital broadcasting of audio and visual signals — an engineering programme covering production, capture, processing, compression, coding, transmission and display of acoustic and optical signals in one framework.
programs.whatYouStudy: Signal-level engineering of sound and picture: studio and broadcast technology (course AVB.2.7 'Τεχνολογία Στούντιο και Μετάδοσης'), image and video processing (AVB.1.4), acoustics, compression and coding, digital broadcasting. This is broadcast/audio engineering, not music production or DJing.
programs.entryRequirements: Holders of a first-cycle degree from a Greek university/TEI department or an equivalent internationally recognised institution, assessed on file plus interview. Priority is given to graduates in Electrical Engineering and Electronic Engineering. Selection = file assessment and interview weighted EQUALLY; the interview assesses overall preparation, motivation and interest relative to the subject. 25 places advertised (2020-21 and 2021-22 calls).
programs.acceptsNonMusic: Yes in principle — this is an engineering MSc and expects no musical training at all. A BSc in Software Engineering is a plausible file, though electrical/electronic engineers are given priority. His engineering background is an ADVANTAGE here, unlike at the conservatories.
programs.portfolioSpec: None. No portfolio is required — file plus interview only. This is the only programme in this batch that a candidate with no portfolio could enter on academic record alone.
programs.auditionSpec: None. No audition. An interview before a selection committee of departmental professors, weighted 50%.
programs.equipmentRequired: Not stated — UNVERIFIED.
programs.facilities: Studio and broadcast technology is taught as a named course, implying studio facilities in the Electrical and Electronic Engineering department — but no facility list was published. UNVERIFIED; ask the secretariat.
programs.intakes: One intake per year, September/autumn.
programs.applicationOpens: UNVERIFIED for future cycles. In 2020-21 the call closed 18 September 2020 and in 2021-22 it closed 23 September 2021, with an extension — PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. Greek ΠΜΣ calls of this type typically open in June–July.
programs.deadline: 23 September 2021 for the last published cycle — PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. For a September 2027 start expect a call in summer 2027, IF the programme is still running.
programs.tuitionEU: €700 per academic semester for full-time students, paid through the institution's ELKE in two equal instalments (weeks 1 and 7 of each semester), except the first instalment of semester one which is paid at enrolment. Part-time students pay 50% of the full-time fee. Extension semesters cost 50% of a full semester's fee. Reduced fees may be granted on documented social/financial grounds by decision of the Departmental Assembly. (Some categories under Art. 35(2) of Greek Law 4485/2017 are exempt.)
programs.tuitionNonEU: The same €700 per semester — Greece does not operate a separate non-EU rate for this ΠΜΣ; the published fee applies to all admitted students. Note this fee schedule is the one published on the programme's own site and has not been updated since roughly 2018 — PRIOR CYCLE - confirm the current figure with mscavb@uniwa.gr before relying on it.
programs.otherFees: Recognition of the Tunisian degree (ΔΟΑΤΑΠ/ΑΤΕΕΝ) may be required and carries a fee; plus Greek residence-permit fee, health insurance, certified translations. Amounts UNVERIFIED.
programs.totalCostEstimate: At €700/semester the tuition is genuinely cheap — roughly €1,400–€2,800 in total depending on programme length (length UNVERIFIED). Athens living costs are the dominant expense and are UNVERIFIED here.
programs.scholarships: The programme states it MAY award 'υποτροφίες αριστείας' (excellence scholarships) depending on its annual finances, by decision of the Departmental Assembly, and only to full-time students who have not taken study extensions. No amount, number or criteria are published — UNVERIFIED. There is no dedicated non-EU scholarship. The Greek State Scholarships Foundation (IKY) and bilateral Greece–Tunisia scholarship quotas should be checked separately.
programs.visaEligible: Yes in principle — a full-time on-campus Greek state second-cycle degree supports a student residence permit (national D visa then residence permit). This is conditional on the programme actually admitting students.
programs.recommendation: Academically the best-fitting Greek option for a software engineer with no music background: it is an audio/broadcast ENGINEERING master, it requires no portfolio and no audition, it selects on file plus interview, and it costs only €700 a semester at a public university. Two serious problems. First, language: everything is in Greek and there is no evidence of English-medium delivery — with Arabic/French/English and no Greek this is close to disqualifying unless the department confirms otherwise. Second, currency: the programme website has posted nothing since the 2021-22 call, which for a Greek ΠΜΣ often means it has stopped admitting, even though the department still lists it. Action, and it is cheap to take: email eee@uniwa.gr and mscavb@uniwa.gr asking (a) whether the ΠΜΣ will admit for 2027-28, (b) whether any teaching or examination is available in English for a non-Greek speaker, (c) the current tuition, ECTS and duration, (d) what a Tunisian applicant must submit and whether ΔΟΑΤΑΠ/ΑΤΕΕΝ recognition is needed. If English is not possible, close this file.

programs.program: ΠΜΣ «Ψηφιακές Μορφές Τέχνης» / MA in Digital Arts — Department of Fine Arts (Τμήμα Εικαστικών Τεχνών)
programs.institution: Ανωτάτη Σχολή Καλών Τεχνών (ΑΣΚΤ) / Athens School of Fine Arts
programs.publicPrivate: PUBLIC. Athens School of Fine Arts is a Greek state higher-education institution (ΑΕΙ) funded by the Ministry of Education; the programme appears in the Ministry of Education's own official programme register (studies.minedu.gov.gr), which lists its tuition as free — a marker of a state-funded ΠΜΣ.
programs.institutionType: State school of fine arts (art academy) with university status
programs.qualification: Δίπλωμα Μεταπτυχιακών Σπουδών (ΜΔΕ) 'Ψηφιακές Μορφές Τέχνης' / Master of Arts (MA) in Digital Arts, 120 ECTS. A real state-recognised second-cycle degree, listed in the Ministry's register — supports a Greek student residence permit.
programs.accreditationStatus: State-recognised and listed in the official Ministry of Education programme register (studies.minedu.gov.gr, programme id 1060), categorised under Arts/Arts Technology, in-person delivery.
programs.language: Greek. The Ministry register states the language of instruction is Greek. There is no English-taught track.
programs.languageRequirement: Not published — UNVERIFIED. A Greek-medium ΠΜΣ at a fine-arts school will in practice require documented Greek. Ask artdm@asfa.gr (+30 210 389 7105) what a non-Greek-speaking non-EU applicant must present.
programs.englishTest: None published — UNVERIFIED. Greek is the operative language here, not English.
programs.durationEcts: 120 ECTS over 4 semesters (2 years), full-time, in person. Source: Ministry of Education official register.
programs.focus: Digital art forms — practice-based contemporary art using digital media. Sound art and audiovisual practice fall within its scope, but it is NOT a music-production or audio-engineering degree.
programs.whatYouStudy: Studio-based digital art practice and research, culminating in artistic work. The programme is run by the Department of Fine Arts, so the frame is contemporary visual/media art rather than music technology. Verify with the department whether a sound-art specialism is supervisable.
programs.entryRequirements: Graduates of Greek or recognised foreign higher-education departments in Fine Arts, Visual Studies, Audiovisual Arts, Applied Arts and Architecture. EXCEPTIONALLY, graduates of other university departments may be admitted, judged on the particular relevance and quality of the artistic work and/or research submitted, in the direction of the programme. Applications are run in cycles; the 19th cycle covers 2026-2028.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: A Software Engineering BSc is outside the listed feeder disciplines, so he would enter only through the explicit exception clause — admitted on the strength of submitted artistic work. In other words the portfolio is the whole case. This is possible but demanding for someone with no body of work yet.
programs.portfolioSpec: Required and decisive. ΑΣΚΤ publishes portfolio guidelines ('οδηγίες για το portfolio') as a separate announcement for each admission cycle. Exact specification for the 2026-2028/next cycle — number of works, format, accompanying text — UNVERIFIED; download the current guidelines from the ΠΜΣ announcements page or ask artdm@asfa.gr.
programs.auditionSpec: No musical audition. Selection is on portfolio and file, with an interview normal for Greek ΠΜΣ — exact procedure UNVERIFIED.
programs.equipmentRequired: UNVERIFIED.
programs.facilities: UNVERIFIED — ask the department about digital/sound studios and whether audio work can be supervised.
programs.intakes: Biennial cycles (the 19th cycle runs 2026-2028), one intake per cycle, autumn start.
programs.applicationOpens: The call for the 19th cycle (2026-2028) has already been announced on asfa.gr. That timing means the NEXT cycle would be 2028-2030 — which does not match a September 2027 target. Confirm with the department whether admission is annual or biennial before planning around it. PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date.
programs.deadline: UNVERIFIED for the relevant cycle — check the ΠΜΣ announcements page on asfa.gr.
programs.tuitionEU: Free. The Ministry of Education register records tuition for this programme as 'Free' (no τέλη φοίτησης).
programs.tuitionNonEU: Free — the same as for EU/Greek students. Greek public ΠΜΣ do not charge a differential non-EU rate; where a programme is fee-free it is fee-free for everyone admitted. This is the cheapest genuine second-cycle art degree found in this sweep.
programs.otherFees: Recognition of the foreign degree, certified translations, residence-permit fee, health insurance, and his own materials/equipment. Amounts UNVERIFIED.
programs.totalCostEstimate: Tuition €0; total cost is Athens living costs for two years plus visa/permit administration. Living costs UNVERIFIED.
programs.scholarships: None specific to this programme were published — UNVERIFIED. Because tuition is already zero, the funding question reduces to living costs; check IKY (Greek State Scholarships Foundation) and any Greece–Tunisia bilateral quota separately.
programs.visaEligible: Yes — full-time, in-person, state-recognised 120-ECTS second-cycle degree at a Greek ΑΕΙ; supports a student residence permit.
programs.recommendation: A free, public, real 120-ECTS master's at Greece's national art school, and the only zero-tuition option found in this sweep — worth knowing about. But it fits him poorly on three counts: it is taught in Greek; it is a fine-arts practice degree in which he would have to be admitted through an exception clause purely on submitted artistic work, with no fine-arts background; and the admission cycle appears biennial with the 2026-2028 cycle already called, which is out of phase with a September 2027 start. It is also not a music-production or audio-engineering course — sound art at most. Treat as a long-shot only if he decides to build a serious digital/sound-art portfolio and can learn Greek. Concrete step if he wants to keep it alive: email artdm@asfa.gr asking whether admission is annual or biennial, whether the exception clause has ever admitted an engineering graduate, whether any teaching is possible in English, and for the current portfolio guidelines.

programs.program: ΠΜΣ «Ακουστικός Σχεδιασμός και Ψηφιακός Ήχος» (ΑΣΠ) / MSc in Acoustic Design and Digital Sound
programs.institution: Ελληνικό Ανοικτό Πανεπιστήμιο / Hellenic Open University (HOU/EAP), Patras
programs.publicPrivate: PUBLIC. The Hellenic Open University is a Greek state university established by law and supervised by the Ministry of Education; it is the country's only public distance-learning university. It charges per-module fees because that is its statutory funding model, not because it is private.
programs.institutionType: State open/distance university
programs.qualification: Μεταπτυχιακό Δίπλωμα Ειδίκευσης (Master's Degree of Specialisation), 120 ECTS. A real, state-recognised second-cycle Greek degree and it appears in the Ministry of Education's official programme register. HOWEVER, being a distance degree, it does NOT by itself support a Greek student residence permit.
programs.accreditationStatus: State-recognised; listed in the Ministry of Education programme register (studies.minedu.gov.gr) under both Arts and Technology. The degree is genuine; the delivery mode is the problem for a visa applicant.
programs.language: Greek. All teaching and assessment is in Greek.
programs.languageRequirement: Applicants must submit a 'Υπεύθυνη Δήλωση' (statutory declaration) confirming sufficient knowledge of the programme's content; degree recognition under Greek law applies to foreign qualifications. No specific Greek certificate level is published for this programme — UNVERIFIED; ask HOU admissions. In practice fluent academic Greek is required.
programs.englishTest: None — irrelevant, the programme is in Greek.
programs.durationEcts: 120 ECTS, minimum 2 academic years, delivered as thematic units (θεματικές ενότητες). From 2025-26 examinations are conducted remotely.
programs.focus: Acoustic design and digital sound — architectural/environmental acoustics plus digital audio. Closer to his stated field than most Greek offerings.
programs.whatYouStudy: Modular thematic units in acoustic design and digital sound. Full unit list on the programme's 'ΘΕΜΑΤΙΚΕΣ ΕΝΟΤΗΤΕΣ' page.
programs.entryRequirements: Holders of an undergraduate degree from a higher-education institution in a relevant field, or an equivalent foreign qualification recognised under Greek law. Applicants must provide a statutory declaration confirming sufficient knowledge of the programme's content. Whether a Tunisian Software Engineering BSc is accepted as 'relevant' is UNVERIFIED — ask HOU.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: Probably yes on paper — this is an acoustics/engineering-flavoured programme rather than a conservatory one, and no music degree is named. UNVERIFIED; confirm with HOU admissions.
programs.portfolioSpec: None published — UNVERIFIED. HOU generally admits on qualification, not portfolio.
programs.auditionSpec: None.
programs.equipmentRequired: Not published — UNVERIFIED, but a distance audio programme will assume the student supplies his own computer, audio interface and monitoring.
programs.facilities: None — distance delivery, no studio access. This is a decisive weakness for someone who needs studio hours and industry contact.
programs.intakes: Annual, in line with HOU's admission cycle. Exact dates UNVERIFIED — check eap.gr.
programs.applicationOpens: UNVERIFIED — HOU admission calls are published on eap.gr, typically in spring/summer for an autumn start. The programme page opened did not state an application period.
programs.deadline: UNVERIFIED — ask HOU admissions.
programs.tuitionEU: €750 per thematic unit for students admitted from 2024-25 onwards (€650 per unit for those admitted up to 2023-24), giving a published total of €3,750 (or €3,250 under the older rate).
programs.tuitionNonEU: The same €750 per thematic unit / €3,750 total — HOU publishes a single rate and does not operate a separate non-EU tariff. Because there is no residence in Greece, there is also no differential.
programs.otherFees: Recognition of the foreign degree under Greek law; certified translations. Amounts UNVERIFIED.
programs.totalCostEstimate: €3,750 in tuition (2024-25 rate onwards) with no relocation, accommodation or visa cost — the cheapest total in this sweep, precisely because he would never leave Tunisia.
programs.scholarships: Not published for this programme — UNVERIFIED. HOU operates limited social-criteria fee reductions; ask admissions.
programs.visaEligible: NO. This is a distance-learning degree with remote examinations from 2025-26 onwards. Greek student residence permits require enrolment in a full-time, in-person programme. It will not get him to Europe. HOU's own page does not state a policy on non-EU international students — UNVERIFIED; if he wants confirmation, ask HOU admissions in writing.
programs.recommendation: Include this in the picture only as the honest alternative to migration, not as a route to Europe. It is a genuine, state-recognised Greek 120-ECTS master's in exactly his subject area — acoustic design and digital sound — at €3,750 total. But it is delivered entirely at a distance in Greek, with remote exams, no studio, no cohort and no student visa. For a man whose whole plan depends on getting a European residence permit and building an international network, that makes it close to useless as a migration instrument, though not worthless as a credential if he could read Greek, which he cannot. Recorded here so the database contains the finding and no later sweep wastes time on it. If he ever wants a distance credential he should look at English-language distance options rather than this one.

programs.program: ΠΜΣ «Βυζαντινή Μουσικολογία και Ψαλτική Τέχνη» / MA in Byzantine Music: Academic Theory and Artistic Performance — Department of Music Studies
programs.institution: Εθνικό και Καποδιστριακό Πανεπιστήμιο Αθηνών / National and Kapodistrian University of Athens (NKUA)
programs.publicPrivate: PUBLIC. Greece's oldest state university (ΑΕΙ), Ministry of Education funded; the programme is listed in the Ministry's own official register of postgraduate programmes.
programs.institutionType: Comprehensive state university, Department of Music Studies
programs.qualification: Δίπλωμα Μεταπτυχιακών Σπουδών, 90 ECTS over 3 semesters. A real state-recognised second-cycle degree; supports a Greek student residence permit for a non-EU national.
programs.accreditationStatus: State-recognised and listed in the Ministry of Education's official programme register (studies.minedu.gov.gr, programme id 1592).
programs.language: ENGLISH. The Ministry register records the language of instruction as English. This is the finding that matters: after enumerating every Arts-discipline master's in the Greek Ministry register, only three are English-taught, and this is the only English-taught MUSIC master's in Greece in that register.
programs.languageRequirement: Not specified on the register entry — UNVERIFIED. Ask the Department of Music Studies what English evidence is required and whether any Greek is needed for the repertoire and sources (Byzantine notation and Greek liturgical texts are unavoidable in this subject).
programs.englishTest: UNVERIFIED — no IELTS/TOEFL band is published on the register entry. Ask the department.
programs.durationEcts: 90 ECTS, 3 semesters, full-time.
programs.focus: Byzantine musicology and the art of psalmody — academic theory plus artistic performance of Byzantine ecclesiastical chant.
programs.whatYouStudy: Byzantine musicology, notation, theory and performance practice of psalmody. Contains no sound design, no music production, no audio engineering and no electronic music.
programs.entryRequirements: Graduates of any Department or School of Higher Education may be admitted following a decision of the Coordinating Committee, provided they have specialised knowledge or experience in the cognitive subjects of the programme. That last clause is the gate: any degree is formally acceptable, but demonstrated knowledge of Byzantine music is required.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: Formally yes — any bachelor's degree, subject to the Coordinating Committee being satisfied of specialised knowledge or experience in Byzantine music. In practice this means chant training, which he does not have.
programs.portfolioSpec: Not published — UNVERIFIED. Ask the department.
programs.auditionSpec: Not published — UNVERIFIED, but an 'artistic performance' strand implies a practical assessment in chant. Ask the department.
programs.equipmentRequired: None expected.
programs.facilities: UNVERIFIED.
programs.intakes: Annual, autumn start.
programs.applicationOpens: UNVERIFIED — check music.uoa.gr postgraduate announcements. Greek ΠΜΣ calls for a September start usually run May–September.
programs.deadline: UNVERIFIED — ask the Department of Music Studies.
programs.tuitionEU: €3,000 for the full-time programme (Ministry of Education register).
programs.tuitionNonEU: €3,000 — the same figure; the Greek register publishes a single fee for the programme and there is no separate non-EU rate. PRIOR CYCLE - confirm the figure for the intake he would join.
programs.otherFees: Degree recognition, translations, residence permit, health insurance — UNVERIFIED.
programs.totalCostEstimate: €3,000 tuition plus Athens living costs for 18 months. Living costs UNVERIFIED.
programs.scholarships: None published on the register entry — UNVERIFIED. Check IKY and the department.
programs.visaEligible: Yes — full-time, in-person, state-recognised 90-ECTS second-cycle degree at a Greek state university.
programs.recommendation: DO NOT APPLY — recorded deliberately as a negative finding, because it answers a question the earlier sweeps left open. Working through the Greek Ministry of Education's official register discipline by discipline, only three Arts master's programmes in the whole country are taught in English, and the only English-taught music master's among them is this one, in Byzantine chant. Everything else in the Greek sound/music-technology landscape — Ionian's sound arts programmes, the Hellenic Mediterranean sound and music technologies MSc, the West Attica audio/video/broadcasting MSc, the Athens School of Fine Arts digital arts MA, the Open University acoustic design MSc — is taught in Greek. The practical conclusion for a Tunisian applicant with Arabic, French and working English but no Greek is that GREECE IS EFFECTIVELY CLOSED to him for this field unless a department confirms English supervision in writing. That is the single most useful thing this record carries; the programme itself is irrelevant to a would-be DJ and producer.

programs.program: Medieningenieurwissenschaften (M.Sc.) — successor title of the former M.Sc. Medientechnologie. CONFIRMED TO EXIST as a real M.Sc.
programs.institution: Technische Universität Ilmenau
programs.institutionType: Technische Universität (state technical university), Free State of Thuringia
programs.publicPrivate: CONFIRMED PUBLIC. State technical university of the Free State of Thuringia. The official Beiträge-und-Gebühren page publishes only a Semesterbeitrag plus statutory administrative fees and explicitly states there are no tuition fees — only possible for a state institution.
programs.qualification: CONFIRMED: Master of Science (M.Sc.), 120 Leistungspunkte, 4 semesters, awarded by a doctorate-granting state university. A genuine second-cycle German degree supporting a §16b AufenthG student residence permit.
programs.accreditationStatus: State university programme under Thuringian higher-education law. Programme-level accreditation seal/expiry still not published on the programme page — STILL UNVERIFIED; check antrag.akkreditierungsrat.de. Note the DAAD course-database entry for this programme still carries the legacy slug 'medientechnologie', which independently confirms it is the renamed continuation of the old M.Sc. Medientechnologie rather than a new unaccredited creation.
programs.language: CONFIRMED bilingual: the official page states 'Deutsch/Englisch'. Ilmenau's own wording is that the programme 'can be completed in either German or English'. So an English-only path IS available here — a correction in his favour over the previous record, which said a German-free path was not guaranteed.
programs.languageRequirement: CORRECTED — the previous record said this was unpublished and possibly no certificate is needed. That is WRONG. TU Ilmenau's official language-certificates page and application rules state: a language certificate is ALWAYS required, in German or English depending on the teaching language chosen; B2 CEFR is the minimum to apply for a master's and yields conditional admission; C1 CEFR gives direct/unrestricted admission. For him the English route applies: he must sit IELTS/TOEFL. B2 is enough to get in the door with conditions, C1 for clean admission. (The sibling English-taught Ilmenau master 'Research in Media Engineering' names IELTS Academic 7 / TOEFL iBT 95 as its C1 equivalents — expect the same table.)
programs.durationEcts: CONFIRMED: 4 semesters, 120 ECTS. Start 1 October or 1 April.
programs.focus: Media/audio engineering: audio signal processing, audio coding (psychoacoustics, quantisation, filterbanks, MPEG audio, parametric coding), video technology, media production technology, software for digital media. Taught into by Ilmenau's Electronic Media Technology and Audiovisual Technology groups; Fraunhofer IDMT — the mp3/AAC institute — is on the same campus.
programs.whatYouStudy: Roughly 34-42% engineering disciplines, 17% media technology, 13-21% research/media project work, 4% soft skills, 25% thesis. A large group media project is a core element. Work in the I3TC laboratories.
programs.entryRequirements: CONFIRMED and CLARIFIED. Official requirement is 'Abschluss eines verwandten Bachelorstudiums' (completion of a related bachelor's) and the programme is NC-frei — no numerus clausus, no competitive ranking. CORRECTION to the previous record: there is no sit-down Master-Eignungsprüfung. Ilmenau runs a fachspezifische Eignungsfeststellung that is a DOCUMENT-BASED review by the faculty of his transcript — no exam to travel for. The deciding factor remains how much maths / electrical engineering / digital signal processing his SMU MedTech transcript shows. Note the sibling Ilmenau media master states a 180-ECTS bachelor as sufficient, so his 3-year BSc is not disqualified on volume the way TH Köln's 210-ECTS rule would disqualify it.
programs.auditionSpec: None. No audition. CONFIRMED.
programs.portfolioSpec: None required. CONFIRMED. This is an engineering master — his lack of a music portfolio is not a barrier. Still the single strongest reason to keep Ilmenau at the top of his German list.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: YES — CONFIRMED. Explicitly an engineering degree; no music degree, conservatory training or audio work experience required or mentioned anywhere in the admission rules.
programs.equipmentRequired: None stated. University laboratories/studios provided.
programs.facilities: I3TC (Ilmenau Interdisciplinary Innovation Test Centre); Electronic Media Technology and Audiovisual Technology group labs (listening rooms, virtual acoustics); campus adjacency to Fraunhofer IDMT.
programs.intakes: CONFIRMED: winter semester (start 1 October) and summer semester (start 1 April).
programs.applicationOpens: CONFIRMED on the official 'application with foreign certificates' page. Non-EU/EEA applicants: winter semester 16 January – 15 May; summer semester 1 August – 15 November. MAJOR PROCESS CHANGE CONFIRMED AND DIRECTLY RELEVANT TO HIM: TU Ilmenau states that all applications for 2027 with international certificates must be submitted through uni-assist (2026 was the last cycle handled in the university's own campus portal). His September/October 2027 intake falls squarely in the uni-assist regime, so he must budget uni-assist's own processing lead time on top.
programs.deadline: 15 May 2027 for an October 2027 start, applying 16 January – 15 May 2027 via uni-assist. Note that Ilmenau has in practice extended this: the winter-semester 2026 deadline was pushed from 15 May to 15 July 2026. Do not plan around an extension, but know one is possible. Master's applications take 6-8 weeks to process and a German student visa takes about 3 months, so a 15 May submission is the right target, not a fallback.
programs.tuitionEU: No tuition fee. Semester contribution only. CONFIRMED.
programs.tuitionNonEU: CONFIRMED IDENTICAL to the EU rate — Thuringia charges no tuition to non-EU nationals. He pays exactly what a German student pays. The only tuition-like risk is the Langzeitstudiengebühr of EUR 500.00 per semester once the standard study period is exceeded (confirmed on the official fee page).
programs.otherFees: CORRECTED IN TWO PLACES. (1) Application fee: TU Ilmenau charges EUR 75.00 for each application submitted with non-European certificates — the previous record's 'EUR 25.00 administrative fee' is WRONG. Since 2027 applications route through uni-assist, budget the uni-assist handling fee (EUR 75 first application, EUR 30 each further) as well, and confirm whether both are levied. (2) Semester contribution: CORRECTED from 'UNVERIFIED, typically well under EUR 200'. For winter semester 2026/27 the Thuringian components are Studierendenwerk Thüringen EUR 95.00 + Deutschlandsemesterticket EUR 226.80 + StuRa contribution EUR 10.00, i.e. roughly EUR 332 per semester. Ilmenau's own DAAD listing quotes 'approx. EUR 320 per semester'. Other published add-ons, all confirmed: EUR 20.00 student ID / study certificate, EUR 20.00 late-payment fee, EUR 20.00 duplicate diploma, EUR 500.00 per excess semester, EUR 50.00 per semester for guest auditors.
programs.totalCostEstimate: Tuition EUR 0. Semester contribution approx. EUR 332 per semester = approx. EUR 664/year (CORRECTED UPWARD from the previous record's implied sub-EUR-400/year). Plus EUR 75 application fee, plus IELTS/TOEFL fee, plus Ilmenau living costs (low by German standards — it is a small Thuringian town), plus the blocked account (Sperrkonto) required for the visa, whose amount is set nationally and must be checked with the German embassy in Tunis for 2027.
programs.scholarships: No programme-specific scholarship published. Realistic routes for a Tunisian national are DAAD Study Scholarships and the Deutschlandstipendium (EUR 300/month, university nomination). Neither is guaranteed. Whether TU Ilmenau nominates in this programme remains UNVERIFIED.
programs.englishTest: CORRECTED — REQUIRED, not 'possibly none'. English B2 CEFR minimum to apply (conditional admission), C1 CEFR for unrestricted admission, evidenced by a recognised certificate mapped through uni-assist's English reference framework (Category 3). Expect IELTS Academic 7 / TOEFL iBT 95 to be the C1 equivalents. He SHOULD book IELTS — the previous record's advice not to book until confirmed is now obsolete. Only exemption is if English is both the official language and the language of education of his home country, which does not apply to Tunisia; a medium-of-instruction letter from SMU MedTech will not clear this bar at Ilmenau.
programs.visaEligible: YES. Full-time, on-campus, state second-cycle degree at a doctorate-granting state university — a textbook basis for a German student residence permit (§16b AufenthG).
programs.recommendation: CONFIRMED as the strongest realistic German target for him, and the re-check strengthened rather than weakened the case. It is accredited-lineage, state-run, tuition-free, NC-free, needs no portfolio and no audition, has no music prerequisite, is completable entirely in English, and accepts a related engineering bachelor on a document review rather than a travel-to-Germany exam. Four things changed on verification and he must act on them: (1) an English certificate IS mandatory — B2 for conditional admission, C1/IELTS 7 for clean admission — so book a diagnostic now and plan a preparation year; (2) the application fee is EUR 75, not EUR 25; (3) the real semester contribution is about EUR 332, not 'well under EUR 200'; (4) his 2027 intake must go through uni-assist, which Ilmenau only switches to for 2027 onward, so the old campus-portal instructions circulating online do not apply to him. One extra find worth putting in front of him: TU Ilmenau runs a sibling M.Sc. 'Research in Media Engineering', also bilingual, which publishes its requirements far more explicitly — a 180-ECTS bachelor in electrical engineering, media technology, computer engineering or COMPUTER SCIENCE, with English C1 (IELTS 7 / TOEFL 95) and no German minimum at all. For a software-engineering graduate that named-CS entry route may be a cleaner fit than 'a related bachelor', and he should apply to both.

programs.program: Medientechnologie (M.Sc.) — Media Technology

programs.durationEcts: CONFIRMED: 3 semesters, 90 ECTS. Entry possible in both winter and summer semesters.

A standard 3-year 180-ECTS BSc does NOT satisfy (c) — he would be 30 ECTS short. The page does note that missing prerequisites may be made up as enrolment conditions (Auflagen), which is the only realistic door. Admission itself is nicht zulassungsbeschränkt (unrestricted) — the filter is entirely the eligibility rules, not competition.
programs.auditionSpec: None.
programs.portfolioSpec: None required.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: YES — it is an engineering master and expects a technical, not musical, background. But the 210-ECTS rule, the 2.7 grade conversion and C1 German are the real filters, and they bite hard on his profile.
programs.equipmentRequired: None stated; laboratory and studio facilities provided.

It has genuinely the best spatial-audio content of any German UAS master here and it costs nothing but EUR 352.70 a semester, so it is not a rip-off and does not deserve AVOID — but for THIS candidate it is effectively blocked for September 2027, because he would have to clear C1 German from zero AND find 30 missing ECTS AND survive a grade conversion, all in eighteen months. If he wants to keep the option alive at near-zero cost, two emails this year decide it: ask the F07 examination committee for a written ECTS assessment of his SMU MedTech transcript, and ask whether the 30-ECTS shortfall can be carried as an Auflage rather than blocking admission. If either answer is no, drop it and put the effort into Ilmenau and Bremen instead.

programs.focus: Popular music and media: history and current developments of popular music, music and media industries, production and mediation cultures, analysis of popular music. It does not advance the DJ/producer craft by a single hour of studio time, and it demands DSH/TestDaF-level German, which is the same 12-18 month investment TH Köln demands but for a much smaller payoff in his chosen direction. Two specific risks the previous record understated: the committee may simply rule a software-engineering BSc not fachverwandt to musicology and reject him on subject grounds regardless of how open the admission is, and the published 23 October deadline is a domestic date that is visa-impossible for a Tunisian national. programs.program: Digitale Medien / Digital Media — M.A. at HfK Bremen (media design track) or M.Sc. at Universität Bremen (media informatics track). One joint programme, two award routes.

programs.languageRequirement: CONFIRMED EXACTLY AS PREVIOUSLY STATED: C1 CEFR, or TOEFL iBT 95 or higher, or IELTS Band 7, or Cambridge CAE, or US UNIcert III or similar. CONFIRMED WAIVER: the requirement is waived if the qualifying degree or the school education was taught in English, with proof. No German certificate is required for admission. programs.entryRequirements: CONFIRMED: proof that AT LEAST 150 ECTS have been acquired in the qualifying degree programme, in a relevant field — computer science, design, media arts, fine arts, architecture, systems engineering and related. A BSc Software Engineering fits cleanly, and 150 ECTS is a notably low bar next to TH Köln's 210. This is the single most important structural advantage of this record for him.

programs.portfolioSpec: CONFIRMED REQUIRED, with the spec differing by route. M.A. (HfK): the guidance states 'a standard number of 10-20 works has proven to be sufficient', spanning artistic, design, academic or professional projects, submitted as PDF, by post, or as a link to a personal website, private upload area or repository. M.Sc. (Universität Bremen): a SINGLE video of no more than 5 minutes demonstrating the breadth of his digital-media work. The 5-minute video route remains the most actionable detail across all six records — it is exactly what one focused year of building can produce. All other documents must be PDF, total upload capped at 50MB with the portfolio exempt.

For a September/October 2027 start he applies 1 April – 31 May 2027 and should expect the same rhythm. programs.tuitionEU: No tuition fee; semester contribution EUR 431.40. CONFIRMED.

programs.totalCostEstimate: About EUR 862.80 per year in semester contributions, plus Bremen living costs (moderate by German standards), plus the blocked account required for the visa, plus the IELTS fee. No tuition, no application fee published.
programs.scholarships: None programme-specific published. DAAD / Deutschlandstipendium only. STILL UNVERIFIED — ask the HfK International Office.
programs.englishTest: IELTS 7.0 / TOEFL iBT 95 / CEFR C1. Waiver only if his SMU MedTech degree or his school education was taught in English AND he can prove it. Worth pursuing hard, because SMU MedTech teaches substantially in English and a medium-of-instruction letter could remove this gate outright — unlike at Ilmenau, this waiver is written into the published requirements rather than restricted to native-English countries.
programs.visaEligible: YES. Full-time state degree at two state institutions.
programs.recommendation: This record survived verification with ZERO corrections — every figure, date and requirement checked out exactly, which is not true of any other entry here. It is the best-documented and most accessible option of the six for him: English-taught with no German required at all, a 150-ECTS entry bar his BSc clears comfortably, software engineering explicitly named as an acceptable background, EUR 431.40 a semester and nothing more, no audition, and an M.Sc. route whose entire portfolio requirement is a 5-minute video. Three action items, in order: (1) request a medium-of-instruction letter from SMU MedTech immediately and send it to the HfK International Office asking in writing whether it waives the IELTS 7 requirement — this single email could remove his largest obstacle; (2) if it does not, book a diagnostic IELTS now, because Band 7 from 'working English' is a genuine year of work; (3) start building the 5-minute video around sound and music-technology projects so that his portfolio year, his application and his career goal all point the same direction. Apply to both the M.Sc. and M.A. routes if permitted — the M.Sc. video is easier to produce than 10-20 finished works. Second official source for application detail: https://www.hfk-bremen.de/en/application/bewerbung-im-digitale-medien-m-a/3

programs.recommendation: Verification confirmed everything material and improved the accreditation picture — accredited 1 October 2023 to 30 September 2031, 120 ECTS, German with no language certificate demanded, 31 May deadline, semester fee only. It is a real, properly accredited, essentially free state degree and nothing about it is a rip-off. But for HIM it stays a C, for two reasons that verification did not soften. First, it is portfolio-gated at the front door: entry runs through an artistic project proposal and an Eignungsprüfung, and he has neither a proposal nor a body of sound work, so this is an aspiration for a later cycle rather than a September 2027 plan. Second, be blunt about direction — this is installation, sonification and research sound art, explicitly framed around acoustic ecology and sound as political act. It does not serve the international-DJ-and-producer goal, and pretending otherwise would waste his portfolio year. Two zero-cost steps if he is drawn to it anyway: download the 'Anforderungen im Eignungsverfahren' document from the programme page so he sees the actual bar rather than a summary, and attend one of the free online information sessions to ask Prof. Bovermann directly whether a software-engineering applicant with a year of self-built sound work has a route. Given Bovermann's own engineering and live-coding background, that answer may be more encouraging than the formal requirements suggest.

The official JGU study-programme record demands only 'der Nachweis hinreichender deutscher Sprachkenntnisse (vergleichbar Niveau A1-GERR)' — German comparable to CEFR A1, required only of applicants without a prior qualification from a German-language institution, and provable either by certificate OR through the interview conducted during the aptitude examination. Additional published rule, confirmed: applicants whose bachelor is not yet conferred at the application deadline need at least 135 ECTS.
programs.focus: Sound-art composition with an emphasis on spatialising and intermedial compositional strategies, drawing new music, ELECTRONIC COMPOSITION, sound art, audiovisual art, radiophonic art and Ars Acustica into one thematic unit. The electronic-composition element is real and is the closest any of the artistic options here comes to his interests.
programs.whatYouStudy: Advanced individual artistic-compositional research; collaboration with media and art institutions; spatial and multichannel work. Career destinations named by the school: independent artistic practice, media, radio, and museum sound design.
programs.entryRequirements: CONFIRMED — THE MOST OPEN DOOR OF THE SIX, in the regulation's own words. Three routes: a bachelor in Music; a bachelor in Art; or, quoted from the official record, 'bei Vorliegen einer hohen künstlerischen Befähigung, festgestellt durch die Eignungsprüfung, ist auch die Zulassung von Bewerber*innen möglich, die einen anderen Studiengang abgeschlossen haben' — applicants who completed a DIFFERENT degree programme may be admitted on high artistic aptitude established by the aptitude examination. That third route is precisely his situation and it is written into the rules, not a favour. Also confirmed: the aptitude examination must be completed within one year of enrolment.
programs.auditionSpec: CONFIRMED, and CORRECTED on one detail. Two-stage Eignungsprüfung, and it is NOT an instrumental audition. Stage 1: pre-selection by committee on submitted materials, after which shortlisted candidates are given a theme for a project sketch 6 to 12 weeks before the interview. Stage 2: an aptitude CONVERSATION in which the candidate presents the prepared project sketch and discusses artistic background and motivation. CORRECTION: the published length is 30 to 45 minutes, with a minimum of 20 minutes per applicant — the previous record's '20-45 minutes' was slightly off. No instrument, no performance, no conservatory technique is tested. For a candidate with no conservatory training this is a far more winnable format than a classical audition, and the 6-12 week preparation window means the decisive work happens at home, not on the spot.
programs.portfolioSpec: CONFIRMED, and it remains the most concretely writable specification of the six. The application must contain: a CV; a written justification of the choice of programme; studiengangsbezogene Arbeitsproben (work samples relevant to the field); and a description of planned artistic projects plus a project sketch in sound-art composition. His portfolio year should be built to produce exactly these four items and nothing else.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: YES, EXPLICITLY — CONFIRMED in the regulation's own wording. Combined with the A1 German bar, this is the most permissive formal profile found anywhere in this set.
programs.equipmentRequired: None stated — STILL UNVERIFIED.

programs.intakes: Winter semester entry, consistent with the confirmed February-to-April aptitude registration window.
programs.applicationOpens: CORRECTED — the previous record said this was not published. IT IS PUBLISHED. He should still confirm the exact 2027 dates with the Studienbüro, but the window is no longer a mystery.
programs.deadline: CORRECTED — the previous record said 'NOT PUBLISHED'. That was wrong. For a September/October 2027 start he registers between 1 February and 1 April 2027. Critically, the pre-selection stage plus a 6-12 week project-sketch preparation window means his real work starts in 2026, not 2027.

programs.tuitionNonEU: CONFIRMED IDENTICAL — no non-EU tuition rate at JGU Mainz.

Expect it to be in the same EUR 330-390 band as the other German records here, since the Deutschlandsemesterticket component of EUR 226.80 is nationally set and JGU includes a broad regional ticket.
programs.totalCostEstimate: Tuition EUR 0 + semester contribution (UNVERIFIED, budget approx. EUR 350-390 per semester on the national pattern) + Mainz living costs (moderate; Rhine-Main is cheaper than Frankfurt itself) + A1 German course fees, which are trivial next to the C1 courses TH Köln and Paderborn would demand + the blocked account for the visa.
programs.scholarships: None programme-specific published. DAAD artistic-field scholarships are the route for a Tunisian national. The Meisterschülerstudium Klangkunst-Komposition at JGU is a post-master artistic track, not a funding source.

programs.visaEligible: YES. Full-time state MMus from a state university.
programs.recommendation: The re-check upgraded this record rather than downgrading it, and it now has a published deadline where it previously had a blank. Everything remarkable about it verified: an applicant from an unrelated degree is EXPLICITLY admissible on artistic aptitude, only A1 German is demanded on paper and can even be evidenced through the interview itself, the aptitude test is a project conversation rather than an instrumental audition, the candidate gets 6-12 weeks at home to prepare the decisive project sketch, and the whole cost is a semester contribution. Two corrections he must act on: the deadline IS published — registration for the Eignungsprüfung runs 1 February to 1 April for the following winter semester, so his date is 1 April 2027, not a mid-summer university deadline; and the aptitude conversation is 30-45 minutes (minimum 20), not 20-45. It stays CONDITIONAL and B rather than A for one honest reason: it is sound-art COMPOSITION — spatial, intermedial, radiophonic, Ars Acustica — not dance-music production, and he must genuinely want that rather than treat it as a side door into Europe. That said, of the three artistic options it is the only one whose curriculum names ELECTRONIC COMPOSITION outright, and it is the only programme in this entire set where a non-music engineering graduate is admissible by written rule rather than by committee discretion. Two things to do this year: get the Studien- und Prüfungsordnung and the confirmed ECTS figure from the Studienbüro, and start building the project sketch, because that single document decides everything. programs.program: Media Production (M.A.) — berufsbegleitend / part-time

programs.language: GERMAN — CONFIRMED on both the English and German official pages.
programs.languageRequirement: Still not published on the programme page — genuinely UNVERIFIED after direct checking. German-taught at a Saxon UAS normally means DSH-2 / TestDaF 4x4. Ask studienberatung@hs-mittweida.de. Moot given the blockers below.
programs.durationEcts: 4 semesters, 120 ECTS, PART-TIME alongside employment (berufsbegleitend). programs.focus: Media production craft plus current-technology topics: virtual production, augmented reality, artificial intelligence, digital storytelling, and management/leadership content. programs.whatYouStudy: Small-group seminars and project work rather than lectures, built on the Faculty of Media's production-training tradition, combining online modules with Friday/Saturday attendance blocks in Leipzig. The programme was created at the express suggestion of Central German media companies to upskill their existing staff.
programs.entryRequirements: CORRECTED — the previous record understated this gate by following the English page. The German page requires a first professionally qualifying degree with at least 180 ECTS AND at least one year of professional experience SPECIFICALLY IN THE MEDIA AND COMMUNICATIONS INDUSTRY ('mindestens ein Jahr in der Medien- und Kommunikationsbranche Berufserfahrung'). The English page drops the industry qualifier and says only 'one year of professional experience' — the German text governs. His 180-ECTS BSc clears the credit bar; he has zero months in the media and communications industry, so he fails the entry rule outright. The 'in exceptional cases the experience may be acquired during the programme' clause is designed for someone already working in the sector, not for an overseas applicant with no sector history. Enrolment is otherwise guaranteed on submission of documents — there is no competitive selection.
programs.auditionSpec: None.
programs.portfolioSpec: None required.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: YES on the music point — CONFIRMED that the first degree need not be in media or communication either, so a BSc Software Engineering is an acceptable academic base. The bar he fails is the one year of media-industry work experience, not the subject of his degree.

programs.intakes: Winter semester and summer semester — CONFIRMED. Programme first ran from winter semester 2025/26.
programs.applicationOpens: Via hs.mw/apply. Opening date not published.
programs.deadline: Not published on either the English or German official programme page — I checked both directly. Secondary sources (Studis Online) give 15 July for the winter semester and 15 January for the summer semester, which matches the standard Saxon UAS pattern, but this is NOT officially confirmed. Verify with Lisa Viehweg, Course Adviser, +49 3727 581309, studienberatung@hs-mittweida.de.
programs.tuitionEU: EUR 0 — CONFIRMED. 'Studiengebühren gibt es nicht' on the German page; 'there are no tuition fees' on the English page. Unusual for a berufsbegleitend master and worth one confirming email, since Mittweida's own fee page notes the university MAY levy charges for distance-learning and continuing-education programmes; this one is nevertheless stated as fee-free.
programs.tuitionNonEU: EUR 0 — no separate non-EU rate exists. Saxony levies no non-EU tuition at state institutions. As a Tunisian national he would pay the same nothing an EU student pays.
programs.otherFees: CORRECTED from UNVERIFIED — the semester contribution is EUR 107 per semester, comprising EUR 92 for the Studentenwerk and EUR 15 for the student body (Studentenschaft). Enrolment is only possible once it is paid. Travel and accommodation for the Leipzig attendance days are on the student.
programs.totalCostEstimate: EUR 0 tuition + EUR 107 per semester (EUR 428 across four semesters) + travel to the Leipzig blocks. Nominally one of the cheapest master's degrees in Europe — and entirely beside the point, because he cannot get in and could not get a visa on it.
programs.scholarships: None published.
programs.englishTest: None — German-taught, so IELTS/TOEFL is irrelevant here.
programs.visaEligible: NO in practice — and the legal reasoning in the previous record needed correcting rather than just repeating. The correction: part-time study is not legally excluded. Section 16b(1) AufenthG grants a residence permit as an ENTITLEMENT ('wird erteilt') for Vollzeitstudium — full-time study. Part-time study appears separately in section 16b(5), where the permit 'kann erteilt werden' — purely DISCRETIONARY. So the honest statement is not 'part-time is refused by law' but 'part-time carries no entitlement, only official discretion'. That discretion will not be exercised in his favour, for a reason specific to this programme: it delivers roughly 20 attendance days over two years and presupposes concurrent employment in the German media industry. An Ausländerbehörde will not accept five contact days a semester as a residence purpose, and he cannot hold the German media job that would supply an alternative residence basis, because he would need a residence permit to take it. The requirement and the remedy are circular.
programs.recommendation: AVOID — and the case against it is now stronger than the previous record made out, on three independently fatal grounds. First, entry: the German page requires a year of experience in the media and communications industry, not merely a year of any work; the English page's looser wording is not the governing text and the previous record was misled by it. He has none. Second, visa: this is a part-time programme with about 20 attendance days total, built for people already employed by Central German media companies. Part-time study carries no residence entitlement under section 16b(1), only discretion under 16b(5), and no authority will grant it on this contact load. He cannot take the job that would fix the problem without the permit the job is supposed to justify. Third, and new: the programme itself is listed as not accredited — the university's system accreditation (held since April 2023) covers the institution and lets it seal its own programmes, but this one launched in winter 2025/26 and has not yet been sealed. None of this is a knock on the institution, which is a legitimate state UAS charging EUR 0 tuition and EUR 107 a semester. It is simply not a migration route, and it is not open to him. Spend no application effort here for September 2027.

programs.program: Media Art & Design (M.A.)
programs.institution: Hochschule der Bildenden Künste Saar (HBKsaar — Saar University of Fine Arts)
programs.institutionType: Staatliche Kunsthochschule (state university of fine arts), Saarland
programs.publicPrivate: PUBLIC — CONFIRMED. State university of fine arts of the Saarland. Its own application pages state 'Die HBKsaar erhebt keine Studiengebühren' (HBKsaar charges no tuition fees).
programs.qualification: Master of Arts (M.A.), 60 ECTS — CONFIRMED to exist and to be currently offered. It is a real state-recognised second-cycle degree, but a SHORT one: the official master overview sets the average duration at one year / 60 CP, with a maximum of two years. That short form is precisely why it demands a 240-ECTS first degree — the German system wants 300 ECTS total at master level, and a 60-ECTS master only reaches that from a 240-ECTS base.
programs.accreditationStatus: State art college programme; programme seal not published on the institution's pages — still UNVERIFIED, check antrag.akkreditierungsrat.de. CONFIRMED AND IMPORTANT: Media Art & Design is NOT among the suspended programmes. The Senate suspended only Master Kuratieren/Ausstellungswesen and Master Museumspädagogik with effect from winter semester 2026/27. Media Art & Design is listed as a live consecutive master alongside Freie Kunst, Kommunikationsdesign and Produktdesign. The earlier warning that it might be withdrawn is resolved in its favour.
programs.language: GERMAN — CORRECTED from UNVERIFIED. The DAAD international programme database lists the language of instruction for this master as 'Deutsch'. The previous record's suspicion was right but is now confirmed rather than assumed. There is no English-taught route into this degree.
programs.languageRequirement: CORRECTED, and materially better news than assumed. HBKsaar requires 'ausreichende deutsche Sprachkenntnisse, mindestens Stufe B2' — B2, NOT the DSH-2/C1 level the previous record told him to assume. Accepted certificates: TestDaF level 4 in all four sections, Goethe-Zertifikat B2, telc Deutsch B2, DSH level 2, or DSD II with at least B2 in all sections. B2 is a realistic target for a fluent French speaker inside the 2026-27 window; DSH-2 would not have been.
programs.durationEcts: 2 semesters / 60 CP standard, maximum 4 semesters — CONFIRMED on the official Masterstudiengänge overview.
programs.focus: Digital technologies and the development of an individual artistic practice: documentary and animation film, visual effects, interactive productions, internet applications, artistic installations, games, media spaces, photography, media art, and explicitly SOUND AND LIGHT ART WORKS. Sound is named as a medium, but this is a media-art degree. It will not teach him mixing, mastering, studio signal flow or record production, and it is not a route into DJing.
programs.whatYouStudy: Projektstudium — self-directed project work on electronic, time-based and interactive productions, with students setting their own priorities and drawing on resources across all departments. Supervised by Profs. Burkhard Detzler, Sung-Hyung Cho and Eric Lanz. Extensive workshops: wood, printing, CNC, 3D printing, metal, plus media project spaces.
programs.entryRequirements: HARD GATE, CONFIRMED: open to graduates of academic or artistic BA programmes with AT LEAST 240 ECTS. His 180-ECTS Tunisian BSc does NOT meet this and he cannot argue his way past it. HBKsaar states that applicants with fewer credits are offered a transition programme drawn from its own former bachelor programmes ('Übergangsprogramm') — the length, cost, residence basis and admission terms of that bridge remain UNPUBLISHED after direct checking of the master overview and application pages. That single unknown decides whether this programme is reachable for him at all. Ask mad@hbksaar.de.
programs.auditionSpec: CORRECTED — the previous record said 'None', which is wrong. Master applicants must pass an EIGNUNGSPRÜFUNG (aptitude examination). After the submitted materials are assessed, shortlisted candidates proceed to an oral/practical examination which is held IN PERSON at the institution in Saarbrücken. For a Tunisian applicant this is a real and expensive obstacle: it means a Schengen short-stay visa and a trip to the Saarland before any study visa exists. Ask mad@hbksaar.de whether remote examination is ever permitted for overseas candidates — do not assume it is.
programs.portfolioSpec: CORRECTED from 'NOT PUBLISHED'. It is published, on the application information page. Media Art & Design applicants must submit a PORTFOLIO OF WORK SAMPLES together with a LETTER OF MOTIVATION and a PROJECT PROPOSAL (Projektvorhaben). Format: PDF, maximum 100 MB; larger material such as video must be supplied as external links (YouTube, Vimeo, cloud storage). Applications go through the SIM application portal. This is an artistic portfolio judged as art — a year of bedroom production tracks will not read as one unless he deliberately builds installation, audiovisual or sound-art pieces with a stated concept.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: YES — no music degree is required, and a computing background is not itself a barrier at a media-art college. The obstacles are the 240-ECTS rule, the German B2 requirement, the in-person aptitude exam, and the need for a genuinely artistic portfolio.
programs.equipmentRequired: Not stated.
programs.facilities: Media project spaces with current hardware and software; wood, printing, CNC, 3D-printing and metal workshops available across departments.
programs.intakes: Winter semester and summer semester — inferred from the two published application deadlines.
programs.applicationOpens: Not published; applications are submitted through the SIM portal.
programs.deadline: CORRECTED from 'NOT PUBLISHED'. The official HBKsaar application information page gives 31 MAY for the following WINTER semester and 30 NOVEMBER for the following SUMMER semester, submitted via the SIM portal. For a September 2027 (winter semester 2027/28) start his deadline is 31 MAY 2027 — which is LATER than the October 2026-February 2027 window he has been planning around, so this one does not clash with his other applications. Note the implication: the aptitude exam would fall in mid-2027, leaving a tight run to a September start.
programs.tuitionEU: EUR 0 — CONFIRMED. 'Die HBKsaar erhebt keine Studiengebühren.'
programs.tuitionNonEU: EUR 0 — CONFIRMED. Saarland levies no non-EU tuition at state institutions and HBKsaar publishes no separate international rate. As a Tunisian national he pays the same nothing an EU student pays. This is now confirmed rather than assumed.
programs.otherFees: CORRECTED from UNVERIFIED — the semester contribution for winter semester 2026/27 is EUR 422.20 for a student enrolled only at HBKsaar, made up of Studierendenwerk Saarland EUR 121.20, accident/liability/theft insurance EUR 1.30, student body fee EUR 22.90, Deutschlandticket semester ticket EUR 226.80, and an administrative fee of EUR 50.00. More than half of it is the nationwide transport ticket, which is genuine value. Students also enrolled at another Saarland institution pay EUR 274.70.
programs.totalCostEstimate: Tuition EUR 0. Semester contribution EUR 422.20 x 2 semesters = roughly EUR 845 for the whole 60-ECTS master, including a year of nationwide German public transport. Add Saarbrücken living costs and the blocked account (currently around EUR 12,000 for the year). Plus the unbudgeted cost of travelling to Saarbrücken for the in-person aptitude exam, and whatever the unpublished transition programme charges. On tuition alone this is one of the cheapest real master's degrees available to him anywhere.
programs.scholarships: None published by the institution. DAAD schemes would be the route, applied for separately.
programs.englishTest: None — German-taught, so IELTS/TOEFL is irrelevant. His unwritten English test is not the obstacle here; German B2 is.
programs.visaEligible: YES for the M.A. itself — full-time degree at a state university of fine arts, squarely within the section 16b(1) AufenthG entitlement. Two caveats specific to this programme. First, a 60-ECTS one-year master gives a short residence window and correspondingly little time to convert into the 18-month post-study job-seeking permit. Second, any preliminary transition programme would need its own residence basis, and a preparatory course is a weaker footing than a degree — clarify with the International Office before committing.
programs.recommendation: CONDITIONAL, rating C — the record is much better documented than before, and most of the corrections went in his favour, but the one obstacle that matters did not move. Corrected on this pass: the master exists and is NOT suspended; teaching is in German; the language bar is B2, not DSH-2, which is genuinely achievable for him; the deadlines are published (31 May for winter, 30 November for summer), so a September 2027 start means 31 May 2027; the portfolio requirement is published and specific (PDF under 100 MB, plus motivation letter and project proposal); there IS an aptitude examination, held in person in Saarbrücken, which the previous record wrongly recorded as 'none'; and the real cost is EUR 0 tuition plus EUR 422.20 a semester including the Deutschlandticket. What did not change is the 240-ECTS entry rule, which his 180-ECTS BSc fails, and the transition programme that might bridge it remains entirely unpublished despite direct checking. So this is not a thin record any more — it is a well-documented programme with one decisive unknown. The action is unchanged and cheap: one email to mad@hbksaar.de and s.rauber@hbksaar.de asking exactly two things now that the rest is settled — the terms, length, cost and residence basis of the transition programme for a 180-ECTS holder, and whether the in-person aptitude exam can be taken remotely from Tunisia. If the bridge is short and carries a visa, this becomes a serious B. If not, it is closed. Separately, be clear-eyed that even on success this is a media-ART degree with sound as one medium among many — it serves an installation and audiovisual practice, not a career as a DJ and record producer. programs.institutionType: Staatliche Hochschule für Musik, Theater und Medien (state university of music, drama and media), Lower Saxony — university status with doctoral rights

programs.language: GERMAN — CONFIRMED. Teaching and all programme materials are German; the English information page describes a German-taught degree.
programs.languageRequirement: CORRECTED from UNVERIFIED — now on record. German at TestDaF level TDN 4 minimum is required, and it is required ONLY of applicants who do not hold a German higher-education entrance qualification. As a Tunisian applicant he falls squarely in that group, so TestDaF 4 is mandatory for him. Note this is TDN 4 across the board, a higher bar than HBKsaar's B2.
programs.durationEcts: CORRECTED from UNVERIFIED — 120 ECTS over 4 semesters, modular, confirmed. Only 17 places are awarded per year, making this a very small and competitive cohort.

programs.whatYouStudy: CONFIRMED as a research and management degree with no studio craft whatsoever. The reformed structure runs six study modules plus an examination module, including three research projects, advanced methods training completed by the end of the third semester, strategic management in media and music, an individual profiling module, and a master thesis with defence. programs.entryRequirements: CORRECTED AND DECISIVE — the previous record described this as 'ambiguous' and it is not. The rule requires a bachelor in communication science, media studies, musicology, or a music-related artistic-academic programme, OR another academically related prior degree, that contains AT LEAST 60 ECTS OF CREDIT IN MUSIC, COMMUNICATION, MEDIA OR SOCIAL SCIENCE COMPONENTS. That 60-ECTS subject quota is the real gate, and it is the fact the previous record missed. A BSc Software Engineering from SMU MedTech will not carry 60 ECTS in those fields — a computing curriculum is mathematics, programming, systems and engineering. Half a year's worth of media, music or social science credit simply is not there to point at. Note also that the phrase 'another academically related prior degree' is what admits, say, a sociology or marketing graduate; it does not dissolve the 60-ECTS quota that follows it. He fails on credit content, not on the absence of a music degree.
programs.auditionSpec: None — CONFIRMED, and worth stating plainly: there is no entrance examination and no interview. Selection is made on submitted documents alone. It is also explicitly confirmed that playing an instrument is NOT a requirement for this programme. The barrier is entirely the academic credit profile.
programs.portfolioSpec: None. Required documents are proof of the relevant bachelor or first degree, a transcript of records with grades (translated where necessary), a CV, and German language proof at TestDaF 4. Optional but recommended: evidence of vocational training, internships, work experience and intercultural experience, plus a prior-study form which the institute specifically recommends for applicants whose background differs from communication, media or music studies — that form would be his only avenue for arguing the 60-ECTS point.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: CORRECTED — the honest answer is EFFECTIVELY NO, for him. No music degree is required and no instrument is needed, which sounds welcoming, but the 60-ECTS subject quota in music/communication/media/social science does the excluding instead. A software engineering graduate does not clear it. He could submit the prior-study form and argue the case into a 17-place cohort, but he would be asking for a discretionary exception on the single criterion the programme uses to filter.
programs.equipmentRequired: None.
programs.facilities: IJK research facilities at Expo Plaza; HMTMH media and music infrastructure in Hannover.
programs.intakes: Winter semester and summer semester — CONFIRMED.
programs.applicationOpens: CORRECTED — the online application window for the winter semester runs from approximately 20 May to 15 June. Applications are submitted through the institute's online platform.
programs.deadline: CORRECTED from 'NOT published'. It is published: 15 JUNE for the winter semester and 15 JANUARY for the summer semester. For a September 2027 start his deadline would be 15 JUNE 2027, well outside the October 2026-February 2027 window he has been planning around.
programs.tuitionEU: EUR 0 — Lower Saxony abolished tuition fees. Semester contribution only.
programs.tuitionNonEU: EUR 0 — CONFIRMED, no separate non-EU rate. Lower Saxony charges no non-EU tuition at state institutions, so as a Tunisian national he would pay only the semester contribution.
programs.otherFees: CORRECTED from UNVERIFIED — the semester contribution at HMTMH is approximately EUR 427 per semester for students at the Expo Plaza site, which is where the IJK is located (the Neues Haus site pays about EUR 395). It comprises the Studentenwerk contribution of EUR 130 for Expo Plaza, the AStA contribution of EUR 13.20 including theatre flat rate and bicycle workshops, and the semester transport ticket, which accounts for most of the balance. Late re-registration costs an extra EUR 50; the re-registration window for the winter semester closes on 30 June each year.
programs.totalCostEstimate: Tuition EUR 0 + roughly EUR 427 per semester (about EUR 1,708 across four semesters, transport included) + Hannover living costs + blocked account of roughly EUR 12,000 per year.
programs.scholarships: None published by the institution; DAAD would be the separate route.
programs.englishTest: None — German-taught. His unwritten IELTS/TOEFL is irrelevant here; TestDaF 4 is what he would need.
programs.visaEligible: YES — full-time state university master, squarely within the section 16b(1) AufenthG entitlement. The visa is not the problem with this one; admission is.
programs.recommendation: AVOID for his stated goal, rating C — and the verification pass turned the previous record's 'ambiguous' entry assessment into a clear no. The programme is real, genuinely prestigious, costs EUR 0 in tuition and about EUR 427 a semester, and carries an unproblematic student visa. Corrections made on this pass: it is 120 ECTS over four semesters, not an unknown quantity; the deadlines are published at 15 June for winter and 15 January for summer, so a September 2027 entry means 15 June 2027; German is required at TestDaF TDN 4 for anyone without a German school-leaving qualification, which includes him; there is no entrance exam, no interview and no instrument requirement, selection being on documents alone; and the semester contribution is about EUR 427 at the IJK's Expo Plaza site. The decisive correction is the entry rule: admission requires a prior degree containing at least 60 ECTS in music, communication, media or social science subjects. That quota, not the absence of a music degree, is what excludes him — a software engineering curriculum does not contain half a year of such credit, and he would be seeking a discretionary exception on the very criterion used to rank a 17-place cohort. Even setting that aside, the fit is wrong in kind: this degree researches the music industry and teaches strategic management of it, in German, with no studio craft anywhere in the seven modules. Nothing in it moves him toward producing records or DJing. Reconsider only if his ambition genuinely shifts from making music to researching or managing the business of it, in which case it becomes a strong option worth learning German for.
