programs.program: Music Technology (Master of Arts) - English-language stream
programs.institution: LEPL Vano Sarajishvili Tbilisi State Conservatoire (TSC)
programs.publicPrivate: PUBLIC. Definitive: the Conservatoire's own official 2026-2027 admission-quota documents head themselves 'LEPL - Vano Sarajishvili Tbilisi State Conservatoire'. LEPL = Legal Entity of Public Law, the Georgian legal form for a state institution. Further proof: one of the two official quota tables is headed 'Quotas (Funded by the State)' and allocates 5 state-funded places to the English-language Music Technology MA - only a state institution distributes state grant places.
programs.language: ACTUAL TEACHING LANGUAGE: English. TSC runs Music Technology as a parallel pair of MA programmes - one taught in English, one taught in Georgian. The English stream was internationally accredited by MusiQuE on 31 March 2025. The entrance interview for Music Technology is explicitly 'an English-language interview on project-related issues'. He would take the English stream; he does not need Georgian.
programs.languageRequirement: For the English-language programmes: 'an internationally recognized certificate confirming English language proficiency at a minimum of B2 level (CEFR), including IELTS, Cambridge English PET, Pitman ESOL International, TOEIC, or TOEFL, OR any other official document issued by an accredited educational institution confirming at least B2-level proficiency in English.' That last clause matters for him: it is a softer route than a hard IELTS band. His SMU MedTech degree transcript or a letter from SMU confirming English-medium instruction at B2 may satisfy it - worth asking enrollment@tsc.edu.ge before he pays for IELTS. No Georgian is required for the English stream. (Georgian-language programmes separately demand a B1 Georgian interview - not his route.)
programs.qualification: Master of Arts. A real, state-recognised second-cycle degree. Georgia is a full member of the European Higher Education Area and a Lisbon Recognition Convention party, so this is a genuine Bologna second-cycle award, not a private certificate. Award title on the official page: Master's degree programme, Composition and Musicology Faculty.
programs.accreditationStatus: Two layers, both real. (1) Georgian state: the institution is an LEPL conservatoire under the national quality system, and it distributes state-funded master's places. (2) International: 'By the decision of the MusiQuE (Music Quality Enhancement) International Higher Music Education Quality Enhancement Center made on March 31, 2025', the Composition and Musicology Faculty's Composition and Music Technology programmes hold full international accreditation. MusiQuE is the AEC-founded specialist agency on the EQAR-recognised track - this is the strongest accreditation signal of anything in this four-country slice.
programs.institutionType: State conservatoire (arts academy). Founded 1917. Composition and Musicology Faculty; Music Technology sits alongside Composition, not inside a performance faculty - which is why the entry route is a project + portfolio rather than an instrumental audition.
programs.focus: Music technology / electronic and computer music composition, in a classical-conservatoire setting. Not a commercial dance-music or DJ school.
programs.whatYouStudy: The official admission requirement document defines the programme's centre of gravity: the candidate is admitted on a self-authored 'Master's Artistic Project', and the two years are spent realising it. TSC's Music Technology department has been the home of electroacoustic music teaching at the Conservatoire - documented teaching content includes software tools, recording techniques, and composing and performing using technology. Detailed module list and ECTS breakdown are NOT published on the public site - UNVERIFIED; request the full curriculum (silabusi) from enrollment@tsc.edu.ge or ir.office@tsc.edu.ge.
programs.durationEcts: 2 years (4 semesters) - stated explicitly on the official MA-Admission page: 'The duration of all the above-mentioned Master's Degree programmes is 2 years (4 semesters).' TOTAL ECTS IS NOT STATED ON THE OFFICIAL PAGE - UNVERIFIED. The Georgian second-cycle norm is 120 ECTS, but I did not find TSC publishing that number on its own domain. Ask enrollment@tsc.edu.ge for the ECTS total in writing - he will need it for any later EU recognition.
programs.tuitionEU: Georgia is not in the EU, so there is no EU/non-EU split. There are two rates: Georgian citizens (published separately) and foreign citizens. The foreign-citizen rate is the one below.
programs.tuitionNonEU: 3,423 EUR per year; total 6,846 EUR for the two-year degree. This is THE RATE HE WOULD PAY as a Tunisian national. Source is TSC's own PDF, titled on the site 'Program Cost per year - MA (for foreign citizens)', at https://tsc.edu.ge/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/2.Program-Cost-per-year-MA.pdf. The PDF's own heading is 'Program Cost per Year with a 20% Fee Increase (euro)' and the line reads 'Technology MA - 3,423 euro per year (total cost: 6,846 euro)'. Note this already includes a 20% increase, so a further rise before Sept 2027 is possible - PRIOR CYCLE (2026-2027 rate) - confirm new figure.
programs.otherFees: Exam/audition participation fee: 50 EUR, or the equivalent of 50 EUR in Georgian lari, for applicants applying WITHOUT the Unified Master's Exam (his category as a foreign applicant). Applicants applying WITH the Unified Master's Exam pay 50 GEL instead. Bank transfer details published at https://tsc.edu.ge/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/Transfer-Details.pdf. Documents in a foreign language must be translated into Georgian and notarised - notary and translation costs UNVERIFIED. Accommodation, health insurance and residence-permit fees not published on the admission pages - UNVERIFIED.
programs.totalCostEstimate: Verified hard costs: 6,846 EUR tuition + 50 EUR exam fee = 6,896 EUR over two years. Living costs in Tbilisi, residence permit fee, insurance and notarised translations are NOT published by TSC - UNVERIFIED. Tbilisi is cheap by European standards, but do not let him budget on a number nobody has published; ask ir.office@tsc.edu.ge for their cost-of-living guidance, and note that TSC does publish a 'Guide for International Students' PDF whose text layer I could not read.
programs.entryRequirements: THIS IS THE PROBLEM FOR HIM. The official MA-Admission page states: 'The prerequisite for admission to Master's degree programmes is a Bachelor's academic degree, higher academic musical education.' Read literally, that demands a music bachelor - which he does not have. However, the Music Technology entrance is assessed purely on artistic project + portfolio + English interview, with no instrumental or theory exam, which is the kind of programme that in practice admits technologists. HE MUST WRITE TO enrollment@tsc.edu.ge AND ASK, IN WRITING, WHETHER A BSc IN SOFTWARE ENGINEERING SATISFIES THE ENTRY REQUIREMENT FOR MUSIC TECHNOLOGY. Do this in autumn 2026, before investing in the portfolio. Additional documents required from a foreign applicant not taking the Unified Master's Exam: bachelor's diploma from an HEI recognised in his country (electronic version of the original), transcript of grades and credits, passport copy, one 3x4 digital photograph, payment receipt.
programs.auditionSpec: There is NO instrumental audition. The official 'Master's Degree Educational Programme of Music Technology - Requirements for the Admission/Exam/Audition Round' document specifies: assessment on a 100-point system, passing range 71-100. The round consists of (A) a written description of the applicant's artistic project (electronic file/folder) plus submission of a portfolio of past artistic activities (electronic file/folder), and (B) an English-language interview on project-related issues, in which the applicant presents the project and answers questions. Crucially, that document states the General Master's Exam applies to the GEORGIAN-language programme; the English-language programme requires only the specialty exam/audition round. Document: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1dfV5yDgkkFwWVWQTrHFew3a78tD8fjCi/view
programs.portfolioSpec: Two separate deliverables, both electronic. (1) A written description of the Master's Artistic Project - i.e. what he proposes to make over the two years. (2) A portfolio of completed creative activities. Both are submitted as an electronic file or folder to enrollment@tsc.edu.ge with the registration pack. Changes to the Artistic Project and Portfolio are permitted up to 25 June of the admission year. No format, length, duration or track-count specification is published - UNVERIFIED; ask the Music Technology department for a spec before he builds it. For him the Artistic Project is the lever: it is a proposal, not a track record, and a software engineer can write a strong one.
programs.equipmentRequired: Not specified on any official page - UNVERIFIED. Submission is electronic, so no equipment is needed to apply beyond a DAW and a computer.
programs.facilities: Officially documented: a Music Technology Department (within the Composition and Musicology Faculty), a Grand Hall and a Recital Hall, a library and a museum. TSC's Music Technology department has hosted electroacoustic-music teaching including recording techniques. NO official inventory of studios, control rooms, consoles or immersive/spatial rigs is published - UNVERIFIED. Ask ir.office@tsc.edu.ge for a studio list with photographs before committing; this is the single biggest unknown about the programme.
programs.intakes: One intake per year, September (start of the Georgian academic year).
programs.applicationOpens: Registration for exam/audition rounds opened 21 May 2026 for the 2026-2027 year. PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. For his September 2027 target he should expect registration to open around late May 2027, which is LATER than most European calls - it does not clash with an Oct 2026 - Feb 2027 European application round, so TSC can be run in parallel as a late fallback.
programs.deadline: Registration closed 3 June 2026; exams/audition rounds 6-18 July 2026; portfolio and project changes accepted until 25 June 2026; full schedule published by 25 June. ALL PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new dates. Expect the equivalent 2027 window to be roughly late May to early June 2027 for registration and early-to-mid July 2027 for the interview.
programs.englishTest: B2 CEFR minimum. IELTS, Cambridge English PET, Pitman ESOL International, TOEIC or TOEFL are named as acceptable, BUT the rule also accepts 'any other official document issued by an accredited educational institution confirming at least B2-level proficiency in English'. He has not taken IELTS - this alternative clause may spare him the test entirely. Confirm in writing with enrollment@tsc.edu.ge.
programs.scholarships: NONE HE CAN WIN. TSC's own fee PDF carries the explicit sentence: '*Scholarships and institutional funding are not available for international students.' There are 5 state-funded places in the English-language Music Technology MA, but those sit in the quota table for applicants applying WITH the Georgian Unified Master's Exam - the domestic route. The separate quota table for applicants WITHOUT the Unified Master's Exam (his route) carries no funding column and simply caps foreign admission at 5% of maximum enrollment capacity. External options he could pursue independently are not offered by TSC and are UNVERIFIED here.
programs.visaEligible: He would need a Georgian immigration (study) visa and then a study residence permit. WHETHER A TUNISIAN NATIONAL NEEDS A VISA BEFORE ARRIVAL IN GEORGIA IS UNVERIFIED - TSC publishes nothing on this and I did not open the Georgian MFA register. Check the visa navigator at the Georgian Ministry of Foreign Affairs (mfa.gov.ge) and the Public Service Development Agency (sda.gov.ge) for the study residence permit. IMPORTANT AND OFTEN MISSED: Georgia is NOT in the EU or Schengen. Studying here gives him no EU residence rights, no Schengen mobility, and no route to an EU post-study work permit. The degree itself is EHEA/Bologna and recognisable in the EU via ENIC-NARIC, but he would be starting his EU access from zero after graduating.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: UNCERTAIN AND DECISIVE - MUST BE ASKED. The stated prerequisite is 'a Bachelor's academic degree, higher academic musical education', which on its face excludes him. Against that: the Music Technology entrance has no musical audition at all, only a project, a portfolio and an English interview - a structure designed for people who make things with computers. This is the single question that determines whether Georgia is on his list. Email enrollment@tsc.edu.ge and ir.office@tsc.edu.ge in October 2026.
programs.recommendation: THE BEST FIND IN THIS ENTIRE FOUR-COUNTRY SLICE, and the only one taught in English. Fit with him is genuinely good: no instrumental audition, no music-theory exam, entry on a written artistic project plus portfolio, an English-language interview, a B2 English rule with a non-test escape clause, MusiQuE international accreditation, and 3,423 EUR/year - cheap enough that self-paying is realistic. Two hard warnings. FIRST: zero funding. TSC states in writing that international students get no scholarships or institutional funding, so this is a pure self-pay decision of about 6,900 EUR tuition plus living. SECOND: the entry rule says 'higher academic musical education' and he has a software engineering BSc - resolve this by email before spending a year building a portfolio for it. Two smaller cautions: the studio inventory is not published, which for a technology programme is a real gap he should close with photographs before accepting; and Georgia is outside the EU and Schengen, so this degree advances his craft and his credential but not his European residence position. Practical sequencing: because TSC registration opens in late May, it does not compete with the Oct 2026 - Feb 2027 European deadlines. He can apply to funded European programmes first and hold Tbilisi as a paid fallback decided in summer 2027. Action list: (1) Oct 2026 - email enrollment@tsc.edu.ge and ir.office@tsc.edu.ge with three questions: does a non-music BSc qualify for Music Technology; what exactly does the portfolio need to contain; what studios and equipment does the Music Technology department have. (2) Ask whether a letter from SMU MedTech confirming English-medium study satisfies the B2 rule. (3) Spend the year building the portfolio and, more importantly, drafting the Master's Artistic Project - that document, not his back catalogue, is what he is admitted on.

programs.program: Звукорежисура (Sound Engineering) - Master's degree, specialty B5 Musical Art
programs.institution: Національна академія керівних кадрів культури і мистецтв / National Academy of Culture and Arts Management (NAKKKiM)
programs.publicPrivate: PUBLIC. Definitive: the rector's order approving 2026-2027 tuition for foreign citizens is headed 'МІНІСТЕРСТВО КУЛЬТУРИ УКРАЇНИ / НАЦІОНАЛЬНА АКАДЕМІЯ КЕРІВНИХ КАДРІВ КУЛЬТУРИ І МИСТЕЦТВ' - i.e. the Academy is a national institution subordinate to the Ministry of Culture of Ukraine, with a rector (Valerii Marchenko) and an academic council (вчена рада) whose 27 April 2026 decision, protocol No 9, sets the fees. State-run, not private.
programs.language: ACTUAL TEACHING LANGUAGE: the official 2026 programme document (OPP) states 'Мова(и) викладання: Українська, англійська' - Ukrainian and English. TREAT THE ENGLISH CLAIM WITH CAUTION. This is a standard formula in Ukrainian OPP documents and usually means individual modules or supervision can be delivered in English, not that a foreigner can complete the whole degree without Ukrainian. Ukrainian admission rules for foreigners generally require an entrance exam in the language of instruction. He must get written confirmation of how much of this 90-ECTS programme is actually deliverable in English before treating it as an English-taught option.
programs.languageRequirement: UNVERIFIED for this specific institution - NAKKKiM's foreign-applicant language rule is not published in readable form on the pages I opened. The Ukrainian norm is either proof of Ukrainian at the required level or completion of a preparatory language faculty (підготовче відділення), typically one year. Ask the admissions office directly. Do not assume the 'англійська' line in the OPP removes a Ukrainian requirement.
programs.qualification: Магістр музичного мистецтва (Master of Musical Art). A real second-cycle degree: the OPP states the level as 'Другий (магістерський)', 'НКР України - 7 рівень, FQ-EHEA - другий цикл, EQF-LLL - 7 рівень', diploma type 'диплом магістра, одиничний, 90 кредитів ЄКТС'. Ukraine is an EHEA member and a Lisbon Recognition Convention party, so this is EU-recognisable in principle via ENIC-NARIC.
programs.accreditationStatus: REAL BUT FLAGGED - READ THIS CAREFULLY. The OPP states verbatim: the programme (EDEBO identifier 35623) 'акредитована умовно (відкладена акредитація)' - CONDITIONALLY ACCREDITED, DEFERRED ACCREDITATION - by decision of the National Agency for Higher Education Quality Assurance (NAZYAVO) of 13 January 2026, protocol No 1 (92), accreditation case No 1769/АС-25. Conditional accreditation in the Ukrainian system means the Agency found shortcomings and gave the programme a period to fix them, with re-assessment to follow. It is a valid accreditation and the degree is a state degree, but this is exactly the kind of status that can complicate later recognition abroad. He should check the current status on NAZYAVO's register before applying, and ask what the identified shortcomings were.
programs.institutionType: National academy under the Ministry of Culture; postgraduate/arts-management profile with a Performative Arts institute. Programme sits in the Кафедра музичного мистецтва (Department of Musical Art) within the Навчально-науковий інститут перформативних мистецтв.
programs.focus: Music recording and sound engineering, with an explicit AI-for-audio strand. This is the closest thing in the four countries to a music-production master's.
programs.whatYouStudy: From the official 2026 OPP, quoted in substance: theoretical content covers musicology, theory and history of music; the professional-technological component covers computer musicology, sound engineering, and digital, computer and multimedia technologies in music/audio production; exact sciences cover foundations of electrical engineering, musical acoustics and modern sound-technical systems; the innovation strand covers 'технології штучного інтелекту для аналізу, синтезу та обробки аудіо контенту' - AI technologies for the analysis, synthesis and processing of audio content. Students carry out 'звукозапис, редагування, мікшування та мастеринг музичного матеріалу' - recording, editing, mixing and mastering - through studio, concert and pedagogical practice, and write a master's thesis. Named modules visible in the department's document library include Mastering, Sound Engineering in MIDI, Sound-technical Apparatus, Multimedia Technologies, Music-Information Technologies, Creative Mixing Techniques, Digital Sound Recording, Electronic Music, Audiovisual Producing, Fundamentals of Sound Design, and Postproduction. Graduate occupational codes listed: 2455.2 Sound Engineer, 3131 Sound Recording Operator, 1229 Chief Sound Engineer, 1229 Studio Head.
programs.durationEcts: 90 ECTS, 1 year 4 months. Both очна (денна) full-time and заочна (distance/part-time) forms are offered, both 1 year 4 months. Stated verbatim in the official OPP.
programs.tuitionEU: Not applicable - Ukraine has no EU/non-EU fee split. There is a domestic rate and a separate foreign-citizen rate, published as two different PDFs.
programs.tuitionNonEU: UNVERIFIED - AND THIS IS A REAL GAP, NOT AN OVERSIGHT. NAKKKiM does publish the figure: the document is titled 'Вартість навчання для іноземних громадян в НАКККіМ у 2026-2027 н.р.' at https://nakkkim.edu.ua/images/Instytuty/VR/1/46/1/Vartist%20navcanna%20dla%20inozemnih%20gromadan2.pdf and is enacted by a rector's order effective 29 April 2026 following academic council protocol No 9 of 27 April 2026. I downloaded it, but pages 2-3 - the actual fee table - are a scanned image with a corrupted text layer and no figure could be read. I will not guess. ASK: the admissions office via the tuition page https://nakkkim.edu.ua/abituriyentam/vartist-navchannia-u-nakkkim-u-2024-2025-navchalnomu-rotsi, or the Department of Musical Art directly, quoting the OPP name 'Звукорежисура', level 'другий (магістерський)', specialty B5.
programs.otherFees: UNVERIFIED. Ukrainian institutions typically charge separately for the invitation letter, document legalisation/recognition (нострифікація), and preparatory language study if required. Ask the admissions office for an itemised list.
programs.totalCostEstimate: CANNOT BE ESTIMATED - the foreign tuition figure is unreadable in the published PDF and no living-cost guidance is published. Any number here would be fabricated.
programs.entryRequirements: UNUSUALLY OPEN, AND THIS IS THE MOST INTERESTING THING ABOUT THIS PROGRAMME FOR HIM. The official OPP states the entry requirement as 'Вимоги до освіти осіб, які можуть розпочати навчання за ОП: Ступінь бакалавра, спеціаліста, магістра' - a bachelor's, specialist's or master's degree. NO FIELD OF STUDY IS SPECIFIED. Unlike Tbilisi, this does not demand 'higher academic musical education'. On the published rule, a BSc in Software Engineering qualifies. He should still confirm in writing, and confirm what the professional entrance examination (фахове випробування) consists of - that is where a music-theory hurdle would hide if one exists.
programs.auditionSpec: UNVERIFIED. NAKKKiM publishes entrance-examination schedules at https://nakkkim.edu.ua/abituriyentam/rozklad-fakhovykh-ta-vstupnykh-vyprobuvan but the content of the professional examination for the master's Звукорежисура programme was not readable on the pages I opened. Ukrainian master's admission normally combines a professional entrance test with a foreign-language test. Request the 'програма фахового вступного випробування' for OPP Звукорежисура, магістр, from the admissions office.
programs.portfolioSpec: UNVERIFIED - no portfolio specification is published for the master's entry. Ask whether a portfolio substitutes for or supplements the professional examination.
programs.equipmentRequired: Not specified - UNVERIFIED.
programs.facilities: Officially documented: 'Навчальна студія звукозапису' - an Educational Sound Recording Studio operated by the department, serving both the Sound Engineering and Music Production programmes. The OPP lists instruments and equipment as 'музичний інструментарій, джерельна база, звукотехнічне обладнання, програмне забезпечення, мультимедійні засоби'. Practice placements are backed by signed cooperation agreements with the National Philharmonic of Ukraine, the National Opera and Ballet Theatre of Ukraine, the Ivan Franko Theatre, Budynok Muzyky, the Kyiv Municipal Academy of Music and the School of Jazz and Variety Art - a genuinely strong placement network. No detailed studio inventory (consoles, monitoring, immersive rigs) is published - UNVERIFIED.
programs.intakes: September (Ukrainian academic year). Ukrainian admission rules allow foreign citizens a longer, separate admission window than domestic applicants, typically running into the autumn.
programs.applicationOpens: UNVERIFIED for foreign applicants at NAKKKiM specifically. Domestic 2026 applications ran to 1 August 2026 - PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. Ukrainian foreign-applicant windows are usually July to October/November of the intake year.
programs.deadline: UNVERIFIED - PRIOR CYCLE domestic reference only (1 August 2026). Confirm the foreign-applicant deadline for the 2027-2028 year with the admissions office.
programs.englishTest: UNVERIFIED. Given that the teaching language is primarily Ukrainian, the relevant test is more likely a Ukrainian-language requirement than an English one. Ask explicitly.
programs.scholarships: UNVERIFIED, and realistically unlikely. Ukrainian state-funded (державне замовлення) places at arts institutions are generally reserved for Ukrainian citizens and specific protected categories; other foreign nationals are admitted on a paying basis within quotas. There is no published international scholarship scheme at NAKKKiM that I could open.
programs.visaEligible: Legally yes - Ukraine issues student visas (type D) and temporary residence permits to enrolled foreign nationals, and the state maintains an electronic invitation system for foreign students. BUT SEE THE RECOMMENDATION FIELD: legal eligibility is not the operative question for Ukraine right now.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: YES ON THE PUBLISHED RULE - the OPP requires only 'a bachelor's, specialist's or master's degree' with no subject named. This is the most open entry rule of any programme found in these four countries. Confirm the content of the professional entrance examination before relying on it.
programs.recommendation: ACADEMICALLY THE BEST-MATCHED PROGRAMME IN THIS SLICE, AND PRACTICALLY THE ONE I WOULD ADVISE HIM NOT TO PURSUE. Take the match seriously first: 90 ECTS in 1 year 4 months, entry open to any bachelor's degree, a curriculum that runs from electrical engineering and musical acoustics through MIDI, mixing, mastering, sound design and postproduction to AI audio synthesis, a working recording studio, and placements at the National Philharmonic and the National Opera. For a software engineer who wants to become a producer, the syllabus is close to ideal. Now the reasons to stop. FIRST AND DECISIVE: Ukraine is at war. Kyiv is under regular missile and drone attack, martial law is in force, and no responsible adviser tells a 22-year-old to move there for a discretionary arts master's starting September 2027. Whatever the situation is by then, he cannot plan around it from 2026, and an application cycle he must commit to in late 2026 offers no way to hedge. SECOND: the language. The OPP's 'Ukrainian, English' formula almost certainly does not mean a foreigner can complete the degree in English; assume he would need Ukrainian, probably via a year of preparatory study, and that is two years of his life spent on a language that serves no part of his stated career. THIRD: the programme is only CONDITIONALLY accredited (deferred accreditation, NAZYAVO decision of 13 January 2026) - a status that adds friction to any later recognition in the EU, on top of the friction a Ukrainian wartime degree would already carry. FOURTH: nobody will tell him the price - the official foreign-citizen tuition PDF exists but is an unreadable scan. VERDICT: record it, do not apply to it. If he wants a Ukrainian sound-engineering education, the sane version is to keep this on file and revisit only if the war ends and the programme's accreditation is upgraded to full. His Sept 2027 effort belongs in the EU and in Tbilisi.

programs.recommendation: THE MOST INTERESTING CURRICULUM OF THE THREE - AND THE LEAST ACCESSIBLE TO HIM. On content it is genuinely distinctive: spatial sound systems for theatre, film and television, electronic music technologies, digital signal processing and musical acoustics as named core master's subjects, four elective blocks including sound design, an in-house teaching theatre, and DSP that would build directly on his software-engineering degree. It is the only programme in this whole four-country sweep that puts immersive/spatial audio in the master's core. But three things close it. FIRST, THE WAR: Kyiv, September 2027, discretionary arts master's - the same objection as NAKKKiM, and it is decisive. SECOND, THE LANGUAGE: the university's own rules require an entrance examination in Ukrainian as the language of instruction, with no English route. He would need a preparatory year in Ukrainian before he could even sit the entrance exam - roughly two years diverted into a language with no bearing on a career as an international DJ and producer. THIRD, HE IS THE WRONG APPLICANT: entry runs through an undisclosed creative competition in a screen-sound discipline, with no published open-entry rule, no portfolio spec, and no published price. VERDICT: do not apply. Record it as the strongest evidence that Ukraine has real depth in this field and note it for the future - if he ever wants postgraduate film-sound or immersive-audio training and the country is at peace, this department is worth a second look. For September 2027 it is not a candidate.

programs.deadline: PRIOR CYCLE (2026, CONFIRMED on the official page): dossier deadline Friday 23 January 2026, 12:00 UTC+1; dossier results 5 March 2026; written exam 28 March 2026 (remote); oral-exam eligibility results 5 May 2026; orals 26–29 May 2026; final admissions 3 June 2026; term starts 7 September 2026. programs.tuitionEU: CORRECTED — 254 € per year (not 'unverified'). Source: Enjmin's own official 'Tarifs pour l'année 2025-2026' fee sheet, Master jeux et médias interactifs numériques, formation initiale, EU/EEA/Swiss/Monaco/Andorra students.
programs.tuitionNonEU: CORRECTED — 3 941 € per year, NOT 3 879 €. THIS IS THE RATE HE WOULD PAY. Quoted verbatim from Enjmin's own official tariff sheet (Tarifs 2025-2026): 'Vous êtes un étudiant ou une étudiante extra-communautaire … Le montant des frais d'inscription que vous avez à payer est de 3 941 €.' ALSO CORRECTED: the previous entry said 'no institutional exemption'. That overstates it — the annex records that three EPN (ESGT, INSEAC, EPN5) volunteered exemptions and ENJMIN was not among them, BUT the same document then asks the governing board to approve a scheme covering up to 10% of FI enrolments per programme, on the basis of national fees for students under a partnership convention and 50% of the differentiated fee for candidature libre non-EU students, with 'chaque EPN concernée' running its own academic/social selection. programs.totalCostEstimate: 3 941 € + 105 € CVEC = 4 046 €/year at full rate, or roughly 2 075 €/year if he wins the 50% EPN exemption. Plus ENIC-NARIC comparability fee, plus Angoulême living costs (a genuinely cheap French town — materially cheaper than Lyon, Paris or Strasbourg).

programs.visaEligible: YES — CONFIRMED. Diplôme national de master at a public establishment. programs.recommendation: Still the single best thematic fit in this batch: game audio sits exactly on the seam between a software-engineering BSc and a career in sound, and the official page genuinely accepts any bac+3 background with no music degree. It is a real accredited state master (RNCP 38202) that fully supports a student residence permit, and the language gate is French B2 — a certificate he can realistically get, unlike IELTS which is not even asked for here. CONDITIONAL rather than WORTH IT for one reason only: the gate is a creative dossier plus written and oral exams at a very small, very competitive national school, and he has no portfolio today. His entire 2026 has to go into producing game-audio work aimed at the cahier des charges that drops in mid-December. Second caution: this trains game sound designers, not DJs or record producers — the club/production ambition has to run alongside it. Practical sequencing: file the ENIC-NARIC attestation de comparabilité by September 2026 (four-month turnaround), sit a DELF/TCF B2 by November 2026, then answer the December brief.

programs.facilities: CONFIRMED — backed by the CeLyA (Centre Lyonnais d'Acoustique) cluster spanning eight Lyon research laboratories, with laboratory-based projects and research internships.
programs.intakes: September (annual).

For a September 2027 entry he should treat autumn 2026 as the real start because Études en France binds first.
programs.deadline: CORRECTED/CLARIFIED — the previous entry reported an unconfirmed 30/04/2026 deadline with a 29/05/2026 committee reply. Centrale Lyon's official 'Applying for a master's degree' page confirms 30 April 2026 as the 2026-cycle date for committee responses, and flags that the third/complementary session is open to EUROPEAN applicants only — so a Tunisian national must make the earlier session. PRIOR CYCLE — confirm the 2027 dates. IMPORTANT NEW FINDING: that same official page states the International Master in Acoustics M1 applies through MonMaster (monmaster.gouv.fr), NOT the school's own candidature portal, while separately stating that non-EU international students must apply via Études en France AND submit on candidature.ec-lyon.fr. programs.tuitionEU: CORRECTED — 255 € + CVEC for non-scholarship students from the enlarged EU, academic year 2026-2027; free for French government scholarship holders. Source: Centrale Lyon's official master fees page (the previous entry left this unverified).
programs.tuitionNonEU: CORRECTED — 3 950 € + CVEC for 2026-2027, NOT 3 770 €. THIS IS THE RATE HE WOULD PAY. Source: Centrale Lyon's official 'Frais d'inscription – Masters' page for 2026-2027. The 3 770 € figure on the programme's own application page (master-acoustics.ec-lyon.fr) is stale and reflects the older national reference amount. The school's fees page notes some students qualify for waived differentiated fees by profile and points to Campus France to check eligibility — no automatic exemption for a Tunisian self-funded applicant.
programs.otherFees: CVEC payable in addition — Centrale Lyon's page cites 103 € (2024-2025 rate); the current national CVEC for 2026-2027 is 105 €, as published by UPHF. Budget 105 €.
programs.totalCostEstimate: ~4 055 €/year (3 950 € + 105 € CVEC) plus Lyon living costs. Lyon is France's second most expensive student city — this is the highest total cost of living in the batch alongside Strasbourg. No official living-cost estimate published.
programs.scholarships: Nothing programme-specific published. Two levers: the differentiated-fee waiver by profile mentioned on the Centrale Lyon fees page (check eligibility via Campus France), and the Eiffel scholarship — note Eiffel candidates are nominated BY the institution, so he would need Centrale Lyon to put him forward, meaning contact by autumn 2026 at the latest.
programs.visaEligible: YES — public establishments, French state-accredited national master; the official pages instruct non-EU applicants to run Études en France in parallel for visa purposes.
programs.recommendation: Two figures in the previous entry were wrong and both matter: the non-EU fee is 3 950 €, not 3 770 € (Centrale Lyon's own 2026-2027 fees page supersedes the stale number on the programme site), and the EU rate is 255 €. A new procedural problem also surfaced: Centrale Lyon's official application page says the International Master in Acoustics M1 goes through MonMaster, while also saying non-EU students must use Études en France plus candidature.ec-lyon.fr — the two are inconsistent for a Tunisian applicant, and the complementary late session is restricted to European applicants, so he cannot rely on a spring catch-up. On the merits it remains highly admissible: no portfolio, no audition, no music degree, no French-language gate, and an entry rule written for science graduates, with 'sound perception' and signal processing as a legitimate on-ramp to audio DSP and immersive audio. CONDITIONAL on three things. (1) He must book IELTS or TOEFL — unless he can evidence three years of instruction in English at SMU MedTech, which is the one waiver on the official page that could plausibly apply to him and is worth checking immediately. (2) His curriculum is software, not mechanics or physics; email the programme office with his transcript in autumn 2026 before spending money on the application. (3) It is acoustics engineering, not music production — the DJ/producer ambition runs in parallel, not through this degree. Cost is the full non-EU rate in France's second most expensive student city, so this is also the most expensive of the three viable options.

programs.program: Master mention Musicologie — parcours Création-Production en musiques actuelles (CPMA)
programs.institution: Université de Strasbourg, Faculté des arts, Département de musique
programs.institutionType: Public university (EPSCP)
programs.publicPrivate: PUBLIC — CONFIRMED. State university; its own tuition page publishes the ministerially-set national rate (255 €), the differentiated non-EU rate, and an institutional exemption committee — all public-sector mechanisms.
programs.qualification: Diplôme national de master, mention Musicologie. Real second-cycle state degree supporting a student residence permit. RNCP number not shown on the official pages.
programs.accreditationStatus: State-accredited diplôme national de master at a public university.
programs.language: CONFIRMED — French. An English course sits inside the curriculum but instruction is French.
programs.languageRequirement: CONFIRMED — French C1, listed as a mandatory prerequisite on the official catalogue page ('bonne maîtrise de l'expression et de la rédaction en français', with strong written and oral French described as essential to completing the programme). His French fluency is a genuine advantage here, but he should expect to evidence C1 with a DELF/DALF C1 or a TCF result for the Études en France file.
programs.englishTest: None required.
programs.durationEcts: CONFIRMED — 2 years, 120 ECTS, 724 total teaching hours, in-person only (no distance option). Includes a 120-hour internship. The degree concludes with a dissertation articulated with a public production/recital.
programs.focus: Music production and studio technology in the service of creation, in popular and contemporary music (musiques actuelles). On content, the closest programme in this batch to his stated goal.
programs.whatYouStudy: Critical listening and technical ear training; composition and orchestration with digital audio workstations; sound recording, mixing and mastering; analogue synthesis; composition for audiovisual and video games; sound design and artistic direction; professional practice in music production, publishing and copyright. Project-based pedagogy with substantial autonomous work. Named outcomes: sound engineer, music producer, composer for audiovisual/games, sound designer, artistic director.
programs.entryRequirements: CONFIRMED and unchanged — the official page states eligibility as 'Tout étudiant titulaire d'une licence de musique (ou d'un diplôme étranger équivalent)', i.e. a MUSIC bachelor's degree. Mandatory prerequisites listed: advanced DAW competence; solid practical musicianship; composition and/or production competence; knowledge of sound engineering, acoustics or popular-music instrumentation; familiarity with the contemporary music industry; C1 French; academic research and writing competence; and music history and aesthetics with a popular-music focus.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: NO — CONFIRMED against the official page. The stated entry rule is a music licence or an equivalent foreign degree, and the published prerequisites assume years of formal musical training. A BSc Software Engineering with no conservatoire background and no portfolio does not meet the stated conditions. He could only argue equivalence, and would still have to demonstrate the musicianship prerequisites separately.
programs.portfolioSpec: Not explicitly published as a formal requirement, but given the prerequisites, production work will be assessed in practice. Ask the programme director, Sébastien Lebray (lebray@unistra.fr).
programs.auditionSpec: Not published. The degree concludes with a public production/recital, which indicates a performing or producing standard is expected at entry. Confirm with the department.
programs.equipmentRequired: Not published.
programs.facilities: Studio-based teaching (recording, mixing, mastering, analogue synthesis) at the Faculté des arts, Campus Esplanade, Strasbourg. Studio inventory not published.
programs.intakes: September (annual).
programs.applicationOpens: Not dated on the official pages. Route: French and EU applicants go through Mon Master; non-European candidates resident in an Études en France country apply through Campus France instead. Tunisia is an Études en France country, so HIS route is Campus France Tunisie / Études en France, opening in the autumn.
programs.deadline: Not published on the official pages. Contact the Faculté des arts and Campus France Tunisie for the Études en France campaign closing date for a September 2027 intake.
programs.tuitionEU: CORRECTED/UPDATED — 255 € for master level, academic year 2026-2027 (the previous entry cited 2025-2026). Source: University of Strasbourg's official tuition-fees page. A reduced rate of 167 € applies to gap-year/additional-qualification enrolments.
programs.tuitionNonEU: CONFIRMED at 3 950 € for master level, now for academic year 2026-2027. THIS IS THE RATE HE WOULD PAY. New detail found: Strasbourg also publishes a REDUCED differentiated rate of 2 633 € for certain enrolment types. Strasbourg operates a Tuition Fee Exemption Committee (commission d'exonération) to which international students may individually apply to the University President for exemption from differentiated fees — this is a real lever but discretionary and the success rate is not published. Categories automatically exempt (PhD students, refugees, long-term French residents, reciprocal exchange programmes) do NOT cover him.
programs.otherFees: CVEC payable in addition — 105 € for 2026-2027 (national figure; Strasbourg's page links out rather than stating it).
programs.totalCostEstimate: ~4 055 €/year (3 950 € + 105 € CVEC) plus Strasbourg living costs, unless the exemption committee reduces him to the 255 € national rate.
programs.scholarships: Nothing programme-specific. The relevant levers are the Unistra Tuition Fee Exemption Committee and the national Eiffel / Campus France Tunisie routes.
programs.visaEligible: YES — public university, diplôme national de master. Note his applicant route is Études en France, not Mon Master.
programs.recommendation: Everything the previous entry said about eligibility is confirmed by the official pages, and the fee figures have been updated to the 2026-2027 year (255 € national, 3 950 € non-EU, plus a newly noted reduced differentiated rate of 2 633 € for certain enrolments). To be clear about the AVOID: this is a legitimate, accredited, visa-supporting public master's degree — the problem is not the institution, it is that HE IS NOT ELIGIBLE. The official entry rule is a licence de musique or an equivalent foreign degree, and the published prerequisites (practical musicianship, composition and production competence, popular-music history and aesthetics, advanced DAW work) describe someone with years of formal musical training. He has a software-engineering BSc, no conservatoire background and no portfolio. Applying for September 2027 would waste the application slot and the Études en France cycle. On content it is the best match in France for what he actually wants — mixing, mastering, analogue synthesis, DAW composition, music for games, and the business of production, at low fees if the exemption committee rules for him — so do not delete it, just do not build the 2027 plan around it. The only route that keeps it alive: write to Sébastien Lebray (lebray@unistra.fr) in autumn 2026 asking whether a non-music bachelor with a strong production portfolio can be considered under 'diplôme étranger équivalent', and spend 2026-27 producing finished, mixed and mastered work to make that argument. Realistically a 2028 or 2029 target, not 2027.

programs.program: Master mention Musicologie — parcours Musiques Appliquées aux Arts Visuels (MAAAV), M1 and M2
programs.institution: Université Lumière Lyon 2, UFR Lettres, sciences du langage et arts (LESLA), Campus Rachais
programs.institutionType: Public university (EPSCP)
programs.publicPrivate: PUBLIC — CONFIRMED. State university; its official pages publish the ministerially-set national rate (255 €) and the state differentiated non-EU rate (3 950 €), plus CVEC — public-sector mechanisms.
programs.qualification: CONFIRMED — Diplôme national de master, mention Musicologie, parcours MAAAV. RNCP N°39199, registered with France Compétences (stated on the official M2 page). Real second-cycle state degree supporting a student residence permit.
programs.accreditationStatus: CONFIRMED — diplôme national de master, RNCP 39199.
programs.language: French. An English-language course sits inside the curriculum (semester 3 TD), but instruction is in French.
programs.languageRequirement: No certificate level published on the official pages. Assume French B2/C1 will be demanded in the Études en France file. Ask the LESLA scolarité (lesla.m1maaav@univ-lyon2.fr).
programs.englishTest: None required.
programs.durationEcts: CONFIRMED — M1 60 ECTS + M2 60 ECTS (S3 30 ECTS, S4 30 ECTS), 2 years total. M1 includes a compulsory internship of at least 12 weeks full-time in semester 2, in film, animation, video game or multimedia production; M2 semester 4 is a compulsory internship (minimum 12 weeks full-time) plus report and defence. In-person only, Campus Rachais, Lyon.
programs.focus: Composing and producing music for the moving image — cinema (animation, live action, documentary), video games, advertising, television and multimedia.
programs.whatYouStudy: CONFIRMED from the official M2 page, semester 3 (30 ECTS): musical composition and orchestration applied to image, electronic music and synthesis, advanced mixing, English, cinematic culture and research methodology, history of film sound, and intellectual property law. Semester 4 (30 ECTS) is the compulsory internship plus report and defence. Core competences: image analysis, orchestration technique, and command of digital audio workstations.
programs.entryRequirements: CONFIRMED — M1 entry by competitive selection, 16 places ('une promotion de 16 étudiants compositeurs'), open to holders of a licence in ANY field, or via VAPP with at least 5 years of professional activity in music. Critically, the official M1 page states the target profile as 'Etre déjà compositeur au moment du recrutement' — already a composer at the time of recruitment — with command of music notation, orchestration and DAW tools. M2 entry CONFIRMED as requiring completion of M1 MAAAV ('avoir effectué un master 1 MAAAV'), so there is no lateral entry at M2.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: Formally YES, substantively NO. A licence in any discipline is accepted, which on paper admits his BSc Software Engineering. But the official page requires the applicant to already be a composer commanding music notation and orchestration. The open-discipline rule exists to admit self-taught composers, not career changers with no music.
programs.portfolioSpec: A composition portfolio is the selection instrument: three recent personal compositions in varied styles written to three short films (3–5 minutes maximum each) — three audio files (wav or mp3) synchronised to the films, plus three corresponding scores in PDF. NOTE this specification comes from the programme's dedicated site maaav.fr rather than the univ-lyon2.fr catalogue pages; confirm the exact 2027 brief with the scolarité.
programs.auditionSpec: Selection is by concours on the composition portfolio. Whether an interview follows is not stated on the official pages.
programs.equipmentRequired: CONFIRMED on the official M1 page and MORE DEMANDING than previously reported: a powerful computer (MacBook Pro, iMac or high-spec PC) with at least 1 TB SSD storage; professional DAW software (Logic Pro X, Reaper or Cubase); quality headphones; and an audio interface with microphone inputs. This is a published mandatory technical prerequisite and a real cost line of roughly 2 000–3 000 € on top of tuition.
programs.facilities: Campus Rachais, Lyon. Students work on their own DAW rigs (see equipment requirement). Studio inventory not published.
programs.intakes: September (annual), 16 places.
programs.applicationOpens: Not dated on the official pages. Route: the official M1 page states applications are made exclusively through Mon Master (monmaster.gouv.fr); the M2 page uses eCandidat and explicitly notes that Campus France procedures are required for non-EU students in designated countries. As a Tunisian national resident in Tunisia he goes through Études en France / Campus France Tunisie rather than Mon Master — confirm with the scolarité before the campaign opens.
programs.deadline: Not published. Contact lesla.m1maaav@univ-lyon2.fr and Campus France Tunisie.
programs.tuitionEU: CONFIRMED — 255 € at master level, academic year 2026-2027, from Lyon 2's official droits d'inscription page.
programs.tuitionNonEU: CONFIRMED — 3 950 € at master level for non-EU students, academic year 2026-2027, from Lyon 2's official droits d'inscription page. THIS IS THE RATE HE WOULD PAY. Also CONFIRMED: Lyon 2's own page states its transitional exemption regime 'prend fin dès la rentrée 2026/2027' and that prior automatic exemptions no longer carry over — limited exemptions remain only in 'des cas très spécifiques'. A new non-EU entrant in 2027 should assume the full 3 950 €. Fees are annual and non-refundable after 15 November.
programs.otherFees: CVEC 105 € for 2026-2027, payable in addition. Plus the mandatory home-studio rig described under equipmentRequired.
programs.totalCostEstimate: ~4 055 €/year (3 950 € + 105 € CVEC) plus Lyon living costs, plus a one-off ~2 000–3 000 € for the mandatory computer, DAW licence, interface and headphones.
programs.scholarships: Nothing programme-specific. The transitional exemption has ended for 2026/2027 onward, so the practical levers are Eiffel and Campus France Tunisie.
programs.visaEligible: YES — public university, diplôme national de master, RNCP 39199.
programs.recommendation: All the previous entry's key claims are confirmed, and two things are now firmer: M2 entry is explicitly reserved for students who completed M1 MAAAV, so there is no lateral entry, and the mandatory equipment list is more specific than reported (1 TB+ SSD, Logic Pro X / Reaper / Cubase, audio interface with mic inputs, quality headphones) — a real 2 000–3 000 € cost on top of tuition. The AVOID is about eligibility, not legitimacy: this is a properly accredited public master (RNCP 39199) that supports a residence permit. But the gate closes it for him. Sixteen places a year, decided on three original compositions scored to three short films with PDF scores, and an official page stating the candidate must ALREADY be a composer commanding music notation and orchestration. He cannot write orchestral scores and has one year, not five. The unusual open-discipline rule (a licence in any field) makes it look reachable for a software engineer, and the M2 content — electronic music, synthesis, advanced mixing, composition for image — reads beautifully against his goals, which is exactly why it needs the explicit warning. Report it so he knows it exists; do not queue it for 2027. If film and game scoring genuinely attracts him, this is a 2029-2030 target reachable only after sustained composition study. The Enjmin sound-design route and the two engineering routes are the ones that fit the profile he actually has.

programs.program: MA Sound and Music
programs.institution: Queen's University Belfast — School of Arts, English and Languages / SARC (Sonic Arts Research Centre)
programs.publicPrivate: PUBLIC — CONFIRMED. The official course page publishes the statutory NI fee-status architecture (Northern Ireland £7,700 / Republic of Ireland £7,700 / England-Scotland-Wales £10,400 / EU Other £23,000 / International £23,000) and references the Department for the Economy postgraduate tuition-fee loan of up to £10,000. Only a state-funded, publicly regulated institution carries that structure. Royal Charter university, Russell Group.
programs.institutionType: Comprehensive research university with a specialist research centre (SARC) for sound and music
programs.accreditationStatus: CONFIRMED — real second-cycle degree. MA awarded by Queen's University Belfast, a UK degree-awarding body under Royal Charter. Confirmed on page: capstone MUS7109 Portfolio Dissertation is a 60-CATS core module; full 180-CATS taught masters. Supports a UK Student visa and is recognised in Tunisia without argument.
programs.qualification: MA (Master of Arts) — genuine second-cycle taught masters, 180 CATS. CONFIRMED on page: 1 year full-time / 2 years part-time; places available 30 (Full Time), 20 (Part Time).
programs.focus: Interdisciplinary sound and music: composition, musical instrument design, musicology, performance, recording, sound art. NOT a commercial DJ/producer course. This is an arts-and-research programme, not a production programme — an important mismatch with his stated career goal.
programs.whatYouStudy: CONFIRMED. Semester 1 core: 'Collaborative and Interdisciplinary Practice' and 'Knowing Music'. Optional modules confirmed on page include MUS7106 Musical Instrument Design (bridging technology, music and biology; digital musical instrument design, human-computer interaction, science and technology studies), MUS7107 Postwar Modernism and Postmodernism, MUS7102 Critical and Creative Approaches to Song, plus Immersive Sound, Critical Studies in Improvisation, Experimental Practices in Irish Traditional Music, Source Studies, and electives from outside Music. Semester 2 core: MUS7109 Portfolio Dissertation (60 CATS), which may be submitted as performances, compositions, instrument designs, sound installations or sound-recording portfolios each supported by a critical essay, instead of a written dissertation. Teaching uses the Sonic Lab and studios with 'real world' and socially engaged projects.
programs.language: English — CONFIRMED. Wholly English-taught, Northern Ireland. No other language of instruction.
programs.languageRequirement: CONFIRMED VERBATIM: 'Evidence of an IELTS score of 6.5, with not less than 5.5 in any component, or an equivalent qualification acceptable to the University is required (taken within the last 2 years).' Additionally, non-EEA nationals must satisfy UKVI immigration requirements for English language for visa purposes. He has NOT sat IELTS. 6.5 overall with a 5.5 floor is reachable from a working-English baseline with roughly 6 months of structured preparation, and the 5.5 floor is forgiving.
programs.englishTest: IELTS Academic 6.5 overall, no component below 5.5, taken within the last 2 years. Equivalents accepted at the University's discretion. Not yet taken — must be sat by roughly spring 2027.
programs.durationEcts: 1 year full-time (2 years part-time). 180 CATS = 90 ECTS equivalent.
programs.intakes: One intake, late September.
programs.deadline: PRIOR CYCLE FIGURE — page states: 'Applicants are advised to apply as early as possible and ideally no later than 14 August 2026 for courses which commence in late September.' It also warns: 'In the event that any programme receives a high number of applications, the University reserves the right to close the application portal prior to the deadline stated on course finder.' For a SEPTEMBER 2027 start, expect an equivalent mid-August 2027 nominal date, but treat spring 2027 as the real deadline because of early closure and because the Harrison bursaries are allocated to applicants received by the earlier School-website deadline.
programs.applicationOpens: UNVERIFIED for the 2027 cycle — the page does not publish a portal opening date. Queen's normally opens the postgraduate portal in the autumn preceding entry (so roughly October 2026 for September 2027). Confirm with the School of Arts, English and Languages (Music) or pgapplications@qub.ac.uk.
programs.entryRequirements: CONFIRMED VERBATIM: 'Normally a minimum of a 2.2 Honours degree or equivalent qualification acceptable to the University in a relevant subject, including music, performing arts, art and design, media production, ethnomusicology, and creative technologies. Exceptions may be made in the case of applicants with extensive relevant professional experience who are invited to submit an RPEL statement as part of the application.' DECISIVE FOR HIM: BSc Software Engineering is NOT on that list of relevant subjects. Computer science and software engineering are absent. He would have to be routed through RPEL (Recognition of Prior Experiential Learning) — but note the page frames RPEL as being for applicants with 'extensive relevant professional experience', which he does not have and will not have by 2027. This is the hardest entry gate of the six.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: NO, not on the stated route. The enumerated relevant subjects are music, performing arts, art and design, media production, ethnomusicology and creative technologies. Software engineering / computer science are not listed. The only door is RPEL, which is explicitly framed around extensive relevant professional experience he does not have. A portfolio year alone does not manufacture professional experience.
programs.portfolioSpec: CONFIRMED VERBATIM and mandatory if entering via RPEL: 'Applicants seeking entry via RPEL are required to provide a statement which must include a sample of original work and a contextual paragraph about the work which will be assessed by the RPEL Assessor to determine if an offer of admission can be made. The statement must include a link to an online video recording of one of the following: an extract from a public performance, documentation of a sound-based installation, demonstration of a musical instrument design, or a recording of a composition (audio or video with the option of also submitting a notated score of the same piece). Recordings that exceed a maximum length of 10 minutes will not be considered, and it is the responsibility of the applicant to ensure the link to the work sample remains available online.' Note the four permitted formats are all art-music/installation formats — a DJ mix or a set of dance-music productions is an awkward fit for all four categories.
programs.auditionSpec: No formal audition. The RPEL work-sample video (maximum 10 minutes) substitutes for it.
programs.tuitionEU: £23,000 for 'EU Other' — CONFIRMED. Page footnote: 'EU Other students (excludes Republic of Ireland nationals living in GB, NI or ROI) are charged tuition fees in line with international fees.' NI and ROI £7,700; GB £10,400.
programs.tuitionNonEU: £23,000 per year — CONFIRMED as the International rate, and THIS IS THE RATE HE WOULD PAY as a Tunisian national. This is the most expensive of the six by roughly £5,000. Page states all fees relate to a single year of study and 'will be subject to an annual inflationary increase', so budget above £23,000 for 2027/28.
programs.otherFees: CONFIRMED on page: recommended texts £30–£100 per text if purchased rather than borrowed from the library; £30–£75 per year for photocopying, memory sticks and printing; possible transport, accommodation and materials costs associated with a major project or dissertation; printing and binding; additional charges for graduation ceremonies, examination resits and library fines. No compulsory equipment purchase. No tuition deposit figure published on the course page.
programs.totalCostEstimate: £23,000 tuition (rising with annual inflationary increase) plus Belfast living costs plus the UKVI maintenance requirement he must evidence for the Student visa. The exact maintenance figure is not on this page — check the gov.uk Student visa 'money you need' page for the current monthly amount outside London and multiply by 9. Belfast is materially cheaper than most of the UK and Queen's advertises affordable purpose-built student accommodation, but the tuition dominates: realistically £30,000+ all-in.
programs.fundingLevel: Partial — and only marginally so. £3,000 off £23,000 is 13 per cent.
programs.scholarships: CONFIRMED VERBATIM: 'Three Douglas C Harrison bursaries of £3,000 each are available and will be allocated to the top applicants for the MA Sound and Music to offset tuition fees. All eligible students who have applied through the QUB portal for the MA Sound and Music by the deadline stated on the School website will be automatically considered for this award. No late applications will be considered. The awards shall be made as payment towards postgraduate fees in September/October.' No separate application form — early submission is the whole mechanism. CRITICALLY, the two large funding streams on the page are CLOSED to him: the Department for the Economy tuition-fee loan of up to £10,000 is restricted to NI/EU students, and the UK postgraduate loan of up to £11,836 is restricted to UK-domiciled students. QUB's general International Scholarships page (qub.ac.uk/Study/international-students/international-scholarships) is not enumerated on the course page — UNVERIFIED. Chevening remains the only realistic route to full funding here for a Tunisian.
programs.visaEligible: Yes in principle — CONFIRMED that the page directs non-EEA applicants to UKVI English-language-for-visa requirements, and Queen's is a long-established Student-route sponsor. The MA is a full Level 7 degree, so it supports a Student visa and the Graduate Route. Confirm current sponsor licence status on the UKVI Register of Licensed Sponsors before paying anything.
programs.facilities: CONFIRMED on page: SARC houses the Sonic Lab (described by QUB as the most advanced music venue on the island of Ireland), professional-quality audio recording and broadcast production studios, fabrication facilities and a multipurpose interaction lab; plus the Music building's Harty Room concert hall. Weekly Music @ QUB concerts, seminars, workshops and masterclasses. Page states teaching requires students to work on location, in the studio and in the Sonic Lab. Genuinely world-class — but oriented to sonic art and research, not commercial record production.
programs.equipmentRequired: None stated as compulsory. Students may wish to provide a personal computing device.
programs.valueVerdict: CONDITIONAL — leaning AVOID for him. This is unambiguously a genuine, state-recognised, accredited second-cycle degree from a Russell Group university, so it is not a diploma-mill AVOID. But it charges the highest fee of the six (£23,000) for a programme whose stated relevant subjects EXCLUDE his degree, whose alternative route requires professional experience he does not have, and whose content (sonic art, instrument design, musicology) points away from DJing and record production. He would be paying the most money for the worst fit and the lowest admission probability. Only defensible if Chevening pays.
programs.recommendation: ALL FIGURES IN THE PRIOR RECORD CONFIRMED — no corrections needed. £23,000 international fee, IELTS 6.5/5.5, 2.2 in a listed relevant subject, three £3,000 Harrison bursaries, 14 August 2026 advisory deadline, 30 full-time places, MUS7109 at 60 CATS, and the 10-minute RPEL video cap are all verbatim correct. The prior record's honest assessment also stands and I am reinforcing it: this is the weakest of the six FOR HIM. Three hard blockers stack. First, software engineering is not among the enumerated relevant subjects. Second, the only alternative route, RPEL, is written for applicants with 'extensive relevant professional experience' — a portfolio built over one year is not professional experience, and the four permitted work-sample formats (public performance extract, sound installation documentation, instrument-design demonstration, composition recording) do not naturally accommodate a set of electronic-music productions or a DJ mix. Third, £23,000 is £5,000 to £9,500 more than every other option here for content that is furthest from his goal. The Harrison bursaries are automatic on early application so there is zero cost to trying, but £3,000 off £23,000 does not change the economics. Treat this as a stretch application to make ONLY alongside a Chevening bid, and only if the portfolio year produces something that genuinely fits one of the four RPEL categories. If he wants one UK application at this tier, USW is the better use of the effort.

programs.program: MSc Audio Engineering
programs.institution: University of Hertfordshire — School of Creative Arts
programs.city: Hatfield (Hertfordshire, about 30 minutes north of London by train)

Page confirms lectures, seminars and tutorials are typically scheduled over two consecutive days a week plus extra workshop, performance and recording sessions, with substantial expected self-directed studio practice. Key staff CONFIRMED: Bruce Aisher (Programme Leader for PG Music; work on over 100 tracks including a US Billboard Club Chart No.1, a Platinum album; products by Apple, Clavia, Native Instruments), John Brough (formerly chief engineer at Metropolis Studios, worked with Queen), Dr Kyriacos Michael, Rob Wright (Head of Music).

programs.facilities: CONFIRMED VERBATIM and genuinely exceptional for the price band: a large recording studio with a 32-fader Neve Genesys Black analogue mixing console (Neve 1073 mic-preamps plus 88R and 1084 EQ), 64-channel Pro Tools HD MADI system, PMC IB2S-A midfield monitors, Neumann surround monitoring, two racks of high-end analogue and digital outboard compression, EQ and effects (Neve, Focusrite, Drawmer, 1176, LA2A, Pultec), and UAD DSP processing with a full plug-in suite; a medium-size second studio with a Neve Genesys, Pro Tools HD, RedNet and Neumann 5.1 monitoring; acoustically-treated surround-equipped iMac mix/production spaces with Slate Raven MTi touchscreen control, RedNet and Kawai acoustic pianos; live recording booths and spaces; surround-sound monitoring rooms; a dubbing suite for A/V work (foley, ADR); dual-monitor Apple iMac labs running Logic, Ableton Live, Reason, Pro Tools, Max/MSP, Native Instruments Komplete and EastWest Composer Cloud; a state-of-the-art performance venue with a Soundcraft Vi1 console and full RedNet integration; outboard including Digidesign Pro Tools, Lexicon, TL Audio, TC Electronic and Focusrite; and top-quality dynamic, condenser and ribbon microphones including Soundfield, Neumann, AKG, Coles, Shure, Audio-Technica and Beyerdynamic. programs.valueVerdict: CONDITIONAL. It is a genuine accredited Level 7 degree from a public university, the studio estate is the best of the six, and the effective net fee after automatic scholarships (about £14,000–£15,000) is far better than the prior record implied. But the entry wording assumes you already ARE an audio person, no degree-classification floor is stated so the studio-competence expectation carries the whole gate, and the full-time programme specification is titled MA while the page says MSc. Conditional on (a) a portfolio year that produces demonstrable studio and DAW competence, (b) written confirmation of the award title, and (c) accepting a roughly £15,000 self-funded tuition bill plus a £5,000 deposit to capture the scholarship.
programs.recommendation: CORRECTIONS MADE. Two things in the prior record were wrong or incomplete and both matter. FIRST, fundingLevel was 'Check' and scholarships were recorded as 'Not stated / UNVERIFIED'. That is now corrected: Hertfordshire runs automatic, no-application international scholarships — a Chancellor's International Scholarship of £500–£4,000 assessed automatically from the course application, plus one-off postgraduate awards of £3,500 (deposit by 30 April), £3,000 (by 17 July) or £3,000 (by 14 August), plus a £1,000 full-payment discount. Awards generally do not stack, so assume about £3,000–£4,000, bringing net tuition to roughly £14,000–£15,000 — materially cheaper than the prior record suggested and cheaper than USW's headline. SECOND, a real cost was missing: those early scholarships require a minimum £5,000 TUITION DEPOSIT cleared by the stated date. That is a big early cash call he must plan for. CONFIRMED UNCHANGED: £17,950 international 2026/27, IELTS 6.5 with no band below 5.5, the 26/09/2027 start with apply links already live, the entry wording, and the Neve studio estate. The MSc-versus-MA discrepancy is CONFIRMED and is sharper than the prior record stated — it is specifically the FULL-TIME 2026 specification that reads 'MA Audio Engineering' while the part-time one reads 'MSc'. Since he would study full-time, get the parchment title in writing before paying a deposit. Net judgement: strong programme, best facilities, viable net cost, but of the two Herts music options this one has the narrower subject wording ('related subjects' rather than 'related discipline'), no stated classification floor to lean on, and content aimed at studio engineering rather than at becoming an artist. Prefer the MA Music Production and Artist Development unless he specifically wants to be an engineer rather than a producer.

For a screen-sound programme the obvious evidence to volunteer is a short reel: a dialogue edit, a foley pass, an ADR example and a mixed scene. Note this is DIFFERENT evidence from what the music-production programmes want, so choosing this course means splitting his one portfolio year across two incompatible bodies of work.
programs.auditionSpec: None stated.

programs.scholarships: CORRECTED — the prior record said 'Not stated on the course page' and 'UNVERIFIED'. programs.valueVerdict: CONDITIONAL — and only as a hedge. It is a genuine accredited Level 7 degree at a public university with the same forgiving 2:2 'related discipline' entry wording and the same automatic scholarships, so on the mechanics it is perfectly sound. The problem is not the programme, it is the fit: it trains screen-sound post-production professionals, which is a different career from international DJ and producer. Spending roughly £25,000 all-in and a year of his life on the wrong craft is poor value even though the degree itself is legitimate.
