The £5,000 deposit requirement was also missing. Everything else CONFIRMS exactly: £17,950 international, IELTS 6.5 with no band below 5.5, the 22/09/2027 start with live apply links, and entry wording that is word-for-word identical to the MA Music Production and Artist Development (1st/2:1/2:2 in Music, Music Technology, Music Performance or a related discipline, or five years' industry experience, with the studio-competence expectation for all applicants). The award title is CONFIRMED clean across the page and both 2026 programme specifications. NET JUDGEMENT unchanged and reinforced: include this only as a hedge. Screen sound is legitimate and employable and the entry bar is identical to the programme he actually wants, but it points away from his stated goal, and choosing it would force him to split his single portfolio year between two incompatible bodies of evidence — released music productions for the MA, versus a dialogue-edit and foley reel for this. He cannot build both well in twelve months. If he wants Hertfordshire, the MA Music Production and Artist Development is the door; use this only if that programme fills or rejects him.

programs.program: MA in Music and Technology (course code CR_GMUTE_9) — with a parallel MSc in Music and Technology (CR_GMUST_9) on the same programme
programs.institution: Munster Technological University (MTU) — MTU Cork School of Music
programs.publicPrivate: PUBLIC — CONFIRMED. MTU is an Irish state technological university established under the Technological Universities Act 2018 (merger of Cork IT and IT Tralee), funded through the Higher Education Authority. The course page publishes the classic Irish public-sector fee split (EU €4,000 total, non-EU €13,500) and the University publishes Academic Council policies and governance documents. MTU Cork School of Music is MTU's own conservatoire at Union Quay, not a separate private body.
programs.institutionType: Technological university containing a purpose-built conservatoire (MTU Cork School of Music, Union Quay)
programs.accreditationStatus: CONFIRMED — the cleanest accreditation evidence of the six. The course page states verbatim: 'The Masters in Music and Technology is a full-time Level 9 course of study worth 90 ECTS credits.' NFQ Level 9 is Ireland's master's level. An Irish public university award at NFQ Level 9 with 90 ECTS is directly and unambiguously recognisable across the EHEA and in Tunisia — no equivalence argument needed, unlike UK CATS credits which require conversion.
programs.qualification: MA or MSc — one programme, two award routes with separate course codes (CR_GMUTE_9 for the MA, CR_GMUST_9 for the MSc) and separate apply links. Both are full NFQ Level 9, 90-ECTS master's degrees. The route is shaped by the nature of the 30-credit independent project taken June–August and by elective choices. Discuss the pathway with the course coordinator before applying.
programs.focus: Use of technology to enhance music creation of all kinds. Core areas: computer music, recording studio, acoustics and psychoacoustics, sound synthesis. Explicitly hands-on, with core studies assessed primarily by project work.
programs.whatYouStudy: CONFIRMED VERBATIM: 'The first two semesters (September-January and January-June) each have a 30-credit load, delivered through a combination of 5-credit mandatory and elective modules.' A full-time student normally studies SIX modules per semester. Independent work is undertaken over the final June–August period for a 30-credit project. Core studies: computer music, recording studio, acoustics and psychoacoustics, sound synthesis. Electives are drawn from multimedia, music performance, engineering and computer science — which is exactly where his software engineering background becomes an asset rather than a liability. Teaching staff span music performance and composition, art, multimedia, business, electronic engineering and computer programming, with integration discussed in computer-music classes and industry seminars. ACCS (Accumulation of Credits and Certification of Subjects) and part-time routes exist with flexibility on module load.
programs.language: English — CONFIRMED. Ireland; all teaching in English. No Irish-language requirement.
programs.languageRequirement: CORRECTED — the prior record overstated its certainty. It claimed as 'VERIFIED' that Cork School of Music programmes sit in MTU's Level 2 band at IELTS 6.5 with no section below 6.0. The official MTU English-language page is INTERNALLY INCONSISTENT on this point. Under the heading 'Applicants to Courses at MTU CORK Campus' — and Cork School of Music is in Cork — the bands are given as: Level 1 = all undergraduate programmes plus postgraduate ENGINEERING, MATHEMATICS AND COMPUTER SCIENCE programmes (IELTS 6.0 with no section below 5.5); Level 2 = postgraduate MEDIA AND BUSINESS programmes (IELTS 6.5 with no section below 6.0). CSM is not named in the Cork list at all. It is only under the separate 'Applicants to Courses at MTU KERRY Campus' heading that Level 2 is defined as 'Postgraduate Media, Business, CCAD and CSM programmes' — which looks like an MTU copy-paste error, since CSM and CCAD are Cork institutions. So 6.5 with no band below 6.0 is the PROBABLE requirement and the safe planning assumption, but it is NOT verified for Cork, and there is a real possibility this CS-and-engineering-adjacent programme falls under Level 1 at 6.0/5.5. MTU's own page adds: 'Please note some programmes have a higher requirement in English Language. You should contact the International Office for further details.' HE MUST EMAIL AND CONFIRM — the difference between 6.0/5.5 and 6.5/6.0 is months of preparation for someone at a working-English baseline.
programs.englishTest: Plan for IELTS Academic 6.5 with no section below 6.0 (Level 2), but CONFIRM IN WRITING with MTU International Office — the Cork-campus band table may place this programme at Level 1 (IELTS 6.0, no section below 5.5). NEW AND USEFUL: alternatives are confirmed for both levels. Level 2 accepts PTE Academic 63 (no section below 59), TOEFL iBT 90 (Listening 23, Reading 21, Speaking 22, Writing 23), Duolingo 120 with no individual section below 110, Cambridge English 176 (no section below 169). Level 1 accepts PTE 59, TOEFL iBT 80, Duolingo 105 with no section below 100, Cambridge English 169. The Duolingo option is materially cheaper and faster to sit than IELTS and was not flagged in the prior record. Test must be taken within 2 years of programme start; MTU accepts the IELTS One Skill Retake if retaken within 60 days of the original test.
programs.durationEcts: 1 year full-time, 12-month intensive (September to August). 90 ECTS, NFQ Level 9. Part-time and ACCS routes available with flexible module load.
programs.intakes: One intake, September.
programs.deadline: CONFIRMED and CRITICAL. The course page states: 'Irish/EU: 31st August 2026. Non-EU: 31st May 2026' — PRIOR CYCLE, confirm the 2027 dates. NOTE AN INCONSISTENCY ON THE PAGE ITSELF: the entry-requirements section carries stale text reading 'Non EU applicants - deadline is 31st May 2025', a leftover from an earlier cycle. Either way the pattern is unambiguous and decisive: THE NON-EU DEADLINE IS THREE MONTHS EARLIER THAN THE EU ONE. For a September 2027 start he must plan to submit by roughly 31 May 2027, which means the English test must be sat and reported by about March 2027 and the interview window falls in July/August 2027. This is by far the earliest hard deadline of the six and it is the single most likely thing to catch him out.
programs.applicationOpens: UNVERIFIED for the 2027 cycle — the page does not publish an opening date, though 'apply now' links are live for both course codes. Confirm the 2027 opening with CSM.FullTimeCoursesCork@mtu.ie. Note the page confirms there is no charge for applying; you are only asked to pay an acceptance fee if a place is offered and you wish to accept it.
programs.entryRequirements: CONFIRMED VERBATIM: 'Applications are invited by way of a submitted application form and shortlisted candidates will be interviewed in July/August, if required, where the applicant must display musical competence. Normally, an Honours 2.2 Degree in a cognate area is required and work-based experience is an advantage.' And: 'Recognition is given for relevant prior learning where the applicant does not have a relevant Honours Degree, and the applicant should contact the course coordinator.' The page separately explains RPL: 'Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL) is when formal recognition is given for what you already know prior to starting on a programme or module... You can apply for RPL in any MTU accredited programme or module.' FOR HIM: 'cognate area' is the open question, but given the programme draws electives from engineering and computer science and its staff include electronic engineers and programmers, a BSc Software Engineering is a far more natural cognate fit here than at any other institution in this set. The 2.2 floor is forgiving. The real hurdle is the July/August interview requirement to 'display musical competence'.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: YES — the most usable route of the six for a computer science graduate. The programme explicitly draws electives from engineering and computer science, its teaching staff include electronic engineers and computer programmers, and formal RPL is offered where the applicant lacks a relevant Honours degree with a direct instruction to contact the course coordinator. Note also that MTU's own Cork band table classifies postgraduate engineering, mathematics and computer science as a recognised category, which supports reading software engineering as cognate. The binding constraint is the interview's musical-competence test, not the degree subject.
programs.portfolioSpec: No formal portfolio specification is published — CONFIRMED. The gate is the July/August interview at which the applicant 'must display musical competence'. He should arrive with produced work he can play and discuss articulately, plus a clear account of how his software engineering skills apply to computer music, synthesis and audio DSP. Because no spec is published, he should email the Music and Technology course coordinator via CSM.FullTimeCoursesCork@mtu.ie in autumn 2026 to ask precisely what evidence the panel expects — well before the 31 May non-EU deadline. This is the single highest-value email he can send.
programs.auditionSpec: Not a formal instrumental audition. CONFIRMED: an interview in July/August for shortlisted candidates, 'if required', at which the applicant must display musical competence. This is a competence interview, which is far more accommodating to a self-taught electronic producer than a conservatoire audition would be.
programs.tuitionEU: €4,000 IN TOTAL for EU applicants — CONFIRMED verbatim as a total for the programme, not per year.
programs.tuitionNonEU: €13,500 — CONFIRMED, and THIS IS THE RATE HE WOULD PAY as a Tunisian national. By a wide margin the cheapest of the six: roughly €4,000 to €10,000 less than the UK options once sterling is converted, and less than half the Queen's Belfast fee. Even against the best-case Hertfordshire net figure of about £14,000–£15,000 (roughly €16,000–€17,500) after automatic scholarships, MTU is still cheaper with no scholarship required at all.
programs.otherFees: CONFIRMED AND EXPANDED. (1) An acceptance fee of €500 payable online if a place is offered — the page states this fee 'is deductible from the overall course fee', so it is a deposit rather than an extra charge, but it is cash required up front. (2) NEW, missed by the prior record: a USI membership levy of €7, introduced following a student referendum affiliating to the national Students' Union, which must be paid before the start of Semester 1. Trivial in amount but it is a real mandatory charge. (3) Ireland requires private medical insurance for non-EEA students as a condition of immigration permission — not quantified on the course page but a genuine additional annual cost, typically a few hundred euro.
programs.totalCostEstimate: €13,500 tuition, of which €500 is paid as a deductible acceptance deposit, plus the €7 USI levy, plus mandatory private medical insurance for non-EEA students, plus Cork living costs, plus the financial evidence the Irish Immigration Service requires for a student permission. Living-cost and immigration-evidence figures are not on the course page — check the Irish Immigration Service student permission requirements and mtu.ie/international/non-eu/cork-campus/. Even so, this is comfortably the lowest total of the six.
programs.fundingLevel: None confirmed at programme level — but the €13,500 headline does more for him than any partial scholarship elsewhere in this set. On net cost this beats every UK option even after their scholarships.
programs.scholarships: No programme-specific scholarship is published on either course page — CONFIRMED absent. MTU publishes a general 'Grants, Scholarships and Financial Assistance' page whose contents are UNVERIFIED here, and Irish state SUSI grants are closed to non-EEA students. The Government of Ireland International Education Scholarship is the realistic full-funding route for a Tunisian studying in Ireland and should be pursued in parallel. Ask the MTU Fees Office directly what a non-EU postgraduate can apply for. Note that the low headline fee means he needs far less scholarship money here to make the numbers work.
programs.visaEligible: Yes in principle — MTU is an Irish public university and the course page links directly to its non-EU visa guidance at mtu.ie/international/non-eu/cork-campus/, and separately warns that even applicants exempt from an English test for entry may still need one for visa purposes, so he should check Irish visa English requirements for Tunisia specifically. Irish student permission for non-EEA nationals requires the programme to appear on the Interim List of Eligible Programmes (ILEP); NFQ Level 9 degree programmes at public universities are standard ILEP entries, but CONFIRM the specific course code appears on the current ILEP before paying the €500 acceptance fee. An NFQ Level 9 award also opens the Third Level Graduate Programme (post-study stay-back) for eligible graduates.
programs.facilities: MTU Cork School of Music is a purpose-built conservatoire building at Union Quay which MTU describes as one of the finest music-education facilities in Europe with an outstanding technological infrastructure, and the programme is designed specifically to exploit those resources. Recording studios and computer-music labs. Less itemised on the page than Hertfordshire's inventory, so request a facilities list or arrange a visit — the studio estate here is almost certainly a step below Hertfordshire's two Neve Genesys rooms, which is the honest trade-off for the much lower fee.
programs.equipmentRequired: None stated.
programs.valueVerdict: WORTH IT — clearly the best value of the six for him. It is an unambiguously accredited NFQ Level 9, 90-ECTS master's from an Irish public university, it costs €13,500 (less than half Queen's and cheaper than the UK options even after their scholarships), it is taught in English, it explicitly offers RPL to applicants without a relevant honours degree, its electives are drawn from engineering and computer science so his BSc is an asset, and it supports an Irish student permission plus post-study stay-back. Cheap, accredited, and genuinely open to a non-music engineering graduate — that is the WORTH IT definition met on every clause.
programs.recommendation: STILL THE STANDOUT OF THIS SET — but two corrections to the prior record, one of them important. FIRST AND MOST IMPORTANT, the English requirement was stated with false confidence. The prior record said it was 'VERIFIED' that Cork School of Music sits in MTU's Level 2 band at IELTS 6.5 with no section below 6.0. It is not verified. MTU's official page defines the CORK campus bands as Level 1 (all undergraduate plus postgraduate engineering, mathematics and computer science) at IELTS 6.0/5.5 and Level 2 (postgraduate MEDIA AND BUSINESS programmes) at 6.5/6.0 — CSM is not named in the Cork list at all. CSM appears under Level 2 only in the KERRY campus table, which is almost certainly an MTU error since CSM is a Cork institution. Plan for 6.5 with no band below 6.0 as the safe assumption, but email the International Office to confirm, because if this programme is treated as Level 1 the bar drops to 6.0/5.5 and saves him months. MTU's page explicitly invites this query. SECOND, useful alternatives to IELTS were missed: Level 2 accepts Duolingo 120 with no section below 110, TOEFL iBT 90 with stated section minima, and PTE Academic 63 — Duolingo in particular is cheaper and faster to sit from Tunisia. THIRD, a small missing fee: a mandatory €7 USI membership levy payable before Semester 1, on top of the €500 deductible acceptance fee. Also note the page contains stale text giving the non-EU deadline as 31 May 2025 alongside the header figure of 31 May 2026 — ignore the stale line, but the 31 May pattern is the point. EVERYTHING ELSE CONFIRMS: €4,000 EU total and €13,500 non-EU, NFQ Level 9 with 90 ECTS verbatim, two 30-credit taught semesters of six 5-credit modules each plus a 30-credit June–August project, Honours 2.2 in a cognate area, the July/August musical-competence interview, and formal RPL with a direct instruction to contact the course coordinator. ACTION PLAN: (1) email CSM.FullTimeCoursesCork@mtu.ie this autumn asking two questions — which English band applies to CR_GMUTE_9, and what evidence of musical competence the interview panel expects; (2) confirm the course code is on the current ILEP; (3) sit the English test by March 2027; (4) submit by 31 May 2027, three months ahead of the EU deadline; (5) apply for the Government of Ireland International Education Scholarship in parallel. This is his primary target.

programs.program: MSc Music Engineering and Production
programs.institution: University of South Wales (Prifysgol De Cymru)
programs.publicPrivate: PUBLIC — CONFIRMED. USW is a Welsh publicly-funded university formed from the merger of the University of Glamorgan and the University of Wales, Newport. The course page carries the decisive tell: the fee note states the University may increase the maximum fee for home students on full-time undergraduate courses only where the Welsh Government increases the permitted level of fee inflation — a statutory fee cap that applies only to state-regulated Welsh higher education institutions. It also operates a published Contextual Admissions Policy and a Fees and Debt Management Policy under Welsh regulation.
programs.institutionType: Modern comprehensive university; the Cardiff Atrium is its creative-industries campus
programs.accreditationStatus: Real second-cycle degree — MSc awarded by the University of South Wales, a UK degree-awarding body regulated in Wales. Level 7, 180 credits. Supports a UK Student visa and the Graduate Route, and is recognised in Tunisia as a master's.
programs.qualification: MSc. 1 year full-time, September start at Cardiff; 2 years part-time also offered, charged per 20 credits.
programs.focus: Music engineering and production aimed at a career as a professional producer in the music industry and related fields, with practical application of knowledge to generate creative work and transferable application to film and animation. Stated career paths on the page: Music Producer, Sound Engineer, Composer and Performer, Sound Designer, Teacher/Lecturer.
programs.whatYouStudy: Advanced music engineering and production, including a Production Portfolio component confirmed in the course structure. CONFIRMED and genuinely differentiating: an innovative postgraduate placement scheme places MSc Music Engineering and Production students with the BBC National Orchestra and Chorus of Wales, giving hands-on experience in sound engineering and orchestral music production with top professionals in the field. No other programme in this set offers a named broadcast-orchestra placement.
programs.language: English — CONFIRMED. Wales; this programme is taught in English. USW offers Welsh-medium provision in other subjects but not here, and no Welsh-language competence is required.
programs.languageRequirement: CONFIRMED VERBATIM: 'International applicants will need to have achieved an overall of IELTS 6.0 with a minimum of 5.5 in each component/TOEFL 4 overall and a minimum of 4 in each component or equivalent.' THIS IS THE LOWEST ENGLISH BAR OF THE SIX and is a decisive advantage for someone who has not yet sat a test — half a band below Queen's and Hertfordshire, and a full band below MTU's likely Level 2. ALSO CONFIRMED VERBATIM and worth pursuing: 'If you have previously studied through the medium of English, IELTS might not be required, please visit our country specific page for further details. If your country is not featured, please contact us.' If his SMU MedTech Tunisia BSc Software Engineering was delivered in English, he should ask USW admissions in writing whether that removes the test requirement entirely. That single email could save him months and the test fee.
programs.englishTest: IELTS 6.0 overall with a minimum of 5.5 in each component, or TOEFL 4 overall with a minimum of 4 in each component, or equivalent. Possibly waivable if his BSc was English-medium — check the country page and ask admissions. Lowest bar in this set.
programs.durationEcts: 1 year full-time; 2 years part-time available. 180 UK credits = 90 ECTS equivalent. Full-time fees are per year; part-time fees are per 20 credits.
programs.intakes: September, at the Cardiff (Atrium) campus, campus code B. Full-time and part-time.
programs.deadline: No hard published deadline — CONFIRMED absent. USW operates rolling online applications with separate forms per start date and study mode. UNVERIFIED as a published date; ask USW admissions for the international/CAS cut-off. HOWEVER there is now a concrete and valuable early date: the Early CAS Scholarship requires being CAS-ready by 31 MAY for a September intake, worth an extra £500. Treat 31 May 2027 as his working deadline.
programs.applicationOpens: ALREADY OPEN for September 2027 — CONFIRMED. Dedicated 'September 2027 Full-time' and 'September 2027 Part-time' application links are live on the course page as of August 2026.
programs.entryRequirements: CONFIRMED VERBATIM: 'Typically we require a 2:1 Honours Degree in an appropriate area. However, if you have solid professional industry experience rather than academic achievement, this may be acceptable for entry to study at this level through a process called Accreditation of Prior Experiential Learning (APEL).' Also confirmed: 'We welcome international applications with equivalent qualifications of our entry requirements' with country-specific equivalence pages. And USW operates a published Contextual Admissions Policy: it 'supports students who have the potential to succeed and who may have faced barriers that make it more difficult to access university', meaning a lower offer may be made based on background and individual circumstances. THE REAL CAVEAT: the 2:1 floor is a full classification higher than the Hertfordshire programmes' 2:2. That is the one place where USW is stricter than Hertfordshire. But 'an appropriate area' for a MUSIC ENGINEERING master's is a materially easier argument for a BSc Software Engineering than 'music' would be.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: YES — the most straightforwardly satisfiable subject requirement of the six. The requirement is a 2:1 in 'an appropriate area', not in music. For a programme titled Music ENGINEERING and Production, an engineering degree is a natural read. Combined with APEL, contextual admissions and the explicit digital-portfolio requirement, this is the clearest published path for a software engineer who spends a year building a body of work. The caveat is the 2:1 classification, not the subject.
programs.portfolioSpec: REQUIRED AND EXPLICITLY SPECIFIED — CONFIRMED VERBATIM: 'Please provide evidence of a website or any other form of digital portfolio as part of your application. This should be the first section of your personal statement or uploaded in section 12 of the application form.' This is the most concrete and checkable portfolio instruction of the six, and it tells him exactly what to build over the coming year. Note the format: a LINK to a website or digital portfolio, not a physical or time-limited submission — so a well-built personal site, or a curated SoundCloud/Bandcamp presence with production credits and process documentation, satisfies it. Unlike Queen's ten-minute video cap and four permitted art-music formats, there is no restriction on genre or duration, so electronic music and DJ work fit without contortion.
programs.auditionSpec: None stated. No audition, no interview requirement published.
programs.tuitionEU: £17,900 per year full-time — EU students pay the international rate post-Brexit. UK/Home full-time £11,060 per year; UK part-time £1,229 per 20 credits. Note: USW does operate a separate EU Scholarship scheme ensuring EU students' tuition does not exceed the Home rate, but that is not available to a Tunisian national.
programs.tuitionNonEU: £17,900 per year — CONFIRMED as the International full-time rate for 2026/2027, and THIS IS THE HEADLINE RATE HE WOULD PAY before scholarship. That is now resolved, and the answer is strongly in his favour. USW's official international scholarships pages confirm: (1) CHANCELLOR'S INTERNATIONAL DEVELOPMENT SCHOLARSHIP of £2,500 for students from eligible regions — and the official eligible-countries page lists TUNISIA EXPLICITLY BY NAME under Africa, alongside Algeria, Egypt, Libya and Morocco. MECHANISM CONFIRMED VERBATIM: 'You will be automatically considered for one of these awards when we receive your application. You do not need to make a separate application and confirmation of the scholarship will be included in your offer letter.' CONDITIONS: he must be self-funding (students sponsored by their government or a company are NOT eligible), must pay the minimum deposit stipulated in the offer letter by the date on the Acceptance Form, and scholarships do not apply to English language courses or placement years. programs.valueVerdict: WORTH IT. It is an accredited Level 7 MSc from a Welsh public university, explicitly open to a non-music engineering graduate ('an appropriate area', plus APEL and contextual admissions), it has the lowest English requirement of the six with a possible waiver if his BSc was English-medium, it publishes the only concrete portfolio specification he can actually build toward, and it carries a confirmed automatic £2,500–£3,000 scholarship for which Tunisia is named by name — bringing effective tuition to about £14,900, the lowest of the four UK options. programs.recommendation: CONFIRMED AS THE STRONGEST UK PICK, and UPGRADED on the most important axis. THE MAJOR CORRECTION: the prior record listed fundingLevel as 'Check' and said awards open to a Tunisian were UNVERIFIED. They are now verified and they are good. USW's Chancellor's International Development Scholarship of £2,500 names TUNISIA EXPLICITLY on its official eligible-countries list, is awarded AUTOMATICALLY with no separate application, and is confirmed in the offer letter. On top of that, an Early CAS Scholarship adds £500 if he is CAS-ready by 31 May — USW's own worked example confirms £2,500 becomes £3,000. Effective tuition therefore falls from £17,900 to about £14,900, guaranteed rather than competitive. That is a better funding position than Hertfordshire's (whose comparable awards demand a £5,000 tuition deposit cleared months in advance) and it is the difference between 'check with the office' and 'money he can bank on'. Two conditions matter: he must be SELF-FUNDING (government- or company-sponsored students are excluded, so a Chevening award would displace this rather than add to it), and he must pay the deposit stipulated in the offer letter by the date on the Acceptance Form. EVERYTHING ELSE CONFIRMS EXACTLY: £17,900 international 2026/27 with a within-course fee-hold commitment, IELTS 6.0 with 5.5 in each component (the lowest bar of the six) with a possible waiver if he studied through the medium of English, the 2:1 in 'an appropriate area' with APEL and contextual admissions, the verbatim digital-portfolio requirement (website or digital portfolio, first section of the personal statement or section 12 of the form), September 2027 full-time and part-time apply links already live, and the BBC National Orchestra and Chorus of Wales placement. THE ONE HONEST CAVEAT that keeps this at B rather than A: the 2:1 floor is a full classification stricter than Hertfordshire's 2:2, and the studio facilities are undocumented on the page where Hertfordshire's are exhaustively listed — he should request a facilities list before committing. HIS TWELVE-MONTH PLAN FOR THIS APPLICATION: build the website/digital portfolio USW explicitly asks for, since it is the only published spec in this set and it accommodates electronic music and DJ work without contortion; email admissions to ask whether his English-medium BSc waives IELTS, and if not sit it targeting 6.0 with no band under 5.5; apply early in the 2027 cycle and aim to be CAS-ready by 31 May 2027 to capture the extra £500. Rank this second overall behind MTU Cork, and first among the UK options.

Verbatim highlights: 'state-of-the-art recording studios and Dolby Atmos certified sound lab'; Studio 1 has a Dolby Atmos 7.1.4 speaker system and an Avid S6 console, BNU being 'one of the first Universities in the UK to adopt Dolby Atmos into a music environment'; Studio 2 has an Audient ASP8024 mixing desk with outboard by Neve, Universal Audio, Teletronix, Focusrite, Tegeler, Maag and Manley, monitoring by Genelec and Adam Audio; 'Studio three and the Electronic Music Studio are based around Avid S3/S4 control surfaces and UAD Apollo x8 audio interfaces'; edit booths have Avid microphone preamps; individual edit rooms up to large Pro Tools Ultimate studios with attached live rooms and vocal booths. A DEDICATED ELECTRONIC MUSIC STUDIO is directly relevant to his stated goal and exists at none of the other three on published evidence. The page also promises extensive studio time.
programs.equipmentRequired: None stated as compulsory. The generic additional-costs note mentions specialist equipment may be needed.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: YES — unambiguously, and uniquely so among these four. '2:1 and an interest in pursuing a career in music' contains no subject restriction whatsoever, and the institutional floor is a 2:2 with experience able to substitute. This remains the single most important finding about this programme.
programs.recommendation: Still the best entry-fit of the four and the cheapest, and two corrections make it stronger than the previous record allowed: the facilities ARE documented, in detail, and include a dedicated Electronic Music Studio, a Dolby Atmos 7.1.4 room with an Avid S6, and Pro Tools Ultimate rooms with live rooms and vocal booths — and the module list is published, with Immersive Audio Production, Sound Art & Composition, Future Production Technologies, Social Media Marketing and The Live Music Industry mapping unusually well onto a DJ/producer career. He satisfies the published entry requirement today: a 2:1-equivalent BSc plus a stated interest in a music career. No portfolio gate, no music degree, no audition, and September 2027 is published as the start date. ONE CORRECTION CUTS THE OTHER WAY AND IS NOW THE CRITICAL PATH: the English requirement is published after all and it is IELTS 6.5 overall with 6.0 in EVERY band (or TOEFL iBT 88) — the highest bar of the four and a harder floor than USW's or Ulster's 5.5. He has not tested. Book a diagnostic now and plan the IELTS around a 6.0-in-every-band target, because that is the only published criterion he does not already meet. Second, note the part-time route is closed to international students, so it is full-time or nothing. Third, get the 2027/28 international fee in writing, since the page warns it will change. Funding remains the open risk — no award he can win has been identified, so this is a ~£28,000-£30,000 self-pay year unless Chevening or GREAT comes through.

programs.program: MMus Creative Musicianship (pathway: Composition and Creative Audio)
programs.institution: Ulster University — Faculty of Arts, Humanities and Social Sciences, School of Arts and Humanities
programs.publicPrivate: PUBLIC — CONFIRMED. Ulster University is a UK publicly-funded university established by Royal Charter, operating within the Northern Ireland Department for the Economy fee regime; the course page advertises Student Finance NI tuition-fee loans for NI/ROI students and routes GB students to their national funding bodies, and publishes an official International and EU (excluding ROI) fee schedule.
programs.institutionType: Multi-campus comprehensive public university
programs.accreditationStatus: CONFIRMED — real second-cycle degree. Award line reads 'Master of Music', conferred by Ulster University, a UK degree-awarding body under Royal Charter. Nested suite (PGCert / PGDip / MMus): PGCert and PGDip take two semesters full-time; the full MMus requires three semesters including the 60-credit Final Project, and the regulations state verbatim '(b) the Final Project module is not exempted for those wishing to complete the MMus award'. Ensure any offer is for the MMus, not a nested exit award — a PGCert or PGDip is not a master's.
programs.qualification: MMus (Master of Music), 180 credits. Full-time three semesters = one calendar year; part-time six semesters = two calendar years.
programs.focus: Practice-based musicianship across genres, described as 'a flexible, practice-based course for musicians wishing to develop or refresh their professional expertise for work in the creative industries'. Three named pathways; the relevant one is Composition and Creative Audio, covering the combination of acoustic and electronic sources, film music, and interactive and mixed media. The other two are Performance Studies and Music and Communities.
programs.whatYouStudy: Across semesters one and two: two complementary Specialism modules covering recent developments in the chosen pathway plus technical, research and communication skills; a Practice module devoted to developing individual creative practice with one-to-one tuition; a Seminar module for contextual, aesthetic and theoretical study. Plus modules in Music Technology and Society and a Research Project, within which 'work placements are available as an option'. Semester three: Final Project (60 credits), 'a sustained period of self-directed, practice-based work related to their chosen specialism'. Assessment is 100% coursework on every module — no exams — and 'can take many forms, for example: essay, research paper, presentation, performance, lecture recital, workshop activity, practical/design work and portfolio submission'. Postgraduate module pass mark is 50%. Teaching includes visiting creative industry professionals and a departmental musician-in-residence.
programs.language: English — CONFIRMED (teaching in English; Northern Ireland).
programs.languageRequirement: CONFIRMED verbatim on the course page: 'The minimum requirement for this course is Academic IELTS 6.0 with no band score less than 5.5. Trinity ISE: Pass at level III also meets this requirement for Tier 4 visa purposes.' Ulster recognises other tests at comparable IELTS-equivalent scores. Tied with USW for the lowest English bar of the four and a real advantage for someone who has not yet tested.
programs.durationEcts: Full-time: three semesters, one calendar year in total, for the MMus (two semesters for PGDip/PGCert). Part-time: six semesters, two calendar years. CONFIRMED verbatim: 'Currently timetabled as one contact day per week full-time, plus any relevant instrumental/vocal tuition and work in the library' — an unusually light contact pattern leaving substantial studio and production time. 180 UK credits = 90 ECTS equivalent.
programs.intakes: September. CONFIRMED — the dedicated 2027/28 course page publishes 'Start Date: September 2027' and 'Start dates: September 2027'. His exact target intake.
programs.deadline: Not published on the 2027/28 page — CONFIRMED absent. CONFIRMED routing: applicants from outside the UK and Ireland must use the International Portal at international.ulster.ac.uk; the direct Ellucian application route is restricted to those who live in the UK or Ireland and are not applying as international students. Ask the international admissions team for the September 2027 cut-off.
programs.applicationOpens: The 2027/28 course page is live as of August 2026 with both application routes displayed. Exact portal-opening date unverified — ask via the International Portal.
programs.entryRequirements: CONFIRMED verbatim: 'Applicants must meet the University's minimum entrance requirements and, in addition, a) hold a second-class honours degree or better in music or another relevant discipline from a recognised institution, or b) an equivalent qualification or c) be able to provide other evidence of ability and experience appropriate to the course.' Plus: 'The University will consider applications on the basis of experiential learning for those who do not hold the normal entry qualifications. The onus is on the applicant to evidence that they have relevant experience equating to degree study at the honours level.' FOR HIM: route (a)'s 'another relevant discipline' and route (c)'s open 'other evidence of ability' make this accessible on paper — but the proposal and the compulsory interview/audition are the real gates.
programs.portfolioSpec: A WRITTEN PROPOSAL is required — CONFIRMED verbatim: 'A written proposal outlining the intended area of individual study (i.e. the Specialism and, ideally, an idea of what the third-semester project might involve) should support the application.' This asks for research and practice INTENT rather than finished work, which in principle suits someone still building a portfolio — but it demands he can articulate a specific creative-audio project in writing at master's level. No formal portfolio of recordings is specified, though supporting evidence of ability is clearly welcome under entry route (c).
programs.auditionSpec: CONFIRMED verbatim and unconditional, in the same sentence as the proposal requirement: 'all applicants will be interviewed and/or auditioned.' There is no route into this programme that avoids a live assessment. For a candidate with no conservatory training, no instrument named, and no recorded work yet, this is the decisive obstacle.
programs.tuitionEU: £18,310 for 2026/27 — EU students (except ROI nationals living in NI, GB or ROI) pay the International rate post-Brexit. There is no separate EU rate.
programs.tuitionNonEU: RESOLVED — this was the previous record's biggest gap and it is now filled. Ulster's official 2026/27 International and EU (excluding ROI) fee schedule sets full-time 'Masters courses (except those as detailed below)' at £18,310 per year. Creative Musicianship is not in any of the exception lists (which cover Executive MBA/MPA at £22,680, a named group of MSc/LLM courses at £20,490, Medicine at £39,630, and per-credit-point courses). So £18,310 is the rate that applies to this MMus at 2026/27 prices. The course page confirms '2027/28 Fees: Postgraduate fees are subject to annual review, 2027/28 fees will be announced in due course', so his actual figure is unpublished but £18,310 is the correct planning baseline. Note under the fee rules: a full-time student registering for a PGDip only pays 2/3 of the masters fee and a PGCert only 1/3. CONSEQUENCE: this is NOT a cheap option. It is £2,030 a year MORE than BNU and £410 more than USW's 2026/27 rate — and unlike them it has no scholarships at all.
programs.otherFees: CORRECTED from UNVERIFIED. The course page states under 'Additional mandatory costs': 'None.' It adds that accommodation, travel including car parking, and normal living costs are on top of tuition, and that there are additional fees for examination resits, library fines and graduation ceremonies. A non-refundable deposit applies to international students — see Ulster's non-refundable deposits page. Eligible Ulster alumni get a 10% tuition discount, which does not apply to him.
programs.totalCostEstimate: Now estimable: £18,310 tuition at 2026/27 prices (2027/28 to be announced, expect higher) plus Derry~Londonderry living costs. Ulster's own page calls Derry 'one of the most affordable places to live in the UK', which is a genuine advantage and probably the cheapest living costs of the four. Plan on roughly £29,000-£31,000 for the year — cheap living does not offset tuition that is second-highest of the four with zero programme funding.
programs.scholarships: VERIFIED NEGATIVE and re-confirmed verbatim. Under 'Scholarships, awards and prizes' the course page says: 'None.' The Student Finance NI £10,000 tuition-fee loan is restricted to NI/ROI-domiciled students and is not available to him, and the GB funding bodies likewise. Ulster maintains a general scholarships page and a 10% alumni discount, neither of which he can use. Chevening is the only realistic full-funding route to this programme.
programs.visaEligible: Yes — Ulster operates a dedicated International Portal for applicants from outside the UK and Ireland, and the course page cites Tier 4/Student-route English-language equivalences explicitly. The MMus is a genuine level-7 award supporting a student residence permit, provided the offer is for the full MMus and not a PGCert or PGDip exit award. Confirm the licence on the UKVI Register of Licensed Sponsors.
programs.facilities: Magee campus, Derry~Londonderry. Still NOT itemised for music — the page describes the city, the Martha Magee building, modern teaching blocks, library facilities, the School of Medicine and a Sports Yard, and links a 360-degree virtual tour, but publishes no studio or equipment inventory. This remains the weakest evidence base of the four, and stands in sharp contrast to BNU's room-by-room list. Request a facilities list before applying.
programs.equipmentRequired: None stated, and additional mandatory costs are confirmed as 'None'. But the attendance pattern is 'one contact day per week, plus any relevant instrumental/vocal tuition', which implies an instrument or voice as a practice base. Clarify in writing whether DJ and production practice satisfies this for the Composition and Creative Audio pathway — this is not a trivial question for him.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: YES on the published wording — 'music OR another relevant discipline', plus an explicit 'other evidence of ability and experience' route and a formal experiential-learning route. But the openness on paper is converted into a live test in practice, because every applicant is interviewed and/or auditioned without exception.
programs.recommendation: The previous agent set the right test and the answer is now in. It said: 'If the fee comes back competitive with Bucks New or USW, this becomes a serious contender; if it comes back near Queen's £23,000, drop it.' The fee is £18,310 for 2026/27 — NOT competitive. It is £2,030 more than BNU and £410 more than USW, on a programme that states in its own words that it offers no scholarships, awards or prizes at all. Combine that with the unconditional 'all applicants will be interviewed and/or auditioned' — a live assessment he cannot presently pass, having no conservatory training, no instrument named and no recorded work — and the undocumented music facilities, and the case collapses despite three genuine attractions: the joint-lowest English bar (IELTS 6.0, 5.5 floor), an entry route explicitly accepting another relevant discipline or evidence of ability, and a September 2027 start already published on a dedicated 2027/28 page with a light one-day-a-week contact pattern that would leave real time to produce. Two things also corrected upward: additional mandatory costs are confirmed as 'None', and Derry is among the cheapest UK cities to live in. If he still wants to pursue it, email Ulster for (a) exactly what form the interview/audition takes for the Composition and Creative Audio pathway and whether DJ/production practice satisfies the instrumental-tuition expectation, and (b) a studio facilities list. Otherwise this is second-highest cost, zero funding, and a mandatory audition — put BNU ahead of it.

programs.program: Master's degree (kandidat/KA) in Electronic Music and Sound Art — Elektronisk Musik og Lydkunst
programs.institution: SDMK – Syddansk Musikkonservatorium / Danish National Academy of Music
programs.institutionType: Music conservatoire (state art academy under the Danish Ministry of Culture)

programs.language: DANISH for group teaching — CONFIRMED VERBATIM on SDMK's language-requirements page: 'Group teaching is in Danish.' programs.focus: Electronic music, sound art, electroacoustic composition, sound-as-material practice
programs.whatYouStudy: CONFIRMED. Specialised knowledge, skills and competences to work as an electronic musician, composer or sound artist at the highest artistic level, developing a unique artistic profile. Underlying discipline covers synthesis, electroacoustics, field recording, sound systems, studio and software work.
programs.durationEcts: 2 years / 120 ECTS (Danish conservatoire kandidat) — CONFIRMED
programs.intakes: One intake per year; studies start in August
programs.applicationOpens: 15 October — CONFIRMED verbatim on SDMK's apply/FAQ page: 'Application opens: October 15th'
programs.deadline: 1 December at 12:00 noon — CONFIRMED ('Deadline for application: December 1st at noon'; if it falls on a weekend it moves to the next working day at 12:00). MAJOR CORRECTION TO THE PREVIOUS RECORD ON TWO POINTS. (1) These are NOT a prior cycle. The exam calendar now published references 'Week 50 (December 7-11, 2026)' and 'Nordic Master in Folk Music: Opens again in 2028' — this IS the live round that opens 15 Oct 2026, closes 1 Dec 2026 and admits for August 2027. That is exactly his target intake. (2) The previous record put the Esbjerg entrance exam in weeks 1–2 (4–15 January). That is WRONG for the master. SDMK's calendar lists Esbjerg BACHELOR exams in January ('Electronic music and sound art: Week 2 (January 11-15)') and then separately, for Esbjerg, 'Master programs: Interviews in March/April'. programs.entryRequirements: CONFIRMED verbatim on the official EMOL-KA admission page: either 'A bachelor degree in electronic music from SDMK or an equivalent Danish or foreign music academy' OR 'A bachelor degree (in music) or equivalent from a institution of higher education.' The parenthesis on the second limb is the only crack a non-music BSc could get through, and it is untested. SDMK's FAQ states more bluntly that a music bachelor is required. Treat a Software Engineering BSc as almost certainly insufficient without written derogation.
programs.portfolioSpec: CONFIRMED. One or more artistic works totalling no more than around 25 minutes, submitted as audio files or a multimedia presentation, all self-created with any collaborators clearly credited; plus a written statement of maximum 2 A4 pages covering overall artistic concept, recognised potential, planned artistic projects, artistic background and motivation.
programs.auditionSpec: CONFIRMED — two-part entrance assessment, scored as a single overall mark: (1) a technical exposition of maximum 10 minutes demonstrating diverse sound-working techniques on your own computer/instrument (SDMK provides mixer and speakers); (2) an artistic conversation of maximum 10 minutes on artistic vision, sources of inspiration, target audience and project potential. programs.equipmentRequired: You bring your own computer/instrument; SDMK supplies mixer and speakers for the exposition.
programs.facilities: Conservatoire studio facilities at the Esbjerg campus (Kirkegade 61, DK-6700 Esbjerg). Detailed studio inventory still not published — UNVERIFIED.
programs.tuitionEU: Free — EU citizens study free; small charges for materials may apply during studies.
programs.tuitionNonEU: EUR 10,000 per academic year for master programmes — CONFIRMED on SDMK's Guide for International Students, page last updated April 2026. Two years = EUR 20,000. (For reference the bachelor rate is EUR 13,525/yr.) SDMK warns 'all prices listed above are due to yearly change according to indexation', so budget above this for 2027–2029. Third-party aggregator sites quoting EUR 9,700 are out of date — disregard them.
programs.otherFees: Application fee DKK 500 for master applicants — CONFIRMED, non-refundable, must be RECEIVED before the deadline or the application is invalid; the applicant also covers any bank/handling charges, so the full DKK 500 must arrive. Only SDMK's own bachelor students applying to a master with no entrance exam are exempt.
programs.scholarships: NONE he could win — CONFIRMED verbatim: 'SDMK - Danish National Academy of Music does not offer any scholarships for foreign students.' International applicants must secure funding from their home country.
programs.totalCostEstimate: EUR 20,000 tuition over two years + DKK 500 application fee + Esbjerg living costs + the Danish immigration self-support requirement (check SIRI/nyidanmark.dk for the current documented-means figure). No scholarship offsets any of it.
programs.visaEligible: Yes in principle — CONFIRMED. A full degree at a state conservatoire supports a Danish student residence permit; SDMK's guide tells non-EU/EEA students they must 'apply for and obtain the residence permit before coming to Denmark' and register with the municipality within 5–8 days of arrival. NOTE the hard condition SDMK adds: 'In order to be enrolled and study at the Danish National Academy of Music you must have legal residence in Denmark during the entire study period.'
programs.englishTest: None — the programme is not English-taught, so no IELTS/TOEFL is published.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: Effectively NO — CONFIRMED. The FAQ position (a music bachelor is required for master entry) is the operative barrier; the '(in music) or equivalent' limb on the EMOL-KA page is ambiguous and untested and would need written confirmation from admissions.
programs.recommendation: GENUINE PROGRAMME, GENUINELY ACCREDITED, WRONG FIT FOR HIM — and the previous agent's dates were wrong in a way that matters. This is a real state-conservatoire kandidat in exactly his subject, and the round that feeds his September 2027 target opens 15 Oct 2026 and closes 1 Dec 2026 (the previous record wrongly flagged these as a prior cycle) with the master interview in March/April 2027 (the previous record wrongly put it in January). But it fails him on three independent counts: (1) group teaching is in Danish and he has none; (2) it demands a music bachelor and he has a Software Engineering BSc with no conservatoire training; (3) EUR 10,000/yr with an explicit written no-scholarships-for-foreigners policy, so EUR 20,000 of pure self-pay for a Danish-medium degree he is unlikely to be admitted to. AVOID for the 2027 cycle. The one cheap action worth taking: email lki@sdmk.dk asking whether a non-music BSc plus a strong 25-minute portfolio has ever been admitted under the 'or equivalent' limb — that answer is genuinely unknown and costs him nothing.

programs.auditionSpec: MAJOR CORRECTION AND THE DECISIVE FINDING ON THIS PROGRAMME. The previous record left the entrance examination as 'three components, detail UNVERIFIED'. TEST 2 — Musical performance ability: from an assignment given on the day, and TOGETHER WITH TWO MUSICIANS PROVIDED BY KMH, he must prepare and perform a short piece of music THAT INCLUDES IMPROVISATION. Structure: 30 minutes solo preparation, 15 minutes rehearsal with the two musicians, a performance of maximum 5 minutes, then oral reflection; about 60 minutes total, scored 0–6 on musical interpretation and artistic reflection. TEST 3 — Artistic reflection and musical expression: an on-campus interview of about 20 minutes discussing the Test 1 works, his creative process and his motivation, scored 0–6. Two consequences the previous record missed entirely: (a) he would have to perform live improvised music with professional musicians, which no amount of DAW portfolio work substitutes for; (b) Tests 2 and 3 are in person in Stockholm, so he must travel from Tunisia — and enter Schengen on a short-stay visa — BEFORE any admission decision exists.

After checking the official syllabus and the published entrance-test specification, it is BETTER THAN CLAIMED ON LANGUAGE AND MUCH WORSE THAN CLAIMED ON ADMISSIBILITY, and the second point governs. Resolved in his favour: the language of instruction is ENGLISH, stated verbatim in the KAIM1 syllabus — the previous record's biggest open question, now closed, and he should not waste the email asking it. Also confirmed: no music bachelor required, sound art and music in computer games are named parts of the remit, SEK 264,000/yr, SEK 900 application fee, roughly three full-tuition scholarships institution-wide (plus FAS+ insurance) decided only after May admission. Resolved against him, decisively: the entrance examination is not the written project description the previous record described. Test 1 demands three recorded works including one where he leads and one where he collaborates with other musicians or artists. Test 2 is an ON-CAMPUS live performance in Stockholm where he must prepare and perform improvised music with two musicians KMH assigns him, scored 0–6. Test 3 is a 20-minute on-campus interview. programs.entryRequirements: Official text: a completed Bachelor's Degree in Music Performance or Composition 'or other relevant field of study amounting to a minimum of 180 ECTS credits', normally of 4 years' duration, from a recognised university or university college. Grade requirements: 'None' — selection is entirely by entrance examination and portfolio jury. TWO PROBLEMS FOR HIM the previous entry did not draw out: (1) the 'normally 4 years' duration' clause — a 3-year Tunisian BSc may need justification; (2) 'grade requirements: none' is not generosity, it means his engineering GPA buys him nothing at all. programs.portfolioSpec: CORRECTED WORDING — composition track requires 'Substantial documentation of compositional works (scores, recordings, video documentation etc.) of approx. 45 minutes', plus a CV, letters of recommendation, and a WRITTEN ARTIST STATEMENT (the previous entry's 'two-page written reflection on compositional practice' is not the official wording; the page says artist statement, length unspecified). That is a composer's catalogue, not a producer's demo reel, and notated scores are not something he can generate in twelve months from a software-engineering start.
programs.auditionSpec: Two rounds. Round 1: jury assessment of the submitted portfolio (composition) or a 15-minute video for classical performance / 30-minute video for jazz. Round 2: portfolio-based interview and entrance exams at The Grieg Academy in person, or a digital interview for applicants who cannot travel. Video/portfolio upload deadline 15 January.
programs.englishTest: IELTS Academic 6.5 overall AND 6.5 in each of the four components, or TOEFL iBT 90. No One Skill Retake, no MyBest Score. He has taken neither test — this must be booked well before the December 2026 application.
programs.tuitionEU: Free — EU/EEA/Swiss citizens pay no tuition in Norway; only the semester fee.
programs.tuitionNonEU: NOK 401,704 PER YEAR, 2026/27 — CONFIRMED on both the university tuition table and the programme page ('The tuition fee for the Master's Programme in Music Performance or Composition for the school year 2026/27 is 401 704 NOK'). He pays this as a Tunisian national. MAJOR CORRECTION TO THE PREVIOUS ENTRY'S EURO CONVERSION: two years is NOK 803,408 ≈ EUR 68,000–70,000 at roughly 11.7 NOK/EUR, NOT 'EUR 34,000–35,000'. The previous agent converted one year's fee and labelled it the two-year total — a factor-of-two understatement of the single most important number in this record. EUR 34,000 is the ANNUAL figure. Payment terms: must be paid IN FULL, cannot be paid in instalments, and proof of payment is required before he can even apply for the study permit — so he fronts ~EUR 34,000 before any visa decision. Faculty spread at the same university, confirmed: Humanities NOK 197,000/yr, Psychology NOK 197,000/yr, Social Sciences NOK 197,000–226,000/yr, Science and Technology NOK 226,000/yr, Medicine (Biomedical Sciences) NOK 226,000/yr. programs.scholarships: NONE — CONFIRMED TWICE ON OFFICIAL PAGES. The university tuition page states 'UiB does not offer any scholarships' and the programme page repeats 'The University of Bergen does not offer any scholarships.' programs.totalCostEstimate: Tuition NOK 803,408 over two years ≈ EUR 68,000–70,000, paid in two non-instalment lump sums of NOK 401,704 each, the first before the visa is granted. PLUS documented living funds for the study permit: CORRECTED AND VERIFIED — UDI requires NOK 15,488 per month = NOK 170,368 per academic year for 2026/27 (single-semester figures NOK 77,440 autumn / NOK 92,928 spring). But the permit chain is brutal for him: full-year tuition paid in full first, then documented NOK 170,368 living funds in a Norwegian bank or institutional deposit account, then the permit application. programs.recommendation: KEEP THIS ENTRY, BUT AS A PRICE SIGNAL — DO NOT APPLY. Corrections made to the previous record, in order of importance. (1) THE COST WAS UNDERSTATED BY HALF: two years is EUR 68,000–70,000, not EUR 34,000–35,000; EUR 34,000 is the annual figure. (2) The English requirement is now verified and is a hard gate: IELTS 6.5 overall AND 6.5 in every single component, or TOEFL iBT 90, with no One Skill Retake and no MyBest Score — he has taken neither test. (3) There is a SECOND deadline the previous record missed: 15 December 2026 for the application, then 15 JANUARY for the portfolio/audition video upload. (4) The claim that the Grieg Academy has no electronic/electroacoustic capacity is WRONG — it has a Composition Research Group, an experimental studio under Prof. Daniel Péter Biró, and Assoc. Prof. Stylianos Dimou teaching electroacoustic composition and music technology at graduate level. The correct objection is not absence of technology but wrong genre: this is contemporary art-music composition with scores, not DJ practice or commercial production. (5) Verified figures replacing 'UNVERIFIED': semester fee NOK 700/semester (NOK 650 without the voluntary SAIH contribution); UDI proof of funds NOK 170,368 per year for 2026/27. Everything else in the previous record — NOK 401,704, the no-scholarships statements, the 15 December 2026 date, the no-instalments rule — checks out against the official pages. Bottom line for him: Norway is the most expensive unfunded destination in the sweep, UiB says twice in its own words that it offers no scholarships at all, the fee must be paid in full before the visa is even applied for, and the artistic bar is a 45-minute catalogue of notated and recorded compositions he does not have and cannot build in twelve months. Strike Norway from the funded list entirely.

programs.program: Composition and Performance of Electronic Music (LT: Elektroninės muzikos kompozicija ir atlikimas) — MA

programs.publicPrivate: PUBLIC — CONFIRMED. KTU is a Lithuanian state university; the programme carries the Lithuanian state study-programme code 6211PX025 and appears in the AIKOS national register maintained by the Ministry of Education, Science and Sport. CORRECTION to the previous record: the claim that 'admission runs through the national LAMA BPO centralised system' is WRONG for this programme. KTU master's admission runs through KTU's OWN system, MPIS (Magistrantūros priėmimo informacinė sistema) at https://uais.cr.ktu.lt/ktuis/st_online.startasmag. Its public status is not in doubt, but the stated mechanism was incorrect.
programs.language: LITHUANIAN ONLY — CONFIRMED verbatim on the official page: 'This programme has a Lithuanian-only curriculum and all the learning and assessment processes are carried out in the Lithuanian language.' The English admissions page further redirects entry requirements to the Lithuanian-language description. There is NO English track and none is advertised.
programs.languageRequirement: Lithuanian — sufficient to sit a Lithuanian-language entrance exam and be assessed entirely in Lithuanian. CONFIRMED that KTU publishes NO CEFR level and NO accepted-certificate list for this programme on either the English or Lithuanian page. The practical requirement is functional academic Lithuanian (LMTA's comparable Lithuanian-taught masters demand C1). No English certificate is relevant. Ask studijos@ktu.lt / shmmf@ktu.lt for the formal standard.
programs.qualification: Menų magistras / Master of Arts — CONFIRMED. Second cycle, field of music, state code 6211PX025. This IS a genuine state-recognised second-cycle degree registered in the Lithuanian AIKOS register, not a private 'master' certificate. No correction needed.
programs.accreditationStatus: CONFIRMED accredited/registered Lithuanian second-cycle programme; KTU links the 'STUDIJŲ KRYPTIES VERTINIMAS IR AKREDITAVIMAS' study-field evaluation record and the programme is listed in AIKOS (aikos.smm.lt) and kurstudijuoti.lt under 6211PX025. Exact current accreditation expiry date is still not published on the programme page — check the SKVC register or ask studijos@ktu.lt.
programs.durationEcts: CONFIRMED: 1.5 years (3 semesters), full-time, blended delivery, 90 ECTS total. (Note: the English admissions page renders inconsistently and one automated read of it returned '60 ECTS' — the Lithuanian programme page states 90 kreditai and 1.5 metai. 90 ECTS is correct.) Sem 1 = 30 cr (Composition of Electronic Music 1, Computer Based Music Analysis, Electronic Music Performance 1, Music Media and New Media, Theories of Music Composition and Interpretation); Sem 2 = 30 cr (Composition for Cinema, TV and Computer Games; Electronic Music Composition 2; Electronic Music Performance 2; Virtual Music Instruments; + 6 cr elective from Composition and Performance of Electroacoustic Music / Programming of Electronic Music / Sound Design Studio); Sem 3 = 30 cr Master's Degree Final Project.
programs.focus: Electronic music composition and performance; sound art; music technology; sound design; music for film, TV and computer games.
programs.whatYouStudy: Electronic music production and performance; music/media analysis; music programming; composing for different media; virtual instruments; electroacoustic composition and performance; a 'Sound Design Studio' elective; a 'Composition for Cinema, TV and Computer Games' core module. Taught by working electronic-music composers/producers (Antanas Jasenka, Jonas Jurkūnas, Titas Petrikis, Andrius Laucevičius). Officially described as the first Master's degree of its kind in Lithuania. On syllabus alone this is close to an ideal match for his stated goals.
programs.entryRequirements: CONFIRMED and this is the standout fact. The Lithuanian admission page states the university-track requirement as 'Visų studijų krypčių grupių bakalauro laipsnis' — a bachelor's degree from ANY study field group. A BSc in Software Engineering satisfies the academic prerequisite outright. Only kolegija (college) graduates face a restriction: they need a professional bachelor's in music studies PLUS either 30 credits of supplementary studies (papildomos studijos) or at least 1 year of relevant work experience. A mandatory entrance exam must be passed; failing it or not sitting it removes the applicant from the competition entirely. Competition score = passed entrance exam + motivation assessment (oral, 10-point scale, weight 0.1) + up to 4 bonus points (up to 2 for scientific/artistic activity; 0.5 each for ≥1 year relevant work experience, partial studies abroad ≥24 ECTS, completion of a talent-development programme, diploma with distinction).
programs.auditionSpec: A mandatory entrance exam (stojamasis egzaminas) assessed by the SHMMF faculty admission committee at A. Mickevičiaus g. 37, Kaunas. RE-CHECKED: the faculty's own entrance-exam event page still does NOT publish the exam content, format or marking scheme — it only names the governing document ('Stojamojo egzamino organizavimo ir vykdymo tvarkos aprašas') and states that consultations are given by the study programme director. programs.recommendation: DO NOT APPLY. The degree is entirely legitimate — a real, state-recognised Lithuanian MA (6211PX025) at a public university, correctly described in the previous record on that point — so this is not a diploma-mill warning. It is AVOID for him on cost-versus-access grounds, on three independent blockers, any one of which is fatal. (1) LANGUAGE: 100% Lithuanian teaching, assessment AND entrance exam. He has Arabic, French and working English; reaching exam-standard Lithuanian by an early-2027 application round is not realistic. programs.program: Film Art (LT: Kino menas) — MA, Sound Design (Garso dizainas) specialisation
programs.institution: Lithuanian Academy of Music and Theatre (LMTA), National Film School (Nacionalinė kino mokykla)

programs.languageRequirement: A C1-level Lithuanian language certificate — CONFIRMED as an explicit published requirement on LMTA's own English admissions page, not an inference. programs.qualification: Menų magistras / Master of Arts, 120 ECTS, second cycle, state code 6211PX003 — CONFIRMED on LMTA's own programme page. No correction needed — this is a genuine degree, not a certificate.
programs.accreditationStatus: CONFIRMED accredited Lithuanian second-cycle arts programme; LMTA's programme page links the study-field evaluation and accreditation record ('STUDIJŲ KRYPTIES VERTINIMAS IR AKREDITAVIMAS'). programs.durationEcts: CONFIRMED: 120 ECTS, 2 academic years full-time, 30 ECTS per semester ('Nuolatinės studijos, 2 metai').
programs.focus: Film sound design and film sound post-production, as one of four specialisations inside a film-art master's (Garso dizainas / Kūrybinis prodiusavimas / Operatorinis menas / Režisūra). programs.whatYouStudy: Students choose a specialisation on entry and work with course instructors and specialisation curators. The official sound-specific learning outcome for Garso dizainas: the graduate 'will know sound research methods and will be able to analyse, evaluate and realise feature-film sound and other creative sound projects, taking account of the relevance and artistic value of the idea or theme.' LMTA describes it as the only programme of its kind in Lithuania.

programs.portfolioSpec: UNVERIFIED in its formal specification, but the programme structure makes the substance clear: the degree is built around an individual artistic-research project producing an original short-form audiovisual work plus an analytical paper, so a creative-project proposal and evidence of prior sound work are effectively required. programs.englishTest: Not applicable. LMTA requires B1 English only for its English-taught programmes; Film Art is Lithuanian-taught, so the demanded certificate is Lithuanian C1 instead. His untaken IELTS/TOEFL neither helps nor hinders here.

It is AVOID for HIM because four separate gates each close independently. (1) NO 2027 INTAKE — admission is biennial, the last was 2026, the next is 2028, which misses his target by a full year. (2) C1 LITHUANIAN CERTIFICATE, published as a hard requirement — the steepest language bar in either record, and unreachable for him. (3) NOT OPEN TO INTERNATIONAL APPLICANTS — re-confirmed that Film Art is absent from LMTA's list of masters open to international applicants, which contains only Composition, Music Performance, conducting, Dance Art and the joint programmes. (4) WRONG PROFILE — the cohort is working film-sound professionals deepening first-cycle competences, and he has no film-sound background, no portfolio and no conservatory training. Also note the content mismatch that the funding and language problems tend to overshadow: this is narrative film sound post-production, not electronic music production or DJing, so even if every gate opened it would serve his stated goal only obliquely. programs.institution: Filmová akademie Miroslava Ondříčka v Písku, o.p.s. (FAMO Písek) / International Film School (IFS)
programs.publicPrivate: PRIVATE — CONFIRMED, and now from an independent official source, not just the school's own claim. (obecně prospěšná společnost). Not a veřejná vysoká škola. The previous record's reasoning was right and its conclusion stands.
programs.language: CORRECTED — the previous record's 'Czech, UNVERIFIED whether any English-medium delivery exists' is WRONG. programs.languageRequirement: CORRECTED — both tracks now verified, and they differ sharply. programs.qualification: Czech track: MgA., navazující magisterské studium, programme code N0211P310001, standard duration 2 years. English track: awarded as 'Master of Arts Degree'; FAMO and the Study in Czechia portal both present the English BA/MA as accredited variants of the same Multimediální produkce programme. The MŠMT/NAÚ register (regvssp.msmt.cz) is a JavaScript application that could not be machine-queried, so the register ENTRY ITSELF remains unopened — but the programme code, the mirrored register data on vysokeskoly.com, and the listing on the government Study in Czechia portal all corroborate genuine national accreditation of the Czech-language programme. What is NOT independently confirmed is that the ENGLISH-language variant carries the same accreditation and awards the same MgA. title rather than an in-house 'Master of Arts'. programs.accreditationStatus: PARTIALLY RESOLVED. The Czech-taught N0211P310001 is corroborated as a nationally accredited navazující magisterský programme by three independent sources. The English-taught IFS MA is claimed by the school to be accredited and EU-recognised, but neither the IFS homepage nor the IFS about-page carries any accreditation statement at all — the claim appears only in third-party directory listings and marketing copy. Given the price difference (see below), the single most important question to answer in writing before any payment is: does the English-taught MA appear in the MŠMT register as a language variant of N0211P310001, and does it confer MgA.? If it does not, a Tunisian national would be paying 30,000 EUR for a non-state-recognised private certificate that may not support a residence permit.
programs.durationEcts: 2 years / 4 semesters, full-time, both tracks. 120 ECTS is the Czech norm for navazující magisterské studium; the specific ECTS count is not published on either the Czech or English pages.
programs.focus: Film-school multimedia production with a dedicated sound line. Ateliér zvuku trains 'zvukaře ve filmové, televizní, rozhlasové a divadelní tvorbě' — sound engineers for film, television, radio and theatre. Note carefully what that is NOT: it is post-production and location sound for screen and stage, not music production, not electronic music, not DJing.
programs.whatYouStudy: CORRECTED on the key open question. The previous record flagged as UNVERIFIED whether a sound specialization continues into the master's. It DOES. The FAMO studium page lists eight ateliérs applying to both the bachelor and the follow-up master's, including Ateliér zvuku, and the IFS master's page independently names 'Sound design' among the MA specializations alongside Screenwriting and Directing, Cinematography, Production and Animation. So master-level sound is real at this school. The remaining mismatch is one of content, not existence: this is screen-and-stage sound engineering, whereas the candidate's stated goal is international DJ and music producer. Nothing in either track's published specialization list covers music production, electronic music composition, or club/dance music.
programs.entryRequirements: CORRECTED FROM 'UNVERIFIED'. Czech track: completed bachelor's degree (thesis and diploma required, or supplied at enrolment if the defence is pending); general conditions under § 48 of the Higher Education Act; interview before an admission commission which assesses submitted works and tests cultural, artistic and technical awareness. Foreign applicants face IDENTICAL admission conditions to Czechs but must obtain either general nostrification (valid nationwide) or FAMO's own internal nostrification of the prior degree — Tunisia is NOT on the exemption list (only Germany, Slovakia, Slovenia, Poland, Hungary are exempt). Maximum 35 students admitted across ALL specializations combined. English track (IFS): completed application form, CV, motivational letter, bachelor degree certificate, valid passport, portfolio, plus the B2 English conversation. Nostrification also required.
programs.portfolioSpec: CORRECTED FROM 'UNVERIFIED'. Czech track: the bachelor's thesis from prior study PLUS a portfolio of works matching the chosen specialization; the commission 'individuálně posuzuje možnosti uchazečů a profesní předpoklady' — it assesses each candidate's capabilities and professional prerequisites individually, which is a genuinely low and flexible bar compared with FAMU or a conservatory. English track: master's applicants must submit portfolio samples (mandatory at MA level; optional at BA level). For a candidate with no portfolio yet, the year he has before applying is exactly the right amount of time — but it must contain sound work, not just music tracks, if he wants this school.
programs.auditionSpec: No performance audition. Czech track: an interview before the admission commission on the day of the přijímací řízení, conducted over the submitted works. English track: an online conversation with a native English speaker (which doubles as the language check) rather than a formal audition. Both are conversational rather than performance-based — materially easier for a non-conservatory applicant than any music-academy entrance exam.
programs.equipmentRequired: None required for admission. IFS states the tuition fee covers tuition plus basic equipment for each practical exercise and specialized software — so no separate hardware purchase is implied. Teaching uses Pro Tools and multi-channel recording setups.
programs.facilities: Sound studio with professional audio equipment including Pro Tools and multi-channel recording; small film school with hands-on production access; teaching staff drawn from working industry professionals. IFS claims its teaching staff outnumbers its international students. Small scale means more individual studio time and far less institutional weight than FAMU.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: YES — and this is now well-supported rather than inferred. No music degree, no conservatory training and no film degree is required by either track. The Czech track's own wording is that the commission assesses candidates individually on capabilities and professional prerequisites; the English track asks only for a bachelor's degree in anything, plus a portfolio. A BSc Software Engineering graduate is admissible on paper to both. This is one of the genuinely open doors in the whole search.
programs.englishTest: NONE — no IELTS and no TOEFL, for either track. The English track verifies B2 through an online conversation with a native speaker. For a candidate who has not taken and does not want to pay for a standardised test, this removes a real obstacle. It is the single strongest point in this school's favour for him.
programs.tuitionEU: Czech-taught track: 79,000 CZK per academic year (~3,200 EUR), identical for Czech and EU students, payable before the programme starts. English-taught IFS track: 7,500 EUR per SEMESTER at master's level — the same rate for EU and non-EU applicants, since IFS prices by programme, not nationality.
programs.tuitionNonEU: THE BIGGEST CORRECTION IN THIS RECORD. The previous entry stated a Tunisian would pay 79,000 CZK/year (~3,200 EUR) because FAMO 'publishes a SINGLE rate with no separate non-EU tariff'. That is true only of the CZECH-TAUGHT track, which he realistically cannot enter without Czech. The track actually open to him is the English-taught IFS MA, and its published rate is 7,500 EUR PER SEMESTER — i.e. 15,000 EUR per year, 30,000 EUR for the two-year master's. That is roughly FIVE TIMES the figure previously recorded, and it is not a non-EU surcharge — it is simply the price of the English-medium programme, which the earlier research missed entirely. (The IFS Bachelor and the film courses are 6,500 EUR/semester; only the MA is 7,500.)
programs.otherFees: CORRECTED FROM 'UNVERIFIED'. Czech track: non-refundable administrative fee of 1,000 CZK, paid to account 190 134 906 / 0300 (ČSOB Písek) with the applicant's ID as variable symbol. English track: no application fee published, BUT a deposit of 50% of the first semester's tuition — approximately 3,750 EUR for the MA — must be paid BEFORE formal acceptance, explicitly to 'establish the sincerity of the application'.
