programs.totalCostEstimate: CZECH TRACK (not realistically open to him): ~158,000 CZK tuition over two years (~6,400 EUR) plus ~290,000-380,000 CZK living (~12,000-15,500 EUR) — about 18,000-22,000 EUR total. ENGLISH TRACK (the one he could actually enter): 30,000 EUR tuition plus ~12,000-15,500 EUR living — about 42,000-45,500 EUR total for the degree, before nostrification and visa costs. The previous record's headline of 'roughly 18,000-22,000 EUR' understated his real exposure by more than half.
programs.scholarships: None identified for either track. Private Czech HEIs rarely fund non-EU degree students, and Czech government scholarship schemes are generally tied to public institutions. Assume full self-pay. The 50% pre-acceptance deposit on the English track means he would be committing ~3,750 EUR of his own money before he has an acceptance in hand, let alone a visa.
programs.intakes: CORRECTED FROM 'UNVERIFIED'. Annual September intake. The Czech track runs TWO admission rounds per cycle; the English track has a single annual deadline.
programs.applicationOpens: Applications open well ahead of each round. FAMO explicitly warns on its own admissions page: 'Neposílejte přihlášky a povinné práce poslední den, kdy je deadline!' — do not send applications and required works on the deadline day; send them several weeks early. For a September 2027 start he should have materials ready by early 2027.
programs.deadline: CORRECTED FROM 'UNVERIFIED'. Published dates for the 2026/27 cycle, which map directly onto his 2027/28 target one year later. CZECH TRACK: two rounds — exam 14 May 2026 with applications due 8 May 2026, and exam 3 September 2026 with applications due 7 August 2026. ENGLISH TRACK (IFS): 30 April 2026. Expect the equivalent 2027 dates, i.e. an IFS deadline around 30 April 2027 and Czech-track rounds in May and August/September 2027. Note the IFS April deadline is COMFORTABLE for a September 2027 start and fits his stated Oct 2026 - Feb 2027 preparation window with room to spare.
programs.visaEligible: Czech track: YES if N0211P310001 is confirmed in the MŠMT register — study at an accredited private Czech HEI supports a long-term residence permit for study purposes. English track: PROBABLY, but this is precisely where the unresolved accreditation question bites. If the English MA is an accredited language variant of N0211P310001, it supports the permit; if it is an in-house 'Master of Arts' outside the register, it may not, and he would have paid a 3,750 EUR deposit and potentially far more for a qualification that does not underpin his residence. Resolve this in writing BEFORE the deposit. Also note the sequencing risk the previous record correctly identified and which is now worse: the deposit falls due before acceptance, which is before any visa decision.
programs.recommendation: The previous record treated this as a cheap Plan C fallback at ~3,200 EUR/year. That framing collapses once the English track is priced correctly. The route he can actually walk — English-taught, no IELTS, non-music bachelor accepted — costs 7,500 EUR per semester, 30,000 EUR for the degree, roughly 42,000-45,500 EUR all-in. The route that costs 3,200 EUR/year requires Czech language proficiency as a precondition of commencing study, which he cannot reach from zero by September 2027 while also building a portfolio. So the cheap option and the accessible option are not the same option, and the earlier entry conflated them. On top of the price, three things push this to AVOID for HIM specifically. First, fit: Ateliér zvuku and the IFS Sound design line train sound engineers for film, television, radio and theatre — screen and stage post-production. His goal is international DJ and music producer. Neither track's published specialization list contains music production, electronic music, or composition. He would pay 30,000 EUR to learn a genuinely skilled trade that is adjacent to, not aimed at, what he wants. Second, accreditation asymmetry: the Czech programme's national accreditation is well corroborated, but neither the IFS homepage nor its about-page makes any accreditation statement whatsoever, and the English MA's register status and degree title (MgA. or an in-house 'Master of Arts') are unconfirmed. Paying master-level money for a private award whose state recognition is unverified is exactly the trap to refuse. Third, money at risk before certainty: a 50% first-semester deposit, about 3,750 EUR, is demanded before formal acceptance and therefore long before a visa decision. That said, record the genuine positives honestly, because they are unusual and may matter if better options fail: no IELTS or TOEFL at all, a conversational rather than performance-based entrance, explicit willingness to assess non-traditional candidates individually, a confirmed master-level sound specialization, a portfolio requirement he has a full year to satisfy, and an April deadline that fits his timeline comfortably. If he ever reconsiders, he must first get in writing (1) the English MA's entry in the MŠMT register and the exact degree title, (2) confirmation the deposit is refundable on visa refusal, and (3) a syllabus showing how much music-production content, if any, the sound line contains. Until then this is a 30,000 EUR answer to a question he has not asked.

programs.program: Audiovizuální tvorba a divadlo — CORRECTED STRUCTURE: this is a SPECIALIZATION within the umbrella programme 'Dramatická tvorba a média', not a standalone programme. programs.intakes: Annual, September start.

Navazující magisterské applications are due 31 MARCH — the published 2026/27 cycle date is 31 March 2027, which is in fact the deadline for a September 2027 start and therefore lands squarely on his target intake. (Note the faculty runs different deadlines by level and specialization: 30 November for some bachelor specializations, 28 February for others including the BcA. in Audiovizuální tvorba a divadlo, and 31 March for master's specializations.) programs.recommendation: The previous record recommended not pursuing this, and that conclusion is confirmed — but the reasoning was incomplete, and the newly verified facts make the case far more emphatic. The earlier entry treated the Czech language requirement as unknown and worth asking about; it is in fact published, certificated and set at C1 CEFR, the highest tier at the faculty, applied specifically to Audiovizuální tvorba a divadlo and demonstrable only through a Charles University or Masaryk University examination or a Czech secondary-school leaving exam. For a Tunisian applicant with no Czech at all in August 2026 and a 31 March 2027 deadline, that is not a hurdle to plan around — it is a closed door. Even setting language aside, the programme fails on content: it is a theatre and new-media creation degree in which sound design is not a named specialization, admission is decided on a portfolio of theatre/film/new-media work he does not have and would not produce while building a music-production portfolio, and both admission rounds are conducted in Czech. Zero tuition at a genuine public arts academy is real value, and the 31 March deadline fits his September 2027 target perfectly — which is exactly why this needs to be marked clearly rather than left looking attractive on price. Do not apply. The entry's lasting worth is the negative finding, now doubly confirmed: JAMU's Theatre Faculty is widely assumed to host a sound-design master's and it does not; JAMU's real audio degree is the joint VUT Brno Audio Engineering Ing. already in the database. Keeping this record closes that gap permanently.

programs.publicPrivate: PUBLIC — CONFIRMED from primary source. programs.language: Polish. Teaching, the three-stage entrance examination and the oral specialist examination are in Polish. programs.languageRequirement: Polish at a level sufficient to sit an oral examination on electroacoustics, studio technique, microphone technique and timbral solfège plus a qualification interview. programs.qualification: magister sztuki — a real, state-recognised second-cycle degree. CONFIRMED.
programs.accreditationStatus: Fully accredited public art academy; POL-on register; supports a non-EU student residence permit. CONFIRMED.
programs.durationEcts: 2 years / 4 semesters, full-time. CONFIRMED on the official admissions page. ECTS not published; 120 ECTS is the standard for a Polish 4-semester second-cycle art degree — confirm with Dział Nauczania.
programs.focus: Sound recording and sound realization across classical, popular/entertainment and electroacoustic music, plus sound for audiovisual forms and live broadcast. CONFIRMED. Closest of the six to actual music production.
programs.whatYouStudy: Deepened sound realization in classical, rozrywkowa and electroacoustic music; sound for audiovisual forms; realization of live programmes; studio technique, microphone methods, electroacoustics, timbral solfège (solfeż barwy), specialist English.
programs.entryRequirements: A completed first-cycle degree, PLUS a positive tonal audiometric (hearing) test — CONFIRMED verbatim: 'Od kandydata wymagany jest pozytywny wynik badania audiometrycznego'. PLUS the three-stage entrance examination. The oral examination presupposes a completed first-cycle sound-engineering education.
programs.portfolioSpec: MANDATORY AND HEAVY — CONFIRMED verbatim: 'trzech autorskich nagrań o różnej instrumentacji' (three original recordings of differing instrumentation), scores optional; one of the three may be replaced by a film soundtrack excerpt, radio-drama fragment or a self-chosen sound scene. These must be his own engineering work, not DJ mixes.
programs.auditionSpec: Three stages, CONFIRMED: (1) presentation and defence of the three original recordings; (2) oral examination on electroacoustics, studio technique, microphone methods, timbral solfège and specialist English, including identifying recording errors and assessing audio quality by ear, plus film-soundtrack assessment; (3) qualification interview on motivation, intended specialization and career plans. The trained-ear tasks are the decisive obstacle for a self-taught applicant.
programs.equipmentRequired: He must be able to produce three properly engineered multi-instrument recordings, which requires a recording space, microphones and a DAW during the portfolio year. A laptop and headphones will not satisfy the acoustic-instrument brief.
programs.facilities: Academy recording studios and concert halls. UNVERIFIED in detail — ask the Wydział office.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: FORMALLY YES (any first-cycle degree is eligible), PRACTICALLY NO. CONFIRMED unchanged. The oral examination is pitched at graduates of a first-cycle realizacja dźwięku programme; a BSc Software Engineering with no conservatory training would almost certainly fail timbral solfège and aural error detection.
programs.englishTest: None. English appears only as 'specialist English' inside the Polish-language oral examination. CONFIRMED.
programs.tuitionEU: 0 PLN for Polish and EU/EEA citizens on full-time studies. CONFIRMED.
programs.tuitionNonEU: MAJOR CORRECTION — THE PREVIOUS '~4,000 EUR PER YEAR' FIGURE IS UNSUPPORTED AND SHOULD BE DELETED. I downloaded and read the operative document: 'Decyzja Rektora Akademii Muzycznej im. G. i K. Bacewiczów w Łodzi z dnia 30 kwietnia 2026 r. w sprawie ponoszenia przez cudzoziemców odpłatności za studia rozpoczynających naukę w roku akademickim 2026/2027'. It sets fees ONLY for foreigners taking studies IN ENGLISH — first cycle: wokalno-aktorska 55 200 PLN / 13 020 EUR, instrumentalistyka (keyboard) 40 000 PLN / 9 440 EUR, instrumentalistyka (strings/wind/percussion) 42 000 PLN / 9 905 EUR per year; second cycle: wokalno-aktorska 49 300 PLN / 11 627 EUR, instrumentalistyka 56 300 PLN / 13 278 EUR, rytmika 45 000 PLN / 10 613 EUR per year. NO fee whatsoever is set for Polish-taught programmes, and 'Muzyka w mediach i produkcja muzyczna' does not appear in the decision at all. The strong inference is that a foreigner admitted to this Polish-taught master's pays NO tuition. That is a materially better financial picture than previously recorded, but it must be confirmed in writing before relying on it — e-mail kancelaria@amuz.lodz.pl / +48 42 662 16 00.
programs.otherFees: CORRECTED. Wpisowe (entry fee) is 180 PLN / 43 EUR — CONFIRMED verbatim in the same Rector's decision — NOT the ~200 EUR previously reported. Entrance examination fee 150 PLN for all fields. Fees payable in two equal semester instalments, due 15 October and 1 March. Łódź living costs ~2,000-3,000 PLN/month, among the lowest of Poland's big cities.
programs.totalCostEstimate: CORRECTED DOWNWARD. If Polish-taught study carries no fee for foreigners (as the 2026/2027 decision implies), the whole degree costs ~180 PLN entry fee + 150 PLN exam fee + ~48,000-72,000 PLN living over two years, i.e. roughly 11,500-17,000 EUR total. The previously projected ~8,000 EUR of tuition appears not to exist.
programs.scholarships: No academy-specific scholarship for non-EU degree students identified. NAWA is the realistic full-funding route and covers art academies.
programs.fundingLevel: Check — probably Full on tuition (no fee set for Polish-taught study), None on living costs.
programs.intakes: One annual intake, September/October start. Entrance examinations in summer. CONFIRMED.
programs.applicationOpens: CONFIRMED for the prior cycle: online registration for first- and second-cycle studies ran 1-29 May 2026.
programs.deadline: CORRECTED WITH REAL DATES. 2026/2027 cycle: registration 1-29 May 2026; second-cycle entrance examinations 22 June - 5 July 2026; first-round results in July. PRIOR CYCLE — for a September 2027 start expect registration ~May 2027 and examinations ~late June/early July 2027. This is far outside the Oct 2026 - Feb 2027 window he assumed.
programs.visaEligible: Yes — accredited public art academy, second-cycle degree, supports a Polish student visa and residence permit. CONFIRMED.
programs.recommendation: REAL PROGRAMME, PROBABLY TUITION-FREE FOR HIM, STILL THE WRONG DOOR FOR 2027. Two corrections improve it: there is no evidence of the ~4,000 EUR/year fee previously recorded (the 2026/2027 Rector's decision prices only English-taught programmes), and the entry fee is 43 EUR not 200 EUR. So money is not the obstacle here — competence is. The entrance examination assumes a completed first-cycle sound-engineering education: timbral solfège, aural detection of recording errors, microphone methods, all conducted in Polish, on top of three original multi-instrument engineered recordings and a passed audiometric test. A single portfolio-building year cannot close a trained-ear gap. Keep it on file as a 2029+ target if he ever completes a first-cycle audio qualification, and use the confirmed fee position as the benchmark when he negotiates with any other Polish public art academy. Concrete action now: e-mail kancelaria@amuz.lodz.pl to get the Polish-taught foreigner fee position in writing.

programs.equipmentRequired: None identified.
programs.facilities: CORRECTED — THE PREVIOUS 'NEGATIVE FINDING' WAS FALSE. The record claimed the Gdańsk music academy has NO sound-engineering, realizacja dźwięku or electroacoustic master's. Zarządzenie Rektora nr 44/2026 and the academy's own 2026/2027 additional-recruitment page both list, on Wydział IV, kierunek 'Jazz i muzyka estradowa', a SECOND-CYCLE specialization 'produkcja muzyczna i realizacja dźwięku' (music production and sound realization) — non-EU fee 8 403 EUR per semester. First, the fee is now known and it is 6 700 EUR per semester — 26,800 EUR for the degree — for a Polish-language music-criticism, journalism and cultural-PR qualification that contains no audio engineering, no music technology and no production content. Paying master-level money in a language he does not speak for a journalism degree is indefensible for a man whose goal is producing and DJing. programs.program: Teorie a praxe audiovizuální tvorby (N0211P310005), navazující magisterský program — specializace Zvuková skladba

programs.focus: Sound design for audiovisual work — film, TV and advertising production and post-production — inside a film-school studio structure. CONFIRMED. Not a music-technology or electronic-music department.
programs.whatYouStudy: Sound within the Audiovisual Arts studio: recording, sound dramaturgy, post-production and mixing for film/TV/advertising, taught alongside camera, directing and screenwriting, editing, production and visual effects so students crew shared productions. programs.entryRequirements: A completed bachelor's degree plus a talent-based entrance examination. CONFIRMED verbatim that for this programme 'můžete podat pouze jednu přihlášku na konkrétní specializaci' — one application only, so he cannot hedge across Zvuková skladba and Střihová skladba (by contrast the Design and Multimédia programmes DO permit multiple applications). programs.portfolioSpec: Required (talentová zkouška). programs.totalCostEstimate: Tuition 0. Realistic total ~300,000-430,000 CZK (~12,000-17,500 EUR) over two years, essentially all living costs. Add a Czech-language preparatory year if needed (typically 100,000-160,000 CZK).
programs.scholarships: No programme-specific entry scholarship for non-EU degree students identified. Czech public universities offer merit and accommodation scholarships to enrolled students. UNVERIFIED whether UTB has an entry scholarship — ask studium@fmk.utb.cz.

programs.visaEligible: Yes — accredited public university, full-time MgA. programme, supports a Czech long-term residence permit for study purposes. CONFIRMED.
programs.recommendation: BEST-VALUE ARTISTIC OPTION IN THE SLICE AND STILL THE HARDEST TO ENTER — assessment unchanged, with one factual fix (Visual Effects IS offered at master level, so there are six specializations competing for the ~25 places, not five). Zero tuition for a Tunisian national, a real film-school studio environment, no music-conservatory gatekeeping. The two obstacles are unchanged and both are hard: the entrance examination is conducted in Czech and doubles as the language screen, and he would need a portfolio strong enough to take one of a handful of Sound Design places. Note also that only one application is permitted for this programme, so there is no hedging. Concrete next step: e-mail studium@fmk.utb.cz asking (a) for the Zvuková skladba section of the current admissions směrnice, and (b) whether the master's talent examination can be sat in English for an international applicant — some Czech art faculties permit this and it would change the whole calculus. If Czech is immovable, this is a 2028/2029 target, not 2027.

programs.program: Elektronika a komunikace / Electronics and Communications (EK), navazující magisterský program — specializace Audiovizuální technika a zpracování signálů / Audiovisual Technology and Signal Processing
programs.institution: České vysoké učení technické v Praze (ČVUT) / Czech Technical University in Prague, Fakulta elektrotechnická (FEL / FEE)
programs.publicPrivate: PUBLIC — CONFIRMED. Veřejná vysoká škola under Act No. 111/1998 Sb.; admission conditions issued as a dean's decree under that Act and the CTU Statute.
programs.language: TWO PARALLEL TRACKS — NOW FULLY CONFIRMED, not merely inferred. The Czech-taught track (free) and the English-taught track (fee-paying) both exist, and 'Electronics and Communications' appears by name on FEL's official list of study programmes conducted in English. Critically, the English programme site en.ek.fel.cvut.cz lists all SEVEN specializations of the English master's and Audiovisual Technology and Signal Processing IS among them (the other six: Electronics, Photonics, Technology of the Internet of Things, Communication Networks and Internet, Mobile Communications, Radio Systems). The previous record's caveat 'confirm before applying which track carries the specialization' can be closed: it is available in English.
programs.languageRequirement: CORRECTED — THERE IS A PUBLISHED BAND, contrary to the previous record's claim that 'no named IELTS/TOEFL band is set, the committee judges it'. FEL's official admission-procedure page names acceptable proof of English proficiency as TOEFL iBT 70 / IELTS 6 / TOEIC 800. He should plan for IELTS Academic 6.0 as a firm target, not treat the requirement as discretionary. For the Czech track: Czech, with the entrance examination in Czech.
programs.qualification: Ing. (inženýr) — real, state-recognised second-cycle engineering degree. CONFIRMED.
programs.accreditationStatus: Nationally accredited public university programme (NAÚ). Supports a Czech long-term residence permit for study. CONFIRMED.
programs.durationEcts: 120 ECTS minimum; standard 2 years / 4 semesters, full-time. Study plan 'Elektronika a komunikace — Audiovizuální technika a zpracování signálů'. CONFIRMED.
programs.focus: Engineering of audiovisual signals — acoustics, sound and image technology, signal processing — organised around the human perceiver. NOT a creative sound-design or music-production degree. CONFIRMED.
programs.whatYouStudy: Sensing, processing and reproduction of audiovisual signals; practical acoustic design and measurement; image and sound technology; modern methods of processing, compression and reconstruction of image, sound and other signals; explicit orientation toward 'člověk jako příjemce audiovizuální informace' (the human as recipient of audiovisual information). Graduates go into television and radio operations, AV and acoustics design, automotive, and biomedical applications. English-language description: 'Get theoretical background and practical skills in acquisition, processing and reproduction of audiovisual signals. Audio, image, video…'
programs.entryRequirements: A completed bachelor's degree, evidenced before enrolment. For the English track the entrance examination is an ONLINE INTERVIEW plus an optional committee-set test. Required documents: transcript of results, English certificate (if not a native speaker), and a MOTIVATION LETTER; documents not in Czech, Slovak or English need certified translation. Nostrification of the foreign qualification must be completed by end of October of the first semester — i.e. AFTER arrival, which materially lowers the barrier at application time. Programme guarantor for the specialization: prof. Petr Páta (pata@fel.cvut.cz); programme responsible: prof. Stanislav Zvánovec.
programs.portfolioSpec: NONE. No portfolio, no creative dossier, no artistic assessment. Applicants are merely 'recommended' to submit evidence of significant achievements in electrical engineering, informatics, mathematics or physics — which a software-engineering graduate supplies directly from his degree and projects. CONFIRMED.
programs.auditionSpec: None. No audition, no musical assessment of any kind. CONFIRMED.
programs.equipmentRequired: None.
programs.facilities: FEL acoustics and audiovisual-technology laboratories at ČVUT Prague; measurement and signal-processing infrastructure rather than creative studios.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: YES — EMPHATICALLY, and confirmed. This is an electrical-engineering faculty programme that actively prefers applicants from electronics, informatics, mathematics or physics. A BSc in Software Engineering is the expected feeder profile. Of the six programmes reviewed, this is the only one where his existing degree is an asset rather than a liability.
programs.englishTest: CORRECTED. TOEFL iBT 70 / IELTS 6 / TOEIC 800, named on FEL's official admission-procedure page. The previous record's 'no fixed band' framing was wrong and would have led him to under-prepare. IELTS 6.0 is well within reach for someone at working-English level, so this is a soft gate, but it is a real one.
programs.tuitionEU: 0 CZK for the Czech-taught track (all nationalities). For the English-taught track EU citizens pay the same fee as everyone else.
programs.tuitionNonEU: CZECH-TAUGHT TRACK: 0 CZK for a Tunisian national — tuition-free status attaches to the language of instruction, not citizenship. ENGLISH-TAUGHT TRACK: CORRECTED FROM 'UNPUBLISHED / TREAT AS UNCONFIRMED' TO CONFIRMED. FEL's official tuition-fees page states master's programmes cost 132 000 CZK per academic year (66 000 CZK per semester), ~5,280 EUR/year, ~10,560 EUR over the two-year degree. The faculty reserves the right to adjust each semester, so re-check for 2027/2028, but the figure is now on the record from the primary source rather than a secondary summary.
programs.otherFees: Application fee 950 CZK per programme AND per specialization — two specializations cost 1,900 CZK. Payment must be made the same day the application is filed; the application enters the procedure only once the fee is paid. Prague living costs ~20,000-28,000 CZK/month, the highest of the six.
programs.totalCostEstimate: Czech track: ~500,000-670,000 CZK (~20,000-27,000 EUR) over two years, all living costs. English track: add 264,000 CZK tuition (~10,560 EUR), so ~30,000-37,500 EUR total.
programs.scholarships: The faculty states high-performing international students may be eligible for scholarships, with no amounts or eligibility rules published. UNVERIFIED — ask the FEL international office whether any entry scholarship is open to a first-year non-EU master's student.
programs.intakes: Main intake for the following academic year, plus an extraordinary second round (mimořádný termín) that FEL has run in consecutive years — a genuine second chance, but requiring a brand-new application even if one was already filed that year.
programs.applicationOpens: Autumn preceding the academic year; the dean's decree for the 2026/2027 cycle was issued 19 November 2025.
programs.deadline: CORRECTED. The previous record gave 31 March as the English-track deadline. FEL's official admission-procedure page states that for the 2026/2027 academic year the deadline for submitting applications is 13 AUGUST 2026. The 31 March date appears to relate to the Czech-taught round (with entrance examination 5 June 2026). PRIOR CYCLE — for a SEPTEMBER 2027 start, diarise a Czech-track deadline around 31 March 2027 and an English-track deadline around mid-August 2027, and confirm both against the dean's decree when it is issued in November 2026.
programs.visaEligible: Yes — accredited public university, full-time Ing. programme, supports a Czech long-term residence permit for study. Note the nostrification requirement lands after arrival (by end of October of semester one), so he must gather diploma, transcripts and legalisations BEFORE leaving Tunisia — the faculty explicitly warns applicants to obtain all documents before travelling.
programs.recommendation: TOP PICK, AND THE RE-CHECK STRENGTHENED IT. Three of the four open questions in the previous record are now closed from primary sources: (1) the English-taught track definitively carries the Audiovisual Technology and Signal Processing specialization — it is one of seven listed on the official English programme site, and Electronics and Communications appears by name on FEL's list of programmes conducted in English; (2) the English-track fee is 132 000 CZK per year / 66 000 CZK per semester, published on the faculty's own tuition page, roughly 10,560 EUR for the whole degree; (3) the English requirement is TOEFL iBT 70 / IELTS 6 / TOEIC 800, not an unbounded committee judgement — so he must actually sit a test, but a 6.0 is comfortably reachable. One correction against him: the English-track deadline is mid-August, not 31 March, which is a different diary entry than previously recorded. Everything that made this the best fit still holds: no portfolio, no audition, no music degree, no conservatory training, an online interview plus a motivation letter, and his BSc Software Engineering as the preferred feeder. It is not a DJ or music-production degree — it is audiovisual signal engineering — but it is credible, affordable, visa-supporting, and puts him inside a Prague audio ecosystem where the production career can be built alongside. Three actions: (1) sit IELTS Academic targeting 6.5 for headroom; (2) e-mail pata@fel.cvut.cz to confirm the specialization runs in English for 2027/2028 and ask about entry scholarships; (3) start Czech from zero anyway, because the Czech track costs nothing.
programs.sourceUrl: https://fel.cvut.cz/en/study-programs/ek-electronics-and-communications/interest-in-studying/masters-degree ; English specializations: https://en.ek.fel.cvut.cz/english/program-characteristics/master-degree/ ; English-taught programme list: https://www.fel.cvut.cz/en/education/study-programs.html ; tuition: https://fel.cvut.cz/en/admissions/admission-procedures/tuition-fees ; deadlines and English band: https://fel.cvut.cz/en/admissions/admission-procedures/step-by-step

programs.program: Multimediálne inžinierstvo (Multimedia Engineering), inžiniersky (second-cycle) study programme
programs.institution: Žilinská univerzita v Žiline / University of Žilina, Fakulta elektrotechniky a informačných technológií (FEIT)
programs.publicPrivate: PUBLIC — CONFIRMED. Verejná vysoká škola under Slovak Act No. 131/2002 Z.z.; the faculty's own admission rules confirm the statutory public regime (no tuition for study in Slovak). Programme listed in the national register at portalvs.sk.
programs.language: Slovak. Teaching, the entrance interview and state examinations in Slovak. No English-taught version of Multimediálne inžinierstvo is advertised. CONFIRMED.
programs.languageRequirement: SLOVAK AT B1 — CONFIRMED verbatim: an applicant who obtained his bachelor's abroad and applies for study in Slovak must submit, with the application or at latest at enrolment, a 'certifikát/doklad o úrovni znalostí zo slovenského jazyka minimálne na úrovni B1'. The rule explicitly adds that the language preparation and its certificate can be completed AT UNIZA before the admission procedure — a concrete, university-run route. This remains materially milder than PWr's C1 Polish fee-waiver threshold or a Czech-language talent examination.
programs.qualification: Ing. (inžinier) — real, state-recognised second-cycle degree. CONFIRMED.
programs.accreditationStatus: Accredited programme in the Slovak national register (portalvs.sk); supports a Slovak temporary residence permit for study. CONFIRMED.
programs.durationEcts: 2 years, full-time (denná forma), 120 ECTS. Still UNVERIFIED on the faculty's own programme sheet — confirm with the FEIT study office.
programs.focus: Multimedia engineering with a declared audio specialization track — a genuine technical/creative hybrid, unusual for an electrical-engineering faculty. CONFIRMED.
programs.whatYouStudy: Theoretical foundations of informatics; digital and analogue processing of IMAGE AND SOUND SIGNALS; processing and transmission of multimedia streams over communication technologies, networks and services; interface and application development. Through compulsory-elective subjects a student can specialise narrowly in AUDIO INFORMATION PROCESSING rather than image or graphics. Creatively oriented subjects are built in so graduates can create and process multimedia works at an appropriate technical, aesthetic and artistic level; the faculty names 'audio technician and designer' as a target job.
programs.entryRequirements: A completed first-cycle degree. CONFIRMED verbatim that a foreign graduate must submit, with the application or at latest at enrolment, a decision recognising equivalence of the first-cycle qualification from a competent Slovak institution, OR may ask UNIZA itself to recognise the document — UNIZA doing it in-house is a real convenience versus separate ministry nostrification. Slovak/Czech graduates in the SAME field with a weighted average up to 2.00 are admitted to Multimedia Engineering without an entrance exam; everyone else — including every foreign applicant and every applicant from a different field — goes through the selection procedure with an interview.
programs.portfolioSpec: YES, AND THE SCORING IS NOW EXACT. CORRECTED AND SHARPENED from the previous record's vague 'up to 70 points combined'. The official rule sets a 100-point maximum built from: (a) weighted GPA from the first-cycle degree, scored 0-30 points scaled linearly from 30 points for a GPA of 1.50 or better down to 0 points at 3.00, then MULTIPLIED BY A COEFFICIENT OF 1.0 if the bachelor's was in the study field 'informatika' and 0.75 if in any other field; (b) at interview, demonstration of general knowledge of informatics and multimedia technologies, 0-40 points; (c) at interview, PRESENTATION OF THE APPLICANT'S CREATIVE ACTIVITY AND OUTPUTS in informatics and multimedia plus overall motivation to study, 0-30 points. Admitted candidates are ranked down to a 61-point floor. So a creative portfolio is worth up to 30 of 100 points and is scored ALONGSIDE, not instead of, IT knowledge — precisely the blend he will have. His Software Engineering degree should attract the 1.0 coefficient as an informatics-field award, but confirm that classification with the study office. Exact portfolio format still UNVERIFIED — request the current 'Zásady a pravidlá prijímacieho konania' and see https://kmikt.uniza.sk/index.php/uchadzaci/moznosti-studia/inzinierske-studium
programs.auditionSpec: No audition. An in-person selection interview only ('prijímacie konanie vrátane prijímacieho pohovoru sa realizuje prezenčne formou výberového konania'). Note 'prezenčne' — in person, so he must plan to travel or request an accommodation. CONFIRMED.
programs.equipmentRequired: None specified. He should assemble a portfolio of audio/multimedia work he can demonstrate and discuss at the interview.
programs.facilities: FEIT multimedia and audio/video processing laboratories (Katedra multimédií a informačno-komunikačných technológií). Specifics UNVERIFIED — ask whether there is studio access.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: YES. No music degree, conservatory training or performance ability is required or assessed. The interview tests IT knowledge plus creative output and motivation. CONFIRMED. Note the 0.75 coefficient penalty applies only to non-informatics bachelors, which should not affect him.
programs.englishTest: None required. Slovak is the operative language; no IELTS/TOEFL is demanded. CONFIRMED.
programs.tuitionEU: 0 EUR for full-time study in Slovak within the standard length of study. CONFIRMED.
programs.tuitionNonEU: 0 EUR — CONFIRMED verbatim from the faculty's own admission rules: 'Zahraniční študenti, ktorí študujú v slovenskom jazyku, školné neplatia.' As in the Czech Republic, the fee attaches to the language of instruction, not to nationality. A Tunisian national on this Slovak-taught Ing. programme pays zero tuition. Applicants admitted under intergovernmental agreements or as Slovak Government scholarship holders are governed by those documents.
programs.otherFees: Application fee still UNVERIFIED — not stated on the admission-conditions page; Slovak public universities typically charge 20-40 EUR. Check the e-application portal at https://vzdelavanie.uniza.sk/prijimacky/index.php. Žilina living costs are the lowest of the six, roughly 450-700 EUR/month.
programs.totalCostEstimate: Tuition 0. Realistic total ~11,000-17,000 EUR over two years, entirely living costs. Add a Slovak preparatory course if he takes UNIZA's. This remains the cheapest credible route of the six.
programs.scholarships: The Governmental Scholarships of the Slovak Republic is the full-degree funding vehicle for non-EU nationals and applies here. UNVERIFIED whether UNIZA offers its own entry scholarship — ask the FEIT study office.
programs.fundingLevel: Full (tuition free) — and potentially fully funded if combined with the Slovak Government Scholarship.
programs.intakes: One annual intake, September start. CONFIRMED.
programs.applicationOpens: Winter/spring preceding the academic year via the UNIZA e-application portal.
programs.deadline: CONFIRMED verbatim for the prior cycle: 'Termín podania prihlášky do 30. 4. 2026' for entry in 2026/2027. For SEPTEMBER 2027 entry expect ~30 April 2027 — later than his assumed Oct 2026 - Feb 2027 window. But the Slovak Government Scholarship application, if he pursues it, closes much earlier and is the real timeline driver. Decisions are posted within 30 days of the admission procedure.
programs.visaEligible: Yes — accredited public university, full-time Ing. programme, supports a Slovak temporary residence permit for study. Qualification recognition must be arranged by enrolment at the latest; UNIZA can perform the evaluation itself. CONFIRMED.
programs.recommendation: CONFIRMED AS THE BEST BALANCED OPTION, AND THE RE-CHECK MADE THE CASE STRONGER, NOT WEAKER. Every load-bearing claim held up against the official admission-conditions page, and the scoring is now exact rather than approximate: a 100-point scale in which his first-cycle GPA is worth up to 30 points at a full 1.0 coefficient (because Software Engineering sits in the informatics field), general IT and multimedia knowledge up to 40, and PRESENTATION OF HIS CREATIVE WORK AND MOTIVATION up to 30. That is the only admission process among the six where a portfolio-building year and an engineering degree are additive rather than in tension. Free tuition for a Tunisian, an explicit audio-processing elective track, no audition, no aural test, no music degree needed, and the lowest living costs of any option. The only real gate is Slovak at B1 with a certificate — and the faculty explicitly says the preparation and certificate can be obtained at UNIZA before the admission procedure, which is the mildest language pathway in the slice and genuinely reachable in the twelve-plus months before an April 2027 deadline. One practical caveat to plan for: the interview is held in person in Žilina. Actions: (1) enrol in Slovak now and target a B1 certificate by early 2027, ideally via UNIZA's own preparation so the certificate is unimpeachable; (2) e-mail the FEIT study office for the current 'Zásady a pravidlá prijímacieho konania' and ask what the creative portfolio must contain and whether his degree counts as the informatika field for the 1.0 coefficient; (3) run the Slovak Government Scholarship application in parallel. Rank this second only to ČVUT — and first if he is willing to learn a language.

programs.program: Design, lumină și sunet în artele spectacolului (Design, Light and Sound in the Performing Arts), studii universitare de masterat
programs.institution: Universitatea Națională de Artă Teatrală și Cinematografică „I.L. Caragiale" București (UNATC), Facultatea de Teatru
programs.publicPrivate: PUBLIC — CONFIRMED. State university under the Romanian Ministry of Education. Verified directly in Hotărârea Senatului nr. 290/27.05.2026, Anexa 1, signed by Rector Prof.univ.dr. Liviu Lucaci and Senate President Prof.univ.dr. Doru Nițescu — a published Senate fee decision with Ministry-allocated budget places is conclusive evidence of state status.
programs.institutionType: State film and theatre university. This programme sits in the Facultatea de TEATRU (domain: Teatru și artele spectacolului), not the Facultatea de Film.
programs.qualification: Diplomă de master — CONFIRMED genuine second-cycle degree (ciclul II). The Senate fee decision files it under 'II. TAXE DE STUDII – CICLUL II – STUDII UNIVERSITARE DE MASTERAT'. 120 ECTS confirmed on the official admissions page. Supports a student residence permit via the Ministry Letter of Acceptance route.
programs.accreditationStatus: CONFIRMED. ARACIS-accredited state university; programme listed on the official 2026-27 admissions portal (admitere.unatc.ro) and in the Senate fee schedule under Faculty of Theatre master's programmes.
programs.focus: Live sound design AND lighting design for the performing arts — the two are equally weighted, not sound-led.
programs.whatYouStudy: Lighting and sound design for stage. CORRECTED/SHARPENED: the official page describes the 3-hour written exam as two tasks involving analysis of lighting/sound design drawn from PLAYS (dramatic texts) plus graphic projection of design concepts. So the discipline is text-driven theatre design — reading a play and designing its light and sound — not studio production or electronic music.
programs.durationEcts: CONFIRMED: 2 years, 120 ECTS, full-time (învățământ cu frecvență).
programs.language: Romanian — CONFIRMED on the official programme page. No English track exists for this programme.
programs.languageRequirement: CONFIRMED via UNATC's own foreign-citizen admission page: non-EU applicants must complete a Romanian preparatory language year UNLESS they hold a minimum B1 Romanian certificate or have completed 4 years of prior study in Romanian. IELTS/TOEFL are irrelevant here — his untaken English tests neither help nor hurt.
programs.entryRequirements: Bachelor's degree (licență) plus diploma supplement, or a faculty certificate for 2026 graduates. CONFIRMED: no field restriction is published — a BSc Software Engineering satisfies the academic condition. Minimum admission mark 6.00/10 (average of the two exams), applying to both budget and fee-paying places. Non-EU applicants go through UNATC's foreign-citizen route with a Ministry of Education Letter of Acceptance.
programs.auditionSpec: CORRECTED ORDER AND DETAIL. Exam 1 is ORAL, 15 minutes, graded 1-10: a discussion based on his portfolio of representative works. Exam 2 is WRITTEN, 3 hours, graded 1-10: two tasks requiring analysis of lighting and sound design from plays plus graphic projection of design concepts. Final grade is the average of the two; minimum 6.00. Both conducted in Romanian. The written paper requires him to draw/diagram design concepts, not just write — an additional skill barrier the previous entry missed.
programs.portfolioSpec: MANDATORY — CONFIRMED. A personal artistic project (un proiect artistic personal) in the performing arts, sound and/or light, accompanied by a 3-5 page theoretical argument submitted in Word format. The required work is THEATRE/PERFORMANCE sound or light. Club tracks, DJ sets and studio production do not satisfy this. He would need to earn credits on actual student theatre productions.
programs.equipmentRequired: Not published — UNVERIFIED. The written exam is theoretical/graphic; the portfolio is documentation-based. Assume he supplies his own laptop and design software.
programs.facilities: Not published — UNVERIFIED. UNATC operates theatre venues and technical stages in Bucharest. Ask the Faculty of Theatre secretariat (secretariat@unatc.ro) for a written inventory before committing.
programs.tuitionEU: CONFIRMED EXACTLY: 8,000 lei per academic year. Verified in Hotărârea Senatului nr. 290/27.05.2026, Anexa 1, section II.1 (Master - Facultatea de Teatru), where 'Design, lumină și sunet în artele spectacolului' is listed at 8.000 lei alongside the other Theatre master's programmes. For comparison the Film Faculty's master's programmes are 13,750 lei — the previous entry's contrast was accurate.
programs.tuitionNonEU: STILL UNVERIFIED, AND I CONFIRM THE PREVIOUS AGENT'S CAUTION WAS CORRECT. I extracted the full text of the Senate decision: it contains no valutar, euro, or foreign-citizen rate anywhere across all six pages. The document covers licență, masterat, doctorat, postgraduate and enrolment fees in lei only. Do NOT assume 8,000 lei applies to him. For calibration, UBB Cluj's verified 2026-27 rate for the theatre domain is €750/month over 9 months (about €6,750/year). He must obtain the euro rate in writing from UNATC's International Students Office (study@unatc.ro) before budgeting.
programs.otherFees: CORRECTED — the previous entry marked this UNVERIFIED; it is now verified. Master's admission registration fee: 400 lei, per Hotărârea Senatului nr. 290, 'TAXE DE ÎNSCRIERE ÎN ANUL UNIVERSITAR 2026-2027', item 2, covering all programmes in both faculties. Optional admission preparation courses cost 150 lei per course (15% discount if paid in full). Additional: document legalisation, translation, Letter of Acceptance costs, and Bucharest living costs (UNVERIFIED).
programs.scholarships: Two Romanian government routes, both open to him in principle. (1) Romanian Government/MFA scholarships via scholarships.studyinromania.gov.ro — CONFIRMED requirement of a minimum study-years average of 7/10 or 'Good'; established under Government Decision no. 288/1993 for non-EU citizens. Deadline historically about 31 March with results about 15 July — PRIOR CYCLE, confirm. Critically for THIS programme the Romanian-only teaching rule is an advantage rather than an obstacle, since the programme is taught in Romanian and a preparatory Romanian year is granted to scholarship holders. (2) ARICE scholarships with the Ministry of Education, documents by email in the May-June window. PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new dates. Reality check: only 3 budget-funded and 3 fee-paying places exist in total — CONFIRMED on the official page — so even a funded applicant faces a 6-seat lottery.
programs.intakes: September (single annual intake).
programs.applicationOpens: 4 August 2026 for the 2026-27 cycle — CONFIRMED. PRIOR CYCLE, expect early August 2027 for his target intake.
programs.deadline: CONFIRMED AND EXPANDED: registration closes 9 September 2026; document verification 10-11 September; EXAMS 15-20 SEPTEMBER 2026; results per the exam schedule. The previous entry gave the 9 September registration deadline but omitted that he must be physically in Bucharest in mid-September for the exams. Scholarship deadlines are far earlier — about 31 March. PRIOR CYCLE - confirm all 2027 dates.
programs.visaEligible: Yes — CONFIRMED. UNATC operates a foreign-citizen admission route; the Ministry of Education (General Directorate for International Relations and European Affairs) issues the Letter of Acceptance, and UNATC's own guidance states the visa is issued on the basis of that letter plus full payment of the tuition fee. Note that last condition: he must pay the year's tuition up front to get the visa.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: YES on paper — CONFIRMED. A licență in any field is accepted and no music or arts degree clause is published. His BSc Software Engineering is formally sufficient. The real obstacles are elsewhere: a Romanian-language 3-hour written design exam, a live performing-arts portfolio he does not have, and 6 total places.
programs.totalCostEstimate: Domestic-rate scenario: 8,000 lei/year (about €1,600) × 2 years = about €3,200, plus 400 lei admission fee. Non-EU euro-rate scenario: UNVERIFIED, but if it tracks the regional arts norm of roughly €750/month × 9 months, budget about €6,750/year and about €13,500 over two years, plus a preparatory Romanian year if he lacks B1. Add Bucharest living costs. Fully covered if he wins a Romanian Government or ARICE scholarship.
programs.recommendation: CONFIRMED AS REAL, BUT DOWNGRADED — AND I HAVE FOUND HIM A STRICTLY BETTER PROGRAMME AT THE SAME UNIVERSITY. Everything structural checks out: it is a genuine ARACIS-accredited 120-ECTS second-cycle master's, the domestic tuition of 8,000 lei/year is confirmed verbatim in the Senate decision, the admission fee is 400 lei, and it is eligible for Romanian government scholarships whose Romanian-only teaching rule actually suits it. But it is a poor fit for HIM and I am rating it C rather than treating it as a serious second application. Four reasons. First, it is half lighting design, examined in a 3-hour written paper in Romanian that requires analysing plays and producing graphic design projections — a skill set he has no route to in one year. Second, the portfolio must be a live performing-arts project with a 3-5 page theoretical argument; club music and studio work do not qualify. Third, there are 6 places in total. Fourth and most importantly: THE SAME UNIVERSITY RUNS 'Interactive Technologies for Performing and Media Arts', a 120-ECTS MA taught entirely in ENGLISH, which explicitly welcomes applicants from science and engineering backgrounds, whose second admission test is a practical software demonstration in Processing, Max/MSP, TouchDesigner, Unity or Blender, and which accepts a 1500-2000 word English essay IN PLACE OF a portfolio for candidates who do not yet have one. That programme is 13,750 lei/year with 3 budget and 4 fee places, needs no Romanian at all, and its non-EU admission runs 10-27 June with an ONLINE exam option. For a Tunisian software engineer with no portfolio and no Romanian, that is a categorically better application than this one. He should apply to ITPMA and treat Design lumină și sunet as, at most, a throwaway second option only if he has by then genuinely built stage-sound credits.
