programs.program: Digital Interactive Arts (Arte digitale interactive), MA
programs.institution: Universitatea Babeș-Bolyai din Cluj-Napoca (UBB), Facultatea de Teatru și Film — Departamentul de Cinematografie și Media
programs.publicPrivate: PUBLIC — CONFIRMED. Romania's largest state university, ARACIS-accredited. Verified directly in the UBB Senate Regulation on fees for 2026-2027, which is structured as a Senate decision (abrogating Hotărârea Senatului nr. 13/17.02.2025 at art. 16) — conclusive evidence of state governance.
programs.institutionType: Comprehensive state university; Faculty of Theatre and Film, Department of Cinematography and Media
programs.qualification: Diplomă de master — genuine state-recognised second-cycle degree (ciclul II), accredited under the Bologna Process per the official programme page. Supports a non-EU student residence permit via the Ministry of Education Letter of Acceptance.
programs.accreditationStatus: ARACIS-accredited state university; the programme page states accreditation by the Romanian Ministry of Education under the Bologna Process. Listed among the English-taught master's programmes of the Cinematography and Media department.
programs.focus: Digital interactive arts / new media. Sound is a single elective, not the spine of the degree.
programs.whatYouStudy: CONFIRMED AND EXPANDED with the full four-semester curriculum. Semester I: Interactive Digital Performance, Production Management, Creative Performing Arts Project, plus electives in Visual Culture, Performance Theory or Practice as Research. Semester II: Creative Industries, Curatorial Models in Digital Media, Creative Visual Arts Project, plus electives in Augmented Reality or Visual Programming. Semester III: New Media Documentary, Creative Transmedia Project, Management and Marketing for Independent Artists, plus electives in Spectatorship Studies or Visual Storytelling. Semester IV: Academic Ethics, Directed Reading and Dissertation Writing, Digital Technologies in Art, plus electives in Sound Design or Interactive Media. CRITICAL: 'Sound Design for Digital Media' is an elective in SEMESTER IV ONLY — the final semester — and it competes with 'Interactive Media' for the same elective slot. So across a two-year degree he would take at most ONE sound course, in his last six months. The previous entry called sound 'one elective'; that is right, but it understated how late and how marginal it is. Note also 'Visual Programming' (Sem II elective) and 'Augmented Reality' — those play to his coding background more than the sound course does.
programs.durationEcts: 4 semesters (2 years), full-time. Total ECTS still NOT stated on the official programme page — UNVERIFIED. A Romanian two-year master's is normally 120 ECTS and UBB's fee regulation treats it as a standard masterat, but get this in writing from the faculty.
programs.language: ENGLISH — CONFIRMED on the official programme page, with the admission interview also 'conducted in English'. IMPORTANT CAVEAT DISCOVERED: the faculty's own tuition page lists Digital Interactive Arts under its Romanian-language programme listing. This is most likely an artefact of the Romanian version of the website rather than a second Romanian-taught cohort, but because the whole case for this programme rests on it being English-taught, he must confirm the teaching language in writing before applying.
programs.languageRequirement: English. The specific certificate and band remain UNVERIFIED — no English test requirement is stated anywhere on the programme page or in the admission criteria, and UBB's central non-EU degree-student page was unreachable (HTTP 404) at the time of checking. Because he has not taken IELTS or TOEFL, this is his single most urgent question. CORRECTED CONTACT: the programme page names Assistant Professor Cristina Pop-Tiron (cristina.pop-tiron@ubbcluj.ro) as the contact — the previous entry gave constantin.parvulescu@ubbcluj.ro and Prof. Rodica Mocan, which are not the contacts published on the current page. Faculty secretariat: +40 264 590 066 / +40 264 405 357. Confirmed advantage: no Romanian requirement and no preparatory Romanian year, since Romanian rules exempt students on foreign-language programmes.
programs.entryRequirements: CORRECTED AND IMPROVED — the previous entry said 'no field restriction published', which understated the case. The official page states the programme 'addresses graduate students in visual arts, architecture, music, theater, and film AND GRADUATES FROM OTHER FIELDS interested in a theoretical and practical interdisciplinary approach to new digital technologies in visual, performing, and cinematic arts.' So non-arts graduates are EXPLICITLY invited by name, not merely un-excluded. His BSc Software Engineering is squarely within the published eligibility. Non-EU applicants apply through UBB's Centrul de Cooperări Internaționale with a Ministry of Education Letter of Acceptance.
programs.auditionSpec: CONFIRMED AND EXPANDED. An ONLINE interview conducted in English — note 'online', which means no travel cost for the entrance exam, a real advantage over UNATC's Romanian-taught programmes. Assessment covers: ability to articulate the concept and relevance of the proposed project; domain knowledge; command of terminology; and general knowledge of cinema and media studies. That last criterion is new and worth flagging — he will be assessed on general cinema and media studies knowledge, an area where a software engineering graduate has no formal grounding and should read deliberately during his portfolio year.
programs.portfolioSpec: MANDATORY, TWO PARTS — CONFIRMED: (1) an individual artistic project, submitted in writing, demonstrating interest in interactive technologies, and (2) a portfolio of artistic works, either previous work or work related to the proposed project. The application is complete only on confirmed receipt of both. The project may be PROPOSED rather than completed — the interview tests whether he can argue its relevance. For a software engineer this remains among the most reachable portfolio requirements available: a generative music system, a reactive audio-visual installation, an audio plugin or a game-audio prototype all qualify and all build on skills he already has.
programs.equipmentRequired: Not published — UNVERIFIED. Assume a personal laptop capable of running Max/MSP, TouchDesigner or equivalent.
programs.facilities: Not published — UNVERIFIED, no inventory available. Direct this question to Cristina Pop-Tiron: what studio, lab and multi-channel audio facilities are actually available to master's students, and is the Sound Design elective taught with hardware or only in software?
programs.tuitionEU: Romanian/EU fee-paying and budget places per UBB's domestic schedule. Specific figure for this programme UNVERIFIED — see ubbcluj.ro/ro/taxe. Payment terms confirmed on the faculty page: four equal instalments (October, December, March, May), 10% discount for full payment by 15 October, late-payment penalty 0.04% per day.
programs.tuitionNonEU: €950 PER MONTH — CONFIRMED VERBATIM. I extracted the full text of the UBB Senate fee regulation and located Anexa nr. 4 ('Taxe de şcolarizare în valută ale cetăţenilor care studiază pe cont propriu în România, proveniți din state care nu sunt membre ale Uniunii Europene...'). Row 11 lists the Faculty of Theatre and Film split across two domains: 'domeniul teatru și artele spectacolului' at €750/month and 'domeniul cinematografie şi media' at €950/month, for masterat, învățământ cu frecvență. Digital Interactive Arts sits in the Department of Cinematography and Media, so €950/month is the rate he pays. Art. 15.2(a) confirms fees are payable over 9 months where the curriculum has no distinct practice period, or 10 months where it does. At 9 months that is €8,550/year and €17,100 over two years; at 10 months, €9,500/year and €19,000. The previous entry's figures were correct — but he should confirm in writing whether this curriculum triggers the 10-month rule, a €950/year difference, and separately confirm the domain classification, worth €1,800/year.
programs.otherFees: €50 non-refundable admission dossier processing fee for non-EU applicants — CONFIRMED VERBATIM at art. 15.1 of the Senate regulation: 'Pentru procesarea dosarului de admitere se va achita o taxă de 50 Euro, indiferent de nivelul de studiu sau forma de învățământ'. Art. 15.2(c) confirms tuition EXCLUDES accommodation and meals, and art. 15.4 confirms any other personal costs including housing, food and transport are the student's own. A separate dissertation defence fee applies per Anexa nr. 6 (amount UNVERIFIED). Add document legalisation, translation, Letter of Acceptance costs and Cluj-Napoca living costs.
programs.scholarships: The Romanian Government/MFA route (scholarships.studyinromania.gov.ro) is established under Government Decision no. 288/1993 for non-EU citizens and requires a minimum study-years average of 7/10 or 'Good' — CONFIRMED. But the critical catch stands and I could NOT resolve it: the MFA scheme's published rule is that bachelor's and master's beneficiaries study only in Romanian, with only doctoral holders permitted a foreign language, which would exclude an English-taught master's from MFA funding. The scholarship portal's public pages do not state the language rule explicitly, so this must be settled by direct enquiry. This single question decides whether the programme is a €17,100 self-pay or a funded option. ARICE may operate differently — verify separately. NOTE THE ASYMMETRY: the very feature that makes this programme accessible to him (English) may be what disqualifies it from the main Romanian scholarship, whereas UNATC's Romanian-taught programmes are scholarship-eligible but linguistically closed to him.
programs.intakes: September
programs.applicationOpens: Application 13-17 July 2026; exam 24 July 2026; final results 30 July 2026 (2026-27 cycle) — CONFIRMED. PRIOR CYCLE. Non-EU applicants must start months earlier for the Letter of Acceptance.
programs.deadline: 17 July 2026 for the 2026-27 cycle — CONFIRMED. For a September 2027 start expect a mid-July 2027 window, with the Ministry Letter of Acceptance process beginning several months earlier. PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new dates.
programs.visaEligible: Yes. UBB admits non-EU students on the 'cont propriu valutar' basis through its Centrul de Cooperări Internaționale, and Anexa nr. 4 of the Senate regulation exists precisely to price that category — institutional proof the route is live. The Ministry of Education Letter of Acceptance supports the Romanian long-stay study visa and student residence permit. Full-time (învățământ cu frecvență) status is confirmed, which is what the permit requires.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: YES, EXPLICITLY AND BY NAME — this is stronger than the previous entry claimed. The official page names 'graduates from other fields' as an intended audience alongside arts graduates. No music degree, no conservatoire training and no instrumental audition are required. Selection turns on an interactive-technology artistic project, which a software engineering graduate is unusually well placed to produce. Caveat: the interview also assesses general cinema and media studies knowledge, which he must read up on.
programs.totalCostEstimate: About €17,100 in tuition over two years (€950 × 9 months × 2), or about €19,000 if the 10-month practice rule applies, plus the €50 application fee, plus a dissertation defence fee, plus Cluj-Napoca living costs (UNVERIFIED, no official figure), plus IELTS/TOEFL costs. No preparatory language year needed, saving a full year of time and money relative to every Romanian-taught option.
programs.recommendation: CONFIRMED ACCURATE ON FEES AND ELIGIBILITY, BUT ITS HEADLINE CLAIM IS FALSE AND ITS RANKING MUST CHANGE. Everything financial checks out verbatim: €950/month for the cinematografie și media domain, 9-10 months a year, €50 dossier fee, all confirmed in Anexa nr. 4 and art. 15 of the UBB Senate regulation. Eligibility is better than previously described — the page explicitly invites 'graduates from other fields', so his BSc is named-in rather than merely not excluded. CORRECTION 1, and it is the important one: the previous entry asserted this is 'the ONLY English-taught programme with meaningful sound content found anywhere in Hungary, Romania or Bulgaria'. That is wrong. UNATC Bucharest runs at least five English-taught master's programmes — Design for New Media, Visual Effects, Audiovisual Preservation and Programming, Interactive Technologies for Performing and Media Arts, and Art of Game Design — all listed in its Senate fee decision at 13,750 lei per year, roughly €2,750, with budget places available. ITPMA in particular is a 120-ECTS English-taught MA that trains students in 'digitally controlling sound, light, image and code for the arts', explicitly welcomes science and engineering graduates, and accepts a 1500-2000 word essay in place of a portfolio. It costs roughly one third of this programme and has MORE sound content, not less. CORRECTION 2: the contact is Cristina Pop-Tiron, not the names previously given. CORRECTION 3: the Sound Design elective falls in semester IV and competes with Interactive Media for the same slot, so he may take at most one sound course, at the very end. Rating B rather than A: it is a legitimate, well-matched, visa-supporting degree with an online English entrance interview and no language-year penalty, but at €17,100 it is expensive for a programme where sound is a single final-semester elective, and its scholarship eligibility is unresolved. Actions in order: (1) apply to UNATC ITPMA as the primary Romanian target and treat this as the parallel application; (2) ask studyinromania.gov.ro in writing whether an English-taught master's can be MFA-funded; (3) ask Cristina Pop-Tiron what English certificate is required, whether the fee domain is cinematografie și media (€950) or teatru (€750), and whether the curriculum triggers 9 or 10 months of fees; (4) spend the portfolio year building ONE strong interactive audio project with proper documentation, which serves both applications.
programs.sourceUrl: https://teatrufilm.ubbcluj.ro/cinema-media-romana/master/digital-interactive-arts/ (official programme page: English teaching language, 4 semesters, full curriculum, eligibility wording including 'graduates from other fields', online English interview, portfolio and project requirements, contact Cristina Pop-Tiron, July 2026 dates) and https://www.ubbcluj.ro/ro/taxe/files/2026-2027/Regulament-privind-taxe-de-admitere_scolarizare_finalizare-a-studiilor-2026-2027.pdf (UBB Senate fee regulation 2026-27: art. 15.1 €50 dossier fee, art. 15.2 nine/ten-month payment rule, Anexa nr. 4 row 11 confirming €750/month teatru și artele spectacolului and €950/month cinematografie şi media at master's level) and https://teatrufilm.ubbcluj.ro/taxe-de-scolarizare/ (instalment schedule and 10% early-payment discount)

programs.program: Sound Design — szakirányú továbbképzés (postgraduate specialist training). WARNING: THIS IS NOT A MASTER'S DEGREE.
programs.institution: Moholy-Nagy Művészeti Egyetem (MOME) / Moholy-Nagy University of Art and Design
programs.publicPrivate: PUBLIC-FOUNDATION — CONFIRMED as previously described. MOME operates under the Hungarian 'közfeladatot ellátó közérdekű vagyonkezelő alapítvány' (public-interest asset management foundation) model introduced in 2021. It is a state-recognised university in the Hungarian higher-education register and hosts Stipendium Hungaricum places on its DEGREE programmes, but it is no longer directly state-maintained and sets fees commercially. Not a private company, not a church institution, not a diploma mill.
programs.institutionType: University of art and design
programs.qualification: NOT A MASTER'S DEGREE — CONFIRMED. The award is a szakirányú továbbképzés (postgraduate specialist training) qualification. It requires a prior degree to enter and does issue an oklevél, but it does NOT confer a mesterfokozat (second-cycle master's degree) and sits outside the Bologna second cycle. WATCH THE MARKETING: Hungarian press coverage launched it as 'Magyarország első diplomát adó Sound Design képzése' — Hungary's first degree-granting sound design programme. In Hungarian usage 'diploma' here means the specialist-training oklevél, NOT a master's degree. Anyone reading that headline in translation will be misled. A two-semester szakirányú továbbképzés is typically 60 credits, half a master's volume.
programs.accreditationStatus: A genuine accredited Hungarian szakirányú továbbképzés at a state-recognised university — not a scam. But categorically outside the Bologna second cycle. It is marketed in English under a menu called 'Programmes' alongside genuine MA courses, which is exactly how a careful applicant gets caught.
programs.focus: Sound design for film, games and spatial audio
programs.whatYouStudy: CONFIRMED. Three core areas: film sound, video game sound design, and spatial sound composition, taught through practical projects so participants build a portfolio during the course. Combines industry-standard software training with theoretical grounding in art history, positioning graduates as 'applied artists'. Led by sound artist Krasz Ádám (director of MOME TechPark) and Hajnóczy Csaba DLA. Instruction covers Pro Tools and Ableton.
programs.durationEcts: 1 year / 2 semesters, delivered as an EVENING course (esti) — CONFIRMED by both MOME's own English page and independent Hungarian press, which describe flexible weekly contact hours specifically so the course can be completed alongside employment. Credit total not published — UNVERIFIED, but a two-semester szakirányú továbbképzés is normally 60 credits. Part-time evening delivery is by itself disqualifying for a Hungarian study residence permit.
programs.language: HUNGARIAN — CONFIRMED. MOME's own English-language programme page states 'Language: Hungarian'. There is no English track. Teaching, application documents and the admission interview are all in Hungarian. His Arabic, French and English are of no use here.
programs.languageRequirement: Hungarian. No formal certificate level is published — UNVERIFIED — but the motivation letter, CV and admission interview are conducted in Hungarian, so functional Hungarian is required in practice. IELTS and TOEFL are irrelevant and will not help him.
programs.entryRequirements: Formally: a completed bachelor's, master's, or university/college-level degree ('Alap- vagy mesterfokozat, illetve egyetemi vagy főiskolai szintű végzettség'), so his BSc satisfies the paper condition. SUBSTANTIVELY he is excluded: applicants must already be familiar with at least one DAW at working level (Pro Tools and Ableton are the taught tools), must already have sound-design and music-theory fundamentals, and must supply a professional portfolio. The programme is explicitly aimed at people already working in sound, media, filmmaking, game development or creative fields, plus career-changers who already hold visual/media arts or design qualifications.
programs.auditionSpec: Three stages: (1) online application form; (2) document upload; (3) admission interview in Hungarian. For the 2026 intake interviews were held 3-4 September 2026, with only the strongest applicants invited on the strength of motivation letters and portfolios. PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new dates.
programs.portfolioSpec: MANDATORY. Required uploads: motivation letter (max 1 A4 page), CV, a PROFESSIONAL PORTFOLIO of existing work — explicitly a showreel or previous musical works, maximum 100 MB — and a scanned degree certificate. He has no portfolio and could not submit an application today. Unlike UNATC ITPMA and UBB Digital Interactive Arts, there is NO essay or proposed-project alternative.
programs.equipmentRequired: Working knowledge of at least one DAW is an explicit entry condition; Pro Tools and Ableton Live are the taught tools. Personal laptop assumed.
programs.facilities: MOME operates the MOME Sonic Studio and a Spatial Experimentation Studio, and the course runs out of MOME TechPark — genuinely strong spatial-audio facilities by regional standards. This is the one respect in which the programme is better than its rivals. No published equipment inventory — partly UNVERIFIED.
programs.tuitionEU: 790,000 HUF per semester, self-funded (önköltséges), so 1,580,000 HUF for the full two-semester course — CONFIRMED. Roughly €4,000 at prevailing rates, but the published figure is in forint and the conversion should not be relied on.
programs.tuitionNonEU: The SAME 790,000 HUF per semester. MOME publishes a single self-funded rate for this course with no separate international tier, so his rate as a Tunisian national is 1,580,000 HUF total. This does not make it accessible — the barriers are language, format and immigration status, not price.
programs.otherFees: A non-refundable special procedure fee of 5,000 HUF per application; non-payment excludes the applicant from the admission procedure entirely. NEW WARNING — A SECOND, SEPARATE TRAP AT THE SAME UNIVERSITY: MOME Open (open.mome.hu/sound-design) sells a DIFFERENT and much weaker 'Sound Design' short course at 450,000 HUF + 27% VAT = 571,500 HUF gross. It consists of 10 theory sessions (Mon/Wed 17:00-20:30), 4 practical workshops and 6 weeks of personalised practice, entry requires only a secondary school diploma plus basic solfège and basic DAW skills, and it is NOT a szakirányú továbbképzés and NOT accredited higher education at all. Its lower price and lower entry bar make it look like an easier way in. It is not — it is a paid short course with no qualification value and no immigration value whatsoever. He must not confuse the two.
programs.scholarships: NONE for this course. Stipendium Hungaricum does NOT fund it. Tunisia IS an eligible Stipendium Hungaricum sending partner — the Tunisian Republic is named in the official 2026/27 Call with the Ministère de l'Enseignement Supérieur as sending partner, deadline 15 January, covering a monthly stipend, an accommodation contribution, a tuition waiver and medical insurance — but the Call restricts postgraduate specialist training and partial study to particular frameworks, and applicants may apply only in the study fields fixed in the Hungary-Tunisia bilateral educational cooperation programme. A Hungarian-taught, part-time, non-degree evening course is not a realistic Stipendium Hungaricum target. Check the Tunisia entry at stipendiumhungaricum.hu/partners/ for the exact agreed fields, since that route may still be worth pursuing for a genuine MA elsewhere in Hungary.
programs.intakes: September (the 2026 cohort started 14 September 2026). PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date.
programs.applicationOpens: Application form deadline 24 August 2026; document upload deadline 27 August 2026; interviews 3-4 September 2026 (2026 intake). PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new dates.
programs.deadline: 24 August 2026 for the 2026 intake. PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date.
programs.visaEligible: ALMOST CERTAINLY NOT — CONFIRMED, and for two independent reasons, either of which is fatal. (1) It is a szakirányú továbbképzés, not a degree programme. (2) It is delivered as a part-time EVENING course, verified against both MOME's own page and independent Hungarian press coverage, and Hungarian study residence permits require full-time (nappali) enrolment in a degree programme. Do not apply expecting a student residence permit. If he wants it in writing, ask MOME's international office whether the course issues the enrolment certificate accepted by the National Directorate-General for Aliens Policing — but expect no.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: Formally yes, substantively no. Any bachelor's satisfies the paper condition and no music degree is named, so his BSc technically qualifies. But he must already possess sound-design and music-theory fundamentals, already work fluently in a DAW, and already hold a professional showreel or body of musical work. This is a specialisation course for practising professionals, not an entry route.
programs.totalCostEstimate: 1,580,000 HUF tuition plus 5,000 HUF application fee, plus Budapest living costs, plus whatever it costs to reach functional Hungarian — with no degree and no residence permit at the end of it. Not a viable expenditure.
programs.recommendation: CONFIRMED IN FULL — DO NOT PURSUE. I re-verified every load-bearing fact and the previous assessment holds without correction: szakirányú továbbképzés not a master's, Hungarian-only, evening/part-time, 790,000 HUF per semester, professional portfolio and working DAW skills required on entry. AVOID is the right verdict, and the reason matters: MOME charges 1,580,000 HUF — genuine master's money in this region, more than a year at UNATC's English-taught MAs — for something that is NOT an accredited second-cycle degree and will NOT support a student residence permit. That is the exact pattern the brief asks to be called out. It will surface prominently in any search he runs: marketed in English, on a well-known university's site, under a menu called 'Programmes', launched with press coverage calling it 'Hungary's first degree-granting sound design programme', covering precisely his interests with genuinely excellent spatial-audio facilities. It fails on four independent grounds, any one of which ends it: not a master's; taught wholly in Hungarian with a Hungarian interview; part-time evening delivery that blocks the visa; and an existing professional showreel plus working Pro Tools and Ableton skills he does not have and cannot fake. ONE NEW WARNING I ADD: MOME Open separately sells a cheaper 571,500 HUF 'Sound Design' short course requiring only a secondary school diploma. It is not accredited higher education at all and is an even worse trap precisely because it looks easier to get into. He should engage with MOME only for its full MA programmes, where Stipendium Hungaricum money is genuinely available to Tunisian nationals — noting that MOME's Média design MA is not offered in English, and Budapest Metropolitan University's Media Design MA states plainly 'We do not offer this course in English'. Hungary is largely closed to him for audio at master's level; Romania, via UNATC's English-taught MAs, is not.
programs.sourceUrl: https://mome.hu/en/programmes/sound-design (official MOME programme page: 'Qualification: Specialist training', 'Night course', 'Language: Hungarian', '790 000 Ft / félév - Önköltséges') and https://mome.hu/hu/sound-design-jelentkezes (official application page: entry conditions, portfolio requirement, deadlines, 5,000 Ft procedure fee) and https://open.mome.hu/sound-design/ (the separate, non-accredited MOME Open short course at 450,000 Ft + VAT = 571,500 Ft gross, evening 17:00-20:30, secondary-school-diploma entry) and https://magyar.film.hu/filmhu/hir/sound-design-szakiranyu-kepzeset-indit-a-mome.html (independent confirmation of szakirányú status, one-year duration, evening/flexible format, target audience)

programs.program: Regie muzicală (Music Directing / Sound Direction) — studii postuniversitare. WARNING: THIS IS NOT A MASTER'S DEGREE.
programs.institution: Universitatea Națională de Muzică din București (UNMB) / National University of Music Bucharest
programs.publicPrivate: PUBLIC — CONFIRMED. State university of music under the Romanian Ministry of Education. The completion certificate is co-issued by the Ministry of Education and UNMB, which is itself proof of state status. UNMB also publishes its own 'Metodologia admitere cetățeni străini NON-UE 2026-2027', the standard apparatus of a Romanian state university.
programs.institutionType: State music university (national conservatoire)
programs.qualification: NOT A MASTER'S DEGREE — CONFIRMED VERBATIM. The award is a 'certificat de competență profesională' (professional competency certificate) for the occupation of music director, C.O.R. code 265228, issued jointly by the Ministry of Education and UNMB. It is officially inscribed in the National Registry of Postgraduate Programmes, so it is a real state-registered qualification and NOT a scam — but it is a postgraduate professional certificate, not a second-cycle (ciclul II) degree, and confers no master's.
programs.accreditationStatus: Genuine and state-registered (Registrul Național al Programelor Postuniversitare; Ministry-issued certificate), but categorically outside the Bologna second cycle. This is precisely the category the brief warns about: a real, reputable institution selling a real but non-degree postgraduate award whose name reads like a master's in exactly the field he is searching.
programs.focus: Music directing / sound direction (classical tonmeister discipline)
programs.whatYouStudy: Music direction (regie muzicală), the classical Romanian tonmeister discipline. Detailed syllabus not published on the official page — UNVERIFIED. The entrance exam content is itself the clearest evidence of the discipline's nature: melodic dictation, notation of transposing instruments, timbral hearing and instrument recognition. This is built entirely on classical-music aural skill. There is nothing here about electronic production, DJing, DAWs or club music.
programs.durationEcts: CONFIRMED VERBATIM: 146 contact hours, 15 ECTS, in-person attendance. For scale, a genuine Romanian master's is 120 ECTS over two years — at 15 ECTS this is one-eighth of a master's. It is a short professional course.
programs.language: Romanian — CONFIRMED. Instruction is explicitly delivered in Romanian, in person.
programs.languageRequirement: Not separately published — UNVERIFIED — but since teaching is in Romanian and the entrance exam is oral and written in Romanian, Romanian competence is required in practice. IELTS/TOEFL are irrelevant. UNMB does publish a non-EU admission methodology; ask its postgraduate office whether that route even applies to postuniversitare courses.
programs.entryRequirements: A bachelor's degree or equivalent — CONFIRMED. No music degree is formally named, but the entrance exam assumes conservatoire-level aural training, which functions as a de facto music-degree requirement.
programs.auditionSpec: DISQUALIFYING FOR THIS CANDIDATE — CONFIRMED IN SHARPER DETAIL THAN PREVIOUSLY RECORDED. Two components. (1) WRITTEN test: melodic dictation of up to 16 measures with a key signature of up to two sharps or flats, plus identification and notation of transposing instruments. (2) ORAL exam: identifying instrument timbres by ear and answering related questions. Taking a 16-bar melodic dictation in up to two accidentals is a skill built over years of formal solfège; identifying transposing instruments and their written-versus-sounding pitches is standard conservatoire theory. Someone with no music degree, no conservatoire training and one year of self-study will not pass this.
programs.portfolioSpec: None specified — CONFIRMED. The gate is the aural-skills examination, not a portfolio. Which is worse for him, not better: a portfolio he could build in a year, an ear he cannot.
programs.equipmentRequired: Not published — UNVERIFIED.
programs.facilities: UNMB operates a Centre for Electronic Music and studio facilities, and runs a separate optional module 'Producție Muzicală în Studioul de Muzică Electronică' for its own students. Facilities inventory UNVERIFIED. Note that module is for enrolled UNMB students and is not a standalone entry route.
programs.tuitionEU: 8,000 lei for Romanian participants, payable in three instalments — CONFIRMED.
programs.tuitionNonEU: €1,600 for international participants, payable in three instalments — CONFIRMED VERBATIM on the official page. This is the rate he would pay as a Tunisian national, and it is one of the very few places in this sweep where a distinct non-EU figure is actually published rather than inferred. It is cheap because the course is short and non-degree, not because it is good value for him.
programs.otherFees: 100 RON registration fee (taxă de înscriere) plus 150 RON enrolment fee (taxă de înmatriculare) — CONFIRMED.
programs.scholarships: None. Romanian Government/MFA and ARICE scholarships fund licență, masterat and doctorat cycles at accredited institutions. A 15-ECTS postgraduate certificate is not a study cycle and would not be covered. Do not expect funding.
programs.intakes: Not published on the official programme page — UNVERIFIED. Ask UNMB's Studii Postuniversitare office.
programs.applicationOpens: Not published — UNVERIFIED. Ask UNMB.
programs.deadline: Not published — UNVERIFIED. Ask UNMB's Studii Postuniversitare office. Moot in practice, given everything below.
programs.visaEligible: ALMOST CERTAINLY NOT. A 146-hour, 15-ECTS postgraduate certificate is not a degree programme and will not support a Romanian long-stay study visa or student residence permit for a third-country national. Romania's Letter of Acceptance machinery is built around the licență, masterat and doctorat cycles. Do not plan a move to Romania around this.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: NO in practice — CONFIRMED. The formal condition is only a bachelor's degree in any field, but the entrance examination requires 16-bar melodic dictation, notation of transposing instruments, and aural timbre and instrument recognition. These are conservatoire skills. Without a music background he would fail the exam, and no amount of DAW proficiency substitutes.
programs.totalCostEstimate: €1,600 tuition plus 250 RON in fees, plus Bucharest living costs for the duration. Irrelevant in practice, since it confers no degree and supports no residence permit.
programs.recommendation: CONFIRMED IN FULL, NO CORRECTIONS NEEDED — DO NOT PURSUE. I re-checked every figure against the official UNMB page and all of them are exact: 146 hours, 15 ECTS, Romanian instruction, 8,000 lei domestic and €1,600 international in three instalments, 100 RON registration plus 150 RON enrolment, certificate of professional competency C.O.R. 265228 registered in the National Registry of Postgraduate Programmes. This entry was accurate. AVOID stands. Searching 'music direction Romania master' or 'regie muzicală' leads straight here, at Romania's national music university, at an apparently affordable €1,600 for international students. It is not a master's degree. It is a 146-hour, 15-ECTS professional certificate — one-eighth the volume of a real second-cycle degree — it will not support a student residence permit, it is taught in Romanian, and its entrance exam is a conservatoire aural test (16-bar melodic dictation in up to two accidentals, transposing-instrument notation, timbral recognition) that he cannot pass without years of solfège. The low price signals what it is; it is not a bargain. Note also that UNMB's genuine master's portfolio contains NO sound-technology programme: the Faculty of Composition, Musicology and Music Pedagogy offers only Stil și limbaj compozițional, Sinteză muzicologică, Stilistică dirijorală, Jazz și culturi muzicale pop, Educație muzicală contemporană and Culturi muzicale religioase, and the Faculty of Musical Interpretation offers only performance-stylistics masters. UNMB is a dead end for him and should be closed off entirely — the Romanian opening is at UNATC, whose English-taught MAs need no Romanian and no conservatoire ear.

programs.focus: Game audio / sound design
programs.whatYouStudy: Sound engineering and sound design for video games. Interview syllabus (unchanged 2025/26 → 2026/27): (1) physical acoustics, behaviour of sound in space, sound phenomena; (2) sound-technical devices — electroacoustic transducers, mixing desks, amplifiers, processors; (3) spatial sound formats; (4) computer and electronic music technologies. programs.durationEcts: CORRECTED. Not 'two years only'. The 2026/2027 handbook offers this specialty as 'една или две учебни години' — ONE OR TWO academic years. The handbook also resolves the previously unverified credit total: one-year master's = minimum 60 credits (for holders of a bachelor's in the SAME specialty); two-year master's = minimum 120 credits (ECTS).
programs.language: Bulgarian. CONFIRMED — no English-taught track for this specialty.
programs.languageRequirement: CONFIRMED. Foreigners must demonstrate Bulgarian ('За чужденците се изисква да владеят български език'), by one of three routes: (1) a document issued by a Bulgarian higher-education institution; (2) passing written AND oral Bulgarian examinations before a commission appointed by the NMA Rector; or (3) completing NMA's one-year preparatory course in language and specialised preparation, which ends with examinations in all subjects including written and oral Bulgarian. IELTS/TOEFL are irrelevant and not accepted.
programs.entryRequirements: CORRECTED — AND THIS REVERSES THE PREVIOUS RECORD'S CENTRAL FINDING. The 2026/2027 handbook, section IX, states verbatim: „Специалност „Звукорежисура и звуков дизайн за игри“, срок на обучение две години. Необходимо е кандидатът да притежава музикална образователно-квалификационна степен „Бакалавър“.“ A MUSIC bachelor's degree IS now required for the two-year track. The one-year track is worse: it requires a bachelor's specifically in „Звукорежисура, звуков и медиен дизайн“, and external candidates must have graduated in „Звукорежисура“ at another HEI. The previous agent's finding rested on the 2025/2026 handbook, where the clause was genuinely absent — I checked both PDFs side by side and the clause was ADDED for 2026/2027. Additional hard requirement for foreign-diploma holders: documents for the Bulgarian recognition procedure must be filed with the Учебен отдел during the academic year PRECEDING application and at least two months before the candidate documents themselves.
programs.auditionSpec: Single-stage oral interview (събеседване) on the four technical topics. No instrumental audition, no solfège. Format CONFIRMED unchanged for 2026/2027 — but now academically out of reach for him.
programs.portfolioSpec: CONFIRMED — no portfolio is demanded by the published exam programme for external candidates; admission is by interview on the technical syllabus. (NMA's own graduating students are instead admitted on their diploma-project defence: an independent sound-recording product plus a written theoretical exposition.)
programs.equipmentRequired: Not stated in the 2026/2027 handbook. Ask the ТКДФ office (sbogdanova@nma.bg, 0882 33 50 43).
programs.facilities: Not published for this specialty. NMA operates sound-engineering studios; no equipment inventory is published. Ask the department.
programs.tuitionEU: State-commissioned (държавна поръчка) places, free of tuition, for Bulgarian/EU candidates; minimum grade Мн. добър 4.50 on each entrance/state exam to be ranked for them. Fee-paying places require minimum Добър 4.00. The domestic fee-paying rate is not published in the handbook.
programs.tuitionNonEU: €8,500 per academic year — CONFIRMED VERBATIM on NMA's official non-EU page: „За магистратура – 8500 евро“. This is the rate he would pay as a Tunisian national. Preparatory language year: €5,500. (For reference: bachelor €7,000, doctorate €10,000.) Non-EU nationals are NOT eligible for state-subsidised places.
programs.otherFees: CORRECTED. The candidate application fee is €100 / 195.58 BGN — not '100 leva'. The 300 BGN/€153.39 and 450 BGN/€230.08 figures the previous record cited are the fees for the RECOGNITION PROCEDURE for a foreign master's-level qualification (standard vs. after-deadline/expedited), not the application fee. Bulgarian-language examination fee €50. Legalisation, apostille and certified Bulgarian translation of all foreign documents, plus NACID recognition, are additional. Sofia living costs additional and not published.
programs.scholarships: None a Tunisian national can win. State-subsidised places are closed to non-EU nationals. The ПМС 103/1993 and ПМС 228/1997 channels require Bulgarian origin or North Macedonian citizenship; ПМС 264/2024 requires temporary-protection status in Bulgaria. Only theoretical route: a Bulgaria–Tunisia bilateral education agreement — enquire at the Bulgarian Embassy in Tunis. Treat as fully self-funded.
programs.englishTest: None. No IELTS or TOEFL is required or accepted anywhere in this admission. His untaken English test is irrelevant here — which is not an advantage, because the substitute demand is certified Bulgarian.

Non-EU direct admission (without preparatory course): до 12 юни 2026 г. Non-EU with preparatory course: до 25 юни, then 1–3 September. programs.deadline: For a September 2027 start, expect the same shape: ТКДФ documents late May – early June 2027, non-EU direct-admission deadline around 12 June 2027. Exact 2027 dates publish on nma.bg/priem each spring. Because foreign-diploma recognition must start a full academic year earlier, the real deadline for him would have been autumn 2026.
programs.visaEligible: Yes in principle — NMA runs a published „извън ЕС“ channel producing the MES Certificate of Acceptance required for a Bulgarian type-D visa and student residence permit. Irrelevant in his case because he cannot clear the academic entry rule.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: NO — CORRECTED. This is the single most important change to the previous record. The 2026/2027 official handbook explicitly requires a MUSIC bachelor's for the two-year track, and a sound-engineering bachelor for the one-year track. A BSc Software Engineering is not an eligible entry qualification for either. The previous record's headline claim ('unlike Musicology/Composition/Conducting, the sound-engineering specialties carry NO such clause') was true of the 2025/2026 handbook and is false for 2026/2027.
programs.totalCostEstimate: Moot — he is ineligible. For reference had he qualified: €17,000 tuition over two years, plus €5,500 if the preparatory language year were needed, plus €100 application, €50 language exam, ~€153–230 recognition fee, plus Sofia living costs.
programs.recommendation: PREVIOUS RECORD OVERTURNED — HE IS NOT ELIGIBLE. The 2025/2026 handbook did not require a music bachelor's for this specialty; the 2026/2027 handbook, section IX, does, in the same boilerplate sentence used for Musicology, Composition and Conducting. I verified this by extracting and comparing both official PDFs directly. Unless NMA reverses the clause again for 2027/2028 — worth one email to sbogdanova@nma.bg, but do not plan around it — a BSc Software Engineering graduate cannot apply. Everything that made this look like the best academic match in the sweep (technical interview instead of an audition, no portfolio, game audio and spatial sound content) is now behind a door he cannot open, and even if it reopened, the €8,500/year with no winnable scholarship and the certified-Bulgarian requirement would still stand. Remove it from the shortlist.

This specialty keeps its own separate, much later calendar: for 2026/2027 — documents 14–25 September 2026; document review, exams and interview 28–29 September 2026; results 30 September 2026; enrolment 1–2 October 2026; classes begin 5 October 2026. (The previous record's '15–19 September 2025 / exams 23–24 September' was the superseded 2025/26 cycle.) The rest of ТКДФ runs 26 May – 4 June.
programs.deadline: Expect mid-to-late September 2027 for a September/October 2027 start. This is the programme's real problem for him: a mid-September application decided on 30 September leaves no time to obtain a Certificate of Acceptance, a type-D visa and a residence permit before teaching begins on ~5 October. Non-EU applicants who studied in Bulgaria have separate 1–15 June and 1–15 September windows. Raise the sequencing with the international office before committing.
programs.visaEligible: Yes in principle via the MES Certificate of Acceptance route — but the September calendar sits badly against Bulgarian visa processing. Treat as a live risk, not a formality.

programs.totalCostEstimate: ~€17,000 tuition over two years, plus ~€5,500 if a preparatory language year is required, plus ~€300–400 in application, recognition and language-exam fees, plus Sofia living costs (not published; budget separately).
programs.recommendation: THE ONLY BULGARIAN DOOR STILL OPEN TO HIM — AND IT LEADS TO THE WRONG ROOM. Now that the game-audio specialty has closed to non-music graduates, this is the sole programme at either Bulgarian academy that a software-engineering graduate can legally enter. It is a real, accredited, state-recognised master's; no music degree, no audition, no portfolio. But the verified syllabus is narrower and more local than the previous record suggested: it is about how Bulgarian music organisations are financed and run, the role of Bulgarian state and municipal cultural institutes, and the professions of the Bulgarian music sector — assessed in a Bulgarian-language interview plus a motivation discussion. It teaches him nothing about sound design, production craft or electronic music, which is what he says he wants and what his portfolio year is meant to build. Add €8,500/year with no scholarship he can win, mandatory certified Bulgarian, and an application window that closes five days before term starts. Keep it on the list only as evidence that Bulgaria has been checked properly, not as a plan.

programs.entryRequirements: CORRECTED — THE DECISIVE UNKNOWN IS NOW ANSWERED, AND THE ANSWER IS NO. The official 2026/2027 candidate handbook, p. 34, states the conditions verbatim: „Условия към кандидатите: - да са придобили степен „Бакалавър“ в сферата на музикалното изкуство; - не се допускат кандидати с трайни слухови нарушения.“ A bachelor's IN THE FIELD OF MUSICAL ART is required, and candidates with permanent hearing impairments are excluded. A BSc Software Engineering does not qualify. Separately confirmed: holders of foreign higher-education diplomas must have COMPLETED the Bulgarian academic-recognition procedure at the moment of submitting master's documents.
programs.auditionSpec: CORRECTED — the previously 'UNVERIFIED' exam is published, and it is a three-stage examination including an ear test. Stage I: aural analysis of fragments of musical works — (a) identifying the instruments sounding in a given recording; (b) determining the amplitude-frequency differences between two recordings of the same work. Stage II: a written test on the specialty (sample questions cover tone vs. noise, dynamic and tempo terminology, what determines timbre, WAV and AIFF, mono/stereo/surround, whether MIDI is digital, MIDI technology and what it transmits, master keyboard, balanced vs. unbalanced cable, ADC/DAC converters, the sampling rate and bit depth of standard audio CD) plus an interview. Stage III: interview with the commission on electroacoustic transducers (microphones and loudspeakers), computer systems, hardware, software and peripherals, musical acoustics and sound engineering. Stages I and III are effectively a trained-ear audition — the written test alone is preparable by a software engineer, the aural analysis is not, without ear training.
programs.portfolioSpec: No portfolio is required — CONFIRMED. The exam is aural, written and oral. This is not the advantage it looks like: the aural stage is harder for him than a portfolio would be.

Редовно обучение - 7600 евро“. This is the rate he would pay as a Tunisian national. Bulgarian diploma-recognition procedure, apostille, legalisation and certified translation costs are additional and unpublished. Plovdiv living costs additional — materially cheaper than Sofia.

Irrelevant to him because he fails the academic condition.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: NO — CORRECTED from UNVERIFIED. The 2026/2027 official handbook requires a bachelor's degree in the field of musical art. This closes the programme to him.
programs.totalCostEstimate: Moot — he is ineligible. For reference: ~€11,400 tuition for 1.5 years full-time, plus €4,600 if the language course is required, plus €24 candidate fee and recognition/translation costs, plus Plovdiv living.
programs.recommendation: THE OPEN QUESTION IS ANSWERED AND IT RULES HIM OUT. The previous record correctly identified 'is a music bachelor's required?' as the question on which everything turned, and correctly refused to guess. AMTII's official 2026/2027 candidate handbook answers it on page 34: a bachelor's in the field of musical art is required. Two further published facts, both previously unverified, reinforce the verdict — the entrance examination has three stages including an aural analysis (identify the instruments in a recording; hear amplitude-frequency differences between two masters of the same piece), and candidates with permanent hearing impairments are excluded. Even setting the degree rule aside, an untrained ear would not pass stage I. There is no scholarship route: every channel AMTII operates requires Bulgarian origin, North Macedonian citizenship or temporary-protection status. Substantively this was the best studio-craft curriculum in the Bulgarian set and the cheapest per year in the cheapest city — it is simply not available to him. Drop it; do not spend the year emailing the Учебен отдел about it.

programs.program: Медийно музикално редакторство (Media Music Editing), магистър
programs.institution: Академия за музикално, танцово и изобразително изкуство „Проф. Асен Диамандиев“ – Пловдив (AMTII Plovdiv)
programs.publicPrivate: PUBLIC — CONFIRMED. Same evidence as Тонрежисура: admission based on Arts. 21 and 68 ЗВО, foreign-student fees under Art. 95(8) ЗВО, ПМС government channels, published NEAA institutional accreditation, MES founding authority.

programs.focus: Music for media / radio and broadcast editing
programs.whatYouStudy: CONFIRMED from the official specialty page. Studied disciplines: Музикална публицистика, Музикално оформление, Съвременна музикална култура, Методика на работа в медии, Практика в радио, Практика в телевизия, Звукотехника, Звукови монтажи, История и стилове в поп и джаз музиката, Реторика, Техника на говора, Музика и медии, Реклама и медии, Чужд език. programs.durationEcts: 1 year full-time (редовна) after a bachelor's — CONFIRMED on the specialty page and in the 2026/2027 handbook. ECTS total not published.
programs.language: Bulgarian, and more so than any other programme in this set — the curriculum is built on Bulgarian-language journalism, rhetoric, speech technique and radio/TV practice, and the entrance test itself examines Bulgarian orthography and punctuation.
programs.languageRequirement: No separate certificate is published, but the entrance examination functions as a native-level Bulgarian test in its own right (see auditionSpec). AMTII prices a €4,600 Езиков курс. Confirm with uchebenotdel@artacademyplovdiv.com. IELTS/TOEFL irrelevant.
programs.entryRequirements: CORRECTED — previously UNVERIFIED. The official 2026/2027 handbook, p. 35, states verbatim: „Условия към кандидатите: - да са придобили степен „Бакалавър“ в областта на музикалното изкуство; - не се допускат кандидати с трайни говорни, гласови и слухови нарушения.“ A bachelor's IN THE FIELD OF MUSICAL ART is required, and candidates with permanent speech, voice or hearing impairments are excluded. Foreign-diploma holders must have completed the Bulgarian academic-recognition procedure before submitting documents.
programs.auditionSpec: CORRECTED — the exam is published and is doubly disqualifying. Stage I, a test of linguistic and musical culture: (1) correcting spelling errors in given Bulgarian words; (2) explaining the meaning of given musical terms; (3) correcting punctuation and factual errors in a given Bulgarian text; (4) aural recognition of well-known Bulgarian and foreign performers and groups (Elvis Presley, The Beatles, Deep Purple, Queen, Pink Floyd, U2, Madonna, Eminem, Rihanna, Lady Gaga and others). Stage II: an oral test of speech technique in front of a microphone, plus an interview. Ranking is the arithmetic mean of the two stages; a mark below Добър 4.00 fails. A non-native speaker cannot pass a Bulgarian orthography-and-punctuation correction test or a Bulgarian microphone speech-technique assessment.
programs.portfolioSpec: No portfolio required — CONFIRMED. Irrelevant given the language exam.
programs.equipmentRequired: Not published.
programs.facilities: Curriculum implies access to radio and television studios, a recording studio and reporter field equipment. No published inventory.

Part-time €4,200 exists but will generally not support a residence permit. This remains the lowest total-tuition figure of any real master's in the Bulgarian set, purely because the programme is one year long.
programs.otherFees: CORRECTED. Master's candidate fee €24 / 46.94 BGN flat (review of documents by commission, with or without interview) — not €24–€40. Diploma recognition, apostille, legalisation and translation additional. Plovdiv living costs additional.

programs.acceptsNonMusic: NO — CORRECTED from UNVERIFIED. A bachelor's in the field of musical art is explicitly required.
programs.totalCostEstimate: Moot — he is ineligible on two independent grounds. For reference: €7,600 for the year, plus €4,600 if the language course is required, plus €24 and recognition costs, plus Plovdiv living.
programs.recommendation: THE PREVIOUS RECORD'S INSTINCT WAS RIGHT AND IS NOW PROVEN. It was included 'for completeness so he can rule it out knowingly', on the grounds that the language barrier was the subject matter rather than an obstacle. The official 2026/2027 handbook confirms this literally: the first stage of the entrance examination asks candidates to correct spelling errors in Bulgarian words and punctuation and factual errors in a Bulgarian text, and the second stage is an oral assessment of speech technique in front of a microphone. On top of that — and this is new — the handbook requires a bachelor's degree in the field of musical art and excludes candidates with permanent speech, voice or hearing impairments. He is ineligible on the degree rule before the language test even begins. It trains a Bulgarian radio music editor. Cross it off.

First, the published entry rule limits admission to graduates of six named music specialties at NMA Sofia and AMTII Plovdiv — a Tunisian software-engineering graduate cannot qualify now or after any portfolio year. programs.program: Arta sunetului de film (The Art of Film Sound), studii universitare de masterat
programs.institution: Universitatea Națională de Artă Teatrală și Cinematografică „I.L. Caragiale“ București (UNATC), Facultatea de Film
programs.publicPrivate: PUBLIC — CONFIRMED. State university under the Romanian Ministry of Education, ARACIS-accredited, with Ministry-allocated state-budget places; fees set by Senate decision (Hotărârea Senatului nr. 290/27.05.2026) published on the institutional .ro domain. Rector Prof.univ.dr. Liviu Lucaci; Senate President Prof.univ.dr. Doru Nițescu.
programs.institutionType: Film and theatre university (state) — Romania's national film school
programs.qualification: Diplomă de master — CONFIRMED a genuine state-recognised second-cycle degree (ciclul II) under Legea învățământului superior nr. 199/2023. Supports a student residence permit for a third-country national via the Ministry of Education Letter of Acceptance.
programs.accreditationStatus: CONFIRMED. ARACIS-accredited state university; the programme is listed on the official 2026/2027 admissions site, on the dedicated foreign-citizens master's admission page, and in Annex 1 (II.2, Faculty of Film) of the Senate fee decision.
programs.focus: Film sound design and post-production
programs.whatYouStudy: Film sound as an art form: sound design, recording, editing and post-production for cinema, worked through DAW projects. The competition bibliography is the professional film-sound canon: Yewdall 'Practical Art of Motion Picture Sound', Sonnenschein 'Sound Design', Chion 'Film, A Sound Art' / 'Audio-Vision' / 'The Voice in Cinema', Murray 'Sound Design Theory and Practice', Holman 'Sound for Film and Television', Purcell 'Dialog Editing for Motion Pictures', Ament 'The Foley Grail', Viers 'The Sound Effects Bible' and 'The Location Sound Bible', Rumsey & McCormick 'Sound and Recording', Schafer 'The Soundscape', Weis & Belton 'Film Sound: Theory and Practice'. Toolchain: Avid Pro Tools, Steinberg Nuendo, Cockos Reaper, Adobe Audition, Adobe Premiere Pro, Fairlight/DaVinci Resolve.
programs.durationEcts: 2 years, 4 semesters, 120 ECTS, full-time (cu frecvență) — CONFIRMED on both the programme page and the foreign-citizens page.
programs.language: Romanian — CONFIRMED. Not an English-taught programme. UNATC's Faculty of Film does run English-taught master's programmes (Design for New Media, Visual Effects, Audiovisual Preservation and Programming, Interactive Technologies for Performing and Media Arts, Art of Game Design), but Arta sunetului de film is not among them.
programs.languageRequirement: CORRECTED AND SHARPENED — this is stricter than the previous record implied. UNATC's own foreign-citizens page states that foreign nationals may be enrolled in the admission contest / aptitude test only AFTER completing the Romanian-language preparatory year („Cetățenii străini pot fi înscriși la concursul de admitere/testul de aptitudini după absolvirea anului pregătitor de limba română“). Exemption requires one of: Romanian study documents or school records showing at least FOUR consecutive years of study in Romanian within the Romanian national system; or a certificate of linguistic competence of minimum CEFR level B1 issued specifically by an accredited Romanian higher-education institution that organises the Romanian preparatory year, by a Romanian language-and-culture lectorate at a foreign university, by the Institutul Limbii Române, or by the Institutul Cultural Român. A generic B1 certificate from any other provider does not qualify. No IELTS/TOEFL anywhere in this admission.
programs.entryRequirements: CONFIRMED. A completed bachelor's degree worth 180 or 240 credits, with NO field restriction for this programme (contrast Arta imaginii de film on the same page, which requires graduates 'ai facultăților de profil'). Plus a Europass CV, the portfolio, proof of registration-fee payment, baccalaureate diploma, birth certificate, passport valid 6+ months, foreign-credential recognition certificate, a medical fitness certificate from a family physician, and the GDPR declaration. Minimum admission average 6.00/10 for both budget and fee-paying places. Registration is exclusively online via the 2BitsEDU/Edubits platform; portfolios are uploaded to a secure institution-provided folder issued only after registration.
programs.auditionSpec: CONFIRMED. Single stage, two exams, each marked 1–10, final mark the arithmetic mean. Proba 1 — written: film-culture test based on the competition bibliography plus technical sound-design knowledge. Proba 2 — oral: a colloquium on one project of the candidate's choice from his portfolio, presented with the openable DAW session. Tie-break is decided on Proba 2, then Proba 1. No appeals are admitted against oral or practical exams. Both exams are in Romanian.
programs.portfolioSpec: MANDATORY AND SUBSTANTIAL — CONFIRMED, and the binding practical constraint for him. Required at registration: a portfolio of artistic projects with sound design created by the candidate himself (digital copies of films or other relevant sound-design-for-film-and-media projects), plus a Europass CV. At Proba 2 he must present an actual DAW session file from one portfolio piece and be able to open, run and discuss it; candidates are explicitly responsible for verifying the completeness and functionality of the DAW project. He has none of this today. Building it is a genuine twelve-month project and must be spent sound-designing SHORT FILMS, not producing club tracks — the portfolio must show film-sound work.
programs.equipmentRequired: A working DAW project in one of the six named applications. The university provides Pro Tools, Nuendo, Reaper, Audition, Premiere Pro and Fairlight/DaVinci Resolve at the exam; if the required software is unavailable, candidates may bring their own equipment. Practically: a laptop plus a licence for one — Reaper is the cheapest, DaVinci Resolve's free tier includes Fairlight.
programs.facilities: No published studio inventory on the admissions site. UNATC is the national film school with production facilities. Ask secretariat.film@unatc.ro for a facilities list and the studio-access policy for master's students.
programs.tuitionEU: 13,750 lei per academic year for fee-paying places — CONFIRMED VERBATIM in Hotărârea Senatului nr. 290/27.05.2026, Annex 1, section II.2 (Faculty of Film), line 'Arta sunetului de film 13.750'. NEW AND IMPORTANT: the programme has only 3 budget-funded places and 3 fee-paying places. Six seats in total.
programs.tuitionNonEU: STILL NOT PUBLISHED — the previous record's caution was correct and I confirm it. I extracted the full text of Hotărârea Senatului nr. 290/2026: it contains no euro figure and no reference to 'cont propriu valutar', 'străin' or 'terțe' anywhere. All figures are in lei and apply to the domestic fee-paying regime. Romanian non-EU tuition is set per institution above a Government Ordinance 22/2009 floor and is normally quoted in EUR per month; comparable Romanian arts faculties sit around €750–950/month payable nine months a year. DO NOT assume the 13,750 lei figure applies to him. Ask study@unatc.ro and secretariat.film@unatc.ro in writing for the euro rate for a non-EU master's student in Arta sunetului de film — and note that if he wins a Romanian government scholarship the question becomes moot, because scholarship holders occupy budget places.
programs.otherFees: CORRECTED — previously UNVERIFIED, now confirmed from the same Senate decision. Master's admission registration fee: 400 lei (Annex 1, TAXE DE ÎNSCRIERE, item 2), payable online in the admission application. Optional admission preparation courses: 150 lei per course (15% discount if paid in full). Document legalisation/apostille, authorised translation, credential recognition and Letter of Acceptance processing are additional. Bucharest living costs additional — UNATC's own page points candidates to Numbeo rather than publishing a figure.
programs.scholarships: CONFIRMED WITH IMPORTANT CORRECTIONS. (1) Romanian Government / MFA scholarships via scholarships.studyinromania.gov.ro, under Government Decision 288/1993 — open to citizens of ALL non-EU countries, so a Tunisian national qualifies; requires an average of the study years for the last graduated school of at least 7/10 or equivalent 'Good'; excludes only Medicine, Dental Medicine and Pharmacy; at master's level beneficiaries study ONLY IN ROMANIAN, with a fully financed Romanian preparatory year for non-speakers. Covers: exemption from registration, language-testing and aptitude-test fees; tuition for the preparatory year; tuition for the degree; a monthly stipend during both the preparatory year and the degree; and dormitory accommodation subject to availability. 2026/2027 cycle: applications 16 February – 31 March 2026, results announced around 15 July 2026, then the Ministry issues the Letter of Acceptance. TWO CAVEATS THE PREVIOUS RECORD MISSED — the Ministry expressly reserves the right to assign a DIFFERENT university in the same field if the candidate's choice cannot be honoured, and later requests to change field or university are refused; and the scholarship does not waive UNATC's own aptitude test, so he must still pass Proba 1 and Proba 2 in Romanian and place within three budget seats. (2) ARICE scholarships — CORRECTED AND DOWNGRADED. 40 scholarships for 2026/2027, files emailed 11 May – 12 June 2026 to burse2026@arice.gov.ro, Romanian-taught with a free preparatory year to B1. But ARICE explicitly PRIORITISES economics and business administration, agricultural sciences, technical sciences, and oil and gas; other fields are considered only 'to the extent of the places available'. Film sound is not a priority field, so ARICE is a long shot, not a parallel route of equal weight.
programs.englishTest: None required or accepted for this programme. His untaken IELTS/TOEFL is irrelevant to Arta sunetului de film — but it WOULD be needed for UNATC's English-taught master's programmes, which is a reason to sit it anyway.
programs.intakes: September/October (one intake)
programs.applicationOpens: 2026/2027 cycle, Romanian-taught route (which is the route for this programme, including for foreign citizens): online registration 4 August – 9 September 2026; file verification 10–11 September; admission exams 15–20 September 2026. Separately, the English-taught non-EU route ran 10–27 June 2026 with file verification 28–30 June and exams 1–8 July 2026 — that route does NOT include Arta sunetului de film. PRIOR CYCLE — confirm 2027 dates.
programs.deadline: Expect an August–September 2027 registration window for a September 2027 start. The operative deadline for him is far earlier: the Romanian Government / MFA scholarship closes around 31 March 2027, roughly five months before the university's own window, and the preparatory-year requirement means a scholarship awarded in July 2027 would put him into the Romanian language year in September 2027 and into the master's proper in September 2028.
programs.visaEligible: Yes — CONFIRMED. UNATC operates a published admission route for foreign citizens at Faculty of Film master's level; the Ministry of Education issues a 'Letter of acceptance for studies in Romania', which is expressly required to obtain a Romanian long-stay study visa and to enrol, and which for scholarship holders states any obligation to complete the Romanian preparatory year.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: YES — CONFIRMED. The published condition is simply a completed bachelor's of 180 or 240 credits, with no field restriction and no music-degree clause. His BSc Software Engineering is an acceptable academic qualification. The barriers are the portfolio, the Romanian language, and six seats.
programs.totalCostEstimate: Two scenarios. SELF-FUNDED: unquantifiable until UNATC publishes or states the non-EU euro rate; if it lands in the €750–950/month band typical of Romanian arts faculties, roughly €6,750–8,550 per year over two years, plus a Romanian preparatory year, plus Bucharest living, plus 400 lei registration and legalisation costs. SCHOLARSHIP: tuition, preparatory year and accommodation covered, a monthly stipend paid, and registration and aptitude-test fees waived — his cost collapses to visa costs, travel, document legalisation and the gap between the stipend and Bucharest living costs.
programs.recommendation: STILL THE BEST PROSPECT OF THE SIX, AND NOW THE ONLY ONE THAT IS BOTH A GOOD FIT AND OPEN TO HIM — BUT NARROWER THAN THE PREVIOUS RECORD SUGGESTED. Everything structurally good about it holds up under verification: a real 2-year, 120-ECTS, ARACIS-accredited degree at Romania's national film school; no music-degree requirement; the professional film-sound toolchain and canon; and a Romanian government scholarship a Tunisian national genuinely can win, which covers tuition, a free Romanian preparatory year, accommodation and a monthly stipend. Four corrections tighten the picture. First, the programme admits only SIX students a year — 3 on budget, 3 fee-paying — so this is a highly competitive seat, not a place he walks into. Second, the language rule is stricter than reported: foreign nationals may sit the admission exam only after completing the Romanian preparatory year, unless they hold a B1 certificate from a specific short list of Romanian issuers (an accredited Romanian HEI running the preparatory year, a Romanian lectorate abroad, the Institutul Limbii Române or the Institutul Cultural Român) — an ordinary B1 certificate will not do. Third, the MFA scholarship does not buy him admission: he must still pass a written film-culture exam and an oral DAW colloquium in Romanian and place in the top three, and the Ministry reserves the right to send him to a different university in the same field if UNATC cannot take him. Fourth, ARICE is a much weaker parallel route than described — film sound is outside its four priority fields and is considered only if places remain. The non-EU euro tuition rate genuinely is unpublished; I extracted the full Senate decision and it contains no euro figures at all, so the previous record's refusal to guess was right. Concrete plan for a realistic 2028 master's start via a 2027 preparatory year: (a) confirm his SMU MedTech average converts to at least 7/10 — this is a hard eligibility gate, check it first; (b) start Romanian now and aim for a qualifying B1 certificate from an accepted issuer; (c) redirect the portfolio year to sound-designing student short films, not DJ tracks, and finish with an openable, functional Pro Tools or Reaper session he can walk a panel through; (d) email study@unatc.ro and secretariat.film@unatc.ro for the non-EU euro rate and for confirmation of the number of places open to non-EU candidates; (e) apply to the MFA scholarship in the 16 February – 31 March 2027 window, and treat the university's own August–September 2027 registration as the second gate, not the first. One additional option worth putting in front of him: UNATC's English-taught non-EU master's route — in particular Interactive Technologies for Performing and Media Arts (digital control of sound, light, image and code) and Art of Game Design, both 2-year, 13,750 lei, admitted on a separate June–July calendar with an English-language file competition and no Romanian required. Those are not funded by the MFA scholarship, which is Romanian-only at master's level, but they are the same university, the same faculty, adjacent to his interests, and they play directly to a software-engineering background. That is the pairing to research next.

programs.publicPrivate: PUBLIC — CONFIRMED, no change. The 2026/27 master konkurs is issued on the University of Novi Sad's official template ('Obrazac za slanje teksta konkursa... Univerzitet u Novom Sadu') and publishes state-BUDGET-funded places: 152 budget + 108 self-financing across the Academy, of which this programme has 2 budget + 8 self-financing. Budget places exist only at state-founded institutions. Institution-level accreditation dates per the national register: 08.07.2011, 02.06.2017, 11.03.2025.
programs.language: Serbian only — CONFIRMED and now independently corroborated. The konkurs, informator and accredited curriculum are all in Serbian; the entrance exam is conducted in Serbian.
