Ask: Služba za studije i studentska pitanja, 021/422-177 lok. 2 or 021/422-176 lok. 2, aofarts@uns.ac.rs.
programs.englishTest: None. No IELTS/TOEFL appears anywhere in the konkurs or informator. Confirmed. His untaken IELTS is genuinely irrelevant here — the language barrier is Serbian, and it is a much harder one for him than IELTS would be.
programs.qualification: Master akademske studije (MAS) — a real, state-recognised second-cycle degree, 60 ECTS, 1 year, 2 semesters. Professional title per the accredited curriculum sheet: 'Мастер музички продуцент' (Master Music Producer). CONFIRMED verbatim from the official accredited curriculum PDF. Supports a Serbian study residence permit.
programs.accreditationStatus: ACCREDITED — now verified at national level, correcting the previous 'decision could not be machine-read'. The National Body for Accreditation and Quality Assurance in Higher Education (NAT) register 'Vodič kroz akreditovane visokoškolske ustanove i studijske programe u Republici Srbiji', edition of 21 July 2026, lists under Akademija umetnosti, Novi Sad, entry 90: 'ИМТ МАС - МУЗИЧКА ПРОДУКЦИЈА, 03.10.2023, БС 10'. So: accredited 3 October 2023, field IMT (interdisciplinary/multidisciplinary), approved annual intake 10. Serbian accreditation runs 7 years, so this decision is valid through October 2030 and covers his September/October 2027 entry.
programs.durationEcts: 1 year / 2 semesters, 60 ECTS. CONFIRMED from both the informator and the accredited curriculum sheet.
programs.focus: Music production proper — not film sound. Content-wise this remains the closest match in the Serbian state sector to a producer/DJ goal.
programs.whatYouStudy: CONFIRMED verbatim from the official accredited curriculum sheet (mas-muzicka-produkcija-2024.pdf). Compulsory: Muzička produkcija (2+2, both semesters); Zvuk i muzika na filmu (2+1); Savremene tendencije u muzičkoj produkciji 1 (1+2) and 2 (2+2); Muzika-događaj-publika (1+1, both semesters); Master rad – istraživanje (0+0+6); Master rad (0+0+5). Electives, 12 ECTS per semester block chosen from: Dramaturgija savremenog filma (2+1); Metode u muzičkom obrazovanju u digitalnom okruženju (2+0); Istorija elektroakustičke muzike (2+0); Istorija popularne muzike (2+0); Produkcija muzike za nove medije (1+2); Muzika u medijima (1+1). Hours are weekly, as (lectures)+(exercises)+(DON).
programs.entryRequirements: THE DOCUMENTED CONTRADICTION IS REAL — I re-read both source documents and confirm it, but I now judge which one governs. (a) The 2026/27 konkurs, §2, programme-specific clause: 'Студијски програм – Музичка продукција: завршене основне академске студије у четворогодишњем трајању из уметничке области Музичка продукција, или сродан студијски програм (240 ЕСПБ)' — a four-year BA IN THE ARTISTIC FIELD of music production, or a cognate programme. (b) The informator, Opšti uslovi: 'Пријемни испит могу полагати лица која су завршила основне академске студије у четворогодишњем трајању (240 ЕСПБ)' — any four-year 240-ECTS bachelor. CORRECTION OF EMPHASIS: the konkurs is the legally binding enrolment act adopted on the University's template and issued on the basis of a Government decision; the informator is a summary of exam content. Where they differ the konkurs governs. Read that way, a BSc Software Engineering is NOT in the artistic field of music production and is unlikely to be accepted as 'srodan'. Second, the konkurs §2.2 general rule requires 'najmanje 240 ESPB' and lists the ONLY four exceptions permitted at 180 ECTS — Konzervacija i restauracija, the Guitar/Performing Arts joint programme, Kreiranje serija, and Pozorišni oblici modul Lutkarstvo. Muzička produkcija is NOT among them. A Tunisian three-year 180-ECTS licence is therefore ineligible, full stop. Foreign nationals additionally file the diploma-recognition decision, health-insurance proof and Serbian-language proof.
programs.portfolioSpec: CONFIRMED and EXPANDED — the previous record omitted two konkurs-level documents. Informator required documents: diploma or certificate of a completed four-year 240-ECTS bachelor; CV (biografija); motivation letter; MEDICAL CERTIFICATE WITH AN AUDIOGRAM (ophthalmologist, ENT specialist, psychologist); scanned/read ID; photo min. 1200x800 px JPG under 1 MB; proof of payment of the application fee. Separately, 'uz prijavu kandidati prilažu': (1) the medical certificate with audiogram, (2) a PORTFOLIO of works created in the 3 years preceding the date of the entrance exam. ADDITIONALLY required by konkurs §5 and omitted from the previous record: the completed PRIJAVNI LIST (application form, downloadable as Prijavni-list-za-master-studije-2026-2027.pdf) and the UVERENJE O POLOŽENIM ISPITIMA (official transcript of passed exams). Submission is 100% electronic, one e-mail per candidate to aunsprijemni.dramski@uns.ac.rs, all files under 12 MB total, every file named with the candidate's full name, study programme named in the subject line. His one-year portfolio plan does map onto the 'previous 3 years' rule.
programs.auditionSpec: CONFIRMED verbatim. Two stages. PART ONE (pass/fail): written test in the professional-artistic field of Music Production; written analysis/evaluation of a musical work against subjective and objective criteria set by the commission; interview with the commission. Those who pass proceed to multi-day exercises and PART TWO: assessment of submitted works up to 30 points; practical work on the Academy's own material/equipment up to 20 points; oral examination of knowledge in the professional-artistic field of AUDIOVISUAL MEDIA (interview with the commission) up to 30 points. BA grade average scores separately, up to 20 points (10.00 = 20 pts; 6.49–6.00 = 4 pts; below 6.00 scores nothing). A candidate not exceeding 50 total points fails and is not ranked. Mobile phones and auxiliary devices are strictly banned from the exam rooms. Conducted in Serbian.
programs.equipmentRequired: Part two is 'практичан рад на материјалу Академије' — practical work on the Academy's own material, so no personal studio rig is needed for the exam. What he must supply is a portfolio of finished audio work. No published equipment inventory — UNVERIFIED.
programs.facilities: Still UNVERIFIED. Practical studio work is implied (the exam is run on Academy equipment) but no inventory of studios, consoles, control rooms or immersive/Atmos capability is published on any official page. Ask the Katedra za audiovizuelne medije via aunsprijemni.dramski@uns.ac.rs.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: NO on the governing document — this is a correction of emphasis from the previous record, which left it 'ambiguous'. The konkurs restricts entry to a four-year bachelor in the artistic field of Music Production or a cognate programme. Software engineering is not cognate to music production in any ordinary reading. Even on the permissive informator reading he would still face a Serbian-language written subject test in music production, a written musical analysis, a commission interview and a portfolio. Unlike a conservatory master there is no instrumental audition, which is the one thing in his favour.
programs.tuitionEU: Not an applicable category in Serbia. Domestic/self-financing rate for master studies at the Academy, per the Council decision quoted in the konkurs: 125,000 RSD per year. CONFIRMED.
programs.tuitionNonEU: EUR 1,800 for the whole degree — THE RATE HE WOULD PAY. CONFIRMED verbatim: the konkurs quota table has a dedicated column 'Школарина за странце (евра)' showing 1800 against Muzička produkcija (and against every master programme at the Academy; doctoral studies are 2,400). Since the master is one year, EUR 1,800 is the total tuition, not an annual instalment of a longer degree.
programs.otherFees: MATERIALLY CORRECTED — the previous record's '4,000 RSD to the University plus 4,000 RSD to the Academy' figure does not appear in any official document and is withdrawn. Actual published figures: (1) ENTRANCE-EXAM FEE 12,000 RSD — konkurs §6: 'Кандидати који приступају пријемном испиту уплаћују 12.000,00 дин' (previously UNVERIFIED); (2) ENROLMENT COST ON ADMISSION 5,500 RSD — konkurs §6 'Трошкови уписа за кандидате који положе пријемни испит износи 5.500,00 дин', corroborated by the official 'ZA UPIS 2026-2027 JE POTREBNO' sheet which also requires the original diploma for inspection, two 3.5x4.5 cm photos, an index book and two ŠV-20 forms; (3) both paid to account 840-32790845-46, poziv na broj 300 for the Drama Department and interdisciplinary studies; (4) DIPLOMA RECOGNITION at the University of Novi Sad — 30,000 RSD, or EUR 260 if paid from abroad, PLUS a 14,900 RSD administrative tax, applicant bears all bank charges (previously UNVERIFIED; source uns.ac.rs recognition page, applied for online at priznavanje.uns.ac.rs, contact priznavanje@uns.ac.rs / 021 485-2021). Compulsory health insurance for foreign students — cost still UNVERIFIED.
programs.totalCostEstimate: Now largely computable. Tuition EUR 1,800 for the entire 60-ECTS degree. Plus institutional/administrative costs: 12,000 RSD exam fee + 5,500 RSD enrolment + 30,000 RSD (or EUR 260) recognition fee + 14,900 RSD administrative tax, i.e. roughly EUR 480–560 at ~117 RSD/EUR. So about EUR 2,300–2,400 in institution-side costs for the whole master, before living costs, visa fees, health insurance and Serbian-language tuition. Living costs in Novi Sad are not published by the Academy — UNVERIFIED. This remains among the cheapest genuinely accredited music-production masters in Europe.
programs.fundingLevel: Check. 2 state-budget (fee-free) places against 8 self-financing places, per the konkurs quota table for Interdisciplinarne studije. The konkurs simultaneously says foreigners enrol 'under the same conditions as a domestic citizen' AND publishes a separate foreigner tariff of EUR 1,800 — an unresolved tension. Whether a Tunisian may actually compete for one of the 2 budget places is UNVERIFIED and must be asked in writing. Plan for EUR 1,800. Note also the konkurs caveat that anyone who previously studied at the same level in budget status cannot re-enrol in budget status.
programs.scholarships: No programme-level or Academy-level scholarship for non-EU applicants is published on any official page — UNVERIFIED, unchanged after re-checking. Do not assume one exists. Realistic avenues to ask: (1) the Serbian Ministry of Education's bilateral scholarship offers, which are distributed through the applicant's home ministry — he should ask the Tunisian Ministère de l'Enseignement Supérieur whether Serbia offers Tunisia places in a given year; (2) the University of Novi Sad international office. Erasmus+ credit mobility is inbound-only for already-enrolled students and is not an admission route.
programs.visaEligible: Yes in principle — CONFIRMED. This is a nationally registered accredited MAS at a state university (NAT register entry 90), delivered in person, which is the category supporting a Serbian temporary residence permit for education (privremeni boravak radi školovanja). A Tunisian national needs a long-stay visa D before travel, then converts to temporary residence. The konkurs itself confirms the institution enrols foreign nationals and lists the extra documents. Exact visa D document list, fees and processing times are not published by the Academy — UNVERIFIED; authoritative sources are the Serbian Ministry of Interior (MUP) and the Serbian embassy accredited to Tunisia. Serbia is outside the EU and Schengen, so this permit confers no EU mobility.
programs.intakes: One academic intake per year, October start, but with TWO application rounds (see deadline).
programs.applicationOpens: 2026/27 cycle: konkurs text published 29 May 2026 (per the Drama Department admissions page), informators posted July 2026 (the Kreiranje serija informator appeared as late as August 2026). For a September/October 2027 entry, expect the 2027/28 konkurs around May–June 2027 and informators in July 2027 — PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. Note the informator itself states that the Drama Department's application and exam dates 'will be published on the Academy website', so the konkurs is the document to watch.
programs.deadline: CORRECTED — the previous record missed the SECOND application round entirely, which materially improves his odds. 2026/27 cycle, Drama Department / Interdisciplinary studies (PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new dates for 2027/28). FIRST ROUND: electronic application 05.10.2026; entrance exam 07–13.10.2026; preliminary ranking 15.10.2026; final ranking 20.10.2026; enrolment 20.10.2026. SECOND ROUND (DRUGI KONKURSNI ROK): electronic application 21.10.2026; entrance exam 23–28.10.2026; preliminary ranking 30.10.2026; final ranking and enrolment 03.11.2026. Appeals to the Dean within 24 hours of the preliminary list. The timing trap stands: applications close in EARLY OCTOBER of the year of entry, not the preceding winter — but the diploma-recognition process, the audiogram/medical certificate and Serbian-language study must start many months earlier.
programs.recommendation: Content-wise this is still the best-matched accredited music-production master in the Serbian state sector, and at roughly EUR 2,300 all-in it is extraordinarily cheap. But after re-reading the governing documents I am less optimistic than the previous assessment, which called it 'the single best find'. Three gates, and he currently fails all three. (1) THE 240-ECTS RULE IS ABSOLUTE. Konkurs §2.2 lists the only four programmes at the Academy that accept 180 ECTS, and Muzička produkcija is not one of them. If his SMU MedTech BSc is a three-year 180-ECTS licence he is ineligible regardless of talent, portfolio or motivation. Verify this FIRST. (2) THE FIELD RESTRICTION IS REAL. The binding konkurs requires a four-year bachelor 'iz umetničke oblasti Muzička produkcija, ili srodan studijski program'. The permissive informator wording is a summary, not the rule. A software-engineering degree is very unlikely to qualify as cognate. (3) SERBIAN. The entrance exam is a written subject test plus a written musical analysis plus two commission interviews, all in Serbian. Going from zero Slavic to exam-level Serbian in twelve months while also building a first audio portfolio and arranging an ENT audiogram in Tunisia is not a realistic 2027 plan. Everything is verified and correct in the record; what has changed is the honest read of his odds. Concrete next step, one e-mail to aofarts@uns.ac.rs copying aunsprijemni.dramski@uns.ac.rs, asking: (a) can a 180-ECTS three-year foreign bachelor ever be accepted for MAS Muzička produkcija; (b) is a BSc in Software Engineering treated as a 'srodan studijski program' under the konkurs; (c) which Serbian-language certificate and level satisfies the requirement; (d) may foreign nationals compete for the 2 budget places.

programs.program: Master akademske studije DIZAJN VIDEO IGARA (MAS Video Game Design) — Interdisciplinary Studies
programs.institution: Akademija umetnosti (Academy of Arts), Univerzitet u Novom Sadu
programs.institutionType: State art academy, constituent faculty of the public University of Novi Sad. The programme sits under 'Interdisciplinarne studije' and is administered by the Drama Department / Katedra za audiovizuelne medije. CONFIRMED — it is listed alongside Pozorišni oblici, Kreiranje serija and Muzička produkcija on the official Drama Department master admissions page.
programs.publicPrivate: PUBLIC — CONFIRMED, same evidence base as the Music Production entry: constituent of the state University of Novi Sad, konkurs issued on the University template, 2 state-budget places published in the official quota table. Institution accreditation per the national register: 08.07.2011, 02.06.2017, 11.03.2025.
programs.language: Serbian only — CONFIRMED. The programme page, informator, konkurs and accredited curriculum are Serbian; the entrance exam is conducted in Serbian. The national accreditation register flags English-medium programmes explicitly and this one carries no such flag; nor is there a distance-learning variant.
programs.languageRequirement: Foreign nationals must supply 'доказ о познавању српског језика' per konkurs §9, alongside the diploma-recognition decision and health-insurance proof. Required level and accepted certificate NOT published — UNVERIFIED, confirmed again on re-check. Ask Služba za studije, 021/422-177 lok. 2, aofarts@uns.ac.rs.
programs.englishTest: None required. Confirmed.
programs.qualification: Master akademske studije (MAS), a genuine state-recognised second-cycle degree, 60 ECTS, 1 year. The national register classifies it as field IMT (interdisciplinary/multidisciplinary). The exact professional title conferred is still not published in machine-readable form — UNVERIFIED; note that the 'diplomirani umetnik digitalnih medija' title belongs to the FIRST-CYCLE Dizajn video igara programme (accredited 2017), not to this master. Ask the Academy for the uverenje.
programs.accreditationStatus: ACCREDITED — now verified at national level. NAT register 'Vodič kroz akreditovane visokoškolske ustanove i studijske programe u Republici Srbiji', 21 July 2026, under Akademija umetnosti Novi Sad, entry 92: 'ИМТ МАС - ДИЗАЈН ВИДЕО ИГАРА, 05.11.2024, БС 10'. Accredited 5 November 2024, approved annual intake 10, valid 7 years to November 2031 — comfortably covering his 2027 entry. The sibling first-cycle programme is entry 37, also 05.11.2024 (originally 2017), which is what the Academy means when it calls itself the first accredited video-game programme in the Western Balkans.
programs.durationEcts: 1 year, 60 ECTS. CONFIRMED verbatim from the official accredited curriculum table 5.1b.
programs.focus: Video game design. Included here only because game audio sits inside it as an elective strand. This is NOT an audio degree and will not train him as a music producer.
programs.whatYouStudy: CONFIRMED verbatim from the official accredited curriculum table 5.1b. Compulsory: MA701 Žanrovska analiza i sinteza video igara (2+4, 12 ECTS); MA703 Studije video igara (2+0, 4 ECTS); MP2102 Grafičke komunikacije u interaktivnim medijima (2+1, 6 ECTS); MA7002 Imerzivne igre / Immersive Games (2+2, 6 ECTS); MAZRD Završni rad (12 ECTS); MAZRI Završni rad – istraživanje (12 ECTS). Electives MAIZ1, 12 ECTS chosen from — and this is where all the audio content lives: MSMIM Muzika u medijima (6); MA1002 Audiovizuelna artikulacija (6); MA1003 Zvuk u filmskoj umetnosti (6); MA2002 Postprodukcija filmske slike (6); MA4003 Produkcija muzike za nove medije (6); MLVIA Video art (6). Hard ceiling: at most 12 of the 60 ECTS can be audio, and only two of those courses (Muzika u medijima, Produkcija muzike za nove medije) are music-production-adjacent.
programs.entryRequirements: CONFIRMED — clean, permissive, and identical in both official documents, with no contradiction (unlike Music Production). Konkurs §2, programme clause: 'Студијски програм – Дизајн видео игара: завршене основне академске студије у четворогодишњем трајању' — a four-year bachelor, full stop, with NO artistic-field restriction. Informator: 'лица која су завршила основне академске студије у четворогодишњем трајању (240 ЕСПБ)'. The 240-ECTS / four-year rule is the binding gate: konkurs §2.2 permits 180 ECTS only for Konzervacija i restauracija, the Guitar/Performing Arts joint programme, Kreiranje serija and Pozorišni oblici modul Lutkarstvo — Dizajn video igara is NOT among them, so a Tunisian three-year 180-ECTS licence is ineligible here too. Foreign nationals additionally file the diploma-recognition decision, health-insurance proof and Serbian-language proof.
programs.portfolioSpec: CONFIRMED and EXPANDED. Informator required documents: diploma or certificate of a four-year 240-ECTS bachelor; CV; motivation letter; scanned/read ID; photo 1200x800 px JPG under 1 MB; proof of application-fee payment. Separately 'uz prijavu kandidati prilažu': (1) an EXPLICATION of the artistic-research project the candidate plans to realise as the master's thesis; (2) a motivation letter; (3) a PORTFOLIO of the candidate's previous works IN THE FIELD OF VIDEO GAME DESIGN. Additionally required by konkurs §5 and omitted from the previous record: the completed prijavni list and the uverenje o položenim ispitima (transcript). Confirmed: NO medical certificate and NO audiogram is demanded here, unlike Music Production. Submission electronic to aunsprijemni.dramski@uns.ac.rs, one e-mail, 12 MB total, files named with the candidate's name.
programs.auditionSpec: CONFIRMED verbatim. Two stages. PART ONE (pass/fail): test of knowledge of the history and aesthetics of video games; a combined test of creative solution of design tasks; analysis of the submitted entry work plus interview with the commission. Those who pass proceed to multi-day exercises and PART TWO: assessment of works submitted with the application up to 25 points; practical work in video game design up to 25 points; oral examination in the professional-artistic field of video game design (commission interview) up to 30 points. BA grade average adds up to 20 points on the same scale as Music Production. Under 50 total points = fail, no ranking. Conducted in Serbian.
programs.equipmentRequired: Practical exam work is done at the Academy; no personal equipment requirement published. The real requirement is a demonstrable body of game-design work.
programs.facilities: Not published — UNVERIFIED, unchanged. The compulsory MA7002 Imerzivne igre course implies some interactive/VR capability but nothing is documented. Ask Katedra za audiovizuelne medije.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: YES — explicitly and unambiguously, in both the konkurs and the informator. Any four-year 240-ECTS bachelor in any field qualifies; there is no artistic-field restriction. For a software engineer this is the most accessible second-cycle art-academy programme in the Serbian sector on paper, and his coding background is a direct asset rather than a handicap. The trade-off is that it is a game-design degree with an audio ceiling of 12 of 60 ECTS.
programs.tuitionEU: Not an applicable category in Serbia. Domestic/self-financing rate: 125,000 RSD per year, per the Academy Council decision quoted in the konkurs.
programs.tuitionNonEU: EUR 1,800 for the whole degree — THE RATE HE WOULD PAY. CONFIRMED from the 'Школарина за странце (евра)' column of the official 2026/27 konkurs quota table, which shows 1800 against Dizajn video igara. One-year programme, so EUR 1,800 total.
programs.otherFees: CORRECTED, same as the Music Production entry — the previous '4,000 + 4,000 RSD diploma fees' figure is unsourced and withdrawn. Published figures: entrance-exam fee 12,000 RSD (konkurs §6, previously UNVERIFIED); enrolment cost on admission 5,500 RSD (konkurs §6, corroborated by the official enrolment checklist, which also requires the original diploma for inspection, two 3.5x4.5 cm photos, index book and two ŠV-20 forms); both to account 840-32790845-46, poziv na broj 300. Diploma recognition at the University of Novi Sad: 30,000 RSD, or EUR 260 if paid from abroad, plus a 14,900 RSD administrative tax, bank charges on the applicant (previously UNVERIFIED). Compulsory health insurance for foreign students — cost UNVERIFIED.
programs.totalCostEstimate: EUR 1,800 tuition for the whole master, plus roughly EUR 480–560 in exam, enrolment, recognition and administrative-tax fees, so about EUR 2,300–2,400 institution-side for the degree, before living costs, visa, insurance and Serbian tuition. Living costs in Novi Sad not published by the institution — UNVERIFIED.
programs.fundingLevel: Check. 2 state-budget places and 8 self-financing places for 2026/27. Whether a foreign national may compete for a budget place is UNVERIFIED — the konkurs says foreigners enrol under the same conditions as domestic citizens but simultaneously publishes a separate foreigner tariff. Plan for EUR 1,800.
programs.scholarships: None published at programme or Academy level for non-EU applicants — UNVERIFIED, unchanged. Routes to ask: the Tunisian Ministère de l'Enseignement Supérieur regarding any Serbian bilateral government scholarship offer in a given year, and the University of Novi Sad international office.
programs.visaEligible: Yes in principle — CONFIRMED. A nationally registered accredited MAS (NAT entry 92) at a state university, delivered in person, which is the category supporting a Serbian temporary residence permit for education. Tunisian nationals need a long-stay visa D first. Document lists, fees and timelines are not published by the Academy — UNVERIFIED; authoritative sources are the Serbian MUP and the Serbian embassy accredited to Tunisia. Serbia is outside the EU/Schengen.
programs.intakes: One academic intake per year, October start, with two application rounds.
programs.applicationOpens: 2026/27 konkurs published 29 May 2026; informator posted July 2026. Expect the 2027/28 equivalents around May–July 2027 — PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. The informator itself defers the Drama Department dates to the Academy website.
programs.deadline: CORRECTED — the previous record missed the second round. 2026/27 cycle, Drama Department / Interdisciplinary studies (PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new dates for 2027/28). FIRST ROUND: electronic application 05.10.2026; entrance exam 07–13.10.2026; preliminary list 15.10.2026; final list and enrolment 20.10.2026. SECOND ROUND: electronic application 21.10.2026; entrance exam 23–28.10.2026; preliminary list 30.10.2026; final list and enrolment 03.11.2026. Applications close in early October of the year of entry; appeals within 24 hours of the preliminary list.
programs.recommendation: Everything the previous record said about this programme checks out against the official documents, and the accreditation is now pinned down precisely (NAT register, accredited 05.11.2024, intake 10). It remains the only programme in the Novi Sad sweep whose published entry rule admits ANY four-year bachelor with no artistic-field restriction, and his software-engineering background is directly relevant to the curriculum. But it should not be presented to him as a music option in disguise. Audio is capped at 12 of 60 ECTS and only two of those six electives are production-adjacent; the other 48 ECTS are genre analysis, game studies, graphic communications in interactive media, immersive games and a game-design thesis. It will not make him a DJ or a record producer, and spending 2027–28 on it would be a career pivot, not a step toward his stated goal. It also does not solve the two gates that actually block him: the 240-ECTS / four-year first-degree rule applies identically here, and the Serbian-language requirement plus a Serbian-language entrance exam apply identically here. On top of that it demands a video-game-design portfolio he has even less basis to build than an audio one. Report it accurately as what it is: a cheap, accredited, unusually open Serbian master in the wrong subject. It only becomes interesting if he decides he wants to work in games audio and is prepared to learn Serbian.
programs.sourceUrl: https://akademija.uns.ac.rs/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/Tekst-Konkursa-Master-Doktorske-2026.pdf (official 2026/27 konkurs — quota, EUR 1,800 foreigner tuition, 12,000 RSD exam fee, 5,500 RSD enrolment, both rounds, entry clause with no field restriction); https://akademija.uns.ac.rs/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/Informator-MAS-Dizajn-video-igara-2026-27.pdf (official entrance-exam informator — documents, explication, portfolio, exam structure, no audiogram); https://akademija.uns.ac.rs/wp-content/uploads/2019/10/dizajn-video-igara-master-2025.pdf (official accredited curriculum table 5.1b); https://akademija.uns.ac.rs/dizajn-video-igara/ (programme page — note it describes the FIRST-CYCLE programme, accredited 2017); https://akademija.uns.ac.rs/prijemni-dramski-mas/; https://www.nat.rs/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/Vodič-za-studente-21.07.2026.pdf (NAT register 21.07.2026 — entry 92, MAS Dizajn video igara accredited 05.11.2024); https://www.uns.ac.rs/index.php/studije/priznavanje-diploma/priznavanje-strane (recognition fees)

programs.program: Master akademske studije MUZIČKA PRODUKCIJA (MAS Music Production), Fakultet digitalnih umetnosti
programs.institution: Univerzitet Metropolitan
programs.city: Belgrade (delivered in person at the Belgrade campus, Tadeuša Košćuška 63, 11158 Beograd; the university also has a Niš campus, but this programme is Belgrade-only)
programs.institutionType: Private university with four faculties (Information Technologies, Management, Digital Arts, Foreign Languages). This programme is at the Faculty of Digital Arts (FDU Metropolitan — not to be confused with the state FDU Belgrade). The Faculty of Digital Arts also runs MAS Vizuelne komunikacije and MAS/DAS Dizajn novih medija.
programs.publicPrivate: PRIVATE — CONFIRMED, and its standing is now firmly established rather than merely asserted. The university's official accreditation page publishes a dozvola za rad (work licence) first issued 2010 with amendment decisions through November 2025 — the licensing regime for privately founded HEIs. There are no state-budget places; all study is fee-paying. Crucially, the Serbian National Accreditation Body's register of 21 July 2026 lists 'Универзитет „Метрополитан“' with institution accreditation dated 04.06.2010, 21.07.2017 and 21.01.2025, and lists this specific programme (see accreditationStatus). It is a properly licensed and nationally registered university, not a diploma mill.
programs.language: SERBIAN ONLY — CORRECTED from the previous record's 'UNVERIFIED whether an English delivery exists'. Two independent official confirmations. (1) Metropolitan's own official tuition page heads the master price table 'Studijski program (nastava na srpskom jeziku)' — study programme, teaching in the Serbian language. (2) The NAT national register flags language and delivery mode explicitly in the programme name: Metropolitan's other masters appear as 'МАС - ИНФОРМАЦИОНЕ ТЕХНОЛОГИЈЕ И СИСТЕМИ НА СРПСКОМ И ЕНГЛЕСКОМ ЈЕЗИКУ', 'МАС - ДИГИТАЛНИ БИЗНИС НА СРПСКОМ И ЕНГЛЕСКОМ ЈЕЗИКУ', and distance-learning variants carry a '-СНД' suffix. Entry 53, 'ИМТ МАС - МУЗИЧКА ПРОДУКЦИЈА', carries NEITHER. So the accreditation itself covers Serbian-language, in-person delivery only. There is no English track to ask about and no online variant — which is bad for his language situation but good for his visa, since an online programme would not support a residence permit.
programs.languageRequirement: Not published for this programme — UNVERIFIED. The published master admission rules impose no language certificate. In practice, delivery is Serbian-only, so functional Serbian is a de facto requirement whatever the paperwork says. Ask upis@metropolitan.ac.rs in writing.
programs.englishTest: Not published — UNVERIFIED, and irrelevant: the programme is not taught in English, so no IELTS/TOEFL band would help him here.
programs.qualification: Master akademske studije (MAS), 60 ECTS, 1 year, 2 semesters. Professional title: 'Master muzički producent' (Master Music Producer). Field declared as IMT (interdisciplinary/multidisciplinary/dual-field); areas: Dramatic and Audiovisual Arts + Management and Business. This is a genuine second-cycle academic degree, not a private certificate — confirmed by its presence in the national register of accredited programmes.
programs.accreditationStatus: ACCREDITED — CORRECTED and now pinned to a specific decision, replacing the previous record's 'specific accreditation decision number/date NOT published — UNVERIFIED'. The National Body for Accreditation and Quality Assurance in Higher Education (NAT) register of 21 July 2026 lists, under Univerzitet „Metropolitan“, entry 53: 'ИМТ МАС - МУЗИЧКА ПРОДУКЦИЈА, 03.06.2025, БС 20'. So: accredited 3 June 2025, field IMT, approved annual intake 20 students, valid 7 years to June 2032. This is newer than the Novi Sad programme's accreditation and comfortably covers a 2027 entry. Institution accreditation 04.06.2010 / 21.07.2017 / 21.01.2025.
programs.durationEcts: 1 year / 2 semesters, 60 ECTS. CONFIRMED on the official programme page. Note the university's generic master page markets 'master diploma in 10 months'.
programs.focus: Music production plus music-industry management and marketing. Explicitly aimed at building a career in the music industry, including content creation for film, TV, social platforms and streaming services. Of the three programmes reviewed, this is the closest in intent to an 'international DJ and producer' goal, because it pairs the production teaching with branding, marketing campaigns and digital entrepreneurship.
programs.whatYouStudy: CONFIRMED verbatim from the official programme page. Semester 1: AD511 Muzička produkcija 1 (audio technology, music software, arranging, microphone placement, instrument miking, basic mixing and mastering); AD560 Kreativna radionica zvuka (creative sound workshop — practical sound-design projects, experimentation with digital audio tools, sound installations, history of music-scenic performance); AD570 Novi mediji i tehnologija u performansu; Elective block 1 (MK520 Kreiranje digitalnog brenda / MK525 Digitalne marketinške kampanje); Elective block 2 (AD535 Advertajzing / AD565 Digitalna kultura). Semester 2: AD512 Muzička produkcija 2 (theory of analogue and digital recording and sound processing, equipment and techniques, sound formats and carriers); MG525 Upravljanje inovacijama i tehnologijama; Elective 3 (MG535 Digitalno preduzetništvo / MG545 Strateški menadžment i liderstvo); AD591 Završni rad muzičke produkcije – SIR; AD592 Završni rad – izrada i odbrana. Roughly a third of the taught credits are management/marketing, which a software engineer would handle comfortably.
programs.entryRequirements: MATERIALLY CORRECTED — the previous record's claim that entry requirements are 'NOT PUBLISHED' is WRONG. They are published in full at https://www.metropolitan.ac.rs/upis/upis-na-master-akademske-studije/ under 'Opšti uslovi upisa na Master studije'. (1) BASE RULE: 'Na studijske programe Master akademskih studija mogu se upisati studenti koji su prethodno završili četvorogodišnje i ostvarili uslov od 240 ESPB' — a completed four-year bachelor with 240 ECTS, the same gate as Novi Sad. (2) BUT THERE IS A PUBLISHED ROUTE OUT, which Novi Sad does not offer: 'Studenti koji su završili tri godine osnovnih akademskih studija i stekli 180 ESPB bodova imaju mogućnost da upišu četvrtu godinu akademskih studija Univerziteta Metropolitan i nakon završetka iste steknu zvanje diplomirani, na taj način ostvarivši uslov za upis na Master studije' — a holder of a three-year 180-ECTS bachelor may enrol in the FOURTH YEAR of a Metropolitan bachelor programme, obtain the 'diplomirani' title, and thereby qualify for the master. That is directly relevant to him if his Tunisian licence is 180 ECTS, at the cost of an extra year and extra fees. (3) COGNATE vs NON-COGNATE: 'Iz srodne oblasti, određuju se predmeti programa za nastavu u trajanju od godinu dana. Iz nesrodne oblasti, komisija određuje uslove upisa, predlaže nastavni plan i program, utvrđujući broj diferencijalnih ispita koje kandidat mora da položi.' A non-cognate first degree is expressly provided for, via differential exams set by a faculty commission. (4) DOCUMENTS: certified copy of the diploma (or graduation certificate); certified copy of the transcript of passed exams (or diploma supplement); birth certificate showing citizenship; two identical 3.5x4.5 cm photographs; proof of payment of a 1,000 RSD administrative fee; proof of payment of the first tuition instalment; ŠV-20 form (completed at the faculty, not purchased). (5) FOREIGN NATIONALS: they submit a NOSTRIFIED diploma stating the ECTS achieved, or, if recognition is still running, a certificate that the procedure is under way.
programs.portfolioSpec: No portfolio required — this is now a confirmed published finding rather than an unknown. The official master admission page describes the full procedure (online application, then scanned diploma and transcript, then referral to the faculty commission which issues individual admission conditions) and no portfolio appears anywhere in it, nor on the programme page. For an applicant with no body of work yet, this is a genuine structural advantage over both Novi Sad programmes.
programs.auditionSpec: No entrance exam or audition for master entry — confirmed by the published admission procedure, which routes the application to a faculty commission that sets conditions and any differential exams rather than testing the candidate. (The prijemni ispit and the 'direct enrolment without an entrance exam' offer advertised elsewhere on the site relate to bachelor admission.)
programs.equipmentRequired: None published. Teaching takes place in classrooms and a music studio ('predavanja i vežbe u učionici i muzičkom studiu'), and part of the teaching is delivered in a professional studio (see facilities), so no personal rig is required.
programs.facilities: PARTIALLY CORRECTED from 'UNVERIFIED'. The official programme page names a specific industry partner: 'Posebna prednost ovog programa je saradnja sa kompanijom AS STUDIOTON, zvaničnim partnerom master programa Muzičke produkcije, zahvaljujući kojoj studenti deo nastave pohađaju u profesionalnom studijskom okruženju i stiču praktična znanja u radu sa savremenom opremom' — AS Studioton is the official partner and students attend part of their teaching in a professional studio environment working with contemporary equipment. Beyond that, no inventory, console list or immersive/Atmos claim is published — still UNVERIFIED at that level of detail.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: YES — CORRECTED from the previous record's 'probably yes on marketing copy, UNVERIFIED'. It is published policy, not marketing: the master admission rules expressly contemplate applicants 'iz nesrodne oblasti' (from an unrelated field) and provide the mechanism — a faculty commission sets the admission conditions and the number of differential exams. The programme page separately states the studies are intended for 'muzičare, muzičke producente, izvođače, kao i sve zainteresovane kandidate koji žele da kreiraju ili unaprede sopstvenu karijeru u muzičkoj industriji'. So a software-engineering graduate is admissible in principle, subject to differential exams. What he cannot avoid is that those differential exams, like the degree, will be in Serbian.
programs.tuitionEU: Not an applicable category in Serbia. The published rate for the master is EUR 4,500, appearing both on the programme page and in the university-wide price list under 'MASTER AKADEMSKE STUDIJE – UNIVERZITET METROPOLITAN U BEOGRADU ZA 2026/27. ŠKOLSKU GODINU, CENE GODIŠNJIH ŠKOLARINA'. For comparison on the same table: Vizuelne komunikacije EUR 3,990; the IT and management masters EUR 2,990. Muzička produkcija is the most expensive master the university sells.
programs.tuitionNonEU: EUR 4,500 for the degree — CORRECTED, and this is the single most important change to this record. The previous agent reported the non-EU rate as 'NOT PUBLISHED, do not assume it is EUR 4,500, private Serbian universities commonly charge non-regional students more' and built its whole recommendation on that warning. That is wrong. Metropolitan's official master admission page states, under 'Upis stranih državljana': 'Strani državljanin može se upisati na studijski program pod istim uslovima kao i domaći državljani, KAO I POD ISTIM USLOVIMA FINANSIRANJA ŠKOLARINE' — a foreign national enrols under the same conditions as domestic citizens AND under the same tuition-financing conditions. There is no separate foreigner tariff. A Tunisian therefore pays EUR 4,500, the same as a Serbian. The residual caveat is real but minor: the price tables themselves are headed 'ŠKOLARINE ZA NOVE STUDENTE (u EUR) za državljane Srbije i bivših republika SFR Jugoslavije', so the two official statements sit in tension and it is worth one confirming e-mail — but the correct working figure is EUR 4,500, not 'unknown and probably higher'.
programs.otherFees: CORRECTED from 'not published'. Published figures: administrative fee 1,000 RSD payable with the enrolment documents; on enrolment all students must pay a 20% deposit (akontacija) — EUR 900 for this programme — plus a further 20% as the first instalment, no later than 1 October; enrolling after 1 September requires 40% of the tuition up front; the remaining balance runs as 11 monthly instalments of EUR 327.27 with no interest. DISCOUNT: candidates who enrol preliminarily and pay the 20% deposit by 31 March receive a 10% tuition discount, valid for the first year of studies only, and discounts cannot be combined. Nostrification/recognition of his Tunisian diploma is required and is charged separately by the recognising body. Health-insurance cost for foreign students — UNVERIFIED.
programs.totalCostEstimate: EUR 4,500 tuition for the one-year 60-ECTS master, or about EUR 4,050 with the 31 March early-payment discount, plus ~1,000 RSD administrative fee and separate diploma-recognition costs, before living costs in Belgrade, visa and health insurance. If his degree is 180 ECTS he must first fund a fourth bachelor year at Metropolitan, which on the published bachelor table runs EUR 2,990–3,990 depending on programme — pushing the realistic total past EUR 7,000–8,500. Against the state Academy of Arts Novi Sad at EUR 1,800 for a comparable one-year MAS, this is roughly 2.5x on tuition alone. It fails his 'self-pay only if genuinely cheap' test.
programs.fundingLevel: None. A private university with no state-budget places. The only published price reductions are the 10% early-payment discount and interest-free instalments — neither is a scholarship.
programs.scholarships: CONFIRMED: nothing a Tunisian master applicant can win. Re-checked the official Stipendije page. What exists: (1) competition-based full four-year bachelor scholarships for Serbian secondary-school pupils; (2) internal merit scholarships for existing Metropolitan undergraduates in years 2–4, six per year, one per faculty per year level, with fourth-years able to continue tuition-free into a master; (3) a dual-education package created with A+Crowd of Toronto offering free study, EUR 100/month and a guaranteed job, aimed at school-leavers entering IT, management or design. None is open to an incoming foreign master applicant in music production. Anything else would have to be negotiated directly with upis@metropolitan.ac.rs.
programs.visaEligible: Yes in principle, and the case is stronger than the previous record suggested. The programme is a nationally registered accredited MAS (NAT register entry 53, 03.06.2025) at a licensed university, and — importantly for a residence permit — it is accredited for TRADITIONAL IN-PERSON delivery only, with no distance-learning variant, so it is not an online degree that immigration authorities would refuse. That is the class of enrolment that supports a Serbian temporary residence permit for education. A Tunisian needs a long-stay visa D before travel. The university still publishes nothing about visa support or an international-student office — UNVERIFIED at that level; confirm with the Serbian Ministry of Interior (MUP) and the Serbian embassy accredited to Tunisia before paying anything, and ask the university who handles foreign-student enrolment. Serbia is outside the EU/Schengen.
programs.intakes: Rolling. The official admission page states master enrolment 'može se izvršiti bez ograničenja tokom čitave godine'. The Serbian academic year starts in October and the payment schedule is anchored to 1 October, so an October 2027 start is the natural target.
programs.applicationOpens: Rolling, online via the university's application portal. After the online application the candidate receives procedural instructions and submits scanned diploma and transcript; the file then goes to the faculty commission, which issues individual admission conditions and any differential exams. Practical planning date: pay the 20% deposit by 31 March 2027 to secure the 10% discount for a 2027/28 start.
programs.deadline: No published application deadline — rolling admission. The binding dates are financial and immigration ones, not academic: 20% deposit plus 20% first instalment by 1 October; 40% up front if enrolling after 1 September; 31 March for the 10% early-payment discount; and, dominating all of these, the visa D and residence-permit timeline plus the diploma-nostrification timeline, which he should start at least six months ahead.
programs.recommendation: This record needed substantial correction and the programme comes out of it looking better on paper and worse in practice than the previous assessment implied. Three corrections he must hear. FIRST, the previous warning that the price is unknown and probably higher for a non-EU national is WRONG: Metropolitan's own admission rules state that foreign nationals enrol under the same conditions and the same tuition-financing conditions as Serbian citizens, so he pays EUR 4,500 — the published figure, not a mystery. SECOND, the claim that admission requirements are unpublished is also WRONG: they are published in detail, and they are more accommodating than anything at Novi Sad — 240 ECTS required but with an explicit route for a 180-ECTS three-year graduate to complete a fourth Metropolitan bachelor year first; non-cognate first degrees expressly admitted via commission-set differential exams; no entrance exam; no portfolio; rolling admission; full document list published. THIRD, the accreditation is now nailed down: NAT register, accredited 3 June 2025, approved intake 20, in-person Serbian delivery. So it is a real, state-recognised, visa-supporting second-cycle degree — the AVOID verdict reserved for master-priced non-degrees does not apply. What actually blocks him is language and money, not admissions. The programme is accredited for Serbian-language in-person delivery only — the register carries no English-language flag, unlike Metropolitan's own IT and business masters — so an Arabic/French/English speaker cannot follow it in September 2027. And EUR 4,500 (EUR 4,050 with the March discount), or EUR 7,000+ if he must buy a fourth bachelor year first, is 2.5x the state Academy in Novi Sad for a private-university degree with no scholarship he can win. Action if he still wants it: one e-mail to upis@metropolitan.ac.rs asking (a) to confirm in writing that the EUR 4,500 rate applies to a Tunisian national given that the price table is headed for Serbian and ex-SFRY citizens, (b) whether his specific BSc counts as 240 ECTS or requires the fourth-year route, (c) how many differential exams a software-engineering graduate would be set, (d) whether any part of the programme can be followed in English, and (e) whether they issue the enrolment documents needed for a Serbian study visa D.
programs.sourceUrl: https://www.metropolitan.ac.rs/master-studije/muzicka-produkcija/ (official programme page — 60 ECTS, title Master muzički producent, full course list with descriptions, AS Studioton partnership, in-person delivery, EUR 4,500 fee table headed for Serbian/ex-SFRY nationals); https://www.metropolitan.ac.rs/upis/upis-na-master-akademske-studije/ (official master admission rules — 240 ECTS requirement, fourth-year route for 180-ECTS holders, cognate vs non-cognate differential exams, full document list, and the foreign-national clause confirming identical tuition-financing conditions); https://www.metropolitan.ac.rs/upis/skolarine/ (official 2026/27 price list — master table headed 'nastava na srpskom jeziku', EUR 4,500 with EUR 900 deposit and 11 x EUR 327.27, 31 March 10% discount, 1 October payment rule); https://www.metropolitan.ac.rs/o-univerzitetu/akreditacija/ (work licence 2010 with amendments to Nov 2025, accreditation decisions 2017 and 2025); https://www.metropolitan.ac.rs/stipendije/ (scholarships — none for incoming foreign master applicants); https://www.nat.rs/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/Vodič-za-studente-21.07.2026.pdf (Serbian National Accreditation Body register, 21.07.2026 — Univerzitet „Metropolitan“ entry 53, IMT MAS Muzička produkcija accredited 03.06.2025, intake 20, no English-language and no distance-learning variant)

programs.program: Interface Cultures — Master Programme (MA)
programs.institution: Universität für künstlerische und industrielle Gestaltung Linz (Kunstuniversität Linz / University of Arts Linz)
programs.institutionType: Public federal art university (Kunstuniversität) under the Austrian Universitätsgesetz 2002
programs.publicPrivate: PUBLIC — CONFIRMED. The university's own tuition-fee page (kunstuni-linz.at/en/studies/study-admission/tuition-fee) states the international rate is set by 'the 2002 Universities Act' and levies the statutory federal figures (EUR 363.36 / 726.72). It also states plainly that the university 'generally does not offer any scholarships' and that Austrians/equated persons apply to the federal Study Grant Authority — the behaviour of a state institution, not a private provider. Federally funded via the BMBWF. Not a Privatuniversität.
programs.accreditationStatus: CONFIRMED. Real, state-recognised second-cycle degree. Ordentliches Masterstudium under UG 2002 at a federal public university, awarding a Master of Arts. The university's own 'Information for international applicants' PDF describes the exact §64 NAG route: visa to attend the admission exam, return home, then apply for the Aufenthaltsbewilligung – Studierende on the strength of a confirmation of passing the exam issued by studien.office@kunstuni-linz.at.
programs.qualification: Master of Arts (MA), 4 semesters. A genuine second-cycle degree, not a Lehrgang or certificate.
programs.focus: Media art / digital art, interactive art, interface design and participatory practice at the intersection of art, design, technology and artistic research. CORRECTION/UPGRADE: the department's own About text explicitly invites work in 'VR, AR, interactive art, SOUND ART, game design, sustainable IT, HCI research, interaction design, critical data'. Sound art is a named strand — stronger than the previous record implied. It is still NOT music production or audio engineering.
programs.whatYouStudy: Teaching on interactive art and interface technologies; research on cultural aspects of interface and interaction design; focus on critical data and sustainable IT; support in conceptual and practical prototype development. Qualification profile: methodological, conceptual and technological competencies plus supported development of independent artistic projects between physical and virtual worlds (object, performance, immersive setting). Strong Ars Electronica link — the 2026 festival runs 9–13 September in Linz.
programs.durationEcts: 4 semesters. Exact ECTS still not published on any Interface Cultures page — UNVERIFIED (Austrian norm for a 4-semester master is 120). Ask interfacecultures@kunstuni-linz.at.
programs.language: ENGLISH — CONFIRMED by official document. The university's 'Proof of Language Skills' PDF (linked from the central admission page) lists Interface Cultures under: 'The admission boards of the following artistic Master's programmes confirm the required language skills (ENGLISH) as part of the entrance exam.' English is the programme language; German is never required at any point of this degree.
programs.languageRequirement: MAJOR CORRECTION — NO IELTS/TOEFL IS REQUIRED, AT ANY STAGE. Two official statements settle this. (1) The 'Dates entrance examination 2026' PDF: 'Language certificates for international applicants are not required for the entrance exam.' (2) The 'Proof of Language Skills' PDF: for Interface Cultures (and Postdigital Lutherie) 'the admission boards confirm the required language skills (English) as part of the entrance exam' — i.e. the panel judges his English in the interview and no certificate is filed. Contrast this with every other Kunstuni Linz master, all of which are listed in that PDF as needing a German B1 or English B2 CERTIFICATE. Interface Cultures is a named exception. The previous record marked this UNVERIFIED; it is now verified and it is the single strongest thing about this programme for him, because he has not sat IELTS or TOEFL.
programs.entryRequirements: 'To study at Interface Cultures you need a valid bachelor (or equivalent) degree.' The official dates PDF states the enrolment prerequisite for all master's programmes as: 'Master's Degree: a Bachelor's degree or another equivalent certificate' — no subject restriction whatsoever. Plus the departmental entrance exam (portfolio submission + interview). Foreign degrees may need legalisation (see the university's 'Legalization of Foreign Documents in Higher Education' PDF) — a Tunisian BSc will need this, and it takes weeks, so start early. No music degree, no conservatory training, no art degree required.
programs.portfolioSpec: Digital portfolio of own works + letter of motivation + CV + copy of degree, uploaded during online registration at calls.kunstuni-linz.at. The official dates PDF: 'The portfolio must be submitted in digital form. You can find further information on work samples, written examinations and interviews listed by study programme on our homepage and when you are signing up for the exam.' Exact file/format limits are published only inside the live call — UNVERIFIED until a call opens; ask interfacecultures@kunstuni-linz.at.
programs.auditionSpec: No musical audition. A departmental entrance exam consisting of portfolio review and an admission interview (English), held in the department. The sibling programmes run ~30-minute interviews including a 10-minute presentation of selected work samples; international applicants may request Webex participation instead of travelling. CONFIRM Webex availability for Interface Cultures in writing — it removes the visa-to-attend-the-exam problem entirely and is worth more to him than any other single concession.
programs.equipmentRequired: None stated. Department provides shared kit.
programs.facilities: Two dedicated computer rooms, a production workshop, a rapid-prototyping lab (3D printers, soldering stations, laser cutters), and shared equipment including MIDI controllers, cameras, speakers, projectors and VR headsets. No published professional studio, control room or spatial-audio rig. UNCHANGED and still the main substantive weakness for an audio-focused applicant.
programs.intakes: Winter semester (September/October) start. But note there are TWO entrance-exam rounds feeding it (below).
programs.applicationOpens: MAJOR CORRECTION — there are TWO opening dates per year, not one. Per the official 'Dates entrance examination 2026' PDF (document dated 15.07.2026): summer round opens 18 March; autumn round opens 01 August. For a September 2027 start expect roughly 18 March 2027 and 01 August 2027.
programs.deadline: MAJOR CORRECTION — the previous record said 'spring deadline only, UNVERIFIED'. Both rounds are now verified from the official PDF. SUMMER ROUND: online registration + portfolio 18 March – 09 June 2026, entrance exam 30 June – 01 July 2026. AUTUMN ROUND: online registration + portfolio 01 – 25 August 2026, entrance exam 15 September 2026. Both feed academic year 2026/27. PLANNING CONSEQUENCE FOR HIM: for a September 2027 start his two shots are approximately 18 March – 09 June 2027 (exam late June/early July) and 01 – 25 August 2027 (exam mid-September). Neither falls in the October–February window he has assumed — but the August round is a genuine second chance in the same cycle, which almost no directory records. Also worth stating plainly: the autumn 2026 round (registration 01–25 August 2026, exam 15 September 2026) is OPEN AS OF TODAY, 7 August 2026. He has no portfolio, so this is not actionable — but it proves the pattern and he should watch that same page in August 2027.
programs.tuitionEU: EUR 363.36 per semester statutory rate; EU/EEA and Austrian nationals exempt during the standard duration plus a two-semester grace period.
programs.tuitionNonEU: EUR 726.72 PER SEMESTER — CONFIRMED on the university's own tuition-fee page ('Euro 726.72 per semester' for international students) and repeated verbatim on the sibling Postdigital Lutherie admission page ('non-EU-citizens currently have to pay a fee of 726,72 € per semester'). This is the rate he pays as a Tunisian national. EUR 1,453.44 per year; EUR 2,906.88 for the whole 4-semester degree. Among the cheapest real master's degrees in Western Europe. Payment must be complete within the admission period — partial payment is not accepted and non-payment means no admission or de-matriculation.
programs.otherFees: CORRECTION — ÖH student union fee (incl. liability insurance) is EUR 26.20 PER SEMESTER for winter semester 2026/27, not the EUR 24.70 previously recorded. The figure is indexed annually; confirm at enrolment. ADDITION the previous record missed entirely: Austrian student self-insurance (health) runs about EUR 65 per month for students not covered by a parent's policy — roughly EUR 780/year, EUR 1,560 over the degree. This is a bigger line than tuition and it is compulsory in practice for a residence permit.
programs.totalCostEstimate: Institutional cost over 2 years: tuition EUR 2,906.88 + ÖH EUR 104.80 = EUR 3,011.68. Add health insurance ~EUR 1,560. Realistic institutional + insurance total ~EUR 4,570 for the whole degree. Living costs in Linz are the dominant expense and are not published by the university. For the residence permit he must additionally prove sufficient means to the Magistrat der Stadt Linz or BH Linz-Land (annual ASVG-linked figure — confirm with the Austrian embassy in Tunis / OeAD).
programs.scholarships: CORRECTION — the previous record said 'none'. There is one real, winnable instrument: the ÖH Kunstuniversität Linz TUITION FEE GRANT (Zuschuss zum Studienbeitrag), administered by the student union's University Representation. It is a pot of just under EUR 15,000 per semester distributed by a jury (chair of the University Representation, economic advisor, social department advisor) as a REFUND of tuition already paid. It is explicitly open to 'regular degree students (Austrian or foreign nationals)' — so a Tunisian master's student qualifies. Announced each semester via calls.kunstuni-linz.at (e.g. 'Tuition Fee Grant SS24'); contact oeh.sozial@kunstuni-linz.at. It will not fund living costs, but it can plausibly zero out the EUR 726.72. SEPARATELY: the university's own 'scholarships' page is entirely OUTGOING mobility funding for Austrians going abroad — nothing there applies to an incoming Tunisian, and the tuition-fee page states the university 'generally does not offer any scholarships'. External route remains OeAD/grants.at; the Ernst Mach Grant is oriented to short research stays, not full masters — still UNVERIFIED as a full-degree route.
programs.visaEligible: Yes — CONFIRMED, with the exact procedure published. The university's 'Information for international applicants' PDF sets out the visa-required path: (1) apply at the Austrian embassy/consulate for a visa to PARTICIPATE IN THE ADMISSION EXAMINATION; (2) return to Tunisia by the visa expiry; (3) on passing, request the residence permit – student through the Austrian representation, using the confirmation of passing issued by studien.office@kunstuni-linz.at; (4) permit issued by the district authority (Magistrat der Stadt Linz for Linz city). So he may need a visa TWICE — once for the exam, once to study — unless the interview is granted by Webex. Ask for Webex.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: YES — explicitly and without qualification. The official requirement is 'a valid bachelor (or equivalent) degree' / 'a Bachelor's degree or another equivalent certificate'. No subject restriction, no music degree, no art degree, no conservatory training, no audition. A BSc Software Engineering with a strong interactive/sound portfolio is a coherent and even attractive application here.
programs.recommendation: THE BEST-FITTING AND MOST ATTAINABLE PROGRAMME IN THIS SET — and it is stronger than the previous record concluded, because the language question is now settled in his favour. Confirmed advantages: English-taught with the language judged at interview and NO certificate ever required (he never has to sit IELTS or TOEFL for this one); EUR 726.72/semester with a real ÖH fee-refund fund on top; any bachelor accepted; no audition; a portfolio gate a software engineer can genuinely build in a year; sound art named by the department itself; the Ars Electronica connection. Confirmed limits: it is media art, not music production — it will not train him as a DJ or a record producer, and there is no published pro studio or spatial-audio rig. THREE CORRECTIONS TO HIS PLANNING. (1) There are TWO application rounds a year (≈18 Mar–09 Jun and 01–25 Aug), not one, and neither is in his assumed Oct–Feb window. (2) No English certificate is needed — he can stop worrying about IELTS for this application. (3) Start the Tunisian degree legalisation now; it is slower than the portfolio. ACTIONS: email interfacecultures@kunstuni-linz.at and ask (a) for the exact portfolio spec, (b) whether the admission interview can be held via Webex — this would save him an entire embassy visa run for the exam, and (c) the ECTS figure. ALSO FLAG, because it may be the better programme: the same university runs POSTDIGITAL LUTHERIE (MA) in the Tangible Interaction Design department (Prof. Martin Kaltenbrunner, tamlab). Its official admission page states: 'you need a valid bachelor (or equivalent) degree'; 'German skills are not required to join the programme. Our faculty can support German, English and Spanish speaking students'; same EUR 726.72/semester; same two rounds (18 Mar–19 Jun and 01 Aug–01 Sep in 2026). Postdigital lutherie is the design and building of new digital musical instruments — measurably closer to his stated goal than media art is. He should apply to BOTH in the same cycle; the marginal cost is one extra portfolio submission.

programs.program: Zeitbasierte Medien / Timebased Media — Master Programme (MA)
programs.institution: Universität für künstlerische und industrielle Gestaltung Linz (Kunstuniversität Linz / University of Arts Linz)
programs.institutionType: Public federal art university (Kunstuniversität) under the Austrian Universitätsgesetz 2002
programs.publicPrivate: PUBLIC — CONFIRMED. Same federal university, same UG 2002 statutory fee schedule, same BMBWF funding. Not a private provider.
programs.accreditationStatus: CONFIRMED. Ordentliches Masterstudium under UG 2002 awarding a Master of Arts. Supports the §64 NAG student residence permit via the procedure published in the university's 'Information for international applicants' PDF.
programs.qualification: Master of Arts (MA), 4 semesters. A genuine second-cycle degree.
programs.focus: Time-based media: video practice and theory, film theory, SOUND, media installation and staging, interactive systems, design with digital media, innovative programming. Sound is a named component — the reason this programme is on the list.
programs.whatYouStudy: Interdisciplinary work across time-based media — audiovisual culture, moving image, sound, installation, interactive systems and creative coding; professional handling of works and products of audiovisual culture.
programs.durationEcts: 4 semesters. ECTS not published — UNVERIFIED (Austrian norm 120). Ask gerlinde.schmierer@kunstuni-linz.at.
programs.language: GERMAN AND ENGLISH. The official registration/admission page states the programme accommodates both, and that admission interviews can be held in English for international applicants on request. Bilingual in practice, not English-only. The language-certificate rule below confirms the programme expects a student to work in one or the other.
programs.languageRequirement: CORRECTED AND NOW PRECISE — and it is materially worse for him than for Interface Cultures. The official 'Proof of Language Skills' PDF places Timebased Media (MA) in the group requiring 'a German language certificate at level B1 OR an English language certificate at level B2'. Critically: 'The ENGLISH language certificate needs to be submitted AT THE TIME OF ENROLMENT. Otherwise, students need to provide a German language certificate before they can receive the enrolment confirmation for their third semester.' So: no certificate is needed for the entrance exam itself (the dates PDF confirms 'language certificates for international applicants are not required for the entrance exam'), but he MUST hand over an English B2 certificate — i.e. an IELTS/TOEFL or equivalent — when he enrols, or else reach certified German B1 within a year. He has taken neither test. Unlike Interface Cultures, this programme gives him no exemption. Budget for IELTS.
programs.entryRequirements: 'A completed bachelor degree programme in a study area with interdisciplinary focuses' — the page names time-based/interactive media, media design, film, video, sound, or comparable credentials from accredited institutions. Plus the departmental entrance exam. RISK UNCHANGED AND CONFIRMED: unlike Interface Cultures this programme names related disciplines rather than accepting any bachelor. A Software Engineering BSc rides on the 'comparable' clause and on the portfolio. Get it confirmed in writing before investing. Note also that the central dates PDF states the generic master's prerequisite as simply 'a Bachelor's degree or another equivalent certificate' — so the departmental wording is the binding constraint, not the university's.
programs.portfolioSpec: Four-step procedure, all published officially: (1) online registration through the university portal; (2) upload of portfolio AND a short letter of motivation explaining personal goals and fit; (3) admission interview with the Selection Committee, approx. 30 minutes, requiring a ten-minute presentation of selected work samples; (4) result by email and PIN. The committee assesses aptitude and how the work aligns with the programme's academic profile. Exact format/size limits not published — UNVERIFIED.
programs.auditionSpec: No musical audition. A 30-minute selection interview with a 10-minute presentation of work samples. IMPORTANT AND CONFIRMED: 'Interviews occur in-person but international applicants may request Webex participation by notifying gerlinde.schmierer@kunstuni-linz.at.' This removes the need for a separate Austrian visa merely to attend the exam — a concrete, decisive advantage over every Swiss option in this set. Request it in writing at registration.
programs.equipmentRequired: None stated.
programs.facilities: Still not published on the programme pages — UNVERIFIED. The department covers video, film, sound, media installation and interactive systems, so post-production facilities exist, but there is no published equipment inventory (studios, monitoring, spatial audio). Ask gerlinde.schmierer@kunstuni-linz.at for a facilities list before applying — for an audio-focused applicant this is the decisive unknown.
programs.intakes: Winter semester (September/October) start, fed by two entrance-exam rounds.
programs.applicationOpens: CORRECTED — two openings per year: mid-December and mid-March. For 2026/27 the official dates PDF gives 15 December 2025 (winter round) and 18 March 2026 (summer round). Expect roughly mid-December 2026 and mid-March 2027 for a September 2027 start.
programs.deadline: MAJOR CORRECTION — the previous record recorded only the spring round and concluded the deadline falls outside his planning window. That is wrong. The official 'Dates entrance examination 2026' PDF (dated 15.07.2026) lists TWO rounds for Timebased Media (MA): WINTER ROUND — online registration and portfolio 15 December 2025 – 18 January 2026, exam 04 February 2026. SUMMER ROUND — online registration and portfolio 18 March – 07 June 2026, exam 30 June – 01 July 2026. There is NO autumn round for this programme (unlike Interface Cultures). PLANNING CONSEQUENCE: the winter round — roughly mid-December 2026 to mid-January 2027, exam early February 2027 — falls squarely INSIDE his October 2026–February 2027 window. This is one of only two programmes in this set that does. He can apply in the winter round and, if unsuccessful, apply again in the summer round of the same cycle.
programs.tuitionEU: EUR 363.36 per semester statutory rate; EU/EEA nationals exempt for the standard duration plus two semesters.
programs.tuitionNonEU: EUR 726.72 PER SEMESTER — CONFIRMED on the university's tuition-fee page. EUR 1,453.44/year; EUR 2,906.88 for the full degree. Payment in full within the admission period; partial payment not accepted.
programs.otherFees: CORRECTION — ÖH fee incl. insurance is EUR 26.20 per semester for WS 2026/27, not EUR 24.70. Indexed annually. ADDITION: Austrian student health self-insurance ~EUR 65/month (~EUR 1,560 over the degree) for students not covered by a parent's policy.
programs.totalCostEstimate: Institutional: EUR 2,906.88 tuition + EUR 104.80 ÖH = EUR 3,011.68 over 2 years. Plus ~EUR 1,560 health insurance. Plus IELTS/TOEFL exam cost (needed here, unlike Interface Cultures). Plus living costs in Linz and the means-of-subsistence proof for the residence permit.
programs.scholarships: CORRECTION — same as Interface Cultures: the ÖH Kunstuniversität Linz tuition-fee grant fund (~EUR 15,000/semester pot, refunds tuition already paid, explicitly open to foreign nationals) is a real partial route. Apply via calls.kunstuni-linz.at each semester; contact oeh.sozial@kunstuni-linz.at. No programme-level scholarship; the university's published 'scholarships' page is outgoing-mobility funding for Austrians only and is irrelevant to him. External: OeAD/grants.at, UNVERIFIED for a full master's.
programs.visaEligible: Yes — §64 NAG standard route. AND the Webex interview option means he may not need a separate visa to attend the entrance exam, only the study permit. That is a genuine cost and timeline saving.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: PARTIALLY — CONFIRMED UNCHANGED. No music degree is needed anywhere, but the named prior fields are media/film/video/sound rather than 'any bachelor'. A CS/software background must be carried by the 'comparable' clause plus the portfolio. Ask the department in writing before applying.
programs.recommendation: APPLY TO IT ALONGSIDE INTERFACE CULTURES — and the case is now stronger than the previous record allowed, for one reason it got wrong. There is a WINTER round (registration ≈15 December – 18 January, exam early February) as well as the spring round, so this is one of only two programmes in this set whose deadline lands inside his October–February planning window. Advantages: sound is an explicitly named subject; German is never required at entry; the fee is the same EUR 726.72/semester; no audition; the interview can be taken by Webex from Tunis. Disadvantages against Interface Cultures: the bachelor-field requirement is narrower and he must argue 'comparable'; teaching is bilingual rather than English-only; and he WOULD need an English B2 certificate (IELTS/TOEFL) at enrolment, which Interface Cultures waives entirely. No facilities inventory is published — a serious unknown for someone whose goal is production. ACTIONS, all free and all decision-changing: write to gerlinde.schmierer@kunstuni-linz.at asking (a) does a BSc Software Engineering count as 'comparable' for admission, (b) what audio facilities does the department actually have, (c) confirm Webex interview availability, and (d) which English certificates satisfy the B2 requirement. Then sit IELTS in good time — for this programme, unlike Interface Cultures, he cannot avoid it.
