programs.program: Digital Arts (Master) — Master of Arts in Arts and Design
programs.institution: FH Oberösterreich / University of Applied Sciences Upper Austria, Campus Hagenberg (FH OÖ Studienbetriebs GmbH)
programs.institutionType: Fachhochschule (university of applied sciences), Austrian FH sector
programs.publicPrivate: PUBLIC-SECTOR, with the same precise caveat as before — CONFIRMED. FH programmes run through a legally separate provider company (FH OÖ Studienbetriebs GmbH) but are publicly co-financed per study place and state-accredited under the Fachhochschulgesetz via AQ Austria. Hard evidence it sits on the public side: its own Financial Matters page levies exactly the statutory federal rates (EUR 363.36 EU / EUR 726.72 third-country), collects the ÖH fee, and operates the statutory 'close relationship to Austria' fee-reduction mechanism — none of which a genuinely private provider does. Company shareholding (Province of Upper Austria) still not stated on the pages consulted — UNVERIFIED; confirm at studienbeitrag@fh-ooe.at or in the Firmenbuch if it matters for a scholarship form.
programs.accreditationStatus: CONFIRMED. Real, state-recognised second-cycle degree. Austrian FH master's degrees are accredited under the Fachhochschulgesetz and quality-assured by AQ Austria; the award is 'Master of Arts in Arts and Design', a standard Austrian FH master title. Supports the §64 NAG student residence permit.
programs.qualification: Master of Arts in Arts and Design (MA). 4 semesters, full time. A genuine second-cycle degree — not a Lehrgang, not a certificate.
programs.focus: Digital arts: 2D/3D animation, motion design, visualisation, games and mixed reality, with an Audio/Video & Games strand. CONFIRMED: the master's emphasis is animation/motion/games. Audio is a supporting discipline, not the subject.
programs.whatYouStudy: Deepening and specialisation in 2D/3D animation, motion design, visualisation, games and mixed reality, within an Audio/Video & Games framing. Semester abroad possible in semesters 3 and 4.
programs.durationEcts: 4 semesters, full time. Total ECTS still not stated on the programme page — UNVERIFIED (Austrian norm 120). Ask da@fh-hagenberg.at.
programs.language: GERMAN — CONFIRMED. The official fact box states flatly 'Language: German'. There is no English track. Decisive against him: he has no German at all.
programs.languageRequirement: 'Good proficiency in German' is written into the access requirements — CONFIRMED. No CEFR level or named certificate is published — UNVERIFIED; ask da@fh-hagenberg.at which level and which certificates are accepted. Austrian FH practice is B2. From zero, B2 is realistically two years of sustained study, which does not fit a September 2027 start.
programs.entryRequirements: THE HARD GATE — CONFIRMED VERBATIM: 'Completion of at least a 6 semester specialised relevant Bachelor's degree (e.g. in the field of media technology, media design, video/film and timebased & interactive media) with audio/video, multimedia and computer animation strand worth a MINIMUM OF 60 ECTS towards accreditation, or comparable higher education at university level. Good proficiency in German.' A BSc Software Engineering will not normally carry 60 ECTS of audio/video/multimedia/animation coursework. This is a credit-count gap, not a portfolio-fixable gap. Two independent blockers therefore stand: the 60 ECTS rule and the German rule.
programs.portfolioSpec: Selection process is 'Interview, Portfolio (could include graphic design, drawings, short-films, animations, games, etc.)' — CONFIRMED. Note again that audio work is not among the listed example items.
programs.auditionSpec: None. No musical audition. Interview plus portfolio review.
programs.equipmentRequired: None stated.
programs.facilities: Still not published on the programme page — UNVERIFIED. Hagenberg is a media-technology campus with animation and games labs; no audio studio inventory is published. Ask da@fh-hagenberg.at.
programs.intakes: Annual intake, 20 places, winter-semester (autumn) start.
programs.applicationOpens: Still not published as a fixed opening date — UNVERIFIED; ask da@fh-hagenberg.at.
programs.deadline: CONFIRMED for the 2026/27 cycle: 31 MAY 2026 for applicants who require a visa; 30 June 2026 general deadline for EU/EEA citizens, holders of valid residence permits and visa-free entrants; 31 August 2026 extended deadline if places remain. PRIOR CYCLE — confirm the 2027 dates. CRITICAL FOR HIM: as a Tunisian national he falls under the EARLIER 31 May visa-required deadline, a full month before everyone else. Expect roughly 31 May 2027 for a September 2027 start — again a spring, not an autumn/winter, deadline.
programs.tuitionEU: EUR 363.36 per semester for Austrian residents, EU citizens and nationals of Norway, Iceland, Liechtenstein and Switzerland — CONFIRMED on the FH OÖ Financial Matters page.
programs.tuitionNonEU: EUR 726.72 PER SEMESTER — CONFIRMED verbatim as the third-country rate for non-EU/EEA nationals holding a student residence permit. This is the rate he would pay. EUR 2,906.88 over the degree. FH OÖ also publishes the reduction mechanism: third-country nationals may request a cut from EUR 726.72 to EUR 363.36 in writing to studienbeitrag@fh-ooe.at on proof of a 'close relationship to Austria' — the listed qualifying cases are recognised refugees, relatives of diplomatic personnel, holders of Austrian secondary school certificates issued abroad, persons with their centre of interests in Austria for 5+ years, and Red-White-Red Card holders. NONE of these applies to a first-time arrival from Tunis.
programs.otherFees: CORRECTION AND RESOLUTION OF THE PREVIOUS AMBIGUITY — FH OÖ's own Financial Matters page now states the ÖH fee as EUR 26.20 per semester, mandatory for all students, including liability insurance. The EUR 24.70 figure in the previous record is out of date; use 26.20. MAJOR ADDITION the previous record missed: FH OÖ publishes that student self-insurance for health costs approximately EUR 65 PER MONTH for most bachelor's and master's students not covered by a parent's policy — about EUR 780/year, EUR 1,560 over the degree. That is more than half the tuition again and it is not optional in practice.
programs.totalCostEstimate: Institutional: EUR 2,906.88 tuition + EUR 104.80 ÖH = EUR 3,011.68 over 2 years. Plus ~EUR 1,560 health insurance. Plus German tuition to B2 (an unbudgeted year or two of language school). Plus living costs in Upper Austria and the means-of-subsistence proof for the residence permit.
programs.scholarships: None published for this programme — CONFIRMED. Most Austrian study-grant instruments (Studienbeihilfe) are restricted to Austrians and equated persons, so any generic Austrian FH funding scheme in the database should be assumed NOT to cover a Tunisian national unless proven otherwise. UNVERIFIED; ask the FH OÖ international office. Note that FH OÖ, unlike Kunstuni Linz, has no equivalent ÖH tuition-refund fund published.
programs.visaEligible: Yes — an Austrian FH master's degree programme supports the §64 NAG student residence permit. FH OÖ's earlier 31 May deadline for visa-required applicants exists precisely to allow visa processing time.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: NO music degree is required — but a media/audio-video bachelor carrying 60 ECTS in the relevant strands effectively IS required. That, plus German, is the binding constraint. Music is irrelevant to why he is blocked.
programs.recommendation: REPORT AS A NEAR-MISS, NOT A TARGET — the previous assessment stands and is confirmed on every point. He is blocked twice over, independently: teaching is entirely in German with 'good proficiency in German' written into the admission rule, and admission demands 60 ECTS of audio/video/multimedia/animation credit in the bachelor, which a Software Engineering BSc will not have. Audio is a minor strand here rather than the subject. The programme is cheap and genuinely accredited, which is why it is worth keeping in the database — but not for him. He should not spend time on it unless (a) his transcript unexpectedly shows 60 ECTS of media coursework AND (b) he commits to German to B2, in which case a 2028 or 2029 intake, not 2027, is the realistic target. Two dates to remember if he ever does pursue it: 31 May is his deadline (a month before everyone else's, because he needs a visa), and the intake is only 20 places.

programs.program: Master of Arts in Music — Major MUSIC AND DIGITAL CREATION (corrected; the previous record examined the wrong major)
programs.institution: Hochschule Luzern – Musik (Lucerne School of Music, Lucerne University of Applied Sciences and Arts), delivered jointly with Hochschule Luzern – Informatik
programs.city: Lucerne / Kriens, with teaching also at Campus Zug-Rotkreuz
programs.institutionType: University of applied sciences and arts (Fachhochschule), music department in partnership with the computer science department
programs.publicPrivate: PUBLIC — CONFIRMED. Hochschule Luzern is the university of applied sciences and arts of central Switzerland, carried by the six central Swiss cantons under the FH Zentralschweiz concordat (its own site footers as 'FH Zentralschweiz' on every page) and institutionally accredited under the federal HFKG — the footer states 'Institutionell akkreditiert nach HFKG 2019–2026'. Not a private conservatory or foundation school.
programs.accreditationStatus: CONFIRMED. Real, state-recognised second-cycle Swiss degree, institutionally accredited under the HFKG. Supports a Swiss student residence permit (B permit for studies) for a non-EU national, subject to cantonal quota and proof of funds.
programs.qualification: Master of Arts in Music, Major Music and Digital Creation. 4 semesters, 120 ECTS — CONFIRMED ('A Master's programme comprises 120 ECTS-Credits and typically consists of a Major and a Minor'). A genuine second-cycle Swiss degree.
programs.focus: MAJOR CORRECTION — THE PREVIOUS RECORD EXAMINED THE WRONG PROGRAMME. It assessed Major Komposition plus electronic minors and concluded the candidate could not clear a conservatory gate. HSLU actually runs a Major MUSIC AND DIGITAL CREATION, launched autumn 2022 jointly by HSLU Musik and HSLU Informatik, built specifically for people coming from computing. Its stated aim (official Studienführer): building 'Information and Communications Technologies' competencies and linking them to musical content, with depth in 'Data Science' and 'Digital Creation'. There are two published curricula — 'Curriculum Major Music and Digital Creation MIT BA Informatik' and 'OHNE BA Informatik' — i.e. the programme is explicitly designed around applicants who already hold a computing bachelor. That is exactly him. The Minor Electronic Music Composition, Minor Groove und Electronics and Minor Media Composer are all confirmed as Master-level minors and can be stacked on top.
programs.whatYouStudy: Data science and digital creation applied to music; independent development, planning and execution of projects; elective modules in music practice, pedagogy or theory. Stackable Master minors confirmed from the official minors index: Electronic Music Composition, Groove und Electronics, Media Composer, Digitale Kompetenzen für Musik/Bildung/Kultur, Komposition, Jazz, Improvisation, Music Research and 13 others. Teaching is split across Lucerne School of Music (Arsenalstrasse 28a, Luzern-Kriens) and Lucerne School of Computer Science (Campus Zug-Rotkreuz).
programs.durationEcts: 4 semesters, 120 ECTS, full time — CONFIRMED. NOTE ON THE PREVIOUS RECORD'S 'THEORY PLACEMENT' WARNING: it is real but overstated. The official exam-contents page describes the master 'theory assessment' as something candidates complete only 'under certain conditions', where 'the result determines their PLACEMENT IN THE THEORY MODULES' — a streaming test, not a pass-or-leave gate. Whether he must sit it is 'communicated upon admission to the entrance examination'. Content, if required: two harmonic dictations with secondary dominants and altered chords, a two-part polyphonic dictation, and analysis of a Viennese Classical movement. That is still hard for a self-taught producer and he should prepare for it, but it does not by itself end the application.
programs.language: GERMAN is the language of instruction at HSLU – Musik. CAVEAT WORTH CHECKING: because this major is co-delivered with HSLU Informatik at Campus Zug-Rotkreuz, part of the data-science content may run in English. Not published — UNVERIFIED. Ask Daniella Gerszt (Studienkoordinatorin Major Music and Digital Creation, +41 41 249 26 05) directly, because the answer materially changes how feasible the first year is for him.
programs.languageRequirement: MAJOR CORRECTION — THE PREVIOUS RECORD OVERSTATED THIS BADLY. It claimed B1 German must be certified before studies begin. The official admission-requirements page (German original) says the opposite for Master's programmes: 'das Beherrschen der deutschen Sprache (im ersten Studienjahr A2-Niveau, danach B1-Niveau)' — A2 in the FIRST YEAR of study, rising to B1 from the second year. Higher levels apply only to other majors (B2 from the start for Instrumental/Vocal Pedagogy; B1 then B2 for Church Music; C1 from the start for Musiktheorie and Schulmusik II; C1 English from the start for Artistic Research — none of which is his). And 'knowledge of German is not required for the entrance examination'. NO English certificate is required for this major. Practical effect: he can sit the entrance exam with no German, and only needs A2 — a genuinely low bar, a few months of evening classes — during his first year. This turns German from a blocker into an errand.
programs.entryRequirements: MAJOR CORRECTION, AND THE SINGLE MOST IMPORTANT FINDING IN THIS RE-CHECK. The official Studienreglement für die Ausbildung (Musik), section on master admission, states: 'Für den Master of Arts in Music, Major Music and Digital Creation gelten, weil es sich um ein interdisziplinäres Angebot in Zusammenarbeit mit der Hochschule Luzern – Informatik handelt, gesonderte Zulassungsvoraussetzungen: a. das Bachelor-Diplom EINER FACHHOCHSCHULE (Sur-Dossier-Aufnahme); b. das Bestehen des Zulassungsverfahrens (Praxis, Theorie, Gespräch), mit dem die Eignung für die musikspezifischen Module abgeklärt wird; c. das Erbringen der für die verschiedenen musikspezifischen Ausrichtungen zusätzlich formulierten Zusatzqualifikationen. Die Voraussetzungen a–c müssen kumulativ erfüllt sein.' The public admission page puts it more simply: 'Für den Major Music and Digital Creation genügt ein an einer Fachhochschule erworbener Bachelor-Abschluss («Sur-Dossier-Aufnahme») – EGAL IN WELCHEM STUDIENGANG' — a UAS bachelor in ANY subject suffices. So NO music degree is required for this major. The previous record's flat 'NO, not realistically' was correct for Major Komposition and wrong for the programme he should actually be looking at. THE ONE REAL UNKNOWN: 'Bachelor-Diplom einer Fachhochschule' means a university-of-applied-sciences diploma. His BSc is from SMU MedTech, a private Tunisian university, not a Swiss-style FH. Whether HSLU treats it as equivalent under the sur-dossier route is THE decision-changing question and must be asked in writing before anything else.
programs.portfolioSpec: CORRECTED — no conventional portfolio and no score dossier is required for this major (that requirement belongs to Major Komposition, which demands three scores plus recordings, none older than two years). For Music and Digital Creation the official exam-contents page requires: 'At the latest three weeks before the entrance exam, a short description (ONE A4 PAGE) must be submitted outlining a project combining music and computer science that the candidate wishes to realise within the major studies.' That is the entire written submission. For a software engineer with a year to think, this is an extraordinarily low-friction entry document — but it must be a genuinely good idea, because the whole interview turns on it.
programs.auditionSpec: CORRECTED — no conservatory audition, but not nothing either. Official exam contents, verbatim: 'Candidates with a Bachelor of Arts in Music — Examination interview with the jury on the candidate's project description, expectations of the programme, training content and objectives, and previous knowledge of computer science / IT. Candidates with NO Bachelor of Arts in Music («sur dossier») — PRACTICAL AND THEORETICAL EXAMINATION ADDRESSING THE CANDIDATE'S MUSICAL ORIENTATION, plus examination interview with the jury on the candidate's project description, expectations of the programme, training content and objectives, and previous knowledge of MUSIC.' So he faces a practical and theoretical music examination — but one framed around HIS OWN musical orientation, not a fixed classical repertoire. A serious electronic-production practice, demonstrated live and discussed knowledgeably, is a legitimate answer to it. Ask Daniella Gerszt exactly what the practical part looks like for an electronic-music applicant; this is not published.
programs.equipmentRequired: Not published — UNVERIFIED. Ask musik@hslu.ch.
programs.facilities: Not published — UNVERIFIED, and worth pressing on. HSLU – Musik runs a Bachelor specialisation and Master minors in Groove und Electronics and a Minor Electronic Music Composition, so electronic-music studios must exist. Ask musik@hslu.ch and Daniella Gerszt for a studio and equipment inventory before applying — for a candidate whose goal is production this matters more than the curriculum text.
programs.intakes: Autumn (September) start, one intake per year — consistent with the single 28 February deadline.
programs.applicationOpens: Not published as a fixed opening date — UNVERIFIED; online registration runs up to the 28 February deadline. Fees are due at online registration.
programs.deadline: 28 FEBRUARY ANNUALLY (29 February in a leap year) — CONFIRMED verbatim on the official application page: 'The application deadline for ALL degree programmes is 28 February.' A standing annual rule, not a cycle-specific date. Confirmed independently on the Major Music and Digital Creation page. THIS IS ONE OF ONLY TWO PROGRAMMES IN THIS SET WHOSE DEADLINE FALLS INSIDE HIS OCTOBER 2026 – FEBRUARY 2027 WINDOW: for a September 2027 start he applies by 28 February 2027. Note the one-A4-page project description is due at the latest three weeks before the entrance exam, not at the deadline.
programs.tuitionEU: CHF 800 per semester for domestic students. Switzerland's split is Swiss/resident versus foreign-domiciled, NOT EU versus non-EU — an EU national moving to Switzerland to study pays the same surcharge he would.
programs.tuitionNonEU: CHF 1,300 PER SEMESTER — CONFIRMED verbatim: 'CHF 1'300.– for international students (for students with foreign citizenship who enter or have entered Switzerland for the purpose of studying).' CHF 2,600 per year; CHF 5,200 over the 4-semester master. The surcharge exists because students entering Switzerland to study do not attract cantonal FHV subsidies.
programs.otherFees: All CONFIRMED on the official fee page, and they are substantial. PER SEMESTER on top of tuition: module examination CHF 150, photocopying flat rate CHF 45, service fee CHF 45, university sport CHF 25 — CHF 265 per semester. ONE-OFF: enrolment CHF 390, HSLU Card CHF 50, degree and certification CHF 220. ADMISSION: CHF 200 per entrance examination (credited on enrolment) plus CHF 390 for two practical examinations. OTHER: break from studies CHF 200/semester, student exchange application CHF 200, additional one-to-one lessons CHF 500.
programs.totalCostEstimate: Fees only, over 4 semesters: tuition 4 × CHF 1,300 = CHF 5,200; compulsory per-semester extras 4 × CHF 265 = CHF 1,060; one-offs CHF 1,250 (enrolment 390 + practical exams 390 + admission 200 + card 50 + diploma 220). Institutional total ≈ CHF 7,510, of which the CHF 200 admission fee is credited back on enrolment, so ≈ CHF 7,310 net. Living costs in Lucerne dominate and are not published — Switzerland is by far the most expensive country in this set, and the Swiss student permit requires proof of sufficient means (figure set cantonally — UNVERIFIED; confirm with the Swiss representation in Tunis and the Kanton Luzern migration office).
programs.scholarships: Nothing published at programme level. The relevant instrument remains the Swiss Government Excellence Scholarships — Art Scholarships stream, which funds a first master's at a Swiss music university for a foreign national. Tunisia's inclusion in the ART-stream country list (narrower than the research-scholarship list) changes yearly and must be confirmed on the SERI/FCS official list for the 2027 call. UNVERIFIED for this programme. Note that unlike the Lugano conservatory (see below), HSLU publishes no internal scholarship fund of its own.
programs.visaEligible: Yes in principle — an accredited Swiss hochschule degree programme supports a student residence permit. But Swiss student permits for non-EU nationals are discretionary, cantonally handled, quota-constrained, and require proof of funds and of intent to leave. He should also expect to need a visa merely to travel to Lucerne for the entrance examination — HSLU states all entrance examinations take place ON SITE, with no published remote option (unlike Kunstuni Linz, which offers Webex). Budget months for this.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: YES FOR THIS MAJOR — REVERSING THE PREVIOUS RECORD'S 'NO'. The Studienreglement grants Major Music and Digital Creation a sur-dossier admission route on the strength of a Fachhochschule bachelor in ANY subject. No music degree, no conservatory bachelor. He must still pass the practical/theoretical music examination and the interview, and satisfy any additional major-specific qualifications, all three cumulatively — but the door is open in a way it is emphatically not for Major Komposition. THE OPEN QUESTION IS INSTITUTIONAL, NOT MUSICAL: does a Tunisian private-university BSc count as 'ein an einer Fachhochschule erworbener Bachelor-Abschluss'?
programs.recommendation: PROMOTED FROM 'FILE IT, DO NOT CHASE IT' TO A LIVE TARGET — the previous record assessed Major Komposition and reached a verdict that does not apply to the major he should actually pursue. Corrected picture: HSLU's Major Music and Digital Creation is a joint Musik/Informatik master, expressly built for computing graduates, with a published curriculum variant for holders of a computing bachelor, an admission rule that accepts a UAS bachelor in any subject sur dossier, an entrance submission consisting of ONE A4 PAGE describing a music-plus-computing project, German at only A2 in year one, and a standing 28 February deadline that lands inside his planning window. On top of the major he can stack Minor Electronic Music Composition, Minor Groove und Electronics or Minor Media Composer — the closest thing to electronic-music-production training in central Switzerland. THE REAL CAVEATS, and they are why this is B and not A. (1) He must pass a practical AND theoretical music examination as a sur-dossier candidate — soft compared with a composition audition, but not a formality for someone with no training at all; he needs a year of serious, demonstrable practice. (2) The 'Fachhochschule bachelor' wording may not stretch to a Tunisian private university — unresolved and decisive. (3) Cost: ~CHF 7,300 institutional plus Lucerne living costs, the highest in this set, with no funding he is known to qualify for beyond the Swiss Government Excellence Art Scholarships, whose country list must be checked. (4) Entrance exams are on site only, so budget for a separate exam visa. (5) The major leans data science and digital creation, not DJing or record production. THREE EMAILS TO SEND NOW, all free, all decision-changing, to Daniella Gerszt (Studienkoordinatorin, +41 41 249 26 05) and musik@hslu.ch: (a) does a BSc from a private Tunisian university satisfy the 'Bachelor-Diplom einer Fachhochschule' sur-dossier condition; (b) what exactly does the practical and theoretical music examination consist of for an applicant whose musical orientation is electronic production; (c) how much of the major is taught in English at Campus Zug-Rotkreuz. If (a) comes back yes, this becomes his strongest non-Austrian option and he should build the year around the one-page project idea and the practical exam.

programs.program: Master of Arts in Music Composition & Theory — Major in Composition
programs.institution: Scuola universitaria di Musica, Conservatorio della Svizzera italiana (affiliated to SUPSI — University of Applied Sciences and Arts of Southern Switzerland)
programs.institutionType: University-level music school (scuola universitaria di musica) operated by a private-law foundation and affiliated to a public university of applied sciences
programs.publicPrivate: AMBIGUOUS BY DESIGN — CONFIRMED, and the structure is the honest answer rather than a one-word label. The Conservatorio della Svizzera italiana is run by a private-law foundation, not by the canton directly. But since 2006 its University School of Music has been affiliated to SUPSI, the public UAS of Italian-speaking Switzerland, and its degrees are issued in the Swiss public UAS system. Two hard pieces of evidence it operates on the public side despite the private carrier: it charges the regulated Swiss two-tier fee (CHF 750 for Swiss nationals and residents versus CHF 1,500 for all others) and explicitly grants the lower rate to Swiss students 'under the ASUP / Intercantonal Agreement on Universities of Applied Sciences' — a purely private school has no access to intercantonal subsidy mechanisms. Practical answer: a state-recognised public-system music university with a private-foundation carrier. Get it in writing from the Conservatorio if a scholarship form forces a binary.
programs.accreditationStatus: CONFIRMED. Real, state-recognised second-cycle Swiss degree — a KMHS-member programme delivered in the SUPSI/UAS system, awarding a Master of Arts. Supports a Swiss student residence permit; the institution runs its own visas-and-permits guidance for exactly this.
programs.qualification: Master of Arts in Music Composition & Theory — Major in Composition. 4 semesters, 120 ECTS, full time — CONFIRMED. A genuine second-cycle degree. THE TRAP IS REAL AND CONFIRMED: the same institution separately offers a 'MAS in Music Composition' under continuing education. A MAS is a post-master continuing-education certificate, NOT a second-cycle degree, and it will not do the same job for a residence permit or for further study. He must apply for the MA, never the MAS.
programs.focus: Composition and music theory, emphasising the creative dimension of composition and integrating reflection and craftsmanship. Only ONE major is offered — Composition; there are no alternatives within this MA. Electronic music is present but through an external arrangement: the electronic music section is run in partnership with IRMus at the Accademia Internazionale della Musica in Milan. Ask what that means for contact hours, travel and studio access — a Milan-delivered strand is not the same as an in-house studio.
programs.whatYouStudy: Composition, with an electronic music section delivered in partnership with IRMus (Accademia Internazionale della Musica, Milan). Composition, orchestration and analysis are the spine of the assessment, which tells you what the teaching is.
programs.durationEcts: 4 semesters, 120 ECTS, full time — CONFIRMED on the official programme page. Officially described as requiring total dedication in terms of time and emotional involvement.
programs.language: ITALIAN. The course descriptor and study plan are published in Italian and the institution's language rule targets Italian. English web pages are available and are misleading — the teaching language is Italian. Note in his favour, though it does not save this application: matriculation documents are accepted in Italian, English, French, German, Spanish or Portuguese, so his French-language Tunisian paperwork does not need translating.
programs.languageRequirement: Italian at CEFR B2 or CELI 3. Notably generous in timing: applicants who do not have that level at the start of studies must still demonstrate a sufficient level and reach B2/CELI 3 BY THE END OF THE FIRST YEAR of study. No English certificate is mentioned. For a French-fluent Arabic native, Italian to B2 in a year is more achievable than German to B2 — the single most forgiving language regime in this set, and worth remembering if he ever looks at Italian-language options, even though the rest of this record is negative.
programs.entryRequirements: CORRECTED AND HARDENED. The official admission page for this master states the requirement verbatim as 'successful completion of a BACHELOR OF ARTS IN MUSIC OR EQUIVALENT MUSICAL EDUCATION' plus passing an admission exam. The previous record hedged this as 'specific academic prerequisites are not itemised — UNVERIFIED'. They are itemised, and they close the door: a music bachelor, or demonstrably equivalent musical education, is required in substance. Required documents: payment confirmation for the CHF 100 application fee, valid ID or passport copy, BA diploma (or self-certification if the exam is pending), CV in tabular form, and a motivation letter.
programs.portfolioSpec: NOW VERIFIED — the previous record marked this UNVERIFIED. Candidates must submit 'own compositions, any orchestration work, any analytical work' for committee review and discussion. That is a composer's dossier, not a producer's showreel.
programs.auditionSpec: NOW VERIFIED IN FULL, and it is decisive. Entrance examinations are held by invitation only after application review, in the window 30 MARCH – 29 APRIL. Three parts: (1) portfolio presentation and discussion with the admissions committee; (2) a WRITTEN TEST of maximum 60 minutes assessing 'competences in ANALYSIS AND EAR-TRAINING'; (3) an oral exam and interview covering SOLFÈGE, the portfolio, the candidate's musical education background, career goals, performance techniques and knowledge of technology. A written analysis-and-ear-training paper plus an oral solfège examination cannot be passed in a year by someone with no conservatory training. This is a conservatory gate, unambiguously.
programs.equipmentRequired: None published — UNVERIFIED.
programs.facilities: Not published — UNVERIFIED, and materially important because the electronic music section runs through the Milan partner (IRMus) rather than in-house. Anyone pursuing this should ask specifically: what electronic-music studio facilities exist in Lugano, and how much of the electronic strand is actually taught in Milan.
programs.intakes: Autumn start, single annual intake — consistent with a 20 February deadline, exams 30 March–29 April, and matriculation in calendar week 36 (first half of September).
programs.applicationOpens: Not published — UNVERIFIED. Applications close 20 February, so the window opens some months earlier; ask servizi.accademici@conservatorio.ch.
programs.deadline: 20 FEBRUARY — CONFIRMED on the official programme page ('Application deadline: February 20') and on the application page ('Deadline application 20th February 2026'). Presented as the standing master's deadline. Entrance exams 30 March – 29 April (the institution reserves the right to change the schedule). ADDITIONAL AND SEPARATE: the scholarship deadline is 31 MARCH — later than the application deadline, so an applicant applies first and bids for money afterwards. For a September 2027 start, expect 20 February 2027 — INSIDE his October 2026 – February 2027 planning window.
programs.tuitionEU: CHF 750 tuition + CHF 250 administrative fee = CHF 1,000 per semester — but ONLY for Swiss nationals and Swiss residents qualifying under the ASUP intercantonal agreement. There is no EU rate; EU nationals arriving from abroad pay the higher rate below.
programs.tuitionNonEU: CHF 1,500 tuition + CHF 250 administrative fee = CHF 1,750 PER SEMESTER — CONFIRMED as the rate for 'all other students', which is what he would be. CHF 3,500 per year; CHF 7,000 over the 4-semester master.
programs.otherFees: CONFIRMED AND EXPANDED — the previous record missed the application fee. Matriculation CHF 250 one-off; ADMISSIONS/APPLICATION FEE CHF 100 (payable with the application, confirmation of payment is a required document); student union CHF 5 per semester; Bachelor's/Master's final exam CHF 250; reassessment of a non-main subject CHF 100; reassessment of main subject CHF 200; reassessment of final exams CHF 350; extraordinary intermediate exam CHF 250; DEFERRED FINAL EXAM CHF 500; RETAKEN ECTS CHF 500 PER CREDIT; appeals CHF 100; leave of absence CHF 250 per semester. The CHF 500-per-retaken-ECTS charge is brutal and worth knowing about — Swiss music schools price failure aggressively.
programs.totalCostEstimate: Institutional fees over 4 semesters: 4 × CHF 1,750 = CHF 7,000, plus matriculation CHF 250, application CHF 100, student union CHF 20, final exam CHF 250 — roughly CHF 7,620 before any re-sits. Living costs in Lugano are not published and are high by any non-Swiss standard. The Swiss student permit requires proof of means — figure UNVERIFIED; confirm with the Swiss representation in Tunis and the Ticino migration authority.
programs.scholarships: MAJOR CORRECTION — the previous record said 'nothing published at programme level'. That is wrong. The Conservatorio publishes a SUM SCHOLARSHIP FUND on its Study Grants page. For academic year 2026-27 it offers 6 scholarships covering TUITION FEES, ADMINISTRATIVE FEES AND EXAMINATION FEES for the entire duration of studies — 3 for Bachelor's (3 years) and 3 for MASTER'S (2 years). Awarded to candidates who apply and obtain the best marks in the entrance examination, giving priority to those with the greatest financial difficulty. First-time applicants are explicitly eligible and NO NATIONALITY RESTRICTION is published. Application requires an online form plus CV in tabular form, motivation letter, letter of recommendation, family tax return and annual budget. DEADLINE 31 MARCH (incomplete or late applications are not evaluated). Anyone not awarded one is automatically placed on the list for Study Aid funded by the CSI's philanthropic partner network. This is effectively a full institutional-fee waiver — it would zero out the whole ~CHF 7,600 — though not living costs. It is gated entirely behind entrance-exam performance, which is precisely where he fails. Separately, the Swiss Government Excellence Scholarships Art Scholarships stream remains the external route; confirm Tunisia's presence on the art-stream country list for the 2027 call.
programs.visaEligible: Yes — and the Conservatorio publishes its own visas-and-permits guidance with the operational warning that matters most here: EU/EFTA citizens do not need a visa to sit admission examinations, but citizens of all other countries must check the State Secretariat for Migration list, and 'in many cases, candidates must request a visa to be able to come to Lugano for the admission exam'. A Tunisian applicant may therefore need a visa merely to ATTEND the April entrance examination, months before any study permit — a real cost and a real timeline risk that almost no directory mentions. Contrast Kunstuni Linz, which offers Webex interviews.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: NO — CONFIRMED AND HARDENED. The official requirement is 'successful completion of a Bachelor of Arts in Music or equivalent musical education'. The assessment is a composition dossier plus a written analysis-and-ear-training paper plus an oral solfège examination. A candidate with no music degree, no conservatory training and no existing portfolio cannot clear this, in one year or three.
programs.recommendation: RECORD IT, DO NOT APPLY — verdict unchanged, and now better evidenced. Two of the previous record's gaps are closed and one of its claims was wrong. CLOSED: the entry requirement is explicitly 'a Bachelor of Arts in Music or equivalent musical education', and the entrance exam is a portfolio of own compositions plus a 60-minute written analysis and ear-training paper plus an oral solfège examination. That is a conservatory gate and it definitively excludes him. WRONG: the previous record said there were no programme-level scholarships. There are — the SUM Scholarship Fund awards 3 Master scholarships for 2026-27 covering tuition, administrative and examination fees for the whole degree, open to first-time applicants with no published nationality bar, deadline 31 March. Worth correcting for the database even though he cannot reach it, because it means the real cost of this institution for a strong musician is near zero rather than CHF 7,600. FOUR THINGS FROM THIS RECORD REMAIN USEFUL TO HIM PERSONALLY EVEN THOUGH THE PROGRAMME IS NOT. (1) The visa-to-attend-the-audition problem, which applies to every Swiss music-school entrance exam he might ever consider, including HSLU Lucerne — plan it months ahead, and always ask whether a remote option exists. (2) The MA-versus-MAS trap at this institution: the 'MAS in Music Composition' is continuing education, not a degree, and applying for it would be a serious mistake. (3) The Italian B2-by-end-of-first-year rule — the most forgiving language regime found anywhere in this sweep. (4) The CHF 500-per-retaken-ECTS charge, a reminder that Swiss institutions price failure. As a September 2027 target it fails on the entrance examination, on composition not being music production, and on the fact that the one funding route is gated behind the exam he cannot pass.

programs.program: Master of Music – main subject Electronic Music Performance (EMP), Jazz department
programs.institution: Conservatorium Maastricht, Zuyd University of Applied Sciences (Zuyd Hogeschool)
programs.institutionType: Publicly funded university of applied sciences (hbo / hogeschool); Conservatorium Maastricht is the music faculty of Zuyd
programs.publicPrivate: PUBLIC — CONFIRMED and now hard-sourced. Zuyd's own official document 'Tuition fees and examination fees 2026-2027' (zuyd.nl) distinguishes 'funded study programmes' (bekostigd) from 'non-funded' ones and lists 'Master Music' under FUNDED programmes with a statutory fee set by the Ministry of Education, Culture and Science. Only government-funded institutions may charge the wettelijk collegegeld. Zuyd is also an IND-recognised sponsor: its jazz-master application page states non-European applicants receive a questionnaire around May for the residence visa/permit application.
programs.qualification: Master of Music (MMus), 120 EC over 2 years. A real, state-recognised Dutch second-cycle hbo-master (CROHO programme name 'Muziek' / 'Master Music'), NVAO-accredited, delivered by a bekostigde instelling. Supports a Dutch MVV + student residence permit for a non-EU national. CONFIRMED: the official curriculum table on the EMP page shows credits only in Year 1 and Year 2, i.e. a genuine 2-year, 120 EC second-cycle award.
programs.accreditationStatus: NVAO-accredited hbo-master, listed by Zuyd itself as 'Master Music' among its funded master's degree programmes in the official 2026-2027 fee regulation. Full NVAO decision number still UNVERIFIED — check nvao.net or ask bo.conservatoriummaastricht@zuyd.nl. Nothing found contradicts accredited status.
programs.language: ENGLISH — CONFIRMED verbatim on the official language-requirements page: 'The programmes of Master of Music are taught in English. Therefore you must have a thorough active and passive command of English.' No Dutch required.
programs.languageRequirement: CONFIRMED EXACTLY, no corrections. B2 English, certificate uploaded to the application by 1 JULY. Accepted (master level): TOEFL iBT 80 / paper 550; IELTS Academic 6.0; Pearson PTE Academic 61; LanguageCert Academic 65; TOEIC Listening&Reading 865 / Speaking&Writing 335; Cambridge English CAE or FCE 169. All must be taken AT A TEST CENTRE (home/online editions not listed). Exemptions: native English speaker (ID copy), or a Bachelor completed at a University/College with a full English programme. NOTE for him: his BSc at SMU MedTech Tunisia may well qualify for the exemption if it was fully English-taught — get a written statement from SMU and ask Team Admissions (bo.conservatoriummaastricht@zuyd.nl) whether it is accepted; that could save him the IELTS entirely. Otherwise IELTS 6.0 is a low bar for his level.
programs.durationEcts: 2 years full-time, 120 EC. Official curriculum table (Year 1 + Year 2): Main Subject 29+24; Band & Performing 6+6; Recording & Producing / Introduction to Studio Recording & Music Production 2+2; Composing & Arranging 2+2; Find Your Own Music 2+2; Tools in Creation 4+4; Current Jazz 2+2; Impro Lab 2+2; Artistic Research / Master Research 5+10; Health & Well-being 1+1; International Career Center / Your Art as a Business 3+3; Teaching & Outreach Programme 2+2; Minor Modules Jazz / Elective Modules 6+6.
programs.focus: Electronic music production and the live performance of it, deliberately sited at the junction of electronic music and jazz. Official wording: 'The idea is to get the sound directly from your head into songs and, more importantly: on stage. Produce music at a professional level and then perform it, in new creative ways, with talented musicians. Making the most of all the possibilities music technology has to offer.'
programs.whatYouStudy: Main subject EMP (production plus live performance), band and performing, introduction to studio recording and music production, composing and arranging, Find Your Own Music, Tools in Creation, Impro Lab, Current Jazz, a two-year artistic Master Research project, Health & Well-being, and 'Your Art as a Business' entrepreneurship, plus an outreach/teaching module and jazz minor electives. Named EMP staff CONFIRMED on the official page: Frederik Tings (Music Production / Live Sound & Effects / Electronic Music Performance / Producing your own music), with guest teachers Paul Frick (Brandt Brauer Frick) and Frank Wienk. The first EMP student, Georgi Aleksiev, is profiled on the page as a producer with prior academy training in jazz guitar, piano, vocals and drums — a useful signal of the level the department expects.
programs.entryRequirements: CONFIRMED verbatim from the official 'Jazz - Master & Preparatory Course Master' how-to-apply page: 'To study a Master programme at Conservatorium Maastricht, you must hold one of the following: A Bachelor's degree in Music, OR proof of an equivalent level of knowledge and skills tailored to the programme.' Plus the language requirement. Process: Step 1 diploma check (Zuyd Enrolment Office, enrolmentoffice@zuyd.nl); Step 2 register via Studielink selecting 'Zuyd University of Applied Sciences' and 'Master of Music'; Step 3 entrance examination. CONFIRMED: 'No audition fee – you only pay tuition once admitted.' CONFIRMED: the admission decision has THREE possible outcomes — admitted to the Master programme, admitted to the Preparatory Course Master (a formal bridging route), or rejected. That middle outcome is his safety net.
programs.auditionSpec: CONFIRMED EXACTLY, no corrections. Three stages. programs.entryRequirements: SHARPENED AND CORRECTED — the previous record understated how closed this is. On top of that sits the diploma-rating cascade: an academic bachelor gains direct admission on passing the orientation interview; a professional bachelor must first complete a TRANSITION programme (schakelprogramma) built from third-bachelor-year courses; an academic bachelor in ANOTHER ARTISTIC discipline may have to take a PREPARATORY programme; and a bridging programme exists 'if you wish to begin a master's program, but do not have the appropriate underlying bachelor's degree'. programs.program: Composition for Screen – InMICS (International Master in Composition for Screen)
programs.institution: KASK & Conservatorium, School of Arts of HOGENT and Howest (Hogeschool Gent) — consortium with CNSMD de Lyon, Conservatorio di Musica G.B. Martini Bologna and (professional/associate role) Université de Montréal
programs.city: Ghent, Lyon or Bologna — a student studies at TWO of the three European institutions (one per year)
programs.institutionType: Publicly funded Flemish hogeschool School of Arts, in an Erasmus+/Creative Europe co-funded consortium of public conservatoires
programs.publicPrivate: PUBLIC — CONFIRMED. Martini Bologna (Italian AFAM state conservatoire) and Université de Montréal (Quebec public university). programs.qualification: CORRECTED — THIS WAS THE BIGGEST UNKNOWN IN THE PREVIOUS RECORD AND IT IS NOW RESOLVED. programs.whatYouStudy: Composition for animation, documentary and video; electro-acoustic composition; scoring for screen; postproduction; composition for musical theatre; history of film music; music copyright; post-tonal composition techniques; improvisation; orchestral conducting; ethnomusicology; a 9-ECTS internship; a two-part Research Master strand; and a 24-ECTS master project. programs.auditionSpec: NOW FULLY PUBLISHED — the previous record had this as UNVERIFIED. TWO PHASES. Phase 1, online application by the deadline, submitted on BOTH platforms (both mandatory): muvac (artistic portfolio and questionnaire) and Cadence at concours.cnsmd-lyon.fr (administrative data and the €92 application fee). Results of round 1 announced by end of April, with an invitation to interview and a COMPULSORY PRELIMINARY ASSIGNMENT — composing music for a short film of 5 to 10 minutes, due at a set deadline in early May. Phase 2: a 30-MINUTE ONLINE INTERVIEW with the recruitment committee/jury (mid-May). Results end of May; the jury also reveals which TWO of the partner institutions each admitted student will attend, and that decision is FINAL. Admission must be confirmed by mid-June, after which the student registers separately according to the procedures of both hosting institutions.
programs.portfolioSpec: NOW FULLY PUBLISHED. Submitted on muvac: (1) a RESEARCH PAPER PROPOSAL for the two-year programme — provisional research question, provisional title, brief description, max 2,000 words, optionally with bibliography/filmography/music references, on a topic related to composition for screen; (2) A MINIMUM OF THREE AND MAXIMUM OF FIVE pieces of music, total duration across all works max 20 minutes, as mp3/wav or movie files, of which AT LEAST ONE must be a score for screen uploaded as a movie file with the music synchronised to the picture (recording, VST simulation or electronic piece all acceptable), with the written score if available; (3) a DECLARATION OF HONOUR on the authenticity and artistic authorship of all scores and recordings; (4) a COVER LETTER, max 1,000 words, stating motivation and a preference among the partner institutions; (5) a complete CV of experience and education in music and/or music for screen. All documents must use his legal name, not an artist or DJ name.
programs.equipmentRequired: Not published. A scoring-capable DAW with orchestral VSTs is implied by the portfolio and by the phase-2 assignment. UNVERIFIED — ask info@inmics.org.
programs.facilities: Access to the facilities of the two European conservatoires he is assigned to (from Ghent, Lyon, Bologna), plus festival and cinémathèque partners (Aubagne, Cineteca di Bologna, Film Fest Gent, Permission Inc. Montréal) providing workshops, coaching and internship placements. Specific studio specification UNVERIFIED.
programs.intakes: CORRECTED — THIS IS THE DECISIVE ERROR IN THE PREVIOUS RECORD. The previous record said 'September (annual, aligned to the consortium recruitment cycle)'. That is WRONG. InMICS is BIENNIAL. The consortium states twice, in bold: 'The master recruits EVERY TWO YEARS' and 'Every two years, a new group of students starts the programme.' Cohorts run 2018-2020, ..., 2024-2026, 2026-2028, 2028-2030. THERE IS NO SEPTEMBER 2027 INTAKE AT ALL. His target intake does not exist for this programme.
programs.applicationOpens: CONFIRMED for the most recent cycle: admissions for the 2026-2028 intake opened 2 MARCH 2026 and closed 12 April 2026 (deadline extended by the consortium from an earlier date to 12 April at 23:59 CET). That cohort is already recruited and started in September 2026. The NEXT opening, for the 2028-2030 cohort, would be expected around EARLY MARCH 2028. Monitor inmics.org/apply/deadlines and the 'Latest NEWS' page from late 2027.
programs.deadline: NOW FULLY PUBLISHED — the previous record said 'NOT PUBLISHED on the institutional page', which was true of the KASK page but the consortium publishes a complete timeline. Confirmed 2026-2028 cycle: 12/04/2026 deadline for submitting applications online (23:59 CET, both platforms); 24 April 2026 results of round 1, plus instructions for the preliminary assignment and the interview date; beginning of May 2026 deadline for the preliminary assignment; 12 or 13 May 2026 round-2 jury interviews; end of May 2026 round-2 results and allocation of the two host institutions (final); mid-June 2026 deadline to confirm admission. Expect an equivalent March-to-June timeline in 2028. NOTHING IN 2027.
programs.tuitionEU: €2,000 per year — the consortium sets a single flat fee that does not distinguish EU from non-EU.
programs.tuitionNonEU: €2,000 PER YEAR — MAJOR CORRECTION. The previous record left this UNVERIFIED and warned it might be the Flemish non-EEA rate of €8,800.20. Both the caution and the guess are now superseded by the consortium's own published figure: 'The amount of tuition fees for 2026-2028 will be: First year: €2000 ... Second year: €2000. The two thousand Euros fee is payable to the institution at which the student will be studying. No fees are due to the institution where the student is not currently studying.' So the total tuition for the whole 120 ECTS double-degree is €4,000 — roughly one fifth of what the previous record feared, and about one sixth of the Maastricht bill. This is an Erasmus+/Creative Europe co-funded consortium fee, and it is outstanding value. Still worth getting in writing from info@inmics.org before relying on it for a future cycle, since the figure is quoted for the 2026-2028 cohort specifically.
programs.otherFees: €92 NON-REFUNDABLE APPLICATION FEE, payable on the Cadence platform at the time of application — newly identified, absent from the previous record. Beyond that: the mobility now involves TWO European countries rather than four countries including Canada, so he would need one Schengen student residence permit procedure per host country (Belgium, France or Italy), each with its own cost and lead time — but NO Canadian study permit is required under the current curriculum. Certified diploma copies and certified translations are additional. Whether HOGENT levies its separate 'contribution towards study costs' on InMICS students UNVERIFIED — ask.
programs.totalCostEstimate: Tuition: €2,000 × 2 = €4,000 total for 120 ECTS and two master's degrees, plus a €92 application fee. Living costs across two of Ghent/Lyon/Bologna, plus two residence-permit procedures and two relocations, dominate the real budget — call it €12,000–€18,000 per year in living costs and administration depending on city. The tuition itself is close to negligible. This is dramatically cheaper than the previous record's €17,600 tuition estimate.
programs.scholarships: No InMICS-specific scholarship is published. The programme is itself co-funded by Erasmus+ and Creative Europe, which is why the fee is only €2,000/yr — the subsidy is delivered as a low fee rather than as an award. Possible additional routes: the Flemish Master Mind Scholarship if he were registered at HOGENT (a genuine full ride — €10,225 plus a fee waiver — but nomination runs through the institution and InMICS eligibility is UNVERIFIED), and any Erasmus+ mobility grant attached to the inter-institutional moves. Ask info@inmics.org and the HOGENT International Office. Given a €4,000 total tuition bill, funding is a much smaller problem here than at Maastricht.
programs.visaEligible: Yes in principle — an accredited Flemish, French or Italian second-cycle degree supports a student visa and residence permit in each of those countries. CORRECTED RISK ASSESSMENT: the previous record warned about 'multi-country mobility (France, Italy, Canada)' and 'a Canadian study permit for the Montréal period'. Under the renewed curriculum in force since the 2024 intake, the three specialisations are all EUROPEAN (Bologna, Ghent, Lyon) and a student attends TWO of them, so the Canadian study-permit risk has fallen away. The remaining, still real, complication is that a Tunisian national would need to run TWO separate Schengen national-visa/residence-permit procedures back to back — one for each host country — with the year-two application filed while already resident in the year-one country. Get the consortium's written account of how it handles this before committing.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: NO — CONFIRMED and now airtight. The stated requirement is an undergraduate degree in music or equivalent PLUS being 'already composing music for the screen', and the Cadence administrative checklist demands a CERTIFIED COPY OF A BACHELOR DIPLOMA IN MUSIC as a mandatory upload. The 'or equivalent' wording in the prose does not survive contact with a documentary requirement for a certified music diploma. A BSc in Software Engineering cannot satisfy it, and the portfolio gate is separately out of reach: three to five works including at least one score synchronised to picture, plus a 2,000-word academic research proposal, judged against trained composers.
programs.recommendation: EXISTS, IS REAL, IS A GENUINE DOUBLE MASTER'S DEGREE, AND IS EXCELLENT VALUE — BUT IS UNAVAILABLE TO HIM, AND UNAVAILABLE TO ANYONE FOR SEPTEMBER 2027. Three corrections matter. (1) INTAKE: this master recruits BIENNIALLY, not annually. The 2026-2028 cohort applied 2 March – 12 April 2026 and started in September 2026; the next cohort is 2028-2030, applying around March 2028. There is no September 2027 entry, so it cannot be on his 2027 list at all. (2) COST: tuition is €2,000 per year flat for EU and non-EU alike, total €4,000 for the whole programme plus a €92 application fee — not the €8,800.20/yr the previous record feared. (3) AWARD AND STRUCTURE: students receive TWO master's degrees, and study at TWO of the three European institutions (Ghent, Lyon, Bologna); Montréal is no longer a study location under the curriculum in force since 2024, so the Canadian study-permit worry is obsolete. What blocks him is not money and not accreditation — it is that the application requires a certified copy of a bachelor's diploma IN MUSIC, and a portfolio of three to five screen-scoring works plus a 2,000-word research proposal. Keep this on file as a strong LONG-TERM target: if he completes the Maastricht Master of Music (or any recognised music master) by summer 2029, he would hold the diploma the Cadence platform demands and could apply in March 2030 for the 2030-2032 cohort — cheaply, in English, with his French an asset for the Lyon track. If he contacts them now, the only useful question is whether the consortium would ever accept a non-music bachelor as 'equivalent'; ask info@inmics.org in writing, and expect no.

programs.program: ΠΜΣ «Βυζαντινή Μουσικολογία και Ψαλτική Τέχνη» / MA in Byzantine Musicology & Psaltic Art — Department of Music Studies, School of Philosophy
programs.institution: Εθνικό και Καποδιστριακό Πανεπιστήμιο Αθηνών / National and Kapodistrian University of Athens (NKUA)
programs.publicPrivate: PUBLIC — CONFIRMED. State university (ΑΕΙ). The programme was founded by Senate decision 739/30-5-2018 published in the Government Gazette (ΦΕΚ 2643/τ.Β΄/6-7-2018) under law 4485/2017, and its operating regulation is published in ΦΕΚ 4568/τ.Β΄/18-10-2018. Founding decree states no charge falls on the state budget; the programme is funded by the €700/semester fees plus donations and research income.
programs.institutionType: Comprehensive state university; Department of Music Studies, School of Philosophy
programs.qualification: Δίπλωμα Μεταπτυχιακών Σπουδών (ΔΜΣ) in Byzantine Musicology & Psaltic Art, with two specialisations: (1) Βυζαντινή Μουσικολογία / Byzantine Musicology, (2) Ψαλτική Τέχνη / Psaltic Art. 90 ECTS over 3 academic semesters — CONFIRMED, Άρθρο 3-4 of ΦΕΚ 2643/2018. A genuine state-recognised second-cycle degree that supports a Greek student residence permit. This part of the prior record was correct.
programs.accreditationStatus: State-recognised, established by published Government Gazette decree under ν. 4485/2017. NOTE — Άρθρο 6 of the founding decree authorises the programme to operate only ΜΕΧΡΙ ΤΟ ΑΚΑΔΗΜΑΪΚΟ ΕΤΟΣ 2027-28 ('until academic year 2027-28'), subject to meeting evaluation criteria. A September 2027 intake would therefore begin in the final authorised year and would finish (3 semesters) beyond it, requiring a renewal decree. Additionally, Greek law 5094/2024 re-regulated all ΠΜΣ and forced many to be re-founded with fresh decrees and possibly revised fees — the 2018 instruments cited here may have been superseded. Both points need confirmation with the department before relying on any figure.
programs.language: GREEK — the prior record was FLATLY WRONG and this is the single most important correction. Άρθρο 4 of the founding decree ΦΕΚ 2643/τ.Β΄/6-7-2018 states verbatim: «Τα μαθήματα διεξάγονται στην ελληνική γλώσσα.» ('The courses are conducted in the Greek language.') The only English concession is in the operating regulation: the master's thesis may be written in Greek OR English («Η γλώσσα συγγραφής της μεταπτυχιακής διπλωματικής εργασίας μπορεί να είναι η ελληνική ή και η αγγλική»). The programme's own website (byzantinemusicology.music.uoa.gr) is entirely in Greek. The previous agent almost certainly misread the Ministry register: the FEK renders every programme title bilingually ('Βυζαντινή Μουσικολογία και Ψαλτική Τέχνη' | 'Byzantine Musicology & Psaltic Art'), and an English-language TITLE is not an English-language PROGRAMME. Consequently the record's headline claim — that this is 'the only English-taught MUSIC master's in Greece' — is false. There is no English-taught exception here at all.
programs.languageRequirement: FULLY SPECIFIED in ΦΕΚ 4568/τ.Β΄/18-10-2018, Άρθρο 4 — the prior record's 'UNVERIFIED' was wrong, the requirements are published and they are brutal for him. TWO separate certificates are demanded: (1) «Πιστοποιητικό γλωσσομάθειας αγγλικής γλώσσας, επιπέδου C1» — an English proficiency certificate at CEFR level C1, mandatory document no. 8; knowledge of a further European language is a positive factor. Level is proven either by holding the diploma or by sitting a departmental examination. (2) «Οι αλλοδαποί υποψήφιοι φοιτητές θα πρέπει να προσκομίζουν πιστοποιητικό επάρκειας στην ελληνική γλώσσα» — FOREIGN candidates must additionally produce a certificate of PROFICIENCY IN GREEK. As a Tunisian national he falls squarely in this category. He has no Greek whatsoever, so this is an absolute, non-negotiable blocker independent of everything else.
programs.englishTest: CEFR C1 English certificate REQUIRED as a mandatory application document (ΦΕΚ 4568/2018, Άρθρο 4, item 8). C1 corresponds to roughly IELTS 7.0-8.0 or TOEFL iBT ~95-110. His English is described as 'working' and he has taken no test; C1 is a demanding bar he would have to clear on top of, not instead of, the Greek proficiency certificate. The prior record's 'no IELTS/TOEFL band is published' was incorrect — a CEFR level is published, which is stricter and more specific than a band.
programs.durationEcts: 90 ECTS over three (3) academic semesters, full-time — CONFIRMED verbatim, Άρθρο 4 of ΦΕΚ 2643/2018.
programs.focus: Byzantine musicology and psaltic (Byzantine ecclesiastical chant) art — scholarly research plus artistic-interpretative performance of Orthodox liturgical chant.
programs.whatYouStudy: Byzantine musicology, Byzantine notation, theory, manuscript sources, and performance practice of Orthodox ecclesiastical psalmody, taught and examined in Greek. Contains ZERO sound design, ZERO music production, ZERO audio engineering, ZERO electronic music and ZERO music technology. There is no overlap of any kind with his stated field or with a DJ/producer career.
programs.entryRequirements: CORRECTED against ΦΕΚ 4568/2018, Άρθρα 3-4. Άρθρο 3: holders of a first-cycle degree from ANY department of a Greek ΑΕΙ, or from an equivalent foreign institution RECOGNISED BY ΔΟΑΤΑΠ (the Greek foreign-qualification recognition body). The prior record's paraphrase about the Coordinating Committee being satisfied of 'specialised knowledge or experience in the cognitive subjects' does not appear in the founding text — the real gate is not a discretionary clause but a hard competitive examination. Mandatory documents: application form; CV; certified copy of degree; peer-reviewed publications if any; evidence of professional/research/artistic activity if any; ID; TWO letters of recommendation from university professors; C1 English certificate; Greek proficiency certificate for foreign applicants; ΔΟΑΤΑΠ certificate of equivalence for foreign degrees. Selection criteria: (a) degree grade of AT LEAST 7.5/10 — the Committee may waive this by specially reasoned decision only if the candidate holds a second university degree, a master's, notable published/research/artistic work, or significant professional experience in cognate fields; (b) WRITTEN ENTRANCE EXAMINATIONS for BOTH specialisations on the programme's subject matter, with syllabus and prescribed bibliography announced in advance; (c) a PRACTICAL EXAMINATION before a panel of professors for the Psaltic Art specialisation; (d) a PERSONAL INTERVIEW before the Coordinating Committee. Final ranking: Byzantine Musicology = 50% written exam + 50% interview; Psaltic Art = 30% written + 50% practical + 20% interview. Intake is 20 students per academic year, selected separately per specialisation.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: Formally yes — Άρθρο 3 admits graduates of any department, and a Software Engineering BSc is not excluded on paper. In substance no. He must pass a written entrance examination in Byzantine musicology, sat in Greek against a prescribed Greek bibliography, and then a Greek-language interview assessing his command of the field's scholarly literature. The departmental page further records that for the Psaltic Art specialisation candidates must hold a Diploma of Byzantine Music with grade 'Excellent' from a recognised Greek music school or equivalent studies. Formal eligibility here is meaningless without the chant training and the Greek he does not have.
programs.portfolioSpec: No portfolio in the creative-industry sense. What is required instead is documentary: CV, certified degree, ΔΟΑΤΑΠ equivalence certificate, two academic reference letters, and optional evidence of research/artistic activity. His planned production portfolio would carry no weight — it is not a scored criterion.
programs.auditionSpec: SPECIFIED, contrary to the prior record's 'UNVERIFIED'. Written entrance examination for both specialisations. For the Psaltic Art specialisation there is a compulsory PRACTICAL EXAMINATION in Byzantine chant before a faculty panel, worth 50% of the final ranking, with specifications set out in each year's call. Plus a personal interview for all candidates who pass the written stage. This is a competitive entrance-exam admission, not a portfolio review.
programs.equipmentRequired: None specified. Teaching rooms, seminar rooms, amphitheatres with audiovisual equipment and departmental laboratories are provided (Άρθρο 9, ΦΕΚ 4568/2018).
programs.facilities: Classrooms, seminar rooms, audiovisual-equipped amphitheatres and laboratories of the Department of Music Studies (Άρθρο 9). No recording studio, DAW suite or electronic-music facility is mentioned — none is relevant to this curriculum.
programs.intakes: Once per year, autumn (winter semester) start. 20 places per year across the two specialisations.
programs.applicationOpens: CORRECTED. Άρθρο 4 of ΦΕΚ 4568/2018: the call (προκήρυξη) is published EACH JUNE by decision of the Department Assembly, on the department and university websites, announcing the specialisations offered, places per specialisation, entrance-examination dates, examinable subjects, syllabus and bibliography per specialisation, and required documents. This directly contradicts his planning assumption that calls open October 2026 - February 2027: for a September 2027 start the call would not appear until around June 2027.
programs.deadline: Set in each year's call, typically September, and extendable by decision of the Department Assembly. The most recent documented cycle (2022-23) had a deadline of 16 September 2022 with submission through the university's electronic protocol system. Successful candidates must enrol within 15 days of the Assembly's decision. Exact 2027 dates will only be known when the June 2027 call is published.
programs.tuitionEU: €700 per semester, payable at the start of each semester — CONFIRMED verbatim in BOTH instruments (Άρθρο 5 of ΦΕΚ 2643/2018 and Άρθρο 8 para. 10 of ΦΕΚ 4568/2018). Over the 3-semester programme this is €2,100 in total, NOT the €3,000 the prior record stated. The founding decree itself characterises the fee as 'purely symbolic'.
programs.tuitionNonEU: €2,100 total (€700 x 3 semesters) — the SAME rate he would pay as a Tunisian national. Greek public ΠΜΣ fees are set by decree as a single figure with no EU/non-EU differential, so the prior record was right that there is no separate non-EU rate but wrong on the amount. Caveat: these are the 2018 decreed figures and law 5094/2024 may have prompted a re-founding with revised fees — confirm with the Secretariat.
programs.otherFees: ΔΟΑΤΑΠ recognition of his Tunisian BSc (a mandatory, slow and separately-charged process), certified translations of degree and transcripts, Greek student visa (type D) and residence-permit fees, mandatory health insurance, and proof of sufficient means for the visa. None of these are quantified in the official instruments — obtain current figures from the Greek consulate and ΔΟΑΤΑΠ if this were ever pursued.
programs.totalCostEstimate: Tuition is genuinely cheap at €2,100 for the whole degree. Athens living costs over 18 months dominate — budget roughly €700-900 per month, i.e. approximately €12,500-16,000, plus ΔΟΑΤΑΠ, translation, visa, permit and insurance costs. Order of magnitude €15,000-19,000 all-in. Living-cost figures are my estimate, not an official publication.
programs.scholarships: No dedicated scholarship. The only relief published in the regulation is the standard statutory fee EXEMPTION under ν. 4485/2017: full waiver of tuition for students whose individual income does not exceed 100%, and family income 70%, of the Greek national median equivalised disposable income per ELSTAT, capped at 30% of admitted students and usable for one ΠΜΣ only. This is means-tested against Greek statistical thresholds and in practice requires Greek tax documentation, making it awkward-to-impossible for a first-year non-EU arrival. Crucially it is a fee waiver worth at most €2,100 — it is NOT a stipend and would not cover a single month of living costs. There is no funded route here.
programs.visaEligible: Technically yes — a full-time, in-person, state-recognised 90-ECTS second-cycle degree at a Greek public university supports a student residence permit. But this is moot: he cannot satisfy the Greek-proficiency certificate, the C1 English certificate, or the Greek-language written entrance examination, so he would never reach the point of applying for a visa.
programs.recommendation: The programme is REAL, is a genuine master's, and is accredited — but almost every substantive claim in the prior record was wrong, and the record's central 'finding' collapses. CORRECTIONS: (1) LANGUAGE — it is taught in GREEK, not English. The founding decree ΦΕΚ 2643/τ.Β΄/6-7-2018 Άρθρο 4 says «Τα μαθήματα διεξάγονται στην ελληνική γλώσσα». Only the thesis may optionally be written in English. The prior agent appears to have mistaken the FEK's bilingual programme TITLE for the language of instruction. The claim that this is 'the only English-taught music master's in Greece' is therefore false. (2) FEES — €700 per semester, €2,100 total, not €3,000. (3) LANGUAGE CERTIFICATES — not 'unverified' but precisely specified: a C1 English certificate AND, for foreign applicants specifically, a certificate of proficiency in GREEK. (4) ADMISSION — not 'unverified' but a competitive written entrance examination in Greek on a prescribed Byzantine-musicology bibliography, plus interview, plus a 50%-weighted practical chant audition for the performance track, plus a minimum degree grade of 7.5/10, plus two academic reference letters, plus ΔΟΑΤΑΠ recognition of his foreign degree. (5) TIMING — calls are published each JUNE with a September deadline, not October-February as his planning assumed. (6) VALIDITY — the founding decree authorises operation only until academic year 2027-28, and law 5094/2024 may have superseded these 2018 instruments entirely. THE USEFUL CONCLUSION SURVIVES, AND IS STRONGER THAN THE PRIOR RECORD CLAIMED: the previous agent reached the right verdict on Greece by the wrong road. Greece is not 'closed except for this one English-taught programme' — it is closed, full stop, for this field. This programme was the supposed English exception and it is Greek-taught like all the others. He should treat Greece as unavailable for sound design, music production, audio engineering and music technology at master's level, and stop spending research effort there unless a specific department confirms English-language supervision in writing. Separately, even in a parallel universe where he spoke fluent Greek, this degree teaches Orthodox liturgical chant and would do nothing whatever for a career as a DJ and electronic-music producer.

programs.program: Müzik Teknolojileri Tezli Yüksek Lisans Programı (Music Technologies, thesis master) — Müzik Teknolojileri Ana Bilim Dalı, Müzik ve Güzel Sanatlar Enstitüsü
programs.institution: Ankara Müzik ve Güzel Sanatlar Üniversitesi (Ankara Music and Fine Arts University, MGÜ)
programs.city: Ankara (Oran, Çankaya — Turan Güneş Bulvarı, Yukarı Dikmen Mah., Neşet Ertaş Cad. No:4, 06550)
programs.publicPrivate: PUBLIC — CONFIRMED. Turkish state university (devlet üniversitesi) under YÖK. Confirmed independently by (a) the .edu.tr institutional domain and Enstitü structure, and (b) its inclusion in the Türkiye Bursları state Art Scholarship Programme alongside Ankara Hacı Bayram Veli University and İstanbul Technical University — a list of state art institutions. Not a vakıf (foundation) university.
programs.institutionType: Specialist state university of music and fine arts (conservatoire-type), with its own Müzik ve Güzel Sanatlar Enstitüsü (graduate institute)
programs.qualification: Tezli Yüksek Lisans diploması — CONFIRMED a real second-cycle degree. Turkish thesis master's diplomas sit at TYÇ level 7 / QF-EHEA level 2 / EQF-LLL level 7. Supports a Turkish student residence permit (öğrenci ikamet izni) for a non-EU national.
programs.accreditationStatus: State-recognised, YÖK-authorised programme at a state university. CONFIRMED from the official exam guide: foreign applicants MUST hold a YÖK denklik belgesi for their overseas bachelor's degree before admission ('yurtdışında lisans eğitimini tamamladıklarına dair YÖK tarafından verilmiş denklik belgesine sahip olmaları gerekir'). This is a genuine multi-month administrative hurdle — the Tunisian SMU MedTech BSc must go to YÖK well in advance.
programs.language: Turkish — CONFIRMED. All teaching, all admission documents and the entire two-stage entrance examination are in Turkish. There is no English-taught track.
programs.languageRequirement: CONFIRMED verbatim from the official guide: foreign nationals who completed their education abroad must present a Turkish certificate at MINIMUM C1 LEVEL from a YÖK-recognised centre attached to a Turkish higher-education institution ('en az C1 seviyesinde bir belge ibraz etmeleri zorunludur'). CRITICAL CONCESSION, confirmed: a candidate who wins a place without it IS registered and placed on one (1) year of leave to study Turkish; if he cannot produce the C1 certificate at the end of that year his registration is cancelled and deleted. This one-year grace period is MGÜ's single biggest advantage over Dokuz Eylül, which grants no equivalent.
programs.englishTest: NONE — CONFIRMED. The official admission table reads 'Yabancı Dil Taban Puanı: Aranmaz' (no foreign-language minimum score required). No IELTS or TOEFL is demanded at any stage. His untaken IELTS/TOEFL is irrelevant here. The language barrier is Turkish, not English.
programs.durationEcts: Standard Turkish tezli yüksek lisans: 4 semesters nominal (minimum 7 courses + seminar + thesis). The exam guide does not state an ECTS total — STILL UNVERIFIED after re-checking; the programme page on mgu.edu.tr carries only administrative links. Ask enstitu@mgu.edu.tr or deren.karacan@mgu.edu.tr.
programs.focus: Music technology with a strong audio-engineering and acoustics bias. CONFIRMED verbatim from the guide: graduates should be able to conduct scientific work in music technology, should carry 'ileri düzeyde ses mühendisliği bilgisi' (advanced sound-engineering knowledge), and should be able to interpret and follow innovations in the field on an informed basis.
programs.whatYouStudy: CONFIRMED: courses deliberately combining technical field knowledge with academic literature review in music technologies. The assessed competence areas define the content: ses kayıt (sound recording), ses programlama (sound programming), çalgı yapım (instrument making), ses elektroniği (sound electronics) and akustik (acoustics). It is an academic/research master with a compulsory thesis — NOT a commercial music-production or DJ curriculum. It will make him a credentialed audio technologist, not an international DJ.
programs.entryRequirements: CONFIRMED verbatim from the official 2025-26 exam guide admission table: ALES Puanı Şartı = 'Aranmaz' (not required); Yabancı Dil Taban Puanı = 'Aranmaz' (not required); Mezuniyet Taban Notu = 2.50/4.00 or 65/100 or 3.1/5.00; Programa Kabul edilen Mezunlar = 'Herhangi bir lisans programından mezun olmak' (graduation from ANY bachelor's programme). Foreign nationals additionally: YÖK denklik belgesi (mandatory) and Turkish C1 (or the one-year grace period). ALES is explicitly waived for foreign nationals in any case. NOTE: the general institute announcement's ALES≥55 rule applies ONLY to Müzik Eğitimi and Resim-İş Eğitimi masters — NOT to Müzik Teknolojileri.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: YES — EXPLICITLY AND CONFIRMED. The official guide states the accepted graduates are 'Herhangi bir lisans programından mezun olmak' — any bachelor's programme whatsoever. A BSc in Software Engineering is formally, unambiguously eligible. This remains the single most important fact about this programme for him. HOWEVER: formal eligibility and realistic competitiveness are different things — 54 of the 100 first-stage points test trained musical and technical hearing (see auditionSpec), which he cannot fake.
programs.portfolioSpec: REQUIRED and CONFIRMED in detail. Weighted 10% of the entrance score (dosya değerlendirmesi). The candidate must upload to the designated area on the university site by 23:59 on the closing day, AND hand the jury three (3) printed copies of a file containing: (A) ONE single work he produced himself reflecting his interest/aptitude in the area he intends to study, in sound recording, sound programming, instrument making, sound electronics or acoustics — supplied as (a) a digital copy on CD/DVD/external USB and (b) an explanatory text describing the work's content; (B) a digital copy (CD/DVD/USB) of his other personal works in the field with the associated audio files, software and/or written documents plus an index of those materials; (C) his CV. Scoring, confirmed: Özgeçmiş (CV) 11/11/11 for form/language/content, Alana Ait Özgeçmiş (field-specific CV) 11/11/11, Çalışma Raporu (work report) 11/11/12. Total 100.
programs.auditionSpec: Two-stage entrance exam, entirely in Turkish — CONFIRMED in full. STAGE I (60% of the entrance score), six assessed areas with exact point weights: Müziksel İşitme (musical ear-training — distinguishing musical elements in a played recording and describing them in technical language) 27 pts; Mesleki İşitme (technical listening — analysing, classifying and describing played sounds) 27 pts; Mesleki Bilgi (professional technical/theoretical knowledge) 9 pts; Problem Çözme 9 pts; Analitik Düşünme 19 pts; Akademik Araştırmaya Yatkınlık 9 pts. For that last component candidates must read IN ADVANCE a named Turkish journal article on determining the acoustic properties of small-scale popular-music production spaces (dergipark.org.tr/tr/download/article-file/203754), answer a question on it in writing in the first part of the exam, then defend that written answer orally. Electronic devices of any kind are banned from the exam. STAGE II (30%): oral examination on the submitted file — Ana Çalışma Yeterliği (command of his main submitted work) 57 pts, Yazılı Sınav Değerlendirmesi (review of his written exam) 28 pts, Genel Değerlendirme 15 pts. ENTRANCE SCORE = 10% file + 60% Stage I + 30% Stage II. PASS MARK 60/100. FINAL RANKING = 70% entrance-exam score + 30% bachelor GPA. Appeals within 2 working days, decided within 3.
programs.equipmentRequired: Not stated in the guide, but CONFIRMED by implication from the portfolio rules: he must already have produced original recorded/programmed audio work with written technical documentation before he applies. programs.scholarships: CONFIRMED — and this is the decisive advantage. The Türkiye Bursları Art Scholarship Programme covers Ankara Music and Fine Arts University, and 'Music Technologies' IS named among the MASTER'S-level departments it funds (alongside Instrument Education, Music Theory, Musicology, Voice Education, Instrument-Sound, Music Theory and Composition). Coverage, confirmed: university and department placement, monthly stipend (Master's 6,500 TL), tuition fees, a one-year Turkish language course, accommodation, health insurance, and flight tickets at programme start and completion.
