programs.recommendation: RE-VERIFIED LINE BY LINE AGAINST THE OFFICIAL EXAM GUIDE AND THE 2026-27 ANNOUNCEMENT — the previous record was accurate on almost every point and I confirm it. This remains the only fully-funded, formally-open door in this set. Confirmed facts that matter: any bachelor's degree is accepted verbatim; ALES 'Aranmaz'; foreign-language score 'Aranmaz'; Türkiye Bursları names Music Technologies at MASTER'S level. Corrections made: (1) the 2026-27 calendar is now published in full — apply 10–24 Aug 2026, exams 2–4 Sept, results 9 Sept, registration 14–16 Sept; (2) the 15,000 TL fee is a 2024-25 figure with no newer announcement published, and should be treated as a floor, not the price he will pay; (3) the institute-wide ALES≥55 rule applies only to the Education programmes, not to Music Technologies — his file needs no ALES at all. Realistic assessment for HIM: the killer constraint is Turkish, and the Türkiye Bursları package solves it by including a funded Turkish year, which makes the scholarship route far more viable than self-payment. The entrance exam puts 54 of 100 Stage-I points on trained musical and technical ear — with no conservatory background he must spend 2026 on ear training and critical listening, not only on beat-making. The portfolio must be his OWN produced work in recording, sound programming, sound electronics or acoustics with a written technical report: here his software-engineering background is a real asset if he builds audio-DSP, plug-in or acoustics-measurement projects rather than DJ sets. Only 2 foreign-national places (plus 1 lateral-transfer) were advertised — it is very competitive. Concrete plan: start YÖK denklik and Turkish study in autumn 2026; build documented audio/DSP work across 2026; apply to Türkiye Bursları 10 Jan – 20 Feb 2027 naming this programme.

The Enstitü's own academic-units menu lists 'Müzik Teknolojisi BD' as a separate Bilim Dalı with its own master's programme, distinct from 'Müzik Bilimleri ABD' and from 'Müzik ASD (Konservatuvar)'.
programs.accreditationStatus: State-recognised, YÖK-authorised, entered in the Turkish Qualifications Framework (TYÇ) register. Foreign bachelor's degrees require YÖK denklik — CONFIRMED explicitly on the Enstitü's entrance-exam rules page.
programs.language: Turkish — CONFIRMED. The official DEÜ Bologna course catalogue states the language of instruction is Turkish. All admission pages are Turkish-only. No English track.
programs.languageRequirement: CORRECTED AND NOW CONFIRMED (was UNVERIFIED). The Enstitü's official 'Giriş Sınavları Hakkında' page states verbatim: 'Yabancı uyruklu adaylar için DEÜ Senatosu tarafından belirlenen kurum ve merkezler tarafından verilen C1 düzeyinde Türkçe yeterlik belgesi gereklidir.' — a C1 Turkish proficiency certificate from institutions designated by the DEÜ Senate is REQUIRED of foreign nationals. programs.englishTest: NONE — CORRECTED. The previous record said a foreign-language proficiency score was 'listed among admission requirements'. That is WRONG for master's level. The Enstitü's official rules state verbatim: 'Yüksek Lisans Programlarına başvurularda yabancı dil şartı aranmamaktadır.' — no foreign-language requirement for master's applications at all. A YÖKDİL/YDS score of ≥55 is required only for DOCTORATE/Sanatta Yeterlik. GRE/GMAT is required only of foreign nationals applying to Film Tasarımı and Fotoğraf, not Music Technology. programs.durationEcts: 120 ECTS over 2 years / 4 semesters of 15 weeks — CONFIRMED verbatim from the official DEÜ Bologna catalogue ('2 yıl, 1 yılda 2 yarıyıl, her yarıyılda 15 hafta, 120 AKTS'). Minimum 7 courses + 1 seminar + specialisation work + thesis (min. 21 local credits).
programs.focus: Music technology combining music arts/theory with technology; the discipline was established in 2009. The examined subject areas reveal the real technical centre of gravity: acoustics, noise, recording/mixing/mastering technologies, and sound systems.
programs.whatYouStudy: Theoretical study alongside practical application through case studies and research projects, leading to a thesis. The official programme description states it is aimed at candidates targeting an academic career or specialist authority and responsibility in music technology, and that the courses aim to give a strong foundation together with a practical perspective. Aligned with the exam syllabus, this is genuinely audio-engineering-flavoured: acoustics, noise control, studio recording/mix/mastering, sound systems.
programs.entryRequirements: CORRECTED AND CONFIRMED from the official 2026-2027 admission page for the programme. Öğrenci Kaynağı (student source): '4 yıllık üniversite mezunları' — graduates of ANY four-year university programme. Documents: bachelor's diploma (Turkish, via E-Devlet) and transcript (Turkish, via E-Devlet, brought on the exam day). Sınav: 'Mülakat %100' — the Bilim Sınavı is a 100% oral interview. Examined areas: 'Akustik, Gürültü, Kayıt Mix Mastering Teknolojileri, Ses Sistemleri'. Başarı Puanı = Bilim Sınavı 50% + bachelor GPA 50%. Minimum 65 required in the Bilim Sınavı to be counted successful. No ALES is listed for this programme. No foreign-language requirement. Foreign nationals additionally need YÖK denklik and Turkish C1.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: YES — CORRECTED, and this is the biggest change to this record. The previous agent read the Bologna catalogue's 'aynı veya ilgili disiplinlerde lisans derecesi' and the programme blurb's 'öncelikli olarak lisans derecesini müzik teknolojisi alanında almış' and concluded eligibility was doubtful. That reading was wrong. The 'öncelikli olarak' (primarily) sentence sits under 'Program Hakkında' and is a statement of the programme's target audience, NOT an eligibility bar. The binding admission field is 'Öğrenci Kaynağı', and on the live official 2026-2027 admission page it reads '4 yıllık üniversite mezunları' — graduates of any four-year university programme. A Tunisian BSc in Software Engineering is therefore formally eligible. He would compete on a 100% interview about acoustics, noise, recording/mix/mastering and sound systems — subject matter he can genuinely self-study in a year, unlike MGÜ's trained-ear test. Still worth one confirming email about bilimsel hazırlık (scientific preparation year), which the Enstitü may impose on an out-of-field entrant.
programs.portfolioSpec: NONE required for this programme — CORRECTED (was UNVERIFIED). The official admission page lists the Bilim Sınavı as 'Mülakat %100' and the required documents as diploma and transcript only. No portfolio is listed. The Enstitü's general rules confirm portfolios are demanded only 'when required by the programme' and are submitted separately per ASD; Müzik Teknolojisi does not require one. THIS IS DECISIVE FOR HIM: he currently has no portfolio, and this is the only Turkish option in this set that does not demand one.
programs.auditionSpec: No musical audition. CONFIRMED: a single oral interview (sözlü görüşme sınavı), weighted 100% of the Bilim Sınavı, examining Acoustics, Noise, Recording/Mix/Mastering Technologies and Sound Systems. Pass mark 65. Conducted in Turkish.
programs.equipmentRequired: Not stated — UNVERIFIED. The absence of a portfolio requirement means he needs no pre-existing produced work to apply.
programs.facilities: CONFIRMED from the official DEÜ catalogue: the department has a sound recording studio for practical work and an electronics laboratory ('uygulama amaçlı bir ses kayıt stüdyosu ve bir elektronik laboratuvarı mevcuttur'). programs.recommendation: SUBSTANTIALLY UPGRADED ON RE-CHECK — the previous record was wrong on three material points and understated this programme badly. CORRECTIONS: (1) ACCEPTS NON-MUSIC GRADUATES. The binding 'Öğrenci Kaynağı' field on the live official 2026-2027 page reads '4 yıllık üniversite mezunları' — any four-year university graduate. The 'primarily for music technology graduates' line is a description of target audience, not an eligibility rule. The previous record's central objection dissolves. (2) NO FOREIGN-LANGUAGE REQUIREMENT AT MASTER'S LEVEL — stated verbatim in the Enstitü rules; the previous record wrongly implied a YDS/YÖKDİL-type score might be demanded. (3) THE NON-EU FEE IS PUBLISHED: 35,700 TL for 2026-2027, roughly €700–800/year. Additionally confirmed: the foreign-national quota is FIVE places (kontenjan 7+5), two and a half times MGÜ's two; there is NO portfolio requirement; the entrance exam is a single 100% oral interview on acoustics, noise, recording/mix/mastering and sound systems — technical subject matter a software engineer can genuinely learn in a year, unlike MGÜ's 54-point trained-ear test; the department has a verified recording studio and electronics laboratory; and the 2026-27 calendar is published (apply 10–14 Aug, exam 25 Aug, results 31 Aug). On academic fit and admission mechanics this is arguably a BETTER match for him than Ankara MGÜ. THE ONE REAL CAVEAT, and it is serious: DEÜ requires a C1 Turkish certificate from a DEÜ-Senate-approved centre and publishes NO grace period, whereas MGÜ explicitly grants a funded/permitted year to acquire it. Turkish C1 from zero is a two-year project. Action, in one email to gse@deu.edu.tr: (a) is there any Turkish-study grace period or conditional registration for foreign nationals; (b) would a Software Engineering BSc trigger bilimsel hazırlık; (c) confirm the 2027-2028 foreign-national fee. If the answer to (a) is anything other than a flat no, this becomes his strongest self-funded option. Strategy note: apply to BOTH — MGÜ via Türkiye Bursları (Jan–Feb 2027) for the funded route, DEÜ directly (Aug 2027) as the self-funded backup.

programs.englishTest: None for this Turkish-medium programme.
programs.durationEcts: STILL UNVERIFIED. BAU's AKTS page renders the TYYÇ level and programme aims but no ECTS total or duration. Standard Turkish tezli yüksek lisans is 4 semesters; the tezsiz variant is normally 2–3 semesters — consistent with BAU pricing the tezli as an ANNUAL fee and the tezsiz as a single whole-programme fee.
programs.focus: Music — musicology and performance practice. CONFIRMED from BAU's own Bologna description: the programme aims to produce qualified work to academic standards by bringing together approaches to music science and performance practice, and to develop master's candidates who can become sought-after academics. It is NOT an audio-engineering, music-production or DJ degree.
programs.whatYouStudy: Musicology plus performance practice, thesis/project work, academic ethics and research method, in a cohort environment of graduate students from mixed backgrounds. BAU's Conservatory runs a 'Müzik Teknolojileri' sub-module and an UNDERGRADUATE Müzik Teknolojisi department teaching recording, audio editing, mixing and mastering — but the master's on offer is research-and-performance oriented, not production.
programs.entryRequirements: BAU's general master's rule: ALES (or recognised equivalent), plus documents; English certificate only for English-medium programmes. Programme-specific conditions for the Müzik master's — whether a non-music graduate is admitted, whether an audition applies — remain UNVERIFIED. Given the confirmed price, not worth pursuing.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: UNVERIFIED and unlikely to be straightforward — this is a conservatory research/performance master aimed at producing musicologists and academic musicians. He has no music degree, no conservatory training and no performance practice. Even if formally admitted, the programme does not teach what he wants.
programs.portfolioSpec: UNVERIFIED — ask the Konservatuvar. A conservatory research/performance master would normally expect evidence of musical practice, which he does not have.
programs.auditionSpec: UNVERIFIED — a conservatory master normally requires an audition or entrance interview.
programs.equipmentRequired: UNVERIFIED.
programs.facilities: BAU's Conservatory runs a Music Technology department with studio-based teaching of recording, editing, mixing and mastering at UNDERGRADUATE level. Whether master's students in the Müzik programme get studio access is UNVERIFIED.
programs.intakes: Autumn (Güz) and Spring (Bahar) — BAU advertises both graduate application rounds.
programs.applicationOpens: BAU publishes rolling per-semester 'Lisansüstü Başvuru ve Kayıt Süreçleri' announcements. Exact 2027 dates UNVERIFIED — watch bau.edu.tr graduate announcements from roughly May 2027 for a September 2027 start.
programs.deadline: UNVERIFIED.
programs.tuitionEU: Not applicable — a Turkish private foundation university charges the same published tuition to Turkish and foreign students alike.
programs.tuitionNonEU: CORRECTED FROM UNVERIFIED — NOW CONFIRMED, AND IT IS THE DECISIVE FACT. From BAU's official 2026-2027 graduate fee table: MÜZİK (Türkçe, Tezli) = ₺720,000.00 as a YILLIK ÜCRET (ANNUAL fee); MÜZİK (Türkçe, Tezsiz) = ₺1,310,000.00 as a PROGRAM ÜCRETİ (whole-programme fee); Müzik Doktora = ₺630,000.00 annual. Fees include KDV (VAT); a 10% discount applies to payment in full up front. THIS IS THE RATE HE WOULD PAY as a Tunisian national — BAU does not operate a separate non-EU tariff. At 2026 exchange rates ₺720,000/year is very roughly €14,000–15,000 per year, so on the order of €28,000–30,000 for a two-year thesis master's, or ≈€26,000 for the non-thesis variant. NO 'Ses Teknolojileri' entry exists anywhere in the fee table — further confirmation that the sound-technology programme is not running.
programs.otherFees: YÖK denklik, sworn translations and apostille, residence permit, health insurance, Istanbul accommodation — UNVERIFIED amounts, but trivial next to the tuition.
programs.totalCostEstimate: On the order of ₺1,440,000 (≈€28,000–30,000) in tuition alone for the two-year thesis master's, plus Istanbul living costs — the most expensive city in Turkey. By a very wide margin the most expensive option in this set, and roughly forty times Dokuz Eylül's confirmed 35,700 TL/year. Emphatically NOT 'genuinely cheap'.
programs.scholarships: Türkiye Bursları's Art Scholarship does NOT cover Bahçeşehir — CONFIRMED (only Ankara MGÜ, Ankara Hacı Bayram Veli and İTÜ). BAU offers its own graduate discounts and a 10% up-front-payment reduction; the scale of any merit scholarship is UNVERIFIED but a 10% discount on ₺720,000 still leaves ₺648,000 a year. For a candidate who strongly prefers full funding this is close to the worst possible fit.
programs.visaEligible: Yes — a YÖK-recognised foundation university degree supports a Turkish student residence permit. The Müzik master's is a genuine second-cycle degree at EQF 7. BAU IDEA certificates are NOT and would not support a student residence permit as a degree.
programs.recommendation: AVOID — and the re-check strengthened rather than softened that conclusion. The previous record correctly flagged this as a caution but could not price it; I can now. BAU charges ₺720,000 PER YEAR (≈€14,000–15,000/yr, ≈€28,000–30,000 over two years) for a Turkish-taught musicology-and-performance master's at a private foundation university, with no Türkiye Bursları coverage and no meaningful scholarship route. That is master-level money — considerably more than most Western European private programmes — for a degree that (a) is not audio engineering, not music production and not music technology, (b) is taught entirely in Turkish, which he does not speak, (c) is aimed at producing academics and performing musicians, which he is not and does not want to be, and (d) sits at a university whose one relevant programme is dead. RE-CONFIRMED FINDINGS: the 'Ses Teknolojileri' master's that would have suited him is stale on BAU's conservatory page — its own link 404s, it is absent from the live AKTS catalogue, and it does not appear in the 2026-2027 fee table. Three independent confirmations. Do not apply on the strength of that page. And BAU IDEA's 'Audio & Sound Design' is a private certificate, not a degree and not a residence-permit basis — exactly the kind of product to avoid. Only reopen this file if BAU confirms in writing that Ses Teknolojileri is admitting for 2027-28 AND quotes a fee he can actually pay; on current evidence neither will happen.

programs.program: ΠΜΣ «Τεχνολογίες Ήχου, Βίντεο και Μετάδοσης» / MSc in Audio, Video and Broadcasting Engineering — Department of Electrical and Electronic Engineering
programs.institution: Πανεπιστήμιο Δυτικής Αττικής / University of West Attica (UniWA)
programs.city: Athens (Ancient Olive Grove campus / Πανεπιστημιούπολη Αρχαίου Ελαιώνα, Building Z, Room ZB-106)
programs.publicPrivate: PUBLIC. Greek state university (ΑΕΙ) created by law from the former TEI of Athens and TEI of Piraeus, funded by the Greek Ministry of Education. The ΠΜΣ was authorised by ministerial decision in the Government Gazette (ΦΕΚ Β' 3257/8-8-2018), with its study regulation at ΦΕΚ Β' 4879/1-11-2018.
programs.institutionType: State technological/engineering-oriented university
programs.qualification: Δίπλωμα Μεταπτυχιακών Σπουδών (ΔΜΣ) in 'Τεχνολογίες Ήχου, Βίντεο και Μετάδοσης'. On paper a real second-cycle Greek state degree established by Government Gazette decision. IN PRACTICE THIS IS NOW DOUBTFUL — see accreditationStatus. A degree cannot support a residence permit if the programme does not admit students.
programs.accreditationStatus: ESTABLISHED BY ΦΕΚ Β' 3257/8-8-2018 BUT ALMOST CERTAINLY DEFUNCT — the previous record's caution is now upgraded to a firm finding on the basis of six independent signals gathered by reading the programme's own site directly: (1) the most recent call for applications on the site is for academic year 2021-22, closing 23 September 2021 — FIVE consecutive admission cycles (2022-23 through 2026-27) with no call; (2) the site's 'ΗΜΕΡΟΜΗΝΙΕΣ ΑΙΤΗΣΕΩΝ' (application dates) menu contains entries only for 2018-19, 2019-20, 2020-21 and 2021-22; (3) every announcement, timetable and thesis-topic page is frozen at 2021-22; (4) the site has no valid HTTPS certificate and serves only over plain HTTP, with a '© 2018' footer; (5) its 'Διεθνείς Φοιτητές' (International Students) link points to teipireuofficegr.blogspot.gr — the blog of TEI Piraeus, an institution that ceased to exist when UniWA was created in 2018; (6) the fee regulation still cites Ν.4485/2017 art.35(2), a law REPEALED and replaced by Ν.4957/2022, under which every Greek ΠΜΣ had to be formally re-established — there is no evidence this one was. Decisively, the department's own MSc list shows its sibling programmes carrying live 2025-2026 and 2026-27 προκηρύξεις while this one carries none. It also does not appear in the Ministry's public 'Study in Greece' programme finder. The department page listing is a stale entry, not evidence of an operating programme.
programs.language: Greek. Every page, every call for applications and the application form are in Greek only. The programme has an English-language shell page but there is no evidence of any English-medium teaching. Treat as Greek-taught.
programs.languageRequirement: Never published — UNVERIFIED and now moot. Greek ΠΜΣ of this type normally require documented Greek plus a certificate of English for the literature.
programs.englishTest: Never published — UNVERIFIED and moot.
programs.durationEcts: Never published on any page of the programme site — STILL UNVERIFIED after reading the site in full. Fees are quoted per semester with provision for part-time study at 50% and for 'extension' semesters, implying at least three teaching semesters.
programs.focus: Audio and acoustics, moving image/video and optics, and digital broadcasting of audio and visual signals. Confirmed verbatim from the 2021-22 call: specialisation in fields requiring high scientific training and experience in cutting-edge technologies — sound and acoustics, moving image/video and optics, and digital broadcasting of audio and optical signal — covering production, acquisition, processing, compression, coding, transmission and display within a single framework.
programs.whatYouStudy: Signal-level engineering of sound and picture: studio and broadcast technology (course AVB.2.7 'Τεχνολογία Στούντιο και Μετάδοσης'), image and video processing (AVB.1.4), acoustics, compression and coding, digital broadcasting. This is broadcast/audio engineering, not music production or DJing.
programs.entryRequirements: Holders of a first-cycle degree from a Greek university/TEI department or an equivalent internationally recognised institution. Selection procedure CONFIRMED verbatim from the programme's own page: assessment of the candidate's file AND an interview, participating EQUALLY (ισοβαρώς) in the ranking; the selection committee is composed of departmental professors appointed by the Departmental Assembly; the interview assesses overall preparation, motivation and interest, and the candidate's training in relation to the ΠΜΣ subject. Candidates are NOT notified individually — the interview invitation is posted on the noticeboard and website. 25 places were advertised in the last (2021-22) call.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: Yes in principle — this is an engineering MSc that expects no musical training at all, and priority is given to Electrical and Electronic Engineering graduates. A BSc in Software Engineering would be a plausible file. His engineering background would be an ADVANTAGE here, unlike at the conservatories. This is precisely what makes the programme's apparent death so unfortunate.
programs.portfolioSpec: None. No portfolio required — file plus interview only. It was the only programme in this batch a candidate with no portfolio could enter on academic record alone.
programs.auditionSpec: None. No audition. An interview before a committee of departmental professors, weighted 50% against the file.
programs.equipmentRequired: Never stated — UNVERIFIED.
programs.facilities: Studio and broadcast technology is taught as a named course (AVB.2.7), implying studio facilities in the department, but no facility list was ever published. UNVERIFIED.
programs.intakes: Historically one intake per year, September/autumn. No intake evidenced since 2021-22.
programs.applicationOpens: NO CALL SINCE 2021. Historical pattern: the 2020-21 call closed 18 September 2020 and the 2021-22 call closed 23 September 2021, both with extensions. Nothing has been published for 2022-23, 2023-24, 2024-25, 2025-26 or 2026-27. There is no basis for expecting a call in summer 2027.
programs.deadline: 23 September 2021 for the last published cycle (25 places). No subsequent deadline exists.
programs.tuitionEU: €700 per academic semester for full-time students — CONFIRMED verbatim from the programme's own fees page. Paid through the institution's ΕΛΚΕ in two equal instalments, in weeks 1 and 7 of each semester, except the first instalment of semester one which is paid on enrolment. Part-time students pay 50% of the full-time fee, in two equal instalments at the start and middle of each semester. Extension semesters cost 50% of a full semester's fee, paid in full at the start of the semester. Reduced fees may be granted on documented serious social and/or financial grounds arising after first enrolment, by decision of the Departmental Assembly on the Coordinating Committee's recommendation. Categories under art. 35(2) of Ν.4485/2017 are exempt — a law now repealed.
programs.tuitionNonEU: The same €700 per semester — Greece operates no separate non-EU rate for this ΠΜΣ and the published fee applied to all admitted students. CONFIRMED from the programme's own fees page, BUT that page has not been updated since 2018 and still cites the repealed Ν.4485/2017. The figure is real but historical; it describes a programme that is no longer admitting.
programs.otherFees: Recognition of the Tunisian degree (ΔΟΑΤΑΠ/ΑΤΕΕΝ) would carry a fee; plus Greek residence-permit fee, health insurance, certified translations. Amounts UNVERIFIED and moot.
programs.totalCostEstimate: Had it been running, roughly €1,400–€2,800 in tuition depending on programme length, with Athens living costs dominating. Academically the cheapest good technical fit found — which is exactly why its apparent closure matters.
programs.scholarships: The programme states it MAY award 'υποτροφίες αριστείας' (excellence scholarships) depending on its annual finances, by decision of the Departmental Assembly on the Coordinating Committee's recommendation, and only to full-time students who have not taken study extensions — CONFIRMED verbatim, but no amount, number or criteria were ever published. No dedicated non-EU scholarship. Moot while the programme is not admitting.
programs.visaEligible: NO IN PRACTICE. A full-time on-campus Greek state second-cycle degree would support a student residence permit — but only if the programme actually admits students, and on the evidence it has not admitted anyone since September 2021. He cannot obtain a Greek national D visa for a programme that issues no acceptance.
programs.recommendation: AVOID — CORRECTED FROM 'BEST-FITTING GREEK OPTION' TO A CLOSED FILE. The previous record hedged that the programme 'often means it has stopped admitting'; reading the programme's own site directly turns that hedge into a finding. The last call for applications was for 2021-22, closing 23 September 2021. Five consecutive admission cycles have passed with no call. The application-dates menu stops at 2021-22. Every announcement, timetable and results page is frozen at 2021-22. The site has no valid HTTPS certificate and a 2018 copyright footer. Its 'International Students' link points to the blog of TEI Piraeus, an institution abolished in 2018. Its fee regulation still cites Ν.4485/2017, repealed by Ν.4957/2022, under which every Greek ΠΜΣ had to be re-established — with no sign this one was. And the department's own MSc page shows the sibling programmes carrying live 2025-26 and 2026-27 calls while this one carries none. That is a dead programme with a stale directory entry, not a dormant one. This is doubly unfortunate because it was, on paper, the best academic fit in the whole set for him: an audio and broadcast ENGINEERING master requiring no portfolio and no audition, selecting on file plus interview weighted equally, at €700 a semester in a public university, where his software-engineering degree would have been an advantage rather than an oddity. Two things killed it anyway even if it revived: everything is in Greek, which he does not speak, and there is no evidence of English-medium delivery. Action: one cheap email to eee@uniwa.gr and mscavb@uniwa.gr asking whether the ΠΜΣ will admit for 2027-28 and whether it has been re-established under Ν.4957/2022. Expect no reply or a negative one. Do not build any plan around this.

programs.program: ΠΜΣ «Ψηφιακές Μορφές Τέχνης» / MA in Digital Arts — Department of Fine Arts (Τμήμα Εικαστικών Τεχνών)
programs.institution: Ανωτάτη Σχολή Καλών Τεχνών (ΑΣΚΤ) / Athens School of Fine Arts
programs.publicPrivate: PUBLIC — CONFIRMED. Greek state higher-education institution (ΑΕΙ) funded by the Ministry of Education. Listed in the Ministry's own official programme register (studies.minedu.gov.gr, programme id 1060) with tuition recorded as 'Free' — the standard marker of a state-funded ΠΜΣ.
programs.institutionType: State school of fine arts (national art academy) with university status
programs.qualification: Δίπλωμα Μεταπτυχιακών Σπουδών (ΜΔΕ) 'Ψηφιακές Μορφές Τέχνης' / Master of Arts in Digital Arts, 120 ECTS — CONFIRMED in the Ministry register: Master's, In Person, Athens, 4 semesters, 120 ECTS, language Greek. A real state-recognised second-cycle degree that would support a Greek student residence permit.
programs.accreditationStatus: State-recognised and listed in the official Ministry of Education programme register under the subject areas Arts and Technology, delivery mode In Person. Re-verified August 2026 — the register entry is live and current.
programs.language: Greek — CONFIRMED by the Ministry register ('Language of Instruction: Greek'). There is no English-taught track.
programs.languageRequirement: Not published — STILL UNVERIFIED. A Greek-medium ΠΜΣ at the national art school will in practice require documented academic Greek, in a programme whose assessment is substantially oral and critique-based. Ask artdm@asfa.gr (+30 210 389 7105) what a non-Greek-speaking non-EU applicant must present.
programs.englishTest: None published — UNVERIFIED, and beside the point. Greek is the operative language here, not English.
programs.durationEcts: 120 ECTS over 4 semesters (2 years), full-time, in person — CONFIRMED verbatim from the Ministry of Education register.
programs.focus: CORRECTED AND SHARPENED. The official Ministry register describes the aim as specialisation, research and experimentation in the field of CONTEMPORARY VISUAL ARTS practices, through combined time-based, interactive and computational media, together with systematic theoretical grounding in the historical and philosophical-aesthetic study of technical media (photography, cinematography, videography, digital computer systems) and cultural technologies, and the ways these are visually appropriated in the common ground of art, technology and science. Sound art could conceivably be accommodated, but the programme's declared frame is VISUAL. It is not a music-production, audio-engineering or music-technology degree in any sense.
programs.whatYouStudy: Studio-based digital art practice and research in contemporary visual arts, with theoretical study of technical media and cultural technologies, culminating in artistic work. Run by the Department of Fine Arts. Verify with the department whether a sound-art specialism is supervisable at all before assuming it is.
programs.entryRequirements: Graduates of Greek or recognised foreign higher-education departments in Fine Arts, Visual Studies, Audiovisual Arts, Applied Arts and Architecture. EXCEPTIONALLY, graduates of other university departments may be admitted, judged on the particular relevance and quality of the artistic work and/or research they submit, in the direction of the programme. The current call is for the 19th cycle, 2026-2028.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: A Software Engineering BSc is outside every listed feeder discipline (Fine Arts, Visual Studies, Audiovisual Arts, Applied Arts, Architecture). He could enter ONLY through the explicit exception clause, admitted purely on the strength of submitted artistic work. The portfolio would be his entire case, and it would be judged against fine-arts applicants by a fine-arts jury. He has no portfolio and no fine-arts background.
programs.portfolioSpec: Required and decisive. ΑΣΚΤ publishes separate portfolio guidelines ('ΟΔΗΓΙΕΣ ΓΙΑ ΤΑ ΠΡΟΤΕΙΝΟΜΕΝΑ ΠΕΡΙΕΧΟΜΕΝΑ ΚΑΙ ΤΟ PORTFOLIO') as a distinct announcement for each cycle — CONFIRMED, the guidelines for the 19th cycle were published on 16 June 2026 alongside the call. The exact specification (number of works, format, accompanying text) is UNVERIFIED; download the current guidelines from the ΠΜΣ announcements page or ask artdm@asfa.gr.
programs.auditionSpec: No musical audition — this is a visual-arts programme. Selection is on portfolio and file, with an interview normal for a Greek ΠΜΣ. Exact procedure UNVERIFIED.
programs.equipmentRequired: UNVERIFIED.
programs.facilities: UNVERIFIED — ask the department about digital and sound studios and whether audio work can be supervised at all.
programs.intakes: Biennial cycles — each cycle spans two years and admits once. The 17th cycle ran 2024-2026 (17 students) and the 19th cycle runs 2026-2028. NOTE THE NUMBERING ANOMALY: 17th (2024-2026) to 19th (2026-2028) skips an 18th, which could indicate either an intervening 18th cycle in 2025-2027 (i.e. annual admission) or simply a renumbering. This genuinely matters for his timing and MUST be settled with the department rather than inferred.
programs.applicationOpens: CORRECTED AND CONFIRMED. The call for the 19th cycle (2026-2028) was published on 16 June 2026 on asfa.gr, together with the application-submission announcement and the portfolio guidelines, all dated 16 June 2026. As of August 2026 the Ministry register shows the programme as 'No Open Calls — Check back later', i.e. that round has closed. On a biennial reading the next admission would be 2028-2030, which does NOT match a September 2027 target; on an annual reading a 20th-cycle call would appear around mid-2027, which WOULD match. This must be confirmed with artdm@asfa.gr — it is the difference between a viable timeline and a two-year wait.
programs.deadline: The 19th cycle call and portfolio guidelines were issued 16 June 2026; the exact closing date is UNVERIFIED but the round is now closed (Ministry register shows no open calls as of August 2026). Check the ΠΜΣ announcements page on asfa.gr for the next cycle.
programs.tuitionEU: FREE — CONFIRMED verbatim from the Ministry of Education register ('Tuition Fee: Free'). No τέλη φοίτησης.
programs.tuitionNonEU: FREE — the same as for Greek and EU students. CONFIRMED. Greek public ΠΜΣ do not operate a differential non-EU rate; where a programme is fee-free it is fee-free for everyone admitted. This is THE RATE HE WOULD PAY as a Tunisian national, and it is the cheapest genuine, accredited, in-person second-cycle degree in this entire set.
programs.otherFees: Recognition of the foreign degree (ΔΟΑΤΑΠ/ΑΤΕΕΝ), certified translations, residence-permit fee, health insurance, and his own art materials and equipment. Amounts UNVERIFIED.
programs.totalCostEstimate: Tuition €0. Total cost is two years of Athens living costs plus visa and permit administration plus materials. Athens living costs UNVERIFIED but are the entire expense.
programs.scholarships: None specific to this programme published — UNVERIFIED. Because tuition is already zero the funding question reduces entirely to living costs. The department does circulate general postgraduate financial-support and external scholarship notices (e.g. a financial-support announcement for postgraduate students 2026-2027 dated 27 February 2026, and Slovak government scholarships dated 28 July 2026), so it is worth watching that feed. Check IKY (Greek State Scholarships Foundation) and any Greece–Tunisia bilateral quota separately.
programs.visaEligible: Yes — CONFIRMED. Full-time, IN PERSON (explicitly so in the Ministry register), state-recognised 120-ECTS second-cycle degree at a Greek ΑΕΙ. It would support a student residence permit if he were admitted.
programs.recommendation: AVOID FOR HIM — not because there is anything wrong with the programme, but because it fails him on four independent counts simultaneously, and the previous record's 'long-shot' framing was too generous. To be clear about what it IS: a genuinely free, genuinely public, genuinely accredited 120-ECTS in-person master's at Greece's national art school, confirmed in the Ministry of Education register at zero tuition for everyone including non-EU nationals. That is a rare and real thing and worth keeping in the database. But for him: (1) IT IS NOT HIS SUBJECT. The Ministry's own description makes the frame explicitly CONTEMPORARY VISUAL ARTS — time-based, interactive and computational media, with theoretical study of photography, cinematography, videography and digital computer systems. Sound art is at most tolerated; music production, audio engineering and electronic music are absent. (2) IT IS TAUGHT IN GREEK, which he does not speak, in a programme assessed largely through critique and oral defence. (3) HE WOULD ENTER ONLY THROUGH THE EXCEPTION CLAUSE, admitted purely on submitted artistic work, judged by a fine-arts jury against fine-arts graduates — and he has no portfolio and no fine-arts background whatever. (4) THE TIMING IS PROBABLY WRONG: the 19th cycle (2026-2028) was called on 16 June 2026 and has closed, and on a biennial reading the next intake is 2028-2030, a full year past his September 2027 target. If he wants to keep it alive at all, one email to artdm@asfa.gr settles it: is admission annual or biennial and when is the next call; has the exception clause ever admitted an engineering graduate; is any teaching possible in English; and send the current portfolio guidelines. Realistically, close the file.

programs.program: ΠΜΣ «Ακουστικός Σχεδιασμός και Ψηφιακός Ήχος» (ΑΣΠ) / MSc in Acoustic Design and Digital Sound
programs.institution: Ελληνικό Ανοικτό Πανεπιστήμιο / Hellenic Open University (HOU/EAP), Patras
programs.city: Patras (registered seat) — delivery is entirely at a distance, with no campus attendance
programs.publicPrivate: PUBLIC. programs.accreditationStatus: State-recognised; listed in the Ministry of Education programme register. The degree is genuine. The delivery mode is what disqualifies it for a visa applicant.
programs.language: Greek — CONFIRMED from the official HOU programme page. All teaching and assessment is in Greek.
programs.languageRequirement: Applicants must submit a 'Υπεύθυνη Δήλωση' (statutory declaration) confirming they possess the necessary level of knowledge of the programme's subject matter; foreign qualifications must meet recognition criteria under Greek law. programs.englishTest: None — irrelevant, the programme is entirely in Greek.
programs.durationEcts: 120 ECTS, minimum 2 academic years — CONFIRMED. Structured as FOUR thematic units plus the master's thesis: ΑΣΠ50 Acoustic Design, ΑΣΠ51 Sound Insulation and Protection, ΑΣΠ60 Room Acoustics, ΑΣΠ61 Digital Sound, plus Διπλωματική Εργασία. programs.focus: CORRECTED AND MATERIALLY NARROWER THAN PREVIOUSLY RECORDED. The previous record called this 'closer to his stated field than most Greek offerings'. The confirmed unit list shows otherwise: THREE of the four taught units are building and environmental acoustics — Acoustic Design, Sound Insulation and Protection, and Room Acoustics — and only ONE, ΑΣΠ61 Digital Sound, touches digital audio at all. This is fundamentally an ARCHITECTURAL AND ENVIRONMENTAL ACOUSTICS degree with a single digital-audio module bolted on. It is not a music-production, electronic-music or DJ qualification, and it is only marginally an audio-engineering one in the sense he means.
programs.whatYouStudy: Four modular thematic units delivered at a distance: acoustic design; sound insulation and noise protection; room acoustics; digital sound. Then a master's thesis. Assessment by written assignments and remote examinations, all in Greek.
programs.entryRequirements: Holders of an undergraduate degree from a higher-education institution in a relevant field, or an equivalent foreign qualification recognised under Greek law. Applicants must provide a statutory declaration confirming sufficient knowledge of the programme's subject matter. Whether a Tunisian Software Engineering BSc counts as 'relevant' is UNVERIFIED — but the question is academic given the visa problem.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: Probably yes on paper — this is an acoustics/engineering programme rather than a conservatory one, and no music degree is named anywhere. His engineering background would help. UNVERIFIED, and moot.
programs.portfolioSpec: None published — HOU admits on qualification, not portfolio. UNVERIFIED but consistent with HOU practice.

programs.deadline: UNVERIFIED — ask HOU admissions.

programs.tuitionNonEU: The same €750 per thematic unit / €3,750 total — CONFIRMED. HOU publishes a single rate and operates no separate non-EU tariff. Since there is no residence in Greece there is no differential. This is THE RATE HE WOULD PAY as a Tunisian national.
programs.otherFees: Recognition of the foreign degree under Greek law; certified translations. Amounts UNVERIFIED. No relocation, accommodation, visa or permit costs, because there is no relocation.
programs.totalCostEstimate: €3,750 in tuition, with no relocation, accommodation or visa cost — the cheapest total in this sweep, precisely and only because he would never leave Tunisia.
programs.scholarships: Not published for this programme — UNVERIFIED. HOU operates limited social-criteria fee reductions; ask admissions.
programs.visaEligible: NO — CONFIRMED. This is a distance-learning degree, delivered entirely remotely, with remote examinations from 2025-26 onwards, and the Ministry register classifies HOU delivery accordingly. Greek student residence permits require enrolment in a full-time, in-person programme with physical attendance. It will not get him to Europe and cannot be made to. HOU's own pages state no policy on non-EU international students — UNVERIFIED; ask in writing if he wants it in black and white.
programs.recommendation: AVOID — confirmed, and for one more reason than the previous record gave. Everything the previous agent said stands: it is a genuine, state-recognised Greek 120-ECTS master's at €3,750 total, delivered entirely at a distance in Greek with remote exams, no studio, no cohort and no student visa, which makes it useless as a migration instrument for a man whose entire plan depends on a European residence permit. But the re-check adds a substantive correction on SUBJECT: the confirmed thematic-unit list is ΑΣΠ50 Acoustic Design, ΑΣΠ51 Sound Insulation and Protection, ΑΣΠ60 Room Acoustics and ΑΣΠ61 Digital Sound. Three of the four taught units are building and environmental acoustics; only one touches digital audio. The previous record's claim that this is 'exactly his subject area' is wrong — it is an architectural-acoustics degree, closer to noise-control consultancy than to music production, sound design or electronic music. So it fails him three ways: no visa, no Greek, and not actually the field he wants. Recorded so that the database holds the finding and no later sweep wastes time on it. If he ever wants a distance credential he should look at English-language distance options in music technology or audio engineering, not this one.

programs.program: DCSL60 — Diploma Accademico di Secondo Livello in Musica Applicata, indirizzo Sound Design (Biennio)
programs.institution: Conservatorio di Musica "Francesco Venezze" di Rovigo
programs.institutionType: State conservatoire (Conservatorio Statale di Musica) within the AFAM system, under the Ministero dell'Università e della Ricerca
programs.publicPrivate: PUBLIC — CONFIRMED. A Conservatorio Statale di Musica in the AFAM system, awarding a ministerially coded (DCSL60) second-level academic diploma. Confirmed on the official course page, which states the EHEA/EQF mapping directly — a marker no private academy can produce.
programs.qualification: Diploma Accademico di Secondo Livello in Musica Applicata — SourceURL page states explicitly: EHEA 2° ciclo, EQF level 7. CONFIRMED. A real state-recognised second-cycle degree, equated to a Laurea Magistrale. Suitable for credential recognition abroad and for a student residence permit.
programs.accreditationStatus: CONFIRMED state-accredited under ministerial course code DCSL60 in the MUR AFAM register. The official course page publishes the EHEA 2° ciclo / EQF 7 mapping itself, which is unusually explicit for an Italian conservatoire page and genuinely useful for later recognition of the award outside Italy.
programs.language: Italian — CONFIRMED. No English-taught route. The B2 requirement imposed on non-native speakers confirms Italian is the working language of the course.
programs.languageRequirement: B2 Italian (CEFR) for non-native speakers — CONFIRMED, and now with an important clarification the previous report left open. The official page states the B2 may be demonstrated EITHER by a test administered by the conservatoire OR by a valid certificate ('attraverso test o certificazione valida'). So he does NOT necessarily need to buy a CELI/CILS certificate — an in-house test is an accepted route. The previous report listed 'ask whether the B2 must be certified or is tested in-house' as an open question; it is answered, and answered favourably.
programs.englishTest: None. No IELTS or TOEFL required or accepted — the course is not English-taught. His untaken IELTS is irrelevant here, which removes one cost and one deadline from his 2026-27 timeline.
programs.durationEcts: 2 years, 120 CFA/ECTS — CONFIRMED on the official page (stated as 120 ECTS, EHEA second cycle). The previous report's breakdown of 55 CFA year one / 56 CFA year two / 10 CFA thesis sums to 121 and could not be re-confirmed on the page in this pass; treat the 120 total as authoritative and the internal split as indicative only. Request the piano di studi for the exact distribution.
programs.focus: Applied music with a Sound Design orientation. DCSL60 'Musica Applicata' is a separate ministerial course family from DCSL34 'Musica Elettronica' and is oriented toward music and sound applied to media rather than concert electroacoustic composition. For a candidate targeting commercial and media work this framing is a better match than a composition degree — but note it is still not a club/dance-music degree.
programs.whatYouStudy: Composition for music applied to images (the dominant credit block), electroacoustic composition and sound design, music informatics, history of electroacoustic music, and audio post-production and mixing technologies. Centre of gravity is music-to-picture and applied media sound.
programs.entryRequirements: CONFIRMED AND VERBATIM from the official page: 'diploma accademico di primo livello, o di diploma di laurea triennale, o di diploma di conservatorio di previgente ordinamento congiunto ad un diploma di scuola secondaria superiore'. CORRECTION OF DETAIL: the previous report truncated this to '...o di diploma di conservatorio'. The full text matters, but it matters in his favour — the qualifier 'di previgente ordinamento congiunto ad un diploma di scuola secondaria superiore' attaches to the CONSERVATOIRE route, not to the laurea triennale route. 'Diploma di laurea triennale' therefore stands as an unconditioned qualifying title in its own right. His BSc in Software Engineering satisfies the entry rule on its face, with no music-specific precondition. Plus B2 Italian.
programs.auditionSpec: CONFIRMED, and it is the lowest published barrier of the four. A single ORAL assessment, verbatim: 'Presentazione da parte del candidato di un book contenente lavori video o audio, realizzazioni in elettronica o partiture, che saranno oggetto di discussione con la commissione.' The commission evaluates command of electronic music production and realisation across varied instrumental contexts, and prefers candidates strong across all listed areas. DECISIVE POINT, CONFIRMED: there is NO written theory paper, NO solfège or lettura cantata, NO ear-training test and NO instrumental performance requirement published. This is the only one of the four programmes with no musicianship examination at all — the single most important fact in this entire comparison for a self-taught candidate.
programs.portfolioSpec: A 'book' of video works, audio works, electronic realisations, OR scores — CONFIRMED, and note the 'or': scores are only one of four accepted alternatives, so a purely audio/DAW portfolio is fully admissible. This is exactly what a year of self-directed work can produce. Build toward the course's own centre of gravity: three to five cues scored to picture, several original electronic pieces, and demonstrable mixing and post-production work. The commission discusses the book with him, so he must be able to talk about his own production decisions — in Italian.
programs.equipmentRequired: UNVERIFIED — not published on the course page. Assume a personal laptop with a DAW.
programs.facilities: UNVERIFIED — not published. The syllabus implies audio post-production and mixing facilities. Rovigo is a small conservatoire, which usually means better studio access per student than at a large one, but confirm with the segreteria.
programs.tuitionEU: UNVERIFIED — no fee figures are published on the course page, and the conservatoire's site was behind a bot-verification gate during this re-check, so the previous report's fee narrative could NOT be re-confirmed from source. What is safe to say: as a state AFAM institution Rovigo operates the standard Italian ISEE income-banded contributo, paid via PagoPA. Comparable Veneto state conservatoires run roughly €1,800–2,300 at the TOP band, with low and zero bands below that — indicative only, do not rely on it for Rovigo. Request the current Regolamento tasse e contributi from the segreteria.
programs.tuitionNonEU: UNVERIFIED as to amount — and this is the one material gap in an otherwise strong record. IMPORTANT CORRECTION OF CONFIDENCE: the previous report stated as documented fact that foreign candidates are exempt from the admission examination fee and that ESU Padova handles students without a codice fiscale. Neither could be re-verified from the official site in this pass (the site blocked automated access), so both must be treated as UNCONFIRMED rather than established. The structural point does stand on general Italian rule: Rovigo applies the ISEE-band system, not a flat non-EU surcharge, so a Tunisian family income declared through an ISEE parificato/ISEEE should place him at or near the lowest band. The mechanism is favourable; the figures are unknown. Do not build a budget on the previous report's fee-exemption claims until the segreteria confirms them in writing.
programs.otherFees: Tassa regionale per il diritto allo studio (ESU Veneto), payable annually — amount UNVERIFIED. Marca da bollo. An admission examination fee applies; the previous report's claim that foreign candidates are exempt from it is UNCONFIRMED in this pass and should be asked rather than assumed.
programs.totalCostEstimate: Cannot be stated precisely — no contributi table verified. On the standard Italian pattern with an ISEEE filed, plausibly near-zero to roughly €2,000/year in fees. Rovigo is a small provincial Veneto city with materially lower living costs than Bologna, Milan or Turin, roughly €600–850/month, and housing is comparatively easy to find. Two-year all-in is dominated by living costs, plausibly €16,000–22,000 before any ESU scholarship.
programs.scholarships: ESU Padova, the Veneto regional right-to-study agency covering Rovigo, runs income-based borse di studio that are open to non-EU students and can cover fee exemption, a maintenance grant and subsidised housing. This is the realistic funding route and it is means-tested, not merit-gated on musical achievement — which suits him. MAECI Italian government scholarships are the national alternative and are open to Tunisian nationals. UNVERIFIED whether the conservatoire offers any internal award.
programs.intakes: Autumn — Italian academic year. One intake per year.
programs.applicationOpens: UNVERIFIED — not published on the course page. Italian conservatoire ammissioni bandi typically appear in spring. For a September 2027 start, watch conservatoriorovigo.it from about March 2027, and run Universitaly pre-enrolment in parallel on the Ministry's separate and earlier calendar.
programs.deadline: UNVERIFIED — set by the annual Bando di ammissione. Request it from the segreteria in autumn 2026.
programs.visaEligible: YES. A Diploma Accademico di Secondo Livello from a state conservatoire is a full second-cycle degree and supports an Italian student visa (type D) and a permesso di soggiorno per studio. As a non-EU applicant resident abroad he must pre-enrol via Universitaly and compete within the annually published non-EU contingent for the institution — that contingent, not the academic entry rule, is the real practical bottleneck and should be checked early.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: YES — CONFIRMED, and it is the clearest yes of the four. 'Diploma di laurea triennale' is named as a qualifying title in its own right, and the admission assessment is a portfolio book plus an oral discussion with no theory paper, no ear training and no instrumental test. A Software Engineering BSc plus a genuine audio/audiovisual portfolio maps onto the published requirements without any exception needing to be made for him.
programs.recommendation: VALUE VERDICT: WORTH IT. RATING: A. — VERIFIED AND CONFIRMED; this remains the best-matched of the four and the only one with an unobstructed path. Three things line up here that line up nowhere else in this set: the entry rule explicitly accepts any three-year university degree with no music precondition; the admission is a portfolio-and-interview with NO musicianship examination whatsoever (the other two Italian options both impose sung reading, ear training and music history on him); and the cost sits inside the ISEE system, so a low Tunisian family income should translate into a low contributo rather than a flat foreign surcharge. One genuine improvement over the previous report: B2 Italian may be satisfied by an in-house test OR a certificate, so he is not forced to buy a CILS/CELI. Real conditions remain: B2 Italian is mandatory, not advisory, so Italian study must start now — his French makes this the fastest language on his list, realistically 12 months to B2 with sustained work; and the degree's centre of gravity is composition for images and applied media sound, not club music, so his DJ ambition is served only indirectly. One correction to the previous record's confidence: its fee-exemption claims for foreign candidates could not be re-verified and must not be budgeted on. Actions: contact the segreteria in autumn 2026 for the Bando di ammissione, the Regolamento tasse e contributi, and written confirmation of how B2 is assessed and whether the admission exam fee is waived for foreign candidates. Build the portfolio to the syllabus — scored-to-picture cues first, original electronic pieces second, mixing and post-production evidence third. If one place comes out of this whole search, this is it.

programs.program: DCSL34 — Diploma Accademico di Secondo Livello in Musica Elettronica, indirizzo Composizione e Sound Design (Biennio)
programs.institution: METS — Scuola di Musica Elettronica, Conservatorio di Musica "Giorgio Federico Ghedini" di Cuneo
programs.institutionType: Specialist electronic music school (METS) operating as a department of a state conservatoire within the AFAM system, under the Ministero dell'Università e della Ricerca
programs.publicPrivate: PUBLIC — CONFIRMED. METS is the electronic music school of the Conservatorio di Musica 'G.F. Ghedini' di Cuneo, a state conservatoire. The separate metscuneo.it domain is branding, not a separate legal entity: admissions run through mets@conservatoriocuneo.it and the degrees are the conservatoire's own ministerially coded diplomas. Not a private academy.
programs.qualification: Diploma Accademico di Secondo Livello in Musica Elettronica — a real state second-cycle degree, EQF 7, equated to a Laurea Magistrale/Specialistica for access to public competitions per the conservatoire's Manifesto degli Studi.
programs.accreditationStatus: State-accredited under ministerial course code DCSL34 in the MUR AFAM register. Genuine EHEA second-cycle qualification. No concerns.
programs.language: Italian — CONFIRMED. No English-taught route advertised. The oral admission components (presentation of works, music history, motivational interview) are conducted in Italian.
programs.languageRequirement: UNVERIFIED — CONFIRMED AS A GENUINE GAP. No Italian level is published anywhere on the METS admission pages, which is unusual and materially unhelpful. Italian state conservatoires generally require or test B2. Given that the admission process here is heavily oral — a motivational interview, a discussion of his works, and an examination in music history — functional Italian is a practical necessity regardless of what is formally demanded. Ask mets@conservatoriocuneo.it directly.
programs.englishTest: None. Not English-taught, so his untaken IELTS/TOEFL is irrelevant.
programs.durationEcts: 2 years, 120 CFA (standard for a biennio di II livello). CFA values are not stated inline on the METS study-plan page — UNVERIFIED at source; request the piano di studi.
programs.focus: Electronic music, Composition and Sound Design track. METS is one of very few Italian conservatoires running a dedicated, separately branded electronic music school with a full ladder: a preparatory course, two triennio tracks (DCPL34 Musica Elettronica compositional, DCPL61 Tecnico del suono) and two biennio tracks (DCSL34, DCSL61). The institutional commitment to electronic music here is real and unusual.
programs.whatYouStudy: Composition and sound design at second level. Detailed module list UNVERIFIED — the METS study-plan page lists course titles but not inline syllabi. Request the piano di studi from METS.
programs.entryRequirements: CONFIRMED AND VERBATIM: 'L'accesso ai corsi di II livello è riservato a chi in possesso di Diploma Accademico di I livello, di Laurea di I livello o di Diploma di Conservatorio vecchio ordinamento.' A Laurea di I livello — any three-year university degree — is accepted as a plain qualifying title. His BSc qualifies. CORRECTION: the previous report framed this as conditional, claiming university graduates may apply only with 'adeguata e documentata preparazione' and with debiti formativi assigned. That conditional wording does NOT appear on the admission page as fetched; the published rule is unconditional. Bridging coursework may still be assigned in practice, but do not report it as a published entry condition.
programs.auditionSpec: CONFIRMED, TWO-PART, and the second part is the problem. FIRST EXAM (early September): a WRITTEN component, 'Analisi di un brano elettroacustico' — analysis of an electroacoustic piece supplied by the commission. Exemption applies only to holders of a first-level diploma in Musica Elettronica or Musica Applicata, so HE IS NOT EXEMPT and must sit it. Plus an ORAL component: presentation of his own composed works, demonstrated knowledge of audio editing software, twentieth-century music history, history of electroacoustic music, acoustics and psychoacoustics, and a motivational interview. SECOND EXAM: verbatim, 'I candidati in possesso di diploma accademico di I livello di conservatorio sono esonerati dalla prova' — exemption is limited strictly to holders of a first-level CONSERVATOIRE academic diploma. A foreign university BSc does NOT exempt him. He must therefore sit a conventional musicianship examination covering ear training, lettura cantata (sight-singing), intonation and rhythm, and music history to triennio standard. For someone with no conservatory training and no music degree this is a real, substantial obstacle requiring roughly a year of dedicated preparation. CORRECTION: the previous report claimed the METS FAQ describes biennio admission more lightly, as merely a motivational interview, and flagged a 'tension' to resolve. The FAQ as fetched says no such thing — it simply links to the two admission-exam pages. There is no conflicting lighter description and no ambiguity to exploit. The exam pages are authoritative and they are strict.
programs.portfolioSpec: CONFIRMED. Before the exam date, candidates email 'alcuni propri lavori (audio, multimediali, etc…) ed un curriculum vitae' to mets@conservatoriocuneo.it using PERMANENT sharing links (Google Drive, Dropbox, OneDrive) — explicitly not time-limited links. The oral then requires him to present and defend his own electronic compositions. NOTE ON A PREVIOUS OVERSTATEMENT: the previous report claimed the oral demands 'documentation of live-set executions', and treated that as a unique reward for a DJ practice. That specific requirement was not visible on the admission page in this pass. Live-set documentation is very likely welcome as supporting evidence, but do not treat it as a published requirement or as a structural advantage he can bank on.
programs.equipmentRequired: UNVERIFIED — not published. Proficiency with audio editing, mixing and sound-processing software is examined orally, so a personal DAW setup is assumed.
programs.facilities: UNVERIFIED in detail. A dedicated electronic music school with its own staff and a full triennio-to-biennio ladder normally implies better-than-average studio access. Ask for a facilities list or arrange a visit via mets@conservatoriocuneo.it.
programs.tuitionEU: UNVERIFIED as to amounts — not published on the METS pages, and the conservatoire's fee page could not be reached in this pass. Mechanism per the Manifesto degli Studi: fees are organised in ISEE income bands (fasce di reddito), paid in up to three instalments via PagoPA through Isidata, governed by a separate Regolamento sulla contribuzione studentesca annexed to the Manifesto. Request that Regolamento from the segreteria for real figures.
programs.tuitionNonEU: UNVERIFIED as to amount; mechanism documented and the lever is clear. Per the Manifesto, foreign students must present an ISEE parificato, and anyone who does not present an ISEE certificate is placed automatically in the HIGHEST income band. This is the single most important financial action item: filed correctly against a Tunisian family income the ISEE parificato should place him at or near the bottom band; not filed, he pays the maximum by default. There is no flat non-EU surcharge, which is favourable — but the exemption is not automatic, it must be actively claimed through the ISEE parificato process, which itself takes weeks and requires consular-legalised income documents from Tunisia. Start it early. Exact band figures: request the Regolamento contributi.
programs.otherFees: Tassa regionale per il diritto allo studio (EDISU Piemonte) plus marca da bollo, payable with the first instalment via PagoPA through Isidata. Amounts UNVERIFIED for Cuneo specifically; the neighbouring Conservatorio di Torino bundles the EDISU tax plus bollo at roughly €156, indicative only. Contributory irregularity blocks exam sittings, so payment discipline matters.
programs.totalCostEstimate: Cannot be stated precisely without the contributi table. On the Italian ISEE pattern with a parificato filed, expect low hundreds of euros per year in fees; without it, the top band. Cuneo is a small Piedmontese city with the lowest living costs of the four locations, roughly €550–800/month, about 90 minutes from Turin. On cost alone this is the cheapest genuinely relevant option here — but cost is not what decides this one.
programs.scholarships: EDISU Piemonte income-based scholarships are open to non-EU students and can cover fee exemption, a maintenance grant and subsidised housing — the main realistic route, and means-tested rather than merit-gated. MAECI Italian government scholarships are the national alternative and open to Tunisians. The previous report's claim that METS itself advertises paid collaboration contracts and internal scholarships could NOT be re-verified in this pass and should be treated as unconfirmed until METS says so in writing.
programs.intakes: Autumn. Admission exams typically early September, with teaching beginning in November.
programs.applicationOpens: UNVERIFIED as to exact window. The conservatoire publishes an annual 'AMMISSIONI A.A. 20XX/20XX' notice; the 2026/2027 notice appeared around July 2026, which is a PRIOR CYCLE — confirm the 2027/2028 dates directly. Admission exams sit in early September, teaching starts November. Non-EU applicants must complete Universitaly pre-enrolment on the Ministry's separate and earlier calendar. Note the July-notice/September-exam rhythm is TIGHT for a candidate who must also obtain a visa.
programs.deadline: UNVERIFIED — governed by the annual ammissioni notice. Portfolio materials must reach mets@conservatoriocuneo.it BEFORE the exam date, which is the operative deadline for him.
programs.visaEligible: YES. A state conservatoire second-level diploma supports an Italian student visa and permesso di soggiorno per studio, subject to Universitaly pre-enrolment and the annual non-EU contingent.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: PARTIALLY — the formal door is open, the examination door is not. Entry qualification: a Laurea di I livello is explicitly and unconditionally accepted, so his BSc qualifies him to APPLY. But he is exempt from neither exam: he must sit the written electroacoustic analysis (exemption limited to Musica Elettronica/Musica Applicata first-level diploma holders) AND the second exam covering lettura cantata, intonation, rhythm, ear training and music history (exemption limited to conservatoire first-level diploma holders). That is a full musicianship examination for a man with no conservatoire training, no music degree and no formal theory. Eligible to apply is not the same as able to pass.
programs.recommendation: VALUE VERDICT: CONDITIONAL. RATING: B. — A genuine, cheap, well-accredited degree at a serious electronic music school, blocked by one real obstacle that he can only remove with a year of deliberate work. Downgraded from the previous report's enthusiasm on two counts: the supposed FAQ 'tension' suggesting a lighter interview-based admission does not exist, and the 'documented live-set executions' requirement that was said to reward his DJ practice was not found on the page. Neither of the softening factors the previous agent relied on survives verification. What survives is solid: METS is a dedicated electronic music school inside a state conservatoire, a Laurea di I livello is unconditionally accepted as an entry title, the ISEE parificato should drive his fees to near-nothing, and Cuneo has the lowest living costs of any option here. Against that: he must pass an ear-training, sight-singing and music-history examination to triennio standard, plus a written analysis of an electroacoustic piece, in Italian, with no published language level to prepare against. Actions for autumn 2026, in writing to mets@conservatoriocuneo.it: (1) confirm that a foreign three-year Software Engineering degree does not exempt him from either prova, and ask what standard the second prova expects; (2) ask what Italian level is required or tested; (3) request the Regolamento contributi for the lowest ISEE parificato band. Practical judgement: he should apply here as a SECOND choice behind Rovigo, and treat the musicianship gap as work to do rather than a reason to walk away — basic ear training and solfège are the recurring obstacle across the whole Italian conservatoire sector and closing that gap raises his ceiling everywhere, not just at Cuneo. Do not make this his only application.

programs.program: DCSL61 — Diploma Accademico di Secondo Livello in Tecnico del Suono, indirizzo Ingegneria del Suono e Multimedia (Biennio)
programs.institution: METS — Scuola di Musica Elettronica, Conservatorio di Musica "Giorgio Federico Ghedini" di Cuneo
programs.institutionType: Specialist electronic music school within a state conservatoire in the AFAM system, under the Ministero dell'Università e della Ricerca
programs.publicPrivate: PUBLIC — CONFIRMED. Same institution as the DCSL34 record: the Conservatorio di Musica 'G.F. Ghedini' di Cuneo is a state conservatoire and METS is its electronic music school. Reported separately because DCSL61 is a different ministerial course code and a different degree title, with its OWN separate admission page and its own distinct first exam — not a variant of DCSL34.
programs.qualification: Diploma Accademico di Secondo Livello in Tecnico del Suono — a real state second-cycle degree, EQF 7, equated to a Laurea Specialistica/Magistrale for access to public competitions per the conservatoire's Manifesto degli Studi. CONFIRMED as an existing, running course: the METS study-plan page lists 'TECNICO DEL SUONO – INGEGNERIA DEL SUONO E MULTIMEDIA (DCSL61)' among its biennio offerings.
programs.accreditationStatus: State-accredited under ministerial course code DCSL61 'Tecnico del Suono' in the MUR AFAM register. DCSL61 is one of only a small number of second-level sound-engineering diplomas active nationally; other institutions running it include Frosinone, Reggio Calabria and Vibo Valentia, so the code itself is worth chasing elsewhere if Cuneo fails.
programs.language: Italian — CONFIRMED. No English-taught route.
programs.languageRequirement: UNVERIFIED — no Italian level published on the METS pages, same gap as the DCSL34 track. Assume B2 is required or tested, consistent with the sector. The oral exam and motivational interview are in Italian regardless. Confirm with mets@conservatoriocuneo.it.
programs.englishTest: None. Not English-taught.
programs.durationEcts: 2 years, 120 CFA standard for a biennio di II livello. CFA values not stated inline on the METS study-plan page — UNVERIFIED at source; request the piano di studi.
programs.focus: Sound engineering and multimedia — the engineering-side degree rather than the composition-side one. Of the four programmes here this is the closest state-recognised second-cycle qualification to 'audio engineering' as he would understand the term, and the one whose subject matter best exploits his existing software-engineering background.
programs.whatYouStudy: Sound engineering and multimedia at second level, building on the DCPL61 Tecnico del Suono triennio that feeds it. Per the national DCSL61 profile, graduates acquire specific technical and cultural competencies with emphasis on musical repertoire and analytical methodology, including the history of electroacoustic and computer technologies applied to music. Detailed Cuneo module list UNVERIFIED — request the piano di studi.
programs.entryRequirements: NOW CONFIRMED — this was UNVERIFIED in the previous report and is no longer. The dedicated Biennio TS admission page states verbatim: 'L'accesso ai corsi di II livello è riservato a chi in possesso di Diploma Accademico di I livello, di Laurea di I livello o di Diploma di Conservatorio vecchio ordinamento.' A Laurea di I livello is explicitly accepted for THIS track, not merely by analogy with the composition track. His BSc in Software Engineering qualifies him to apply.
programs.auditionSpec: MAJOR CORRECTION — THE PREVIOUS REPORT'S CENTRAL HOPE IS FALSE. The previous agent recorded this as 'UNVERIFIED for this track', stated that METS 'did not publish separate requirements' for Tecnico del Suono, cited the wrong page (/piani-di-studio/) as its source, and hypothesised that admission rests on 'an aptitude and motivational interview rather than a musicianship examination', calling this the 'single highest-value unanswered question'. METS DOES publish a dedicated admission page for this track — /info-per-iscrizioni/esami-di-ammissione-biennio-ts/ — and it disproves the hypothesis. The structure is: FIRST EXAM, practical component — 'Mixaggio e finalizzazione della registrazione su tracce indipendenti di un brano fornito dalla commissione', i.e. mix and finalise a multitrack supplied by the commission; exemption applies ONLY to holders of a first-level diploma in Tecnico del suono or Musica Elettronica (technical track), so he must sit it. Oral component — presentation of an original foley/video sound work, presentation of prior sound engineering projects, and a motivational interview. SECOND EXAM — verbatim, 'I candidati in possesso di diploma accademico di I livello di conservatorio sono esonerati dalla prova'. Exemption is again limited to conservatoire first-level diploma holders, so HE MUST SIT IT: lettura cantata, intonazione e ritmica, ear training, and storia e storiografia della musica to triennio standard. The musicianship hurdle applies here EXACTLY as it does at DCSL34. This track is not the open back door the previous report hoped it was.
programs.portfolioSpec: CONFIRMED and now specific, where the previous report could only guess. Submit 'alcuni propri lavori (audio, multimediali, etc…) ed un curriculum vitae' to mets@conservatoriocuneo.it via permanent sharing links before the September exam. Critically, the oral requires an ORIGINAL FOLEY / VIDEO SOUND WORK plus prior sound engineering projects — so the portfolio year should produce, specifically: a foley-and-sound-design reel cut to picture, multitrack recordings he has engineered, mixes and masters, and any DSP or audio-software work salvageable from his engineering degree. He must also be able to mix a supplied multitrack under exam conditions, which is a trainable, concrete skill — genuinely the most learnable examination in this whole set, and one where his engineering brain is an asset rather than a handicap.
programs.equipmentRequired: UNVERIFIED — not published. A capable DAW setup with mixing capability is implied by the practical exam.
programs.facilities: UNVERIFIED in detail. A sound engineering track with a practical mixing examination implies recording studio and multichannel facilities, and METS runs a DCPL61 triennio feeding this biennio, so the infrastructure exists. Request a facilities list or a visit.
programs.tuitionEU: UNVERIFIED as to amounts. Identical regime to DCSL34: income-banded (fasce di reddito) contribution requiring a valid ISEE at enrolment, per the Regolamento sulla contribuzione studentesca annexed to the Manifesto degli Studi, paid in up to three instalments via PagoPA through Isidata.
programs.tuitionNonEU: UNVERIFIED as to amount; mechanism identical to DCSL34 and the same lever applies. Foreign students must present an ISEE parificato; anyone not presenting an ISEE certificate is placed in the highest income band by default. With a parificato reflecting Tunisian family income he should sit at or near the lowest band. No flat non-EU surcharge. Start the ISEE parificato process early — it requires consular-legalised Tunisian income documents and takes weeks. Request the Regolamento contributi for exact figures.
programs.otherFees: Tassa regionale per il diritto allo studio (EDISU Piemonte) and marca da bollo with the first instalment via PagoPA/Isidata. Amounts UNVERIFIED for Cuneo; roughly €156 bundled at neighbouring Torino, indicative only.
programs.totalCostEstimate: Cannot be stated precisely without the contributi table. On the Italian ISEE pattern with a parificato filed, expect low hundreds of euros per year in fees. Cuneo living costs are the lowest of the four locations at roughly €550–800/month. Two-year all-in plausibly €15,000–20,000, overwhelmingly living costs, before any EDISU scholarship.
programs.scholarships: EDISU Piemonte income-based scholarships, open to non-EU students, covering fee exemption, maintenance and subsidised housing — the main realistic route. MAECI government scholarships as the national alternative. The previous report's claim of METS-internal paid collaboration contracts and scholarships could not be re-verified and should be treated as unconfirmed.
programs.intakes: Autumn. Admission exams typically early September; teaching begins November.
programs.applicationOpens: UNVERIFIED as to exact window — governed by the conservatoire's annual ammissioni notice, which for 2026/2027 appeared around July 2026 (PRIOR CYCLE — confirm the 2027/2028 dates). Universitaly pre-enrolment required separately for non-EU applicants on the Ministry's earlier calendar.
programs.deadline: UNVERIFIED — set by the annual ammissioni notice. Portfolio and CV must reach mets@conservatoriocuneo.it before the September exam date.
programs.visaEligible: YES. State conservatoire second-level diploma supports an Italian student visa and permesso di soggiorno per studio, subject to Universitaly pre-enrolment and the annual non-EU contingent.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: PARTIALLY — CORRECTED DOWNWARD. The previous report called this 'LIKELY THE MOST OPEN OF ANY ITALIAN OPTION FOUND' and speculated that a sound-engineering degree would have no reason to demand solfège. That is now disproven from source: the second prova covering lettura cantata, intonation, rhythm, ear training and music history applies to this track identically, with exemption limited to conservatoire first-level diploma holders. He would sit it. The entry TITLE is open (Laurea di I livello explicitly accepted) and the FIRST exam is genuinely well-matched to him — a practical mix, a foley reel, an engineering portfolio and a motivational interview are all things a software engineer can build toward. But the musicianship examination stands, exactly as at DCSL34. Open on paper, gated in practice.
programs.recommendation: VALUE VERDICT: CONDITIONAL. RATING: B. — CORRECTED SIGNIFICANTLY. The previous report flagged this as 'INVESTIGATE AS A PRIORITY — potentially the best fit of all' on the hypothesis that admission rested on an aptitude interview rather than a musicianship exam. That question is now answered, and the answer is no: METS publishes a dedicated Biennio TS admission page the previous agent never found, and it imposes the same second prova (lettura cantata, ear training, storia della musica) on anyone without a conservatoire first-level diploma. The previous record also cited the wrong source URL. This is not the open door it was billed as. What remains genuinely attractive, and it is not nothing: DCSL61 is a real state second-cycle degree in SOUND ENGINEERING, the subject closest to his actual background and stated career interest; the entry title requirement explicitly accepts his Laurea di I livello; and the first exam — mixing a supplied multitrack, presenting an original foley/video sound work, presenting prior engineering projects, and a motivational interview — is the most learnable and most engineer-friendly assessment of any programme here. His BSc is a real asset in that room. On cost it ties with DCSL34 for cheapest. Verdict for him: apply, but as a co-equal second choice with DCSL34 and behind Rovigo, and only if he commits to closing the ear-training and solfège gap during the portfolio year. Between the two Cuneo tracks he should prefer THIS one over DCSL34 — same musicianship hurdle, but a first exam that plays to his strengths instead of testing compositional skills he does not have. Actions: write to mets@conservatoriocuneo.it in autumn 2026 confirming that a foreign three-year Software Engineering degree exempts him from neither prova, asking the expected standard of the second prova, asking the required Italian level, and requesting the Regolamento contributi. Build a technical portfolio — foley to picture, multitrack recordings, mixes, masters, DSP work — not a compositional one. If Cuneo does not work out, DCSL61 also runs at Frosinone, Reggio Calabria and Vibo Valentia and those are worth checking, as entry rules vary by institution even under a shared ministerial code.

programs.program: Corso accademico di secondo livello in Composizione audiovisiva e sound design (Biennio)
programs.institution: Conservatorio di Musica "Giuseppe Verdi" di Como
programs.institutionType: State conservatoire within the AFAM system, under the Ministero dell'Università e della Ricerca
programs.publicPrivate: PUBLIC — CONFIRMED. A Conservatorio Statale di Musica in the AFAM system with a long-established electronic music department. Its being public is not in doubt; its being reachable is.
programs.qualification: Diploma accademico di secondo livello — a real state second-cycle degree, EQF 7, equated to a Laurea Magistrale for public competitions and further study. CONFIRMED as a genuine second-cycle award: the programme exists and is a real master's-level qualification. It is simply closed to him.
programs.accreditationStatus: State-accredited AFAM second-level academic course. Genuine EHEA second-cycle qualification. No accreditation concerns — this is not a case of an institution charging master-level money for a non-degree.
programs.language: Italian — CONFIRMED on the official course page. No English-taught option.
