programs.languageRequirement: UNVERIFIED — no level published on the course page. Assume B2 Italian consistent with the sector. Academic: the entry qualification blocks him before language becomes relevant.
programs.englishTest: None.
programs.durationEcts: 2 years, 120 CFA — CONFIRMED.
programs.focus: Audiovisual composition and sound design — music and sound for image at second level, framed as a specialisation building on competencies already acquired during first-level studies in Composition or Electronic Music. The framing is the point: this is designed as a continuation for people who already have a first-cycle music degree, not as an entry point for outsiders.
programs.whatYouStudy: Year one: audiovisual communication theory, orchestration, audiovisual composition, music informatics, electives. Year two: advanced audiovisual composition, music applied to images, audio post-production technologies, integrated audiovisual composition. The presence of orchestration and the weight of composition modules confirm this is a composer's degree, taught to people who can already write music on paper.
programs.entryRequirements: HARD BLOCKER — CONFIRMED, but the previous report's description needs CORRECTING as too narrow. The previous report stated entry is restricted to holders of a Composition diploma. In fact the official page accepts a wider set: Diploma in Composizione (previgente ordinamento), diploma accademico di primo livello in Composizione, diploma accademico di primo livello in MUSICA ELETTRONICA, and correlated first-level or previgente-ordinamento courses of the Conservatorio di Como. So Electronic Music graduates are admitted too — the previous report was wrong to exclude them. HOWEVER, the correction does not help HIM: unlike Rovigo and both Cuneo tracks, this course does NOT list a generic 'laurea triennale' or 'Laurea di I livello' among qualifying titles. Every accepted route requires a prior MUSIC qualification. His Software Engineering BSc is not a qualifying title. All candidates must additionally pass a selection examination.
programs.auditionSpec: The hardest examination of the four, and HARDER than the previous report recorded. Verbatim framing: 'Per essere ammessi al biennio è necessario superare un esame di ammissione consistente in una Prova specifica di selezione relativa alla disciplina principale.' WRITTEN tests: 'Realizzazione di una esposizione, di un divertimento e di uno stretto di fuga a 4 voci' on a given subject — i.e. writing the exposition, divertimento and stretto of a FOUR-VOICE FUGUE; composition of a piano piece on a provided outline; orchestration of a piano piece chosen by the commission; and analysis of a significant twentieth-century score. ORAL: CORRECTION — the previous report said 'three original compositions' generically. The page is more specific and more demanding: 'almeno tre composizioni libere: una per piccola orchestra, una per gruppo da camera, una per voce e strumento' — at least three free compositions, one for small orchestra, one for chamber ensemble, one for voice and instrument — plus a discussion of musical competencies. Additionally, candidates arriving from 'un percorso non accademico (c.d. del Previgente ordinamento)' must pass a 'Verifica delle competenze musicali in ambito storico, musicologico e analitico'. Writing a four-voice fugue and orchestrating to commission are skills requiring years of formal harmony, counterpoint and orchestration training. This is categorically out of reach within any realistic timeframe.
programs.portfolioSpec: Not a portfolio in the sense he means it. The three required works are notated scores for small orchestra, chamber ensemble, and voice and instrument — orchestral and chamber writing, not audio productions. A DAW-based electronic portfolio, however good, does not satisfy this requirement. This is the sharpest demonstration in this whole set of how differently Italian conservatoires interpret the phrase 'sound design'.
programs.equipmentRequired: UNVERIFIED — not published. Moot.
programs.facilities: UNVERIFIED — not published on the course page. Como's electronic music department is well regarded. Moot given the entry blocker.
programs.tuitionEU: UNVERIFIED — not published on the course page. Como will operate the standard Italian ISEE-banded contributo system. Not worth pursuing given he cannot enter.
programs.tuitionNonEU: UNVERIFIED — not published. Expect the standard Italian pattern where an ISEE parificato unlocks the income bands and failure to file places the student in the highest band. Whether Como instead applies a flat non-EU rate is UNVERIFIED. Note also that Lombardy and Como's position on the Milan commuter belt make living costs materially higher than at Cuneo or Rovigo — so even setting aside the entry blocker, this was the weakest of the four on cost.
programs.otherFees: UNVERIFIED. Expect tassa regionale per il diritto allo studio (Lombardy), marca da bollo and an admission application fee.
programs.totalCostEstimate: Cannot be stated — no fee data published on the course page. Como living costs are moderate-to-high for Italy at roughly €800–1,100/month, the highest of the four locations.
programs.scholarships: UNVERIFIED — none advertised on the course page. Lombardy regional right-to-study scholarships are open to non-EU students on the standard Italian pattern. MAECI as the national route. Moot.
programs.intakes: Autumn — Italian academic year.
programs.applicationOpens: UNVERIFIED — governed by the annual bando di ammissione, typically spring. Universitaly pre-enrolment required separately for non-EU applicants.
programs.deadline: UNVERIFIED.
programs.visaEligible: Yes in principle — a state conservatoire second-level diploma supports an Italian student visa and permesso di soggiorno per studio. Irrelevant in practice, since he cannot be admitted.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: NO — CONFIRMED AND FINAL. Every qualifying entry title requires a prior music qualification (Composition or Electronic Music at first level, or the previgente-ordinamento equivalents); no generic three-year university degree route is published. And even for those who qualify, the entrance examination requires writing a four-voice fugue, composing a piano piece to a given outline, orchestrating to commission, analysing a twentieth-century score, and presenting three notated compositions for small orchestra, chamber ensemble and voice-plus-instrument. This is categorically closed to a candidate with no formal composition training. There is no angle, no exception route, and no amount of portfolio work in the next year that changes it.
programs.recommendation: VALUE VERDICT: AVOID. RATING: C. — DO NOT APPLY. To be clear about why: this is not a scam and not a fake degree — it is a legitimate, accredited, state second-cycle qualification, and the AVOID verdict is about fit, not integrity. It is simply and completely closed to him. Two corrections to the previous record. First, its entry list was too narrow: the official page also admits holders of a first-level diploma in MUSICA ELETTRONICA, not only Composition graduates — so the course is somewhat more open than reported, just not open in any direction that includes him, because no generic laurea triennale route exists. Second, the audition is HARDER than reported: the three required compositions are specified as one for small orchestra, one for chamber ensemble and one for voice and instrument, i.e. notated ensemble scores, on top of the four-voice fugue, the piano composition, the orchestration and the twentieth-century score analysis. The value of keeping this record is that it marks the boundary of what is reachable. Italian state conservatoire second-level courses vary enormously in openness under similar-sounding titles: Rovigo's DCSL60 admits any three-year degree and assesses by portfolio and conversation; Como's course, in nearly the same subject area, demands a composition diploma and a fugue. Knowing Como sits at the closed end saves him an application, a fee and several weeks. If the audiovisual composition subject matter is what attracts him, Rovigo's DCSL60 Musica Applicata covers substantially the same ground — composition for music applied to images is its largest credit block — and is open to him on the published rules. Choose Rovigo over Como on every dimension that matters: entry, examination, cost of living, and probability of admission.

programs.program: Máster en Enseñanzas Artísticas en Nuevas Tecnologías de la Música Actual: Creación e Interpretación
programs.institution: Real Conservatorio Superior de Música de Madrid (RCSMM)
programs.institutionType: State conservatoire (Conservatorio Superior de Música), Enseñanzas Artísticas Superiores sector — outside the university system but at the same MECES/EQF level
programs.publicPrivate: PUBLIC — CONFIRMED. RCSMM is a centre of the Consejería de Educación of the Comunidad de Madrid. Its own masters pages publish a regional 'precios públicos' scale with income-banded discounts, which is a public-price instrument, not a commercial price list.
programs.qualification: Título Oficial de Máster en Enseñanzas Artísticas. CONFIRMED on the official page as MECES Nivel 3 (Real Decreto 1614/2009) / EQF Level 7, and the page explicitly states it 'habilita acceso al Doctorado'. This is a real state-recognised second-cycle degree, legally equivalent in rank to a Máster Universitario. Not a título propio.
programs.accreditationStatus: Official. Título Oficial de Máster en Enseñanzas Artísticas, MECES 3 / EQF 7 with doctoral access, stated on the conservatoire's own programme page. Ministry-register listing and Fundación Madri+D verification are consistent with this but were not re-read in this pass.
programs.language: Spanish. CONFIRMED verbatim on the official page: 'Tanto el documento del TFM como la defensa oral son en idioma español.' No English track.
programs.languageRequirement: No certificate level is published. The admission process includes a personal interview (10%) plus motivation letter (10%) conducted in Spanish, and the TFM and its defence must be in Spanish. Whether a DELE/SIELE certificate is formally demanded remains UNVERIFIED — ask the Secretaría. Practically he would need solid B2+ Spanish.
programs.englishTest: None. English is not the medium of instruction and no IELTS/TOEFL appears anywhere on the official pages. This removes one obstacle but replaces it with a harder one.
programs.durationEcts: 60 ECTS, one academic year in two semesters. CONFIRMED breakdown: Formación General 16 ECTS; Formación Creativa 20 ECTS; Formación Complementaria 12 ECTS; Trabajo Fin de Máster 12 ECTS. NEW FACTS from the official masters page: attendance is mandatory ('asistencia obligatoria'); timetable is Thursday afternoon, Friday morning/afternoon and Saturday morning/afternoon; maximum permitted duration is 2 years, extendable to 3 with justification; a student must pass a minimum of 12 ECTS in the first year to continue.
programs.focus: New technologies in contemporary art music, in two tracks: Interpretación (contemporary performance, optionally electroacoustic/multimedia) and Composición (contemporary composition with electroacoustic/multimedia creation).
programs.whatYouStudy: Electroacoustic and multimedia creation and performance, contemporary repertoire, technology applied to current art music. It is an academic contemporary-music programme. There is no commercial production, DJ practice, mixing/mastering or music-business content, so even if he got in it would not directly serve the producer/DJ goal.
programs.entryRequirements: CORRECTED AND MADE PRECISE. The official page states the programme is for 'Titulados en Enseñanzas Artísticas Superiores, de Composición o Interpretación' OR 'titulados superiores de Grado o equivalente' from Spanish or foreign universities 'en centros de educación superior musical'. The second route is a degree route, but the qualifying clause is that it must be from a HIGHER MUSIC EDUCATION institution. SMU MedTech is not one. Separately the general RCSMM masters page states the baseline as 'Título Superior de Música, Grado Universitario o equivalente' (MECES 2 / EQF 6) plus programme-specific requirements — marginally looser wording, but the programme-specific music clause governs. HARD BLOCKER stands.
programs.auditionSpec: CORRECTED — the 40% component has TWO alternative forms, which the previous record collapsed into one. Official weighting: personal interview 10% + motivation letter 10% (20% combined); adecuación del programa al perfil 15%; CV, maximum two sides, 15%; related experience 10%; and then EITHER 'Interpretación de obra de música actual (máx. 20 min.)' 40% for the performance track OR 'Composición: presentación de tres obras originales' 40% for the composition track. The composition route is therefore a submitted portfolio of three original works, not a live audition — meaningfully different from what was previously recorded, though still assuming conservatoire-level compositional output.
programs.portfolioSpec: For the composition track: three original works, worth 40% of the admission score, plus CV (max two sides) and motivation letter. For the performance track: a contemporary work of up to 20 minutes. Submission format and file specifications are not published — ask the master coordinator.
programs.equipmentRequired: UNVERIFIED — not published. Ask the conservatoire.
programs.facilities: UNVERIFIED — not detailed on the programme page. RCSMM has electroacoustic studios but no inventory is published.
programs.tuitionEU: CORRECTED — the previously reported discount bands were wrong. The official RCSMM masters page publishes a full price of €12,966.00 for a 60-ECTS master year (€216.10/ECTS) with income-based discounts as follows: family income up to €15,000 → 80% discount → €2,593.20; €15,001–€50,000 → 75% → €3,241.50; €50,001–€100,000 → 70% → €3,889.80; above that → no discount → €12,966.00. Plus a €19 administrative fee (this is on the official page, not a secondary source) and seguro escolar €1.12/year for students under 28. THE FLOOR IS €2,593.20, NOT €648 — the earlier figure was out by a factor of four and was based on non-existent 95/90/85% bands.
programs.tuitionNonEU: THE RATE HE WOULD PAY: between €2,593.20 and €12,966.00 for the single year, plus €19 admin and €1.12 insurance. There is no separate nationality rate — the scale is income-based, not nationality-based, so in principle a Tunisian applicant with a low family income falls in the 80% band at €2,593.20. The open question is EVIDENCE: RCSMM does not publish how a family with no Spanish tax declaration proves 'renta familiar', and if it cannot be evidenced the default is the undiscounted €12,966.00. Ask the Secretaría in writing: 'Un estudiante extracomunitario sin declaración de renta en España, ¿con qué documentación acredita el tramo de renta familiar, y en qué tramo se le sitúa por defecto?'
programs.otherFees: Administrative fee €19 (CONFIRMED on the official masters page — previously logged as an unverified secondary-source figure). Seguro escolar €1.12/year, compulsory for students under 28. Separate Ministry fee for homologación/equivalencia of the foreign degree — amount UNVERIFIED.
programs.totalCostEstimate: Tuition €2,593–€12,966 for the one year depending on how the income band is evidenced, plus roughly €20 in fees. Madrid living costs approximately €1,000–1,400/month, so €9,000–12,600 for the academic year. Realistic all-in for a best-case discount: roughly €12,000–15,000; worst case roughly €22,000–25,000.
programs.scholarships: No programme-specific scholarship is advertised. Spanish MEFP general becas normally require prior legal residence and are not available to a first-time arrival on a study visa. Comunidad de Madrid becas coverage of enseñanzas artísticas superiores másteres for non-EU students is UNVERIFIED.
programs.intakes: September, one intake per year, one academic year.
programs.applicationOpens: CORRECTED — this was previously logged as UNVERIFIED and guessed as 'spring'. The official masters page publishes the 2026-27 calendar: registration 8–23 June 2026, entrance exams 30 June – 4 July 2026 (PRIOR CYCLE). For a September 2027 start expect an early-to-mid June 2027 registration window with exams end of June / early July 2027 — a summer cycle, not a spring one. This matters: it collides with the Italian conservatoire timetable and leaves very little margin before a September start.
programs.deadline: Approximately 23 June 2027, extrapolated from the confirmed 8–23 June 2026 window for 2026-27 (PRIOR CYCLE — confirm when the 2027-28 calendar is published, from about April 2027).
programs.visaEligible: Yes. An official Máster en Enseñanzas Artísticas at MECES 3 supports a Spanish student visa (visado de estudios) and the corresponding student residence authorisation for a non-EU national.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: NO — CONFIRMED as the decisive blocker. Both published entry routes require a music qualification: higher artistic education in Composition or Performance, or a Grado from a higher MUSIC education institution. A BSc in Software Engineering from a technology university satisfies neither. On top of that, 40% of the admission score is a conservatoire-level performance or a set of three original compositions.
programs.recommendation: DO NOT APPLY for September 2027. Two errors in the previous record are now corrected and both make it worse for him, not better: the cheapest possible fee is €2,593.20 and not €648, and the application window is June–July, not spring. The entry gate is unchanged and closed — both routes demand a music qualification and 40% of the score is a performance or three original compositions. One genuinely useful nuance did emerge: the composition route is a submitted portfolio rather than a live audition, so if he ever does obtain a qualifying music degree this is reachable without performance chops. Keep it as a five-year aspiration, not a 2027 application. Do still send the Secretaría the income-band evidence question, because the same Madrid public-price mechanism governs every Madrid enseñanzas artísticas option he might consider later.

programs.program: Máster en Enseñanzas Artísticas en Sonología Aplicada y Creación Sonora (SACS)
programs.institution: Conservatori Superior de Música "Joaquín Rodrigo" de València (CSMV)
programs.institutionType: State conservatoire attached to ISEACV (Institut Superior d'Ensenyances Artístiques de la Comunitat Valenciana), a public autonomous body of the Generalitat Valenciana
programs.publicPrivate: PUBLIC — CONFIRMED. CSMV is an ISEACV-adscribed centre of the Generalitat Valenciana. Corroborated in this pass by the conservatoire's own Secretaría page, which routes fee payment through the regional education system portal and applies the statutory Spanish seguro escolar — both markers of a public centre.
programs.qualification: Título Oficial de Máster en Enseñanzas Artísticas — a real state-recognised second-cycle degree (MECES 3 / EQF 7), legally equivalent to a Máster Universitario and giving doctoral access.
programs.accreditationStatus: Official. Verified by ANECA and homologated by the Ministry of Education; the programme presents itself as the first Sonology qualification to obtain that status. Listed in the Ministry register of Máster en Enseñanzas Artísticas. Not a título propio.
programs.language: Spanish (Castilian), CONFIRMED. Some administration appears in Valencian/Catalan. No English-taught route is advertised.
programs.languageRequirement: No certificate level is published. The access test and interview are conducted in Spanish. Whether a formal DELE/SIELE level is demanded is UNVERIFIED — ask info.sacs@csmvalencia.es. He should plan for a genuine B2 in Spanish by early 2027 regardless.
programs.englishTest: None required. Not an English-medium programme.
programs.durationEcts: 60 ECTS, CONFIRMED, with a cohort capped at 12 students per year ('12 Alumnos cada curso') — CONFIRMED verbatim. CLARIFICATION ADDED: the CSMV Secretaría publishes enrolment rules of minimum 18 and maximum 72 ECTS per year, with part-time defined as 18–36 credits and full-time as 37–72. The 60 ECTS can therefore be taken in one full-time year or spread over two part-time years. The programme's own page shows two TFM deposit convocations (15 May and 15 June), consistent with a one-year full-time default.
programs.focus: Applied sonology and sound creation — by a wide margin the most production-adjacent and most technically relevant of the Spanish public conservatoire masters, deliberately spanning art-music and applied/commercial practice.
programs.whatYouStudy: CONFIRMED on the official site: deep learning applied to sound, mathematics with Python, música comercial (commercial music), composition for video games, live streaming and event production, advanced mixing and mastering, live electronics, and applied research in new technologies. The Python/deep-learning and mixing/mastering strands play directly to a software-engineering background, and the commercial-music plus live-streaming/event-production strands are the closest any Spanish public master gets to his DJ/producer ambition.
programs.entryRequirements: CONFIRMED as a RECOMMENDED profile rather than a legal bar: higher artistic studies in Music in the Sonología specialism, or Composición Musical, or a Grado de Música in Composición Musical, and students are expected to have 'una formación técnica suficiente en el ámbito de la tecnología musical'. That last clause is the one he can actually satisfy — a software engineer arguably has more technical formation in music technology than a composition graduate. But an access test still gates entry and the profile wording is softer than Madrid's or Castellón's, not absent.
programs.auditionSpec: A prueba de acceso is required; provisional and definitive admission lists are published before the test is convened. The CONTENT OF THE TEST IS STILL NOT PUBLISHED anywhere on the official site — this remains the single largest unknown and the reason this programme cannot yet be rated A. Registration for the 2026-27 access test ran 27 February – 14 April 2026 (PRIOR CYCLE). Ask info.sacs@csmvalencia.es directly what the prueba consists of and whether a technology/production portfolio can stand in for conservatoire musicianship.
programs.portfolioSpec: UNVERIFIED — not published. Given the subject matter a sound portfolio is very likely accepted or required. Confirm with the coordinator.
programs.equipmentRequired: UNVERIFIED — not published. The Python/AI and mixing modules imply a personal laptop with a DAW.
programs.facilities: CSMV occupies a purpose-built building near Valencia's Ciutat de les Arts i les Ciències. No studio or lab inventory is published — ask for a visit or an equipment list.
programs.tuitionEU: STILL UNVERIFIED, and I could not resolve it in this pass. The Secretaría page links a fees document hosted on Google Drive that is not machine-readable, and no per-credit figure for másteres in enseñanzas artísticas appears in the page text. Valencian public prices are set by regional decree and have been frozen for several years; Valencian public university master credits sit in the low tens of euros per ECTS. Request the current 'preu per crèdit del màster' directly from the Secretaría.
programs.tuitionNonEU: STILL UNVERIFIED and this remains the highest-value question to press. No differentiated extracomunitario rate appears anywhere in the CSMV material read in this pass — but absence of mention is not confirmation of absence. Valencian decrees have historically not applied the Catalan-style non-EU surcharge to enseñanzas artísticas superiores. Ask in writing: '¿Existe un precio diferenciado por crédito para estudiantes extracomunitarios no residentes en el máster SACS?' If the answer is no surcharge, this is almost certainly the best value-for-relevance option in Spain for him.
programs.otherFees: Seguro escolar €1.12, CONFIRMED on the Secretaría page as compulsory for students under 28 at course start, payable to a CaixaBank account (ES13 2100 6270 5313 0043 4458). Expect additionally an access-test fee and a separate Ministry fee for homologación/equivalencia of the foreign degree — both UNVERIFIED.
programs.totalCostEstimate: Cannot be stated responsibly until the per-credit price is obtained. Valencia living costs are roughly €700–950/month, materially cheaper than Madrid or Barcelona, so roughly €6,300–8,600 for an academic year in living costs. If the credit price proves to be in the Valencian public range with no non-EU surcharge, total all-in for the year would plausibly land under €10,000 — the cheapest genuinely relevant option in this sweep.
programs.scholarships: UNVERIFIED for non-EU applicants; nothing programme-specific is advertised. ISEACV publishes centre-level research funding, not student scholarships. MAEC-AECID is the realistic Spain-wide route for a Tunisian national and does cover official másteres — confirm that enseñanzas artísticas superiores fall within scope for the 2027 call.
programs.intakes: September, single annual intake, 12 places.
programs.applicationOpens: Access-test registration opened 27 February 2026 for the 2026-27 cycle (PRIOR CYCLE). Expect a comparable late-February 2027 opening for September 2027. Separately CONFIRMED for context: enrolment (matrícula) for admitted students ran 14–17 July 2026 with a late window to 29 October 2026 — so the sequence is register in February, test in spring, enrol in July.
programs.deadline: Access-test registration closed 14 April 2026 for 2026-27 (PRIOR CYCLE — confirm the 2027-28 date). Plan on mid-April 2027 and have the portfolio finished by February 2027 so it can be sent with the registration.
programs.visaEligible: Yes. An official Máster en Enseñanzas Artísticas supports a Spanish student visa and student residence authorisation for a non-EU national.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: POSSIBLY — the most open of the three Spanish public conservatoire options, and the only one where the door is not formally shut. The profile is explicitly framed as recommended, and the clause requiring 'sufficient technical formation in music technology' is one a software engineer can argue he meets better than most applicants. The unpublished access test is the real gate. Treat as genuinely uncertain until the coordinator answers in writing.
programs.recommendation: APPLY — still the strongest Spanish public target for him and the most important Spanish lead in this sweep; nothing found in this verification pass weakened it. Everything checkable checked out: 60 ECTS, 12 places, the eight subject areas including commercial music, Python/deep learning, mixing and mastering, game audio and live streaming. What did NOT get resolved is the money and the test content, and those are the two things that decide whether this is an A or a C. Act in autumn 2026, do not wait for the call: email info.sacs@csmvalencia.es with exactly three questions — (1) can a Software Engineering BSc holder with a self-built sound portfolio and no music degree be admitted; (2) what does the prueba de acceso consist of; (3) is there a differentiated per-credit price for non-EU non-residents. Spend the portfolio year building to this syllabus specifically: a Python/DSP audio tool, a game-audio implementation, and three finished mixed-and-mastered electronic tracks. With 12 places, a relationship with the coordinator before applying is worth more here than anywhere else in this list. Spanish to B2 by early 2027 is non-negotiable; his French will make that faster than he expects.

programs.program: Máster en Enseñanzas Artísticas de Composición Multimedia
programs.institution: Conservatori Superior de Música "Salvador Seguí" de Castelló (CSMC)
programs.institutionType: State conservatoire attached to ISEACV (Institut Superior d'Ensenyances Artístiques de la Comunitat Valenciana), Generalitat Valenciana
programs.publicPrivate: PUBLIC. CSMC is an ISEACV-adscribed centre of the Generalitat Valenciana and the study plan went through the Ministry homologation route, which is the public/officially-authorised centre pathway.
programs.qualification: Título Oficial de Máster en Enseñanzas Artísticas en Composición Multimedia — a real state-recognised second-cycle degree (MECES 3 / EQF 7). The official page describes it as a 'máster oficial'.
programs.accreditationStatus: PARTIALLY CORRECTED. What the official course page actually states is that the master is 'acreditado por la Agencia Nacional de Evaluación de la Calidad y Acreditación (ANECA)' and is a 'máster oficial'. The previous record asserted a specific BOE citation (Orden EFP/667/2023, BOE-A-2023-14859) as though it were on the page — it is not; that citation was imported from elsewhere and could not be re-confirmed in this pass. The degree is genuine and official; treat the specific BOE reference as unverified until the order itself is read.
programs.language: Spanish, with Valencian in administration (the site publishes in both). CORRECTION TO THE PREVIOUS ENTRY'S FRAMING: the course page genuinely does not state a language of instruction, so this is an inference from the institution and the site languages, not a confirmed fact. No English-taught route exists.
programs.languageRequirement: Not published. UNVERIFIED — Spanish at working level is assumed rather than certified. Irrelevant in practice given the entry blocker below.
programs.englishTest: None.
programs.durationEcts: CORRECTED TO HONEST UNCERTAINTY: the official course page does NOT state a credit total or duration. 60 ECTS over one year is the ministerial standard for this degree class and is the reasonable assumption, but it is genuinely unstated on the page and should not be reported as fact.
programs.focus: Multimedia and multidisciplinary musical composition — deepening and extending knowledge, research and use of technological tools applied to musical creation environments, per the official page.
programs.whatYouStudy: Technology applied to musical creation across media: multimedia composition, computer-assisted and algorithmic composition, acoustics and psychoacoustics, interactive media generation, plus a Trabajo Fin de Máster. This is a composition degree with a technology apparatus, not a production or audio-engineering degree.
programs.entryRequirements: CONFIRMED VERBATIM on the official page: 'dirigido a graduados y graduadas en la especialidad de composición'. This is a hard blocker. There is no alternative route published for holders of non-music degrees.
programs.auditionSpec: The page links 'Procedimientos de acceso y admisión' but publishes no detail on the course page itself. UNVERIFIED. Given the composition-graduate entry route, expect a portfolio of scores and compositions to be central.
programs.portfolioSpec: UNVERIFIED — not published.
programs.equipmentRequired: UNVERIFIED — not published.
programs.facilities: UNVERIFIED — not published.
programs.tuitionEU: UNVERIFIED on the official page — no price appears anywhere in the course material. The previously cited €500–€1,000 range is a secondary-source estimate with no institutional backing and should not be relied on. Ask the CSMC Secretaría.
programs.tuitionNonEU: UNVERIFIED. Same open question as CSMV Valencia: the Valencian fee decree governs and it is not established whether a non-EU non-resident surcharge applies to enseñanzas artísticas superiores. Ask in writing — though for him the entry requirement, not the price, is what rules this out.
programs.otherFees: UNVERIFIED. Expect seguro escolar €1.12 as at the sister ISEACV centre, plus an access-test fee and a Ministry homologación fee.
programs.totalCostEstimate: Cannot be stated responsibly — no institutional price is published. Castellón is among the cheapest Spanish university cities, roughly €600–800/month living costs. The cost is not the deciding factor here; the entry requirement is.
programs.scholarships: UNVERIFIED — none advertised on the programme page.
programs.intakes: September, one intake per year.
programs.applicationOpens: UNVERIFIED — not published on the course page, which links only an academic calendar PDF. ISEACV runs a common access-test calendar; watch iseacv.gva.es and conservatorisuperiorcastello.com from about January 2027.
programs.deadline: UNVERIFIED — not published. Expect a spring window aligned with the ISEACV access-test calendar; the sister centre in Valencia used 27 February – 14 April for 2026-27 (PRIOR CYCLE).
programs.visaEligible: Yes — an official Máster en Enseñanzas Artísticas supports a Spanish student visa and student residence permit for a non-EU national.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: NO — CONFIRMED. Entry is stated on the official page as being for graduates in the composition specialism, full stop. Without a composition degree he does not meet the published route, and the syllabus (algorithmic and computer-assisted composition) assumes prior compositional training he does not have.
programs.recommendation: DO NOT APPLY for 2027 — the entry requirement was re-read on the official page in this pass and is unambiguous. Two things in the previous record needed correcting for accuracy rather than for outcome: the specific BOE order citation is not on the official page and could not be confirmed, and the 60 ECTS figure is an assumption rather than a published fact. The degree is real and ANECA-accredited; that is not in doubt. Keep this recorded because it completes the map — there are exactly three official Spanish public conservatoire masters in this field (Madrid RCSMM, Valencia CSMV, Castellón CSMC) and only Valencia is realistically open to him. Revisit only if he ever completes a composition qualification: Castellón is cheap, the degree is unambiguously real, and the intake is small enough to be reachable.

programs.program: Màster Universitari en Música com a Art Interdisciplinari / University Master's Degree in Music as an Interdisciplinary Art
programs.institution: Universitat de Barcelona (UB) with Universitat Rovira i Virgili (URV) and Escola Superior de Música de Catalunya (ESMUC)
programs.institutionType: Joint official university master run by two public universities plus the public Catalan music conservatoire; CSIC's Institució Milà i Fontanals collaborates
programs.publicPrivate: PUBLIC. UB (coordinating university, coordinator Dr. Josep Lluís i Falcó) and URV are public Catalan universities; ESMUC is a public centre of the Generalitat de Catalunya. The per-credit pricing follows the Catalan public 'preus públics' decree structure.
programs.qualification: Màster Universitari (official university master), 60 ECTS — a real state-recognised second-cycle degree in the university track, giving doctoral access.
programs.accreditationStatus: Official university master awarded by UB jointly with URV and ESMUC. Genuine EQF 7 second-cycle degree.
programs.language: Catalan AND Spanish — CONFIRMED on the official page as 'Catalan, Spanish'. Catalan is a normal medium of instruction, not a courtesy. There is no English route. He speaks neither, and Catalan in particular is not something French fluency shortcuts.
programs.languageRequirement: No certificate level is published for admission; the requirement is functional ability to follow classes in Catalan and Spanish. Whether UB demands a formal certificate is UNVERIFIED.
programs.durationEcts: 60 ECTS over one academic year, September to June. NEW DETAIL CONFIRMED: classes run Monday to Friday, 16:00–20:00 — a full weekday-afternoon commitment, which rules out combining it with work.
programs.englishTest: None.
programs.focus: Music as an interdisciplinary art — relationships between music and the plastic and visual arts, literature, cinema and new technologies. Musicological and humanities-led.
programs.whatYouStudy: Interdisciplinary connections across music, plastic and visual arts, literature, cinema and new technologies. New technologies appear as an object of academic study, not as a production skill. There is no mixing, mastering, DAW, studio, synthesis, spatial-audio or game-audio training anywhere in it.
programs.entryRequirements: CONFIRMED: a degree in one of the branches of human sciences, preferably history of art, or musicology, communication or musical studies. 'Graduates will also be admitted from other university disciplines, but each case will be studied individually.' Musical expertise is beneficial but explicitly not mandatory. A Software Engineering BSc would be an 'other discipline' individual-assessment case — formally possible, which is unusual for Spain.
programs.auditionSpec: No audition. Admission is by individual assessment of academic record and profile. Musical knowledge is assessed but a high level is expressly not required.
programs.portfolioSpec: No portfolio requirement published. Whether a motivation letter or writing sample is required is UNVERIFIED — ask UB admissions.
programs.equipmentRequired: None published — this is a seminar-based humanities master.
programs.facilities: UB humanities facilities plus ESMUC. No production studio provision relevant to his goals.
programs.tuitionEU: €27.67 per credit, approximately €1,660 for 60 credits. IMPORTANT CAVEAT NOW CONFIRMED: the official page itself labels these figures as referring to the 2021-2022 academic year. They are five years stale.
programs.tuitionNonEU: CORRECTED IN STATUS, NOT IN NUMBER. The published figure is €82 per credit for non-EU students not resident in Spain, approximately €4,920 for the 60-credit degree — but the official page states this is a 2021-2022 figure, and the previous record presented it as current. Do not budget on €4,920; the current Catalan decree rate will be higher. What survives, and is the genuinely transferable finding, is the STRUCTURE: Catalonia applies an approximately 3x surcharge to non-EU non-resident students on official university masters (€27.67 vs €82 per credit in the published year). That multiplier, not the absolute euro figure, is what he should carry to every other Catalan option including UPF and UB programmes.
programs.otherFees: Standard UB administrative and insurance charges on top; amounts UNVERIFIED.
programs.totalCostEstimate: Tuition at least €4,920 for a non-EU non-resident and realistically more given the stale price base, plus Barcelona living costs of roughly €1,100–1,500/month for a September-to-June year, so approximately €15,000–19,000 all-in. Poor value for content that does not serve his goals.
programs.scholarships: None advertised for this programme. Catalan and UB schemes generally require prior residence.
programs.intakes: September, one intake, running September to June.
programs.applicationOpens: UNVERIFIED — the ESMUC page does not publish it and the UB programme pages I attempted returned 404. UB official master pre-inscription normally opens in winter/spring preceding the September start; check the UB masters admissions portal from about January 2027.
programs.deadline: UNVERIFIED — contact UB directly.
programs.visaEligible: Yes — an official Màster Universitari supports a Spanish student visa and student residence permit.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: Yes in principle — CONFIRMED that graduates of other university disciplines are admitted on individual assessment and that high-level musical knowledge is not required. This is genuinely unusual by Spanish standards and is the only thing this programme has going for him.
programs.recommendation: DO NOT APPLY — and note that the fee data point the previous record leaned on is stale. The official page labels the €27.67 / €82 per-credit figures as 2021-2022, so €4,920 is a floor, not an estimate; carry forward the roughly 3x non-EU multiplier as the transferable fact and get current numbers from UB before using them anywhere. The programme itself remains wrong for him on two independent grounds. First, it is taught in Catalan and Spanish, and Catalan is a real barrier that his French does not solve. Second, it is a musicology and interdisciplinary-arts degree in which new technologies are studied rather than practised — no mixing, no mastering, no DAW, no studio, no synthesis. Newly confirmed: classes run Monday to Friday 16:00–20:00, so it would consume his year entirely. It would not move him one step toward being a producer or DJ. Use the fee structure, discard the programme.

programs.program: DCSL34 — Diploma Accademico di Secondo Livello in Musica Elettronica (Biennio)
programs.institution: Conservatorio Statale di Musica "Giuseppe Verdi" di Torino
programs.institutionType: State conservatoire within the AFAM system (Alta Formazione Artistica, Musicale e Coreutica), under the Ministero dell'Università e della Ricerca
programs.publicPrivate: PUBLIC — CONFIRMED. 'Conservatorio Statale', a state institution under the MUR's AFAM division. DCSL34 is a ministerial course code. Its fee regime is anchored to the EDISU Piemonte regional right-to-study tax and payments run through PagoPA, the Italian public-administration payment system — both confirmed on the official fee page.
programs.qualification: Diploma Accademico di Secondo Livello in Musica Elettronica. A real state second-cycle degree: under Italian law the biennio di II livello is equated to a Laurea Magistrale for public competitions and further study, at EQF level 7. Not a private certificate.
programs.accreditationStatus: State-accredited. DCSL34 is a ministerial course code in the MUR AFAM register. Fully recognised across the EHEA.
programs.language: Italian — CONFIRMED by the admission process, which includes a dedicated 'Test di lingua italiana per stranieri' applied 'solo per i candidati di nazionalità estera'.
programs.languageRequirement: An Italian language test forms part of the entrance examination, applied only to candidates of foreign nationality. The required level is not stated on the course page (details are on a separate conservatoire page); Italian conservatoires normally demand B2. Exact level UNVERIFIED — ask the segreteria. Budget the portfolio year for Italian to B2; his French makes this the fastest language acquisition available to him in this whole sweep.
programs.englishTest: None. English is not the medium of instruction.
programs.durationEcts: 2 years, 120 CFA (60 per year) — the ministerial standard for a biennio di II livello. The course page links a Piano di studi PDF rather than stating the total inline, so the inline figure remains UNVERIFIED, but the standard is not in doubt.
programs.focus: Electronic music — electroacoustic composition, music informatics, live electronics and studio practice in the Italian conservatoire tradition, with a notably technical entrance profile.
programs.whatYouStudy: Electroacoustic repertoire and its analysis, electronic and electroacoustic composition, music informatics, electroacoustics, and programming for music. The admission test itself names Max, PureData, Csound and SuperCollider, which tells you where the technical centre of gravity sits. Detailed module list is in the linked Piano di studi PDF — UNVERIFIED in detail.
programs.entryRequirements: CONFIRMED VERBATIM, and this is the decisive good news. Candidates must hold EITHER 'Diploma di Conservatorio (sia di ordinamento tradizionale che di nuovo ordinamento)' OR 'Diploma di laurea (triennale o quinquennale) o di titolo conseguito all'estero riconosciuto idoneo'. A foreign three-year university degree explicitly qualifies. His BSc in Software Engineering meets the formal entry requirement outright. What he must then survive is the entrance examination, not a paper gate.
programs.auditionSpec: Six-part entrance examination, CONFIRMED: (1) presentation of a portfolio — mandatory, uploaded via Dropbox at least one week before the practical exams; (2) practical analysis of electroacoustic repertoire using DAW software and headphones, with analysis tools such as Acousmographe permitted; (3) a test of knowledge in mathematics, informatics, music informatics and electroacoustics, including programming in Max, PureData, Csound or SuperCollider — explicitly 'NON CONDIZIONANTE' (non-binding), so it informs placement rather than gating entry; (4) a motivational interview covering general knowledge of electronic music; (5) a practical composition test, 'SOLO PER I CANDIDATI CHE NON PROVENGONO DA CORSI DI MUSICA ELETTRONICA A INDIRIZZO COMPOSITIVO', consisting of building a short electroacoustic piece from assigned samples — this WOULD apply to him; (6) the Italian language test, only for foreign-nationality candidates. Nothing here assumes conservatoire performance ability.
programs.portfolioSpec: MAJOR CORRECTION, AND THE MOST IMPORTANT FINDING OF THIS ENTIRE RE-CHECK. The official page does not ask for a 'portfolio compositivo' as previously recorded. It asks for 'un portfolio di composizioni E/O lavori di carattere tecnico-scientifico' — a portfolio of compositions AND/OR WORKS OF A TECHNICAL-SCIENTIFIC CHARACTER. Technical and scientific work is an accepted alternative to composition, not a supplement to it. That single conjunction transforms this programme for a software engineer with no music degree: an audio DSP library, a spatialisation engine, a synthesis tool, a machine-listening project or a published technical write-up can carry the portfolio. Uploaded by Dropbox at least one week before the practical exams. The previous instruction to build 'original electroacoustic works, not DJ mixes' was directionally right about DJ mixes but wrong to exclude the technical route, which is where his actual advantage lies.
programs.equipmentRequired: The analysis exam uses DAW software and headphones; whether these are supplied or brought is UNVERIFIED — bring his own headphones. A personal laptop with a DAW is effectively assumed, and familiarity with at least one of Max, PureData, Csound or SuperCollider should be treated as required preparation given the technical test.
programs.facilities: UNVERIFIED in detail — not published on the course page. Torino's Conservatorio has an established electronic music school; ask for a studio visit or equipment list.
programs.tuitionEU: CONFIRMED on the official fee page. Contributo onnicomprensivo annuale of €2,300 for most schools, Triennio and Biennio alike, but €2,500 specifically for Musica Elettronica and Direzione d'Orchestra. Paid in three instalments: first €156.00 (tassa EDISU + marca da bollo) between 20 May and 10 June; second by 30 December; third by 15 March, this last calculated against certified ISEE documentation. A 30% reduction applies to part-time enrolment. Late payment incurs a €60.00 surcharge. Payments run through PagoPA.
programs.tuitionNonEU: €3,500 PER YEAR — THE RATE HE WOULD PAY, CONFIRMED on the official fee page as the contributo onnicomprensivo annuale for extra-UE students not resident in Italy. Over two years: €7,000. It follows the same three-instalment schedule with €156 due first. This flat rate appears to be charged instead of the ISEE-scaled system that applies to EU and Italy-resident students — the official page presents ISEE certification as governing the third instalment for the ordinary regime while stating a single figure for extra-UE non-residents. Whether an ISEE parificato can nonetheless reduce it is UNVERIFIED and worth one email, because a yes would save €5,000 over two years. Torino remains the most expensive Italian conservatoire in this sweep and the one where the low-income route is least clearly available.
programs.otherFees: €156.00 first instalment comprising tassa regionale EDISU Piemonte plus marca da bollo, stated as excluded from the contributo figure. Immatricolazione and frequenza charges are likewise stated as excluded — amounts UNVERIFIED, ask the segreteria. Late-payment surcharge €60.00. Diploma issue fee at graduation UNVERIFIED.
programs.totalCostEstimate: Approximately €7,000 tuition over two years, plus roughly €312 in EDISU and bollo, plus Turin living costs of roughly €800–1,100/month — Turin is among the cheaper large Italian cities. Two-year all-in approximately €27,000–34,000 before any scholarship. An EDISU Piemonte award would cut this substantially.
programs.scholarships: EDISU Piemonte, the regional right-to-study agency, runs income-based borse di studio that non-EU students can win, covering fees, a maintenance grant and subsidised housing — the realistic route to something approaching full funding in Italy. A typical Tunisian family income should place him in the lowest bracket. The bando normally opens in the summer preceding the academic year. EDISU eligibility requires an ISEE parificato in practice; budget time and money for obtaining one via a CAF or Patronato. MAECI Italian Government scholarships are the other national route. No programme-specific scholarship is advertised.
programs.intakes: Autumn — the Italian academic year begins late October or November, with admission exams typically in September.
programs.applicationOpens: UNVERIFIED on the pages read. Italian conservatoire ammissioni bandi are typically published in spring and close in summer. For a 2027/28 start, watch conservatoriotorino.eu from about March 2027. Non-EU applicants must ALSO complete Universitaly pre-enrolment on the Ministry's separate and earlier calendar — this is the step that most often derails non-EU applicants and it cannot be recovered if missed.
programs.deadline: UNVERIFIED. Note the confirmed 20 May – 10 June enrolment instalment window in the fee schedule (PRIOR CYCLE), which implies the admission cycle concludes considerably earlier than a September exam date would suggest. Treat spring 2027 as the real operational deadline.
programs.visaEligible: Yes. A Diploma Accademico di Secondo Livello at a state conservatoire supports an Italian student visa (visto per studio) and permesso di soggiorno per studio. Non-EU applicants resident abroad must pre-enrol through Universitaly before sitting the entrance exam and are admitted against an annually published non-EU contingent — check the conservatoire's contingente for Musica Elettronica early, as it can be very small.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: YES — CONFIRMED, and more strongly than previously recorded. The published entry requirement accepts a foreign three-year degree outright. The conservatoire has built three separate bridges for non-electronic-music graduates: the portfolio explicitly admits technical-scientific work as an alternative to compositions, the technical knowledge test is expressly non-condizionante, and the composition practical is sample-based and applies only to candidates without prior electronic-music composition training. This is the most genuinely open door to a non-music engineering graduate in the entire six-programme set.
programs.recommendation: APPLY — and this now rates higher than in the previous sweep because of one verified phrase. The portfolio requirement is 'un portfolio di composizioni e/o lavori di carattere tecnico-scientifico': technical-scientific work is an accepted alternative, not a supplement. That means his software-engineering output — a DSP library, a synthesis or spatialisation tool, a machine-listening project, a game-audio engine — can carry the single most important element of the application, alongside original electronic pieces rather than instead of a music degree he does not have. Combined with an entry requirement that explicitly accepts a foreign triennale, a non-binding technical test, and a sample-based composition task aimed precisely at candidates like him, this is the clearest path in the set. Three actions in the portfolio year: (1) Italian to a tested B2, fastest of any language option available to him; (2) build a dual portfolio — three or four original electroacoustic pieces PLUS two documented technical-scientific audio projects, and get fluent in Max or SuperCollider since the technical test names them; (3) map the Universitaly pre-enrolment calendar in autumn 2026 and verify the non-EU contingent for Musica Elettronica, because a tiny quota can close an otherwise open programme. The cost is the real caveat: €3,500/year for extra-UE non-residents is the highest Italian figure in this sweep and the flat rate appears not to be ISEE-reducible. Ask the segreteria whether an ISEE parificato changes it, and apply to EDISU Piemonte in the same cycle. Note honestly that this is an electroacoustic composition and music-informatics degree, not a route to commercial dance-music production — it would make him an excellent audio programmer and sound designer, and a technically formidable producer, but the DJ career would be built alongside it, not by it.

programs.tuitionEU: RE-VERIFICATION FAILED THIS PASS — consbo.it fee pages returned 404 or a bot-check interstitial. Carried forward from the 2025/2026 Regolamento tasse e contributi and to be reconfirmed: for Bienni in Direzione d'Orchestra, Direzione di Coro, Musica Applicata, MUSICA ELETTRONICA and Jazz, imposta di bollo €16.00 + assicurazione €10.00 + tassa regionale ER.GO €140.00 + contributo di funzionamento up to €2,000.00, so a maximum of €2,166.00 per year. Other bienni cap at €1,800; trienni at €1,600. The contributo is reduced on a sliding ISEEU scale, with full exoneration at ISEEU up to €22,000 subject to merit conditions, and percentage-based figures across the €22,001–€40,000 bands. Admission application fee €100.00 for Bienni, non-refundable.
programs.tuitionNonEU: THE RATE HE WOULD PAY, carried forward and NOT re-verifiable this pass — treat as high-value but provisional. Bologna's Art. 14 on non-EU international students provides that a non-EU student can access the income-based reduction on the contributo di funzionamento only by presenting ISEEE certification (the foreign-income equivalent of the ISEE) issued by an authorised body such as a CAF or Patronato. Failure to present the ISEEE means automatic assignment to the highest contribution band, and an ISEEE returning €0.00 is rejected and likewise triggers the highest band. Practical consequence: with a correctly filed ISEEE reflecting a typical Tunisian family income he would very likely fall at or below the €22,000 threshold and pay little or no contributo, i.e. roughly €166/year in bollo, insurance and ER.GO tax; without it he pays roughly €2,166/year. That paperwork is worth roughly €4,000 over two years — but confirm the current-year figures with the segreteria didattica before planning on them.
programs.otherFees: Imposta di bollo €16.00/year; assicurazione €10.00/year; tassa regionale ER.GO €140.00/year, paid separately by postal order or bank transfer rather than through PagoPA and NOT reducible by ISEE; admission application fee €100.00 per application. Late-payment penalties apply. Fuori corso students pay higher contributo. Diploma issue fee UNVERIFIED. All carried forward and pending reconfirmation.
programs.totalCostEstimate: Best case with ISEEE filed: roughly €166/year in unavoidable charges, about €330 over two years, plus the €100 admission fee. Worst case without ISEEE: about €4,332 over two years. Bologna living costs are high for Italy at roughly €900–1,300/month and student housing is notoriously scarce — factor that in seriously, as it can outweigh the fee advantage over Turin. Two-year all-in approximately €25,000–34,000 depending on housing, before any ER.GO award.
programs.scholarships: ER.GO, the Emilia-Romagna right-to-study agency, runs income-based scholarships open to non-EU students covering a maintenance grant, fee exemption and subsidised accommodation and meals. Combined with a low ISEEE this is the closest thing to full funding in the Italian state conservatoire system. The bando typically opens in summer. Obtaining the ISEEE through a Patronato or CAF is the prerequisite for both the fee reduction and the scholarship — the single most valuable piece of Italian paperwork he can prepare. MAECI government scholarships are the alternative national route.

programs.recommendation: WORTH PURSUING, but the eligibility question must be answered before he invests anything in it. The syllabus is confirmed and is the best technical fit in this entire sweep for a software engineer — programming languages and systems for audio (7 CFA), multimedia programming, interactive multimodal environments, digital audio spatialisation, and 15 CFA of integrated audiovisual composition covering sound for film, theatre, dance and videogames. Those are modules where his background is an asset. What could NOT be verified in this pass is everything else: the conservatoire's site is behind an active bot-verification layer, so the entry requirements, the B2 Italian requirement, the fee regulation and the ISEEE rule are all carried forward from the prior sweep unconfirmed. First action, autumn 2026: phone or email the segreteria didattica (051 221483 / 051 233975) and ask three things — whether a foreign three-year Software Engineering degree plus a documented electronic-music and technical portfolio is accepted as 'equivalent' for DCSL34 admission, what the Bando di ammissione requires, and whether the ISEEE route to contributo exoneration still stands for a non-EU non-resident. Cite Torino's DCSL34 wording, which accepts any foreign triennale outright, when asking the first question. Meanwhile treat Torino as the primary Italian target and Bologna as the strong second: Torino's door is confirmed open, Bologna's is merely not confirmed shut. Two preparations serve both: tested Italian B2, and the ISEEE paperwork route mapped with a Patronato well before enrolment. And be clear with him about what this is — an electroacoustic composition and sound design degree that would make him a formidable sound designer and audio programmer, not a commercial dance-music production course.
